" data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images " **28;31373;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 989490 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Home inspections have never gone out of style , but they have lost some of their appeal in the frenzied real estate market of &lt;a href= " http : **34;31403;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Greater Vancouver&lt;/a&gt; in the past few years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since about 2015 , the number of inspections has dropped dramatically &amp;mdash ; the first casualty of high-pressure offers of sale on properties when days , and even hours , used to count in whether a sale was completed . The number of inspections is increasing due to the cooling market , but it&amp;rsquo ; s a shortsighted move not to undertake a professional home inspection , says Helene Barton , executive director of the Home Inspectors Association of BC &lt;a href= " https : //hiabc.ca " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; ( HIABC ) &lt;/a&gt; . And changing mandates for home inspectors are affecting the industry , which affects you , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We get calls from people when something goes wrong , and there&amp;rsquo ; s nothing we can do , &amp;rdquo ; she says of those who haven&amp;rsquo ; t had professional inspections. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jonathan Sheppard , HIABC vice-president of &lt;a href= " https : //www.jamesdobney.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;James Dobney Inspections&lt;/a&gt; agrees . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I do believe that 98 per cent of the transactions should have an inspection &amp;mdash ; both new and old builds included because what we find would floor you . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But for many homeowners , it&amp;rsquo ; s just as easy not to have an inspection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If you throw in the do-it-yourself renovations , along with multiples owners , the homes are filled with unprofessional wiring , plumbing , carpentry , smoke and carbon monoxide detectors missing or out of date , decks that are improperly constructed , missing footings , and poorly constructed hand railings with the decks carrying excess weight loads from non-permitted solariums , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some real gems Sheppard cites include crawlspaces with &lt;a href= " http : **34;31439;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;water ingress&lt;/a&gt; , foundations with cracks due to settlement and Douglas fir trees planted within two feet of a building . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The biggest advantage of a home inspection is that we educate the client about the building that is being purchased , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;nbsp ; &lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But to complicate matters , there is no longer a need for inspectors to belong to a professional organization in B.C. In 2016 &lt;a href= " https : **29;31475;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Consumer Protection BC&lt;/a&gt; introduced a new regulation that lowered the requirements necessary to become a home inspector , and reduced the qualifications of trainers for inspectors . Barton points out that if an inspector isn&amp;rsquo ; t a member of the HIABC , the consumer has no recourse and may , in fact , not be getting proper advice and recommendations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sheppard says HIABC inspectors have the highest standards , have mandatory field training and must pass an exam , plus continue ongoing education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The non-aligned inspectors have none of this ongoing commitment , &amp;rdquo ; Sheppard says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s an ongoing battle of sorts , Barton says . So why were the requirements lowered ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have absolutely no idea , &amp;rdquo ; Barton said . &amp;ldquo ; Anything with government is slow , but at least they are working with us. &amp;rdquo ; The HIABC continues to enforce high standards , training and educational requirements as it works with the Minister of Public Safety and the Solicitor-General on this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On top of this , &lt;a href= " http : **34;31506;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;home inspector renewal licensing fees&lt;/a&gt; increased by about 25 per cent each year for three years , with ensuing increases in 2019 to 2020 , by which the fees will almost double from $525 to $1,025. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What it means is that the additional costs will be passed on to the consumer , and such fees may well dissuade people from entering the profession . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Home inspectors are underpaid , &amp;rdquo ; says Barton , who adds that the regulations , coupled with fewer inspections being performed , hits inspectors hard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best advice Barton can give , she says , is to check the HIABC website and go to the &lt;a href= " https : **29;31542;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Find an Inspector&lt;/a&gt; tab to search for qualified inspectors in your area . Interview two or three , she suggests , before choosing one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And don&amp;rsquo ; t rely on your realtor to provide you with a name , or a recommendation whether to undertake an inspection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Experienced realtors control the sale . &amp;nbsp ; Often a home inspection rests in their court with a recommendation either way , &amp;rdquo ; says Sheppard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what&amp;rsquo ; s the advice for homeowners in this situation ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Realtors should be giving out a minimum of three names of inspectors , &amp;rdquo ; Barton says . &amp;ldquo ; Realtors should be at arm&amp;rsquo ; s length from inspectors . " alt= " Condo towers under construction on Gilmore in the Brentwood area of Burnaby. " data-portal-copyright= " Gerry Kahrmann " **28;31898;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 994245 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **33;31928;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; British Columbians living in newer high-rise condos likely have a higher energy footprint than they might think , according to new data from B.C. Hydro . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Crown corporation compared the electricity consumption of condominium buildings that were constructed after 2010 and higher than five storeys to others built in the last four decades , and found the newer condos used almost twice as much electricity per square foot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is due at least in part to newer buildings being equipped with all the latest amenities such as hot tubs , media rooms and gyms. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Hydro has seen an almost 22-per-cent increase in the number of apartment and condominium accounts since 2011. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With 470,000 accounts , apartments and condos are just over one quarter of B.C. Hydro&amp;rsquo ; s residential customers and account for about 18 per cent of the province&amp;rsquo ; s residential electricity consumption . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Vancouver alone , where more than a third of residents live in condos , the number of hydro accounts for apartments and condos has increased by 14 per cent since 2011 . In Victoria , the increase was 10 per cent , and 15 per cent in Kamloops. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;31963;TOOLONG ... title= " Condo towers under construction in the Brentwood area of Burnaby. " alt= " Condo towers under construction in the Brentwood area of Burnaby. " data-portal-copyright= " Gerry Kahrmann " **28;31999;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 919180 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We know with high housing prices in the province , the construction and sale of condominiums has really increased in the last few years as British Columbians are looking to purchase smaller homes , &amp;rdquo ; said B.C. Hydro spokesperson Tanya Fish . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really important for us to understand the changing electricity demand in the province , and really great for B.C. Hydro&amp;rsquo ; s long-term planning . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The largest period of growth in electricity use was between 1999 and 2009 , when high-rise buildings&amp;rsquo ; consumption grew by 65 per cent , from 647,570 kilowatt hours ( kWh ) per year to 1.07 million kWh . The average high-rise condo building ( those with five storeys or more ) built after 2010 uses about 1.05 million kWh of electricity per year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The upward trend has also been seen in condo buildings that are heated by methods other than electricity , such as gas or geothermal. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is despite individual units becoming more energy efficient because of features such as LED lighting and Energy Star appliances . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fish said the increase is largely due to the amenities in newer buildings , such as pools , hot tubs , party rooms , fitness centres and movie theatres . Newer apartment buildings tend to use less electricity than condos because they have fewer of these amenities , she added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elevators , lighting in the lobby , halls and parking garage , and heating and cooling systems also add to the electricity bill . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In newer condo buildings , about 50 per cent of the overall electricity use is covered by a common-use account that is funded by strata fees . If the cost appeared on a resident&amp;rsquo ; s hydro bill , it could add up to an additional $40 each month . The average apartment or condo&amp;rsquo ; s bill is now $43 per month . The average single-family home&amp;rsquo ; s hydro bill is $103 per month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To reduce electricity use , Fish said , developers and strata councils could use occupancy sensors to ensure lights are only on when people are present , upgrade to more efficient lighting , and add automated controls for heating , ventilation and air conditioning systems . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s options there just to cut down on the overall electricity use of the entire building , &amp;rdquo ; Fish said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those living in apartments and condos could also shade their windows on sunny days , use a ceiling fan , and install draft proofing around windows and doors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **31;32029;TOOLONG " **38;32062;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/jensaltman " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;32102;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;32135;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;32177;TOOLONG ... group disputes government claim B.C. NewsMichael Geller : In celebration of woodhttp : **36;32392;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;32430;TOOLONG ... title= " Prodigy is an award-winning project from the Adera Development Corp . " alt= " Prodigy is an award-winning project from the Adera Development Corp . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32466;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 979735 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A few years ago , I was having a conversation with an acquaintance regarding The Lagoons , a condominium development at the entrance to Granville Island . He was certain his third-floor apartment was in a concrete building . I told him it was a wood-frame building with a lightweight concrete topping on the floor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Do you want to bet a bottle of scotch ? &amp;rdquo ; he asked . I told him it would be an unfair bet since I was part of the project&amp;rsquo ; s development team and had watched it being built . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Well it seems like a concrete building , &amp;rdquo ; he responded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was reminded of this exchange at the 15th annual Wood Design Awards organized by WoodWorks , a program of the Canadian Wood Council that celebrates innovative structural and architectural achievements using wood . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In early March , more than 400 architects , engineers , designers , builders , owners and government officials gathered in the Vancouver Convention Centre , an appropriate venue considering the walls are covered in B.C. wood . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There were 103 nominations in 14 categories , showcasing wood&amp;rsquo ; s strength , beauty , versatility , environmental and cost benefits . Submissions came from throughout B.C. , as well as the U.S. and Asia , with international projects in China , Korea and Tajikistan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since 2005 when the program began , there have been some remarkable changes in wood construction in British Columbia . In those days , the maximum permitted height for a wood-frame building was four storeys . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today , six-storey wood-frame buildings are becoming the norm , and during the awards program , it was suggested that one day 12 storeys might be the norm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I thought this might be wishful thinking , but a week later the B.C. government announced changes to the building code to allow the construction of wood buildings up to 12 storeys . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Much of the credit for this code change must go to Brock Commons , an 18-storey wooden student residence at UBC that won multiple prizes at the 2017 awards . At that time , it was the tallest &amp;ldquo ; mass timber&amp;rdquo ; building in the world using new engineered wood products and construction techniques . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While some may question whether taller wood buildings can be sturdy and safe , it is noteworthy that most of Gastown&amp;rsquo ; s older buildings have structures made of wood . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While their heavy timber construction differs from the lightweight &amp;ldquo ; balloon frame&amp;rdquo ; construction used in houses and smaller apartments , today&amp;rsquo ; s new cross-laminated timber &amp;mdash ; or CLT &amp;mdash ; panels , glue-laminated timber , and parallel strand lumber products are the equivalent of heavy timber . These products , made from gluing layers of smaller pieces of lumber together , can be as strong and fireproof &amp;mdash ; yes , fireproof &amp;mdash ; as steel and concrete . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The award categories included residential wood design , commercial and industrial wood design , interior design , use of red cedar , prefabrication and other innovations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For those of us interested in housing design and construction , there were two categories , single-family and multi-family. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The seven single-family finalists included Michael Green , a Vancouver architect who has become internationally acclaimed for his pioneering wood designs . Other finalists included architects Peter Rose and Farouk Noormohamed . However , the winners were Clinton Cuddington and Piers Cunnington of Measured Architecture for their visually striking Shift House . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32496;TOOLONG ... title= " Shift House , a project from Clinton Cuddington and Piers Cunnington of Measured Architecture , took the single-family award at the 2019 Wood Design Awards . " alt= " Shift House , a project from Clinton Cuddington and Piers Cunnington of Measured Architecture , took the single-family award at the 2019 Wood Design Awards . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32532;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 979737 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The jury commented that the shingles , modernized with seven custom colours , were installed on a near 45-degree bias , with similarly coloured shingles paired to create an illusion of 10-by-10-inch hexagonal shapes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the shingles were stained and refined , the architects also used unstained , tongue-and-groove Western red cedar as a secondary cladding . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finalists in the multi-family category included Allwood Place in Abbotsford , Royce in White Rock , Travino Square in Saanich , West Quay in North Vancouver and Yorkson Creek in Langley , with the winner being Adera Development Corp . for Virtuoso . ( Adera won in the same category last year for its Prodigy project. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Designed by Rositch Hemphill Architects , Virtuoso comprises a six-storey mass timber building and townhomes with a stunning West Coast design , and is Canada&amp;rsquo ; s first private residential multi-family building to be constructed using cross-laminated timber . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like Brock Commons , Virtuoso uses CLT panels in its flooring systems . They are exposed at each balcony overhang , enhancing the building&amp;rsquo ; s style and highlighting this beautiful wood material . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another benefit of this innovative floor- and wall-assembly system is that it can significantly reduce sound transmission between homes , exceeding standards in both traditional wood-frame and even concrete construction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was not that long ago that the so-called leaky condo crisis caused significant grief for many B.C. homeowners , architects and developers . While industry experts questioned whether wood construction would ever become popular again , it was evident to everyone attending the awards program that , thanks to new wood products and improved design and construction techniques , wood is back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not just a good thing for the residential construction industry . It is also positive for B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s economy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Michael Geller is a Vancouver architect , real estate consultant and developer . He serves on the adjunct faculty of SFU 's Centre for Sustainable Development and Resource and Environmental Management . Eric Andreasen , Adera&amp;rsquo ; s vice-president of marketing and sales , says the quality of the building is set to be a big selling point . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; ve always been a leader in sustainability and we&amp;rsquo ; ve only built in wood in 50 years , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re taking that concept to the next level with &amp;lsquo ; SmartWood&amp;rsquo ; , which will allow us to beat code when it comes to sustainability . Financially , it&amp;rsquo ; s cheaper to operate on a monthly basis and it&amp;rsquo ; s also helping the planet . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Duet will also incorporate what we&amp;rsquo ; ve trademarked as QuietHome , &amp;rdquo ; Andreasen added . &amp;ldquo ; This is a propriety system of floor design and dividing walls that means our buildings perform better than the competition when it comes to the acoustics . Sound transmission is significantly reduced . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The sales centre for Duet in Burquitlam Plaza at 552 Clarke Road features a demonstration of Adera&amp;rsquo ; s noise-reducing technology . Potential buyers can compare noise levels in specially constructed rooms built either to standard code or using QuietHome. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Duet also features cross-laminated timber &amp;mdash ; or CLT &amp;mdash ; in the floors and elevator shafts of the building . A carbon-sequestering material that uses wood from sustainably managed forests , CLT performs as well if not better than concrete in numerous ways , according to Andreasen . Adera has installed an example at the Duet sales centre so that visitors will be able to experience it for themselves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Andreasen said the location of the six-storey residential building less than three blocks from the Burquitlam SkyTrain station on the boundary of Burnaby and West Coquitlam is also likely to prove popular with a wide range of buyers . In its neighbourhood plan for the area , the City of Coquitlam envisioned a walkable , complete and transit-oriented neighbourhood with a mix of housing types and access to shopping , jobs and amenities . Duet is part of that transformation , according to Andreasen. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very attractive part of the greater Vancouver area right now in terms of the value it offers and the accessibility it provides to downtown , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; Duet will give people an affordable place to live , but also allows them to go anywhere with the SkyTrain or West Coast Express very easily &amp;ndash ; rapid transit on your doorstep . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In times when people are getting a bit more discerning about where they spend their money , they want to make sure they&amp;rsquo ; re buying from somebody who&amp;rsquo ; s been around and has the experience they can count on , &amp;rdquo ; Andreason added . &amp;ldquo ; Over 50 years we&amp;rsquo ; ve worked with the very best trades and consultants in the industry and we&amp;rsquo ; re confident in the product that we&amp;rsquo ; re going to build . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for the homes themselves , kitchens will feature quartz slab countertops with porcelain tile backsplashes and single-handle faucets with pull-down sprays in matte black finishes . The appliance packages are a combination of KitchenAid and Fisher &amp;amp ; Paykel. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Homes at Duet come in two colour schemes , but there&amp;rsquo ; s plenty of opportunity to customize . Adera&amp;rsquo ; s I.D . By Me program allows buyers to personalize kitchens , bathrooms and living areas according to their liking . Options under the program include custom millwork , upgrades to the kitchen appliances , swapping out the tub for a shower with pivoting glass door and adding space-saving custom closet organizers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Duet will include a common kitchen and lounge , secure bike lockers , a storage locker for every home and electric vehicle-charging stalls . The interior designer for the project is Cynthia Florano Designs and the building was designed by Integra Architecture Inc. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32838;TOOLONG ... title= " Duet is a project from Adera in Coquitlam . Andreasen said he expects buyers from a wide range of demographics. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A lot of people grew up in Burnaby and West Coquitlam and have maybe since been living in Yaletown or Kitsilano , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; Many we&amp;rsquo ; ve spoken to are actually coming back to the area or still have family there . It&amp;rsquo ; s the first such registry in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It will ensure people taking those assignments when condo assignments are flipped actually pay their fair share of taxes , &amp;rdquo ; said James . &amp;ldquo ; Right now we have no idea . There&amp;rsquo ; s no registry , there&amp;rsquo ; s no tracking of those kind of flips . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The registry will require all developers currently building condos and other strata buildings to register every four months the status of their unit contracts , starting April 30 . After construction is complete and a strata plan filed with government , the developer must report annually for the next six years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Most developers we believe will follow it , &amp;rdquo ; said James . &amp;ldquo ; They are required by law . There are also fines in place if they don&amp;rsquo ; t. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the registry will not be available for the public and researchers . &amp;ldquo ; This will be private confidential information , &amp;rdquo ; said James . B.C. is creating a public database of beneficial ownership , that will allow people to search the names of those involved in real estate developments , corporations and numbered companies , said James . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Flipping pre-sale contracts &amp;mdash ; known as contract assigning &amp;mdash ; has been a contentious practice in recent years during the hot housing market . &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Some critics have argued pre-sales also allow wealthy foreign investors to get early access to units rather than locals . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The previous Liberal government banned so-called &amp;ldquo ; shadow flipping&amp;rdquo ; of homes in 2016 , which involved multiple quick sales without the original seller&amp;rsquo ; s knowledge and with intermediaries like real estate agents and speculators accused of pocketing the profits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;33157;TOOLONG ... title= " Condo pre-sales , such as this one in Langley , will need to be registered in a new government database . Were a bank or pension fund to do the same thing , there&amp;rsquo ; d be no question it was acceptable behaviour , said Davidoff. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They do make pre-sales more expensive when the market is hot that&amp;rsquo ; s true , &amp;rdquo ; said Davidoff. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; But I personally think buying a pre-sale is a fairly lousy way for a first-time buyer to get into the market . It&amp;rsquo ; s like buying a Bruce Springsteen ticket from a scalper &amp;mdash ; that isn&amp;rsquo ; t really a bad way to get a Bruce Springsteen ticket . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many of the buildings with pre-sold units during the hot housing market in recent years are only now complete . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not obvious that this behaviour makes Vancouver certainly in the long-run less affordable , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily buy that . But that said I think people evading capital gains tax and maybe laundering money or who knows &amp;hellip ; I think the transparency part is good . But that this is the path to affordability for the province , I don&amp;rsquo ; t really buy that argument . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;33223;TOOLONG ... title= " Tom Davidoff , an associate professor at the Sauder School of Business . Email &lt;a href= " **28;33589;TOOLONG " **35;33619;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Rob ShawTue , 26 Feb 2019 21:43:06 **45;33656;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; SellingCondosLocal NewsPoliticsMaking better use of the balconyhttp : **33;33703;TOOLONG ... &lt;p&gt; As apartments become increasingly smaller , it is important to make the best possible use of every square foot of space . However , anyone looking down from a drone flying above Metro Vancouver will observe a significant portion of many apartments is often completely wasted . I refer , of course , to the balcony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Derived from the Italian &amp;lsquo ; balcone&amp;rsquo ; , meaning scaffold , the earliest balconies date back to ancient Greece when they addressed purely functional needs such as increasing air circulation or modulating natural light into a building&amp;rsquo ; s interior . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prior to the 1960s , few Vancouver buildings included balconies since they were generally included in the building area calculation , also known as floor space ratio or FSR . However , to encourage developers to construct balconies , Vancouver City Council in 1964 introduced an FSR exemption for residential open balconies to a maximum of eight per cent of the gross floor area . As a result , new apartment building designs throughout British Columbia began to incorporate balconies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unfortunately , many of these balconies were not used . Consequently , in 1985 , Vancouver City Council adopted Balcony Enclosure Guidelines to allow balconies in existing buildings to be enclosed with glass windows and walls . Council subsequently permitted the enclosure of balconies in new construction , provided the space continued to be separate and distinct from the interior of the dwelling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As written in the 1985 guidelines , &amp;ldquo ; the purpose of an enclosed balcony is to afford an occupant the year-round enjoyment of those uses to which an open balcony normally would be used in fair and warm weather . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To address exterior design , the guidelines stated that &amp;ldquo ; careful attention should be given to preserving the design integrity of facades&amp;hellip ; through a distinctive shape and a predominance of clear glass . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unfortunately , it did not take long before some developers were enclosing all the balconies to increase saleable area . As a result , buildings became bulkier and less attractive . Consequently , in 1995 , council amended the balcony enclosure policy to restrict enclosed balconies to no more than 50 per cent of the permitted balcony area . North-facing balconies and those along busy streets were often enclosed , while others remained open . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Today , Vancouver allows balconies up to 12 per cent of the building area to be excluded from the FSR , but new enclosed balconies are generally included in the FSR . Other municipalities continue to allow open balconies up to eight per cent of the total building area , without counting in the FSR area calculation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , throughout Metro , individual condominium owners have often enclosed their balconies . Sometimes this was done with the formal approval of the strata council and the requisite municipal permits . However , in other cases , no approvals were obtained . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I recently became aware of one Vancouver building where 11 owners who enclosed their balconies decades ago without permits are now being asked to remove their enclosures . No doubt many others could soon find themselves in a similar position . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To address complaints about the lack of variety in highrise building design , increasingly architects are using balconies to add articulation and interest to building facades . One of my favourite examples is architect Jeanne Gang&amp;rsquo ; s Aqua Tower , an 82-storey mixed-use building in Chicago . Its curvilinear balconies vary in dept from 2 to 12 feet , resulting in wave-like forms on all sides of the building . The effect is marvellous . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other equally creative solutions are beginning to appear around Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While these balconies will certainly improve building appearance , often they too will remain unused , especially those in taller buildings where wind buffeting can be so extreme one can hardly leave anything on a balcony without the risk of the wind sucking it off . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While many apartment owners do not use their balconies , they insist on having them because they want to be able to get outside without riding the elevator or because they&amp;rsquo ; re afraid their unit will be harder to sell without a balcony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One Toronto realtor compared the balcony to the architectural equivalent of the NordicTrack machine . &amp;ldquo ; You buy it because you want to see yourself using it , but seldom do ; though at least an exercise machine is usable in winter . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A few years ago , while travelling through Europe , I saw an elegant , transparent , retractable glass system that made balconies more usable year round without fully enclosing them . It consisted of sliding glass panels that could be completely opened and folded against the wall . When it started to rain , the panels could be quickly closed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since the glass was frameless , the exterior design of the building was not really altered . Furthermore , since there was a small air gap at the top and bottom and between the glass panels , the balcony was not completely sealed off like it would be with an enclosed balcony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Several European companies are manufacturing these systems . They include Solarlux , ( solarlux.com ) a German company , and Airclos ( airclos.com ) based in Spain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps the best known is Lumon ( lumon.com ) , a Finnish company that has set up a manufacturing plant in Canada . It claims its glass-panel system can result in 34-per-cent energy savings and significantly reduce noise levels . It also prevents premature balcony degradation by keeping rain , snow , wind , dust and birds away from the balcony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Architects and developers in several Metro municipalities are starting to incorporate retractable balcony glass into their upcoming multi-family projects . It is a trend that I expect to become increasingly popular with prospective apartment buyers and renters. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , while the Lumon system can now be installed in new buildings in Abbotsford , Langley City and Langley Township without counting in the building area calculation , to have wider application in B.C. , it will be necessary for all municipalities to update their zoning bylaws. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The reality is , when these bylaws were drafted , balconies could either be open and excluded from FSR calculations , or fully enclosed and included in FSR. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No one expected that one day a system would be designed that allows balconies to be both completely open or partially closed and evolve into a more sensible and useful space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But then again , we weren&amp;rsquo ; t expecting Amazon&amp;rsquo ; s Alexa , Uber or autonomous cars either . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span class= " doctext " &gt;&lt;span class= " dochighlight " &gt;Michael Geller&lt;/span&gt; is a Vancouver-based architect , planner , developer and educator . He is an adjunct professor at SFU 's Centre for Sustainable Development and can be reached at geller@sfu.ca. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Michael GellerTue , 26 Feb 2019 02:26:02 **45;33738;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; SellingCondosSales slump could signal tough times ahead for B.C. realtorshttp : **32;33785;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;33819;TOOLONG ... title= " A real estate sign is pictured in Vancouver on June 12 , 2018. Email &lt;a href= " **28;34665;TOOLONG " **35;34695;TOOLONG &lt;/em&gt; &amp;lt ; /p &lt;/p&gt; Glenda LuymesFri , 08 Feb 2019 16:10:26 **45;34732;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; SellingBuying &amp;amp ; SellingCommercial Real EstateCondosLocal BusinessLocal NewsReal EstateB.C. government opens exemption process for speculation taxhttp : **37;34779;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;34818;TOOLONG ... title= " Owners of second properties in Metro Vancouver will soon be able to apply for exemptions from the government 's new speculation tax . " alt= " Owners of second properties in Metro Vancouver will soon be able to apply for exemptions from the government 's new speculation tax . " data-portal-copyright= " DARRYL DYCK " **28;34854;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 809849 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;34884;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; VICTORIA &amp;mdash ; All homeowners in B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s largest urban centres will need to apply for exemptions from the province&amp;rsquo ; s new speculation tax or receive a bill , whether they are speculators or not , the government announced Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ministry of Finance said letters outlining the first speculation tax fees and exemption processes will begin arriving at all homes in Greater Victoria , Nanaimo , Kelowna and Metro Vancouver ( excluding Bowen Island and Lions Bay , but including Abbotsford , Mission and Chilliwack ) starting this week . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It will be up to all homeowners to apply for exemptions , with a deadline of March 31 . Those who don&amp;rsquo ; t apply , or qualify , will be sent tax bills due to be paid by July 2 . The opt-out process will become an annual event for property owners under the new speculation tax rules . People who pay mistakenly can get a rebate within six years , according to the ministry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finance Minister Carole James was not available for an interview , but her ministry said the exemption process &amp;ldquo ; will help identify speculators and empty homes , allowing the government to crack down on speculation and make housing more affordable . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government&amp;rsquo ; s decision to levy every property owner in major urban centres with a tax notice , and then force them to apply for exemptions , is a backwards way to implement a misguided tax , said Liberal MLA Shirley Bond . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Just when you think a botched tax can&amp;rsquo ; t get any worse , it does , &amp;rdquo ; said Bond . &amp;ldquo ; Now&amp;nbsp ; residents in communities like Nanaimo , Kelowna and Abbotsford , to name a few , have to register to be exempt from this tax or they will get a bill in the mail for a tax they shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t be paying . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is absolutely astounding to me for an conceived tax that does not target legitimate speculators &amp;mdash ; the majority of people impacted by this tax are hard-working British Columbians . On every front , this is a mess . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NDP government&amp;rsquo ; s speculation tax was announced in the February 2018 budget and described as a way to encourage owners of empty residences to put them onto the rental market , or sell , in areas where housing is unaffordable and rental vacancy rates are low . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although first billed as a surcharge on out-of-province real estate speculators , it was later revealed that &lt;a href= " https : **33;34920;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;an estimated two-thirds&lt;/a&gt; of those who will pay the tax will be British Columbians. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Public blowback forced Finance Minister Carole James to exempt areas like the Gulf Islands , as well as water down the rate before the tax was passed into law in the fall . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because the tax is retroactive , the first letters will actually be for taxes incurred in the 2018 calendar year &amp;mdash ; before the tax rules were even finalized. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;PODCAST : Postmedia columnists Mike Smyth and Rob Shaw start 2019 by examining critical issues and predicting possible outcomes for the year ahead . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is former Premier Christy Clark ready for politics after time away ? Starting in 2019 , the rate rises to two per cent for out-of-province owners , foreigners and satellite families ( households where more than 50 per cent of income comes from outside Canada ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Owners are &lt;a href= " https : **33;34992;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;exempt from the tax&lt;/a&gt; if it is their principal residence , they rent it at least six months of the year ( only three months is required in 2018 ) , they are disabled , the property was just inherited , it&amp;rsquo ; s valued under $150,000 , or a person was away and it was vacant due to medical reasons , residential care , work or spousal separation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Condos and apartments in buildings where stratas ban rentals are also exempt , but only for 2018 and 2019 , to give stratas time to change their bylaws , according to the ministry . &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Michael BernardSat , 20 Oct 2018 13:09:04 **45;35863;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; SellingCondosDouglas Todd : Condos changed Metro Vancouver forever , for better and worsehttp : **35;35910;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;35947;TOOLONG ... title= " Condofication has caused a revolution in urban history -- and no more so than in Metro Vancouver . " alt= " Condofication has caused a revolution in urban history -- and no more so than in Metro Vancouver . " data-portal-copyright= " DARRYL DYCK " **28;35983;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 882742 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;36013;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was the year the Beatles released Hey Jude , Pierre Trudeau was elected prime minister , and &lt;a href= " http : **34;36049;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Rev . Martin Luther King&lt;/a&gt; was assassinated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was 1968 &amp;mdash ; the year that Metro Vancouver got its first condominium complex . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A great deal has changed in the ensuing 50 years . Now roughly one out of three residents of the region live in a condominium . Metro Vancouver has about 600,000 condo units , with the city of Vancouver having 130,000 of those . The province in total has about 900,000 units , according to the Condominium Homeowners Assoc. of B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;36085;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Metro Vancouver&lt;/a&gt; could be the poster city illustrating the results of the legal changes half a century ago that made condominiums possible . A strong case has been made that the &amp;ldquo ; condofication&amp;rdquo ; of Metro Vancouver has done more than anything else to define this West Coast city . It&amp;rsquo ; s come with some benefits , including for many owners , but the deeper structural effects have not all been pretty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The condo metamorphosis has led to increased density , higher land prices , more vacant dwellings , more vertical neighbourhoods , fewer purpose-build rental units , more investor owners ( domestic and offshore ) and discord between different kinds of condo owners and users . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The condo boom has arguably provided many people who could not afford a detached property the chance to own a less-costly dwelling through a strata title , without directly owning a private chunk of land . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; https : //www.youtube.com/watch ? v=4QnpN3laWjc &a; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And it&amp;rsquo ; s clear the property laws that made condominiums possible increased the density and shape of the city and its neighbourhoods &amp;mdash ; bringing far more tower clusters and making land in general more expensive . The vast majority of Metro&amp;rsquo ; s&amp;nbsp ; &lt;a href= " http : **34;36120;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;more than 1,300 highrise residential towers&lt;/a&gt; are condominium buildings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the expansion of condominiums has also , many say , discouraged the construction of purpose-built rental buildings . Developers generally prefer constructing condo complexes , since they can sell the units right away , or in advance , and realize their profits quickly . They don&amp;rsquo ; t have to patiently wait years to collect their profits in rents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the most intriguing pieces ever written about the condofication of Metro Vancouver , and other parts of North America , is by &lt;a href= " http : **34;36156;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Douglas Harris&lt;/a&gt; , a specialist in legal history and property law at the University of B.C. His article is titled Condominium and the City : The Rise of Property in Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the many points Harris makes is that the laws that made condominiums possible in Metro Vancouver contributed to the high-end gentrification of the city , and to some extent the squeezing out of low-income residents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;36192;TOOLONG ... title= " The condo phenomenon ignited in the late 1980s after the Social Credit government shocked many by selling the Expo 86 lands to one of Asia 's most wealthy real-estate developers . ( Photo : Cabinet minister Grace McCarthy , who spearheaded the sale. ) " alt= " The condo phenomenon ignited in the late 1980s after the Social Credit government shocked many by selling the Expo 86 lands to one of Asia 's most wealthy real-estate developers . ( Photo : Cabinet minister Grace McCarthy , who spearheaded the sale. ) " data-portal-copyright= " Colin Price " **28;36228;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 611486 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Much of the explanation for the higher prices in the last two decades lies in the influx of overseas capital and migrants , &amp;rdquo ; Harris writes . &amp;ldquo ; Enormous economic expansion in East Asia coupled with moments of political uncertainty and instability brought people and capital to North America and its west coast in particular . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The condo phenomenon especially ignited in the late 1980s , Harris says , after the Social Credit government shocked many British Columbians by &lt;a href= " http : **34;36258;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;selling Vancouver 's former Expo 86&lt;/a&gt; lands to one of Asia&amp;rsquo ; s most wealthy businessmen , real-estate developer Li Ka-shing of Hong Kong . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; People from Hong Kong , Taiwan and China became particularly active in the skyrocketing condominium market in Metro Vancouver . &amp;ldquo ; Since the 1990s , Vancouver has had the highest residential housing prices in the country , &amp;rdquo ; with condominium law providing the mechanism that &amp;ldquo ; expanded the market for land , embedded the city in international flows of people and capital , and , by doing so , contributed to the rising prices . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the mushrooming of condominium units has made it possible for many residents to buy into housing options other than single-family dwellings , it&amp;rsquo ; s also led to conflicts between those who own them , live in them , rent them and leave them empty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to obtain hard province-wide figures on the number of investor-owned apartments . But one reliable report to Vancouver City council , based on B.C. Assessment data , found 35 per cent of condo units in the city were owned by investors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;a name= " pda10140631 " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;div class= " PDSPoll " id= " PDIcontainer10140631 " style= " display:inline-block ; " &gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div id= " PDsuperContainer " &gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;script type= " text/javascript " charset= " UTF-8 " src= " https : **33;36294;TOOLONG ... &lt;noscript&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **29;36329;TOOLONG " &gt; ... Our **31;36360;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tony Gioventu , executive director of the Condominium Homeowners Association of B.C. , said it&amp;rsquo ; s reasonable to estimate 35 to 40 per cent of the province&amp;rsquo ; s strata units are investor owned . &lt;span style= " color:black ; font-family:Calibri , Helvetica , sans-serif ; font-size:medium ; " &gt;&lt;span dir= " ltr " &gt;&lt;span style= " color:black ; " &gt;&lt;span lang= " en-CA " **34;36393;TOOLONG ... would mean more than 300,000 apartments are not lived in by those who bought them ( whether using money made in a Canada or transferred from foreign lands ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The majority of investor-owned units are rented out , said Gioventu , especially since 2010 , when the B.C. Liberals changed the law to allow developers to designate most new units as rentable for 100 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another result of investment and speculation is that many units remain empty , even in the midst of Metro&amp;rsquo ; s housing and rental affordability crisis . There are hundreds of condo towers in Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s downtown core , and Gioventu estimated 25 to 35 per cent of their units are vacant . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That is just one of many factors that have led to condominium stresses : Between people who live in their apartments , those who rent them , speculators and recreational-property owners who leave them empty and investors who turn them into businesses through Airbnb. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;36429;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " autoplay ; encrypted-media " **34;36465;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; One of the most notorious conflicts involving investor-owners and owner-occupiers was to go this week before B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s Human Rights Tribunal , but was settled out of court Monday with a non-disclosure agreement . It centred on condominium owner Andreas Kargut&amp;rsquo ; s protest against Mandarin-language-only strata council meetings at his Richmond complex . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it&amp;rsquo ; s not hard to find other forms of discord between investors and owner-occupiers . The condominium rental study for Vancouver City council discovered complaints absentee owners were &amp;ldquo ; less willing to spend on additional or unforeseen maintenance&amp;rdquo ; and were negligent at screening renters , some of whom crowd into small units . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While generally defending the many renters in condominiums ( including a large portion of the &lt;a href= " http : **34;36501;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;more than 100,000 international students in Metro Vancouver&lt;/a&gt; ) , Gioventu said serious problems , if not horror shows , are arising because some investors are hawking their units as short-term Airbnb rentals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Too many condo owners don&amp;rsquo ; t realize they&amp;rsquo ; re liable for all damages , complaints and illegal activities related to renters , including those who sub-rent through Airbnb , Gioventu said . Not only do some Airbnb &amp;ldquo ; guests&amp;rdquo ; cause noise problems , flood bathtubs and use their units for illicit purposes , a portion take advantage of their condo security access to break into storage lockers and the units of others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s an understatement to say condominiums have been a game changer in North America . Condofication has caused a revolution in urban history &amp;mdash ; and no more so than in Metro Vancouver . The story of condos is only beginning , and their consequences will continue to unfold in far-reaching ways . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;36537;TOOLONG " **54;36565;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **25;36621;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **26;36648;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;a name= " pda10140632 " &gt;&lt;/a&gt; &lt;div class= " PDSPoll " id= " PDIcontainer10140632 " style= " display:inline-block ; " &gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div id= " PDsuperContainer " &gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;script type= " text/javascript " charset= " UTF-8 " src= " https : **33;36676;TOOLONG ... &lt;noscript&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **29;36711;TOOLONG " &gt; ... NewsPoliticsStaff BlogsDouglas Todd : The ups and downs of highrise livinghttp : **34;37178;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;37214;TOOLONG ... title= " " You never talk to your neighbours . I only see them once a week or less , " says Nelson Lee , who lives with his two adult children in an 800 square-foot apartment on the 25th floor of building in Vancouver 's Coal Harbour neighbourhood . " alt= " " You never talk to your neighbours . I only see them once a week or less , " says Nelson Lee , who lives with his two adult children in an 800 square-foot apartment on the 25th floor of building in Vancouver 's Coal Harbour neighbourhood . " data-portal-copyright= " Jason Payne " **28;37250;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 876277 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rob McDowell thought a condo on the 29th floor of a Yaletown highrise would be the route to contentment. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It had a beautiful view of Burrard Inlet . It had everything I wanted . But I soon realized I felt like I was in a gilded cage . I saw people in the elevator , but that was about it . I realized I wanted to be around people more . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So two years after he bought into the tower at 501 Pacific Boulevard , McDowell moved into a unit that opened onto that building&amp;rsquo ; s leafy courtyard . The &amp;ldquo ; accidental meetings&amp;rdquo ; among families that occur daily in the courtyard have led to lasting friendships. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McDowell&amp;rsquo ; s story offers one perspective on the psychological risks and benefits of residential highrise living . But there are hundreds of thousands of stories from people in Metro Vancouver who live in towers , and Nelson Lee offers another one of them &amp;mdash ; with decided cons and pros . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In general , I love being in downtown Vancouver . I&amp;rsquo ; ve lived in towers in Taiwan and Hong Kong and I love the freedom . But you never talk to your neighbours . I only see them once a week or less . And it&amp;rsquo ; s usually just a polite hello and goodbye , &amp;rdquo ; said Lee , who lives with his two adult children on the 25th floor of a Coal Harbour tower . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lee appreciates towers for the way they house a lot of people on a small footprint of land . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; ve got three people living in 800 square feet and we never turn on the heat , so that helps a little in the battle against climate change , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Defenders of highrise living say the units cost less to buy and rent than ground-level dwellings , create density that increases the range of nearby shops and transit options and , of course , often offer panoramic vistas. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , people skeptical of the rapid expansion of residential highrises , especially in Metro Vancouver and Toronto , maintain they tend to breed loneliness . They&amp;rsquo ; re not great for most children , according to research . Critics also report some Metro Vancouver towers have many empty units &amp;mdash ; and that some of the monoliths create hard , unfriendly streetscapes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both sides of the highrise debate can cite evidence to make their cases . So it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to come to a simple conclusion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Metro has 1,300-plus highrises&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt; Residential towers have become impossible to ignore in Metro Vancouver , where some new ones soar a dizzying 60 storeys and higher . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A city official said Vancouver proper has more than 1,064 residential highrises ( typically defined as buildings of more than five storeys ) . Burnaby has 193 . The City of North Vancouver has 78 . Surrey has 28 . Richmond doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have a count on its many towers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile it&amp;rsquo ; s virtually impossible to find a politician running in the civic elections who is promising to build more of them . Candidates are instead campaigning for the need to add &amp;ldquo ; gentle density ; &amp;rdquo ; buildings for those who can&amp;rsquo ; t afford a detached dwelling and don&amp;rsquo ; t want to raise kids at lofty heights . That&amp;rsquo ; s why we&amp;rsquo ; re mostly hearing about the need for row houses , duplexes and apartment buildings five storeys and under . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It turns out Metro Vancouver , where politicians are devising a &amp;ldquo ; livable region strategic plan&amp;rdquo ; plan for 2040 , does not even keep a tally on the number of highrises . Data gaps like that make it hard to figure out what one thinks of 2016 census results showing &lt;a href= " http : **34;37280;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Metro Vancouver is home to four of the 10 most densely populated municipalities in Canada&lt;/a&gt; : They are New Westminster , White Rock and North Vancouver City , with Vancouver proper topping the country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rooftop cranes dotting the skyline signify more highrises are coming . Michael Ferreira , principal of Urban Analytics , said 237 more highrises are slated for Metro Vancouver , bringing 93,000 new dwelling units . They&amp;rsquo ; re going up in Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s downtown , Burnaby&amp;rsquo ; s Metrotown and Brentwood neighbourhoods , North Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Lonsdale , Richmond Centre , Surrey Metro Centre , Coquitlam&amp;rsquo ; s core and elsewhere . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While construction soars , people argue not only over what towers are doing to neighbourhoods and traffic , but about their design . Some complain too many are massive and hard-edged , while others appreciate some seem to be more livable , and may be contributing to community life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Psychology of highrise living&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt; What do people who live in towers think about the high life ? Feelings are all over the urban map . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Despite enjoying the shops , restaurants and boardwalks of Coal Harbour , Nelson Lee said the downside is there are many empty units in his tower and many Airbnb guests , whose suitcases frequently fill the lobby . In addition , a 47-storey tower is being built directly outside Lee&amp;rsquo ; s window and he laments how , since he works out of his home , he&amp;rsquo ; s going to have to listen to construction for three years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s former chief city planner , Brent Toderian , chooses to live in the &amp;ldquo ; mid-rise &amp;ldquo ; level of his downtown tower , which overlooks both the courtyard and the street . &amp;ldquo ; I often refer to myself as a ground person , &amp;rdquo ; Toderian says . But he&amp;rsquo ; s all for choice , including for residents who want to hover way above terra firma. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;37316;TOOLONG ... title= " Simon Lin lives in a Brentwood highrise in Burnaby , which has views of Metrotown in the background . " alt= " Simon Lin lives in a Brentwood highrise in Burnaby , which has views of Metrotown in the background . " data-portal-copyright= " Jason Payne " **28;37352;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 876278 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Simon Lin , who arrived a year ago from Taiwan , says it&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; so far so good&amp;rdquo ; in the 12th floor two-bedroom unit he bought for his wife and college-student daughter in one of the many new towers popping up at Brentwood in Burnaby. &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a good view . And it&amp;rsquo ; s not as crowded here as in Taipei , &amp;rdquo ; said the 54-year-old retired businessman as he ate a curry salad on a patio outside Whole Foods Market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; William Wu , a 20-year-old student from China , said he found his unit in a 40-storey tower at the east end of Burnaby&amp;rsquo ; s Metrotown through a &amp;ldquo ; Chinese people&amp;rsquo ; s real estate website. &amp;rdquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s not lonely . Smoking a cigarette near the entrance , Wu said he pays his Mainland Chinese landlord $1,800 a month while he hangs out , including in the indoor gym , with other international-student friends who live in the building . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The opinions of people who live or work near Metro Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s expanding new highrise clusters are also mixed , but lean more to the negative . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m not a fan . I think it&amp;rsquo ; s better to have a bit of space and greenery , &amp;rdquo ; said Vancouverite Sandra Freeman , who once lived in a highrise because it was less expensive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jeanne Bridge , who works next to new towers around Brentwood mall , said the ceaseless construction has brought a new supermarket to the neighbourhood but also led to the death of some favourite coffee shops . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **34;37382;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Charles Montgomery , author of Happy City : &lt;/a&gt; Transforming Our Lives Through Urban Design , says he&amp;rsquo ; s not against highrises . But he advocates smaller-scale housing ; especially &amp;ldquo ; co-housing&amp;rdquo ; clusters of 12 family units facing a shared courtyard . Psychological studies of highrise towers , Montgomery said , repeatedly show many residents end up experiencing an emotional paradox : &amp;ldquo ; They feel lonely and crowded at the same time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Karn Bains , 31 , has his own insights on such alienation . As he enjoyed a coffee break at his regular spot on a concrete bench at the quiet base of several luxury condo towers at Nelson and Jubilee in Burnaby , Bains said , &amp;ldquo ; I never see people walking here , or kids playing . All I ever see is cars coming out of the underground parking lots , which is kind of weird . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2&gt;Psychological studies of high rises&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt; The University of Victoria&amp;rsquo ; s Robert Gifford is one of the world&amp;rsquo ; s leading experts on living in high rises . The specialist in psychology and environmental design published a groundbreaking analysis in 2007 of more than 100 studies on whether highrises improve or diminish well-being . It&amp;rsquo ; s gone viral . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many studies showed people are more depressed in highrises , that mental illness increased at higher floor levels , that more crowding reduced the amount of neighbour support , that tower residents worried more about fire and contagious disease , that one&amp;rsquo ; s sense of community attachment is reduced and that , overall , people were less satisfied . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gifford is the first to acknowledge many older studies were skewed because they focused on low-income highrises in the U.S. and Britain . Since then many new skyscrapers have been marketed to wealthy people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nevertheless , Gifford&amp;rsquo ; s survey helped him come to some broad conclusions , including that the upper floors of towers are generally not good for children . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Children are better off in low-rise housing . Highrises either restrict their outdoor activity or leave them relatively unsupervised outdoors , which may be why children who live in highrises have , on average , more behaviour problems , &amp;rdquo ; Gifford writes in &lt;a href= " http : **33;37418;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The Consequences of Living in Highrise Buildings . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Research is also unanimous in finding that rates of helping others are lower in highrise buildings . The nature of most highrises supports anonymity and depersonalization . Residents of highrises encounter many more other residents &amp;hellip ; but have fewer friendships in the building per capita than residents of low rises . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gifford emphasizes , however , that residential towers can work for some people . &amp;ldquo ; Evidence suggests residents in a high rise will be happier if they are not parents of small children , do &lt;em&gt;not&lt;/em&gt; &amp;nbsp ; plan to stay long and are socially competent . &amp;hellip ; Highrises are more satisfactory for residents when they are more expensive , located in better neighbourhoods and residents chose to live in them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;37453;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;37495;TOOLONG ... Todd : Why are Toronto and Vancouver so unhappy ? **36;37531;TOOLONG href= " http : **34;37569;TOOLONG ... Todd : Metro Vancouver 's ranking for ' hygge ' dropping **40;37605;TOOLONG href= " http : **34;37647;TOOLONG ... Todd : Vancouver 's rental and housing markets squeezed by temporary **41;37683;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Like other urban specialists such as Montgomery and Toderian , Gifford says the success of highrises depends a great deal on how they&amp;rsquo ; re designed . Metro has examples of towers that encourage connection , say urbanists . But the region also has more than its share of ugly , Stalinesque highrises that kill residents&amp;rsquo ; satisfaction and enjoyment of the neighbourhood by passersby. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Melbourne , Australia , provides a parallel to Metro . Ranked among the most livable cities in the world , Melbourne is also a gateway city that has been hosting a wave of transnational newcomers and investors , which politicians and developers have responded to with an explosion of highrises. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of Australia&amp;rsquo ; s most acclaimed architects , Kerry Clare , warns sky-high living is harming Australia&amp;rsquo ; s urban fabric , creating &amp;ldquo ; physical and psychological silos&amp;rdquo ; and causing more people to be &amp;ldquo ; detached from street life . &amp;rdquo ; Towers , she said , are largely &amp;ldquo ; built during economic bubbles&amp;rdquo ; and many are empty , investor-owned properties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her complaint jibes with analysis of the tower booms in Vancouver and Toronto . SFU planner Andy Yan and Stephen Punwasi , of Better Dwelling , have created maps that show Metro &lt;a href= " https : **33;37726;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;neighbourhoods with the most unoccupied dwelling units&lt;/a&gt; frequently align with those with the most towers . Highrise clusters at Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Coal Harbour and Joyce SkyTrain Station and Burnaby&amp;rsquo ; s Metrotown are more than 20-per-cent unoccupied . The highrises of Yaletown and Richmond Centre are 15 to 20 per cent empty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not conducive to community connection . As Montgomery , the author of Happy City , walked among the scores of soaring towers of Yaletown , he talked about a &lt;a href= " http : **34;37761;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Vancouver Foundation survey&lt;/a&gt; finding that residents of towers were &amp;ldquo ; half as likely to have done a favour for a neighbour&amp;rdquo ; and more likely to report having trouble making friends . &amp;ldquo ; People living in towers consistently reported feeling more lonely and less connected than people living in detached homes . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The problem of low trust correlates with how &amp;ldquo ; vertical neighbourhoods tend to be home to the city&amp;rsquo ; s most transient residents : foreign students , young people and renters who do not stay long enough to forge deep ties , &amp;rdquo ; he writes in Happy City . There are &lt;a href= " http : **34;37797;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;more than 100,000 international students in Metro&lt;/a&gt; , one of the highest rates per capita in the world . &amp;ldquo ; Crowding , &amp;rdquo ; Montgomery said , &amp;ldquo ; while pushing us together physically , actually pushes us apart socially . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2&gt;High rises and their options&lt;/h2&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since high rises remain attractive to developers , investors and some residents , urban planners urge designing them more thoughtfully . Too many buildings , critics say , are ruthlessly bare-bone , with few design elements that foster human connection . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The possibilities to make them more human-friendly are endless , but often ignored . Many architects say highrise towers need more lush rooftop gardens , gyms and playrooms , scattered among the floors . &amp;ldquo ; After all , kids can&amp;rsquo ; t play in the hallways , &amp;rdquo ; said McDowell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Montgomery strolled the streets of Yaletown , he pointed favourably to highrises where he believes the architects made an effort to help residents have vibrant daily experiences . Their ground levels were not walls of grim concrete , but a &amp;ldquo ; soft&amp;rdquo ; streetscape featuring small shops , restaurants , gardens , greenery , supermarkets and household doorsteps. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Montgomery and Toderian are among the urbanists who praise some of the City of Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s signature &amp;ldquo ; podium and point tower&amp;rdquo ; high rises , which feature a low-rise&amp;nbsp ; apartment building abutting the sidewalk to psychologically soften the massiveness of the high tower behind it . It&amp;rsquo ; s called &amp;ldquo ; the Vancouver model . &amp;rdquo ; However , Montgomery has had depressing experiences among many highrise clusters in Metro , where he often notices blank walls at the base of residential towers . They create a &amp;ldquo ; hard&amp;rdquo ; street atmosphere , and alienation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though Metro Vancouver is known for its dramatic shift to highrises , public discussion remains muted . Despite being in the midst of civic elections , Yan notes , &amp;ldquo ; Nobody in the campaign has said , &amp;lsquo ; Let&amp;rsquo ; s put up more towers . ' &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While towers are &amp;ldquo ; highly efficient investment vehicles , &amp;rdquo ; Yan said &amp;ldquo ; they&amp;rsquo ; re not a panacea&amp;rdquo ; for a region in which one of the biggest challenge of families and businesses is &amp;ldquo ; finding a way to keep people in their mid 30s. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many alternatives to towers , especially for young families , are not often being tried in Vancouver or North America . Melbourne planner Michael Buxton is one tower critic who values how his city is finally starting to build more six-storey apartments . &amp;ldquo ; Substantial increases in urban density don&amp;rsquo ; t require highrise buildings . Many of the world&amp;rsquo ; s densest cities are located in Europe and the Middle East with uniform building heights between three to seven storeys , &amp;rdquo ; Buxton said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Likewise , Yan tends to support those who are calling for more lowrise housing for the &amp;ldquo ; missing middle . &amp;rdquo ; Let&amp;rsquo ; s not forget , the planner said , that most people in New York City don&amp;rsquo ; t live in highrises in Manhattan , but in low-rises in the Bronx and Queens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The debate over the pros and cons of highrise living , to Yan , is part of a crucial larger one for the city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Who are we building for ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;37833;TOOLONG " **33;37861;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **25;37896;TOOLONG " **26;37923;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Douglas ToddSat , 06 Oct 2018 16:38:38 **45;37951;TOOLONG ... NewsRelationshipsStaff BlogsWestcoast Homes and DesignConcord Pacific 's amenity-rich Park George will be big on smart designhttp : **34;37998;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38034;TOOLONG ... title= " Park George is a project from Concord Pacific in Surrey . PNG Merlin Archive " alt= " Park George is a project from Concord Pacific in Surrey . PNG Merlin Archive " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38070;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 871496 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are not many places where a new condo comes with access to two private swimming pools , an outdoor hot tub theatre , a tennis court , a work lounge , a sports social lounge , a virtual spin studio and a video conferencing room . Park George , the latest offering from Concord Pacific in Surrey , is one such place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Part of the reason for the extraordinary range of amenities on offer at Park George is because residents will be able to make use of the facilities that are already in place at Park Avenue , two of Concord Pacific&amp;rsquo ; s previous residential towers nearby . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We call our developments master-planned communities because we try to share the amenities across a number of towers &amp;ndash ; in this case four &amp;ndash ; so that it keeps people&amp;rsquo ; s strata fees down , &amp;rdquo ; explained Grant Murray , senior vice-president of sales at Concord Pacific . &amp;ldquo ; In total , there will be about 110,000 square feet of amenity space , 30,000 square feet of it indoors . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You simply won&amp;rsquo ; t find the same range of amenities in a single residential tower , or even two towers , &amp;rdquo ; Murray added . &amp;ldquo ; And you certainly won&amp;rsquo ; t find them in a location that is so well connected in terms of transit . It&amp;rsquo ; s really a big selling point for us. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Park George&amp;rsquo ; s two towers of 36 and 39 storeys will include 339 homes in total . The neighbourhood around the development has been a decade in the making , when the City of Surrey came up with a long-term plan to transform the city centre into a new urban core . This involved adding multiple highrise residential buildings , retail offerings and amenities , a new location for Surrey City Hall , the expansion of Surrey Memorial Hospital , and a new RCMP headquarters . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Then you&amp;rsquo ; ve also got the extra rapid transit that will be coming to Surrey in the near future , extending the transit options south down to Newton , &amp;rdquo ; Murray said . &amp;ldquo ; We recognized 10 years ago that Surrey was really going to explode in popularity as somewhere people want to live and work . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Park George is going to be dead centre in all of this new development and it&amp;rsquo ; s also right next to two parks &amp;ndash ; Holland Park and Quibble Creek , &amp;rdquo ; Murray added . &amp;ldquo ; That means you&amp;rsquo ; ll never have anything in front of you and there are excellent view corridors . This is because Quibble Creek is a riparian park that is designated as protected green space . It gives you a lovely suburban feel in an urban setting . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Murray explained that the City of Surrey is aiming to transform , not just its residential environment , but its economic one as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everything&amp;rsquo ; s been gearing up to make this a new urban area and they&amp;rsquo ; re hoping to attract high-tech companies to the city in particular , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The City of Surrey&amp;rsquo ; s website talks extensively about its aspirations to become a &amp;ldquo ; Smart City&amp;rdquo ; , which aims to create &amp;ldquo ; sustainable economic development and a high quality of life for&amp;hellip ; residents by considering innovation and technological advancements as a key ingredient in&amp;hellip ; decision making , strategy and investment . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Concord Pacific and Park George , in particular , are well set up to contribute to this vision , according to Murray . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; These are the first towers in Surrey that will have 100-per-cent electric vehicle parking , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; They also have a keyless entry and the WiFi connection will be fantastic so you&amp;rsquo ; ll be able to walk around anywhere in the building and be connected , including in the elevators . With all of these smart ideas , we&amp;rsquo ; re really catering to that generation that does everything with their phone . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kitchens at Park George include Panasonic microwaves and Bosch appliance packages with wall ovens , four-burner gas cooktops , stainless steel hood fans and built-in fridge-freezers . Bathrooms have Grohe fixtures , Kohler sinks and built-in shower niches . There are two colour palettes to choose from &amp;ndash ; Sunrise Chiffon and Evening Silk &amp;ndash ; and suites also come with Blomberg washers and dryers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Murray expects the amenities at Park George to be a key selling point when sales open this month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because the density in the area is so high , you&amp;rsquo ; re generating enough money to be able to put in a huge amount of amenity space , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; The amenities across the four towers really complement each other so there&amp;rsquo ; s always something on offer no matter what you&amp;rsquo ; re into or what the weather is doing at any given time of the year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Homes at Park George will range in size between 573 and 2,056 square feet . &lt;p&gt; Architects can sometimes run a gauntlet when they are designing residential buildings , trying to create an interesting looking structure from the outside without running afoul of design guidelines or compromising the interior space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That is the challenge that Andrew Emmerson and GBL Architects faced when they were asked to design Winona on Cambie , a new 38-unit building along the Cambie Corridor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We wanted to create some energy and movement and cadence to the exterior expression of the building , &amp;rdquo ; Emmerson said . &amp;rdquo ; So we worked with the idea of a flux expression along the fa&amp;ccedil ; ade , &amp;rdquo ; which reflects the flow of traffic on a busy Cambie Street . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The result is a kind of interweaving of balconies and floor orientation vertically and horizontally with the building , which will rise over the next two years at West 61 **25;38246;TOOLONG &amp;nbsp ; Avenue and Cambie , adjacent to Winona Park . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A lot of credit goes to the client , &amp;rdquo ; the architect noted . &amp;ldquo ; When he came to us , he wanted to do something different and challenged us with the design task of breaking out of the mould . He was fairly hands off during the design process and gave us a free rein . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Along the way , the building&amp;rsquo ; s form was designed to optimize sunlight inside the homes while providing shade from the summer sun , he said . As well , stretching out the balconies along the building&amp;rsquo ; s west side facing Cambie served to dampen the sound of traffic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Emmerson said the client also wanted to have a mix of homeowners who reflected the area , whether they are first-time buyers or people moving out of larger single-family homes in the area . As a result , the building&amp;rsquo ; s suites range from relatively modest studios at 418 square feet to three-bedroom penthouses of 2,109 square feet and large private rooftop patios . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mukhan Rai , president of Raichu Development Group , said he is pleased with the final result . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We worked closely with GBL to create Winona&amp;rsquo ; s striking exterior fa&amp;ccedil ; ade , and I am excited that this building will be unlike anything on the Cambie Corridor , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; The stunning geometric architecture of the building is engineered with a unique angled fa&amp;ccedil ; ade that maximizes opportunities for view exposure , privacy and natural light . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rai said many of the homes are indeed spacious . &amp;ldquo ; Someone who is looking to downsize from a single-family home to single-level living will not have to compromise on space or quality of finishes . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He noted all homes include a Sub-Zero and Wolf appliance package in the kitchens , polished Cambria quartz countertops with a waterfall edge and a unique built-in wood-frame detailing over the bathroom vanity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our one- and two-bedroom homes are very spacious as well . From 754 to 874 square feet , these homes are designed for those seeking a lifestyle balance with their home being nearby to urban conveniences such as transit and shops , as well as recreation and parks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Each home offers outdoor living space on a private balcony that includes electricity , gas and water connections .
