All homes have a Blomberg front-load washer and dryer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Appliance packages vary with the suite sizes , with 30-inch integrated refrigerators with two freezer drawers in the two- and three-bedroom homes , while one-bedroom and studio models have 24-inch wide versions . The same applies with 30-inch and 24-inch Wolf built-in convection wall ovens . All homes come with Panasonic microwaves and Asko dishwashers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the bathrooms , 24-by-24-inch tile extends from the floor to walls , and a tiled shower with glass enclosure has a niche and linear shower drain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In main bathrooms , the bathtub has a tile front face that matches the floor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rooftop patios with views of surrounding parks on Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s west side feature an outdoor kitchen with a 36-inch Napolean built-in stainless steel barbecue and a 28-inch flush-mount cabinet with double stainless steel doors for a propane tank and 17-inch Napolean drawers . Topping it off is a 24-inch Marvel undercounter outdoor stainless steel refrigerator . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All homes are covered by a 2-5-10 New Home Warranty and are LEED Gold certified on completion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Project : &lt;/strong&gt; Winona on Cambie &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Project location : &lt;/strong&gt; 7638 Cambie St. , Vancouver &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Project Scope : &lt;/strong&gt; 38&amp;nbsp ; studio , one- , two- and three-bedroom homes , ranging from 418 to 2,109 square feet in a six-storey concrete building . Others are waiting a month , and some have just ended their shoots early . While two weeks seems like a short period , it isn&amp;rsquo ; t in an industry that already comes packed with volatility and uncertainty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are a lot people worried about their livelihood . For instance , a lot of actors and background performers I know that have said , &amp;lsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve got five or six days of booked work and now I have nothing and I live paycheque-to-paycheque , what am I going to do ? &amp;rsquo ; Walker said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; From that standpoint , they are all nervous . They don&amp;rsquo ; t know how long the industry is going to be suspended . There is no work and there won&amp;rsquo ; t be for the foreseeable future . We&amp;rsquo ; re all going to have to calm some nerves and figure out a plan to take care of each other . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The plan now isn&amp;rsquo ; t clear . Industry unions have sent messages to the federal and provincial governments reminding them not to forget about the arts when it comes time to distribute emergency funding . Union websites have posts suggesting members seek out groups that help artists and apply for government benefits . A lot of actors , in particular , are self-employed so they don&amp;rsquo ; t qualify for unemployment benefits , however the Government of Canada just announced its COVID-19 Economic Response Plan . The plan will provide up to $27 billion in direct support to Canadian workers and businesses including those self-employed within the film industry . &amp;nbsp ; The unions have also told members that upcoming dues deadlines will be pushed back and reviewed over the course of this economic downturn . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are dealing with the situation regarding COVID-19 as it unfolds in real time . With things changing so quickly we can&amp;rsquo ; t comment on any specifics . This is an unprecedented situation , not only locally but globally , and we continue to work in the best interest of the professional artists and technicians of the ( International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees ) Local 891 through this difficult time , &amp;rdquo ; said IATSE spokesman Phil Klapwyk in an email to Postmedia News . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The community , of course , reaches well beyond the faces you see on the screen . It literally takes a village to make a TV show or film . The tens-of-thousands of people the industry employs around B.C. include food-vendors , drivers , rental companies , special effects people , hair and makeup folks , and on and on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In this industry , historically , people are always a bit jumpy about when the next job is coming because you don&amp;rsquo ; t always know . But , in the last few years , we have never had to really worry about that , &amp;rdquo ; said Vancouver TV/film hairstylist Jim Dreichel ( See and The Chilling Adventures of Sabrina ) , referring to the rebound in the industry after a slow period about seven years ago . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s been massive . Most of us turn down work all the time because we are already working . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Now there is nothing . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Co-owner Glenn Ennis of Vancouver specialty camera team Peacemaker Filmworks ( Deadpool 1 &amp;amp ; 2 , The Predator , Arrow , Supergirl ) said the company wrapped a major car commercial March 15 , and now is looking at two months of nada. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;39073;TOOLONG ... title= " Peacemaker Filmworks co-owner and stunt actor Glenn Ennis is one of the many , many people in the TV/film-production business in B.C. who have seen work disappear due to COVID-19. There are any number of special events designed to commemorate this , including the Vancouver Symphony&amp;rsquo ; s Beethoven Experience set of concerts and events March 7 through 21. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , I hear you ask , isn&amp;rsquo ; t every classical music season a Beethoven year ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40603;TOOLONG ... title= " Ludwig van Beethoven . " alt= " Ludwig van Beethoven . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;40639;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1223982 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1959 , the great Leonard Bernstein talked about our fixation with the composer in his book The Joy of Music . In one of his landmark essays he noted , with more than a hint of exasperation : &amp;ldquo ; Ever since I can recall , the first association that springs to anyone&amp;rsquo ; s mind when serious music is mentioned is &amp;lsquo ; Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; . When you walk into a concert hall bearing the names of the greats inscribed around it on a frieze , there he sits , front and centre , the first , the largest , the most immediately visible , and usually gold-plated. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet Lenny had his answers about why Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s stature remains larger than life , and I have a few ideas too : he&amp;rsquo ; s that good , that radical , that human , that uplifting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Good thoughts to keep in mind during a year of multiple helpings of the great master&amp;rsquo ; s work , mostly good , sometimes bad , rarely indifferent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What has the VSO got in store for us , and how will it add to our understanding of LvB ? I think it&amp;rsquo ; s all about creating a nuanced understanding of context : what his music meant in his own time , and how his legacy evolved through the ages up to the present day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The centre of the Beethoven Experience is two concerts , &lt;strong&gt;A Most Remarkable Night , Parts 1 and 2&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( March 13 and 14 at the Orpheum ) &lt;/em&gt; . This is a two-evening duplication of a single early 19th century program the VSO describes as &amp;ldquo ; an astounding four-hour concert that saw the premi&amp;egrave ; res of both the 5th and 6th Symphonies , the Choral Fantasy , and his Piano Concerto No. 4 , along with an improvised piano fantasy &amp;mdash ; Beethoven conducting and playing all of it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This program is pragmatically stretched out over two evenings to suit 21st century audiences , for whom a four-hour-plus extravaganza would be too much of a good thing . Placing three masterworks in proximity enables a new way of hearing ultrafamiliar repertoire , just like conductor Otto Tausk&amp;rsquo ; s trilogy of late Mozart symphonies last season . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;In the Heart of the Symphony&lt;/strong&gt; ( &lt;em&gt;March 11 ) &lt;/em&gt; , takes the renowned Fifth Symphony to unfamiliar turf for the orchestra : the heritage Commodore Ballroom . The strategy is bring the audience up close and real personal with the orchestra , and I think it&amp;rsquo ; s a simple , great idea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tracing how the Beethoven myth grew and mutated over time is another aspect of the Beethoven Experience . **27;40669;TOOLONG : Chamber Concert&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( March 9 , Christ Church Cathedral ) &lt;/em&gt; &amp;nbsp ; will include a performance of Brahms&amp;rsquo ; s landmark Piano Quintet . It demonstrates how Beethoven impressed the best and brightest of the mid-19th century composers , and also includes baritone Tyler Duncan singing Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s An die ferne Geliebte. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The decision to reprise former VSO composer-in residence Rodney Sharman&amp;rsquo ; s Archaic Smile in &lt;strong&gt;Beethoven The Modernist&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; ( March 7 at the Orpheum ) &lt;/em&gt; , shows that contemporary figures still feel a connection to Beethoven as the grandfather ( I use the gender intentionally ! ) of the radical tradition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;40698;TOOLONG Eroica&lt;/strong&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;em&gt; ( March 20 and 21 at the Chan Centre ) , &lt;/em&gt; led by Australian-born composer , conductor and violist Brett Dean offers another object lesson in how today&amp;rsquo ; s composers still think of Beethoven as almost a contemporary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dean&amp;rsquo ; s program includes the Eroica Symphony and his own Beethoven-themed Testament . Provocatively , and the concert starts with Die grosse Fuge &amp;mdash ; a contrapuntal behemoth originally designed as the ending of an already elephantine string quartet ; Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s idiosyncratic homage to the fugue will played here by a full string orchestra . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As with the VSO New Music festivals , the hope is that audience members see themselves as participants rather than passive listeners . Davis " **28;41489;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1223647 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Clements&amp;rsquo ; film will open the 15th annual Vancouver International Women in Film Festival , which takes place at the Vancity Theatre from March 3 to 8 . The film is one of nine feature films at the festival . Also on the program are seven documentaries and 26 short films . In the festival there are eight Canadian premieres . The Argentinian drama The Rabbit&amp;rsquo ; s House about a young girl living with activists in the mid seventies will have its world premiere at VIWFF. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s always an honour to be included in a festival that celebrates women filmmakers , &amp;rdquo ; said Clements , a Metis multiple disciplined artist who lives on Galiano Island . &amp;ldquo ; Being able to be in a community and to see other women&amp;rsquo ; s work and to see , you know , what they&amp;rsquo ; re making and see what stories they&amp;rsquo ; re really passionate about , I think it just feeds you . There&amp;rsquo ; s a feeling when you&amp;rsquo ; re at these festivals , yes you&amp;rsquo ; re there for your baby , but you really are being inspired and kind of motivated , propelled by what other artists are doing and how they got to do it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;41519;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;41555;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Put on by the Women in Film and Television Vancouver organization , the VIWFF not only celebrates great cinema made by women but it offers a full slate of supportive programming including panels , seminars , artist talks , pitch sessions , a screenplay competition , social events and an awards gala . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I really think it&amp;rsquo ; s just like an incubator of ideas and possibilities , &amp;rdquo ; added Clements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The concept for Red Snow , which also gets it theatrical release in &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Ottawa , Vancouver and Toronto on March 13th , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; goes back a decade to when Clements was looking at photos of Canadian soldiers in Afghanistan . In the pictures were often Pashtuns and it was the images of those ethnic Afghans that really struck Clements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was looking at a photo essay of Canadian soldiers in Afghanistan . And I just started looking at the faces of the Indigenous people there and you know , in certain angles they looked like Indigenous people in Canada . This was really great . What would happen if these two ancient cultures that had survived so many wars were face to face ? And what does modern tribalism look like ? And how do we survive using our identity ? You know , as people ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film was shot in 20 days ( some of those days the temperature dropped to -51 degrees ) on location outside of Yellowknife and here in B.C. near Ashcroft , Kamloops and Cache Creek . Four languages are spoken in the film : Pashtun , English , Gwich'in and Inuvialuktun. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;41591;TOOLONG ... title= " Galiano Island filmmaker Marie Clements ' latest film Red Snow was shot near Yellowknife ( seen here ) as well as in locations in the B.C. Interior . Photo credit : Samantha Hefford " alt= " Galiano Island filmmaker Marie Clements ' latest film Red Snow was shot near Yellowknife ( seen here ) as well as in locations in the B.C. Interior . Photo credit : Samantha Hefford " data-portal-copyright= " Samantha Hefford " **28;41627;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1223648 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Clements has been a writer in residence for many theatrical organizations and universities . Her work in the theatre has earned her awards and nominations and her plays have been translated into different languages . Right now she is busy developing screenplays , making music videos , working on a four-part miniseries with the CBC and a documentary with the NFB. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everything&amp;rsquo ; s percolating . Everything&amp;rsquo ; s moving forward , &amp;rdquo ; said Clements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Interactive digital media and community outreach components have been created as part of the Red Snow experience . The opening night gala on March 3 will feature the debut of two singles from the brand new Red Snow soundtrack . Dirt Walkers and We Are Still the People will be performed live by a band of Afghan and Canadian Indigenous musicians including : &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Mozhah Jamalzadah , Wayne Lavallee , Marina Hasselberg , Edris Fayaz and Majid Qiyam&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Telling Indigenous stories has always been the plan for Clements . Now she says the industry and the consumers have started to really catch up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s been a significant shift , &amp;rdquo ; said Clements . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really exciting to be a storyteller at this time . And I do think that those doors that were , you know , closed for so long are opening . And I think audiences , you know , want to engage in Indigenous stories . I think we&amp;rsquo ; re just looking to consume what we don&amp;rsquo ; t know . To see things that we haven&amp;rsquo ; t seen , you know , be involved in a dialogue that we might not have had even five years ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Canada , it&amp;rsquo ; s exploding with some really phenomenal directors and filmmakers and storytellers so I think it&amp;rsquo ; s a real sign that there&amp;rsquo ; s a critical mass of stories coming out that are high quality and really original and have a lot of craft , &amp;rdquo ; added Clements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After the 7 p.m. screening of Red Snow Clements and some of her actors will be on hand for a Q&amp;amp ; A. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;41657;TOOLONG ... title= " Galiano Island filmmaker Marie Clement , seen here on set in the North West Territories , has plenty of irons in the fire including projects with the CBC and the NFB . Davis " **28;41693;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1224285 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another Indigenous film worth highlighting at the festival is Unceded Chiefs . The documentary is making its Canadian premiere here at VIWFF on March 7 . The film from local director Doreen Manuel looks at the B.C. First Nations leaders who joined together to reject Prime Minister Pierre Elliot Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s proposed 1969 White Paper Policy . That policy was setting out to abolish all legal documents that had previously existed , including the Indian Act , and all treaties within the country . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;42611;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1217255 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many say you&amp;rsquo ; ve got to spend money to make money , and blockbuster film Sonic the Hedgehog did just that here in B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Paramount Pictures film is racing its way to the top of the box office , but not before it spent $37.5 million in B.C. during its 2018 production . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to figures released Thursday by the Motion Picture Association of Canada , the production spent $22 million on local labour , creating 1,450 jobs for local cast and crew when it spent 53 days filming in B.C. two years ago ( figures in Canadian dollars unless otherwise noted ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The professional artists and technicians of IATSE Local 891 love a challenge and bringing this much loved video game character to the big screen fit the bill , &amp;rdquo ; said Phil Klapwyk with IATSE Local 891 , which represents film workers across B.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Sonic the Hedgehog isn&amp;rsquo ; t just a creative and technical success ; it provided good jobs for many B.C. crew members . We&amp;rsquo ; re definitely hoping for a sequel ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An additional $15.5 million was injected into the local economy for production-related goods and services , including $490,000 on catering , $1.6 million on hotels and accommodations , $350,000 on hardware and lumber , and $300,000 on wardrobe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Production for the film , which is based on the classic Sega video game franchise about a speedy blue hedgehog , took place across B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s South Coast , with the majority of its filming locations on Vancouver Island . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;42641;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;42677;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Campbell River&amp;rsquo ; s Shelter Point Distillery , Nanaimo&amp;rsquo ; s Diplomat Hotel , Belcarra&amp;rsquo ; s Camp Howdy and Squamish&amp;rsquo ; s Stawamus Chief Park all feature in the film . A key action sequence &amp;ndash ; which sees Jim Carrey&amp;rsquo ; s Dr. Ivo Robotnik chasing Sonic , voiced by Ben Schwartz , and his human companion played by James Marsden &amp;ndash ; was filmed in the area around Vancouver Island&amp;rsquo ; s Highway 19. &lt;a href= " https : **33;42713;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The span was closed for five days in August 2018&lt;/a&gt; to allow for production to stage a number of vehicle-related stunts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Filming in B.C. provided us with incredible local cast and crew , and beautiful locations for Sonic the Hedgehog , &amp;rdquo ; said Lee Rosenthal with Paramount Pictures . &amp;ldquo ; We found great partnership in the local business community , and they satisfied all of our production-related needs . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sonic the Hedgehog hit theatres on Feb. 14 and raked in US $70 million over that country&amp;rsquo ; s four-day Presidents Day long weekend , &lt;a href= " https : **33;42748;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;according to the Hollywood Reporter&lt;/a&gt; . The film also debuted to US $43 million from its first 40 international markets . The film cost US $87 million to make . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The movie had initially been forecast to bring in US $45 to $50 million domestically over the four-day period , but beat that projection with US $58 million over just three days . Ferrari earns honour as the best sports movie of 2019http : **36;47092;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;47130;TOOLONG ... title= " Matt Damon and Christian Bale star in James Mangold 's drama about racing car legends car designer Carroll Shelby and British driver Ken Miles and the pairs bid to unseat Ferrai as the best in the racing game . " alt= " Matt Damon and Christian Bale star in James Mangold 's drama about racing car legends car designer Carroll Shelby and British driver Ken Miles and the pairs bid to unseat Ferrai as the best in the racing game . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of VIFF " **28;47166;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210524 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anyone who has driven an automobile with a manual stick shift can relate to the rush &amp;mdash ; the pure pop of adrenalin &amp;mdash ; that comes from gearing up or down , especially in a fast-moving vehicle . It&amp;rsquo ; s precisely that feeling , the spine-tingling sensation of cornering before the big straightaway , that defines Ford vs . Ferrari , the best sport movie of 2019. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The relationship between man and machine that finds its visual metaphor in driver and stick shift is referenced time and time again during the two-hour , 32-minute film based on the true story of American race car designer Carroll Shelby and his hand-picked driver , the temperamental Brit Ken Miles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although we&amp;rsquo ; re introduced to the Riverside International Raceway in California and the Daytona Beach International Speedway in Florida , the story is all about the corporate infighting , hierarchical politics , personal demons and irrepressible egos that made the 1966 running of the iconic 24-hour race at Le Mans , France , one of the most notable in auto racing history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Under the direction of James Mangold , the cinematography of Phedon Papamichael and the razor-sharp film editing of Andrew Buckland , Michael McCusker and Dirk Westervelt , Ford vs . Ferrari takes us inside the Ford GT40 Mk I that finished in a sweep of the top three positions at Le Mans in 1966. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Extreme close ups of the driver Miles &amp;mdash ; shifting back and forth from his sweaty face and riveted eyes to his sure hand on the clutch &amp;mdash ; are used repeatedly to bring us as close as possible to the RPMs and laws of physics that make auto racing a never-ending pursuit of speed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Led by Donald Sylvester , Paul Massey , David Giammarco and Steven Morrow , a sound department of 37 engineers , mixers , boom operators , foley artists and editors do the rest , giving Ford vs . Ferrari the palpable crispness and raw authenticity that has resulted in four nominations at the 92nd Academy Awards on tap Sunday night ( CTV ) at the Dolby Theater in Hollywood . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ford vs . Ferrari is up for an Oscar for best picture , best film editing , best sound editing and best sound mixing , making it the most critically-acclaimed and nominated sport movie since The Fighter earned seven Academy Award nominations in 2010 . The epic yet extremely focused First World War movie 1917 will almost certainly follow up its Golden Globe for best drama with the Oscar for best picture , but there&amp;rsquo ; s no question that the audiovisual intensity of Ford vs . Ferrari has a very good chance at being rewarded in one or more of the editing or sound categories . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The movie starring Matt Damon as Shelby and Christian Bale as Miles has scored multiple nominations ( 65 ) and award wins ( 21 ) over the past 60 days , not including eight of 22 categories in The Sport Market Movie Awards for 2019 . By doing so , Ford vs . Ferrari equals the most recent accomplished Formula One racing film Rush &amp;mdash ; the story of the deep-seated rivalry between Austria&amp;rsquo ; s Nikki Lauda and England&amp;rsquo ; s James Hunt &amp;mdash ; which won eight times in The Sport Market Movie Awards in 2013. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both Damon and Bale are solid in their respective roles , but it is the former Batman who is literally in the driver&amp;rsquo ; s seat for much of Ford vs . Ferrari ( billed and marketed as Le Mans &amp;rsquo ; 66 in most parts of Europe ) . Bale was last recognized nine years ago in the sport movie genre for his role as Dicky Eklund , the half-brother of Boston boxer Micky Ward , in The Fighter . He won the Oscar for best supporting actor while Melissa Leo took home best supporting actress as Ward&amp;rsquo ; s mother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He didn&amp;rsquo ; t receive an Academy Award nomination as best actor for his role as Miles , but Bale&amp;rsquo ; s depiction as the talented mechanic and mercurial driver in Ford vs . Ferrari did earn him best actor nominations at the Golden Globes and Screen Actors Guild Awards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ford vs . Ferrari is this year&amp;rsquo ; s box office champion among sport movies &amp;mdash ; with big screen receipts of US$222 million on the eve of its digital release this Tuesday &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; and wins six other categories of The Sport Market Movie Awards , including best picture , best drama , best cinematography , best editing , best sound and best supporting actress ( Caitriona Balfe ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was clearly the year&amp;rsquo ; s best sport movie &amp;mdash ; and one of the best all-time technical performances in the sport genre in sound and editing &amp;mdash ; in an interesting crop of 42 releases in 2019 ( including a dozen foreign language dramatic productions and 15 sport documentaries ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Netflix original High Flying Bird not only showed us what it would look like if Jerry Maguire ( 1996 ) married Moneyball ( 2011 ) , it demonstrated how streaming companies have completely reshaped the landscapes of movie production , distribution and promotion in recent years . The excellent sport business movie that puts an agent ( Ray Burke played by Andre Holland ) in the middle of the NBA and its players in a lockout is one of several produced this past year by the studio arm at Netflix . It wins three categories in The Sport Market Movie Awards , including best direction by Stephen Soderbergh , best screenplay by Tarell Alvin McCraney and best supporting actor for Melvin Gregg ( who plays Burke&amp;rsquo ; s client Erick Scott ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47196;TOOLONG ... title= " Adam Sandler accepts Best Actor for Uncut Gems onstage during AARP The Magazine 's 19th Annual Movies For Grownups Awards at Beverly Wilshire , A Four Seasons Hotel on January 11 , 2020 in Beverly Hills , California . " alt= " Adam Sandler accepts Best Actor for Uncut Gems onstage during AARP The Magazine 's 19th Annual Movies For Grownups Awards at Beverly Wilshire , A Four Seasons Hotel on January 11 , 2020 in Beverly Hills , California . " data-portal-copyright= " Kevin Winter " **28;47232;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1210535 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , another Netflix production ignored by the Academy this weekend , scores as the best sport-themed movie of the year . It is Uncut Gems , the crime thriller starring Adam Sandler in a compelling dramatic turn as Howard Ratner , a charismatic jeweller who gets himself into trouble in a high-stakes sports betting jam . Kevin Garnett , one of the best power forwards in NBA history , plays himself as Ratner&amp;rsquo ; s client , making his 2008 championship ring a co-star in the flick . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Uncut Gems also features notable performances by newcomer Julia Fox and Idina Menzel as Ratner&amp;rsquo ; s wife Dinah . Menzel is best-known as the speaking and singing voice of Elsa in the animated Disney franchise Frozen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the other sport movie releases from 2019 that are worth a watch is the year&amp;rsquo ; s best sport documentary &amp;mdash ; Diego Maradona &amp;mdash ; and Fighting With My Family , a biopic dramedy starring Florence Pugh as English WWE wrestler Saraya-Jade Bevis , better known as Paige . Pugh is this year&amp;rsquo ; s best actress in a sport movie and Fighting with My Family , which also features Dwayne Johnson a.k.a . Photo : Kevin Winter/Getty Images " alt= " Production designer Dennis Gassner is nominated for his seventh Academy Award for his work on the film 1917 . Photo : Kevin Winter/Getty Images " data-portal-copyright= " Kevin Winter " **28;47904;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204375 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year , the period film that has brought him to the big show with his seventh Academy Award nomination ( his last nomination was 2018&amp;rsquo ; s Blade Runner 2049 ) is the epic First World War drama from Sam Mendes about a pair of young soldiers ( Dean-Charles Chapman and George MacKay ) who are sent out on a mission to try to deliver a message to stop an attack that would result in huge loss of life for the English army . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best-picture favourite and recent BAFTA sweeper , including production design for Gassner and Sandales , is a visual masterpiece that looks like it&amp;rsquo ; s one long continuous shot . It isn&amp;rsquo ; t . It&amp;rsquo ; s a series of shots that are meticulously put together to give the overwhelming impression that it is one shot and that you , the viewer , are right there beside the scared young men as they make this perilous journey through the French battlegrounds. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This marks the fifth time Gassner has worked with Mendes , and the ninth film he has done with master cinematographer Roger Deakins. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It took over a year to complete 1917 . Each scene and shot was put together like an intricate dance with the utmost in complicated choreography . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You can only do that when you have a lot of experience and especially with the camaraderie that Sam and Roger and I have . Old relationships , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner. &amp;ldquo ; It was kind of an inch-by-inch journey . Defining it , measuring it , discussing it , and designing it and building it and shooting it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;47934;TOOLONG ... title= " Schofield , George MacKay , foreground , with fellow soldiers in 1917 , the new epic from Oscar-winning filmmaker Sam Mendes . " alt= " Schofield , George MacKay , foreground , with fellow soldiers in 1917 , the new epic from Oscar-winning filmmaker Sam Mendes . " data-portal-copyright= " Photo Credit : Fran ? ois Duhamel " **28;47970;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204386 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for his actual design , Gassner said he had a sense of what he wanted to create as soon as he finished reading Mendes&amp;rsquo ; s script . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I really wanted to have a dreamscape environment or a slightly surreal one , because that kind of goes to the context of what those boys must have gone through , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner. &amp;ldquo ; The surreal element of war . It certainly was not their normal lives . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Everything you see in this movie is real and no detail goes unnoticed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everything you saw was created by artists . So , I used the term the art of war . It is going to be an approach that everything is going to be exact , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner about his brief to those working with him on the design of the film . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s going to be perfect in the way that it would have been done as if we were doing it for real . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Every person who worked on this film , I talked to them about that . That was their edict : to make sure that everything they did was precise . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Each step and movement was laid out before shooting . There was not an inch of the film that wasn&amp;rsquo ; t measured , marked and considered to the highest degree . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Beat for beat was laid out . It was a very complicated thing to do , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner. &amp;ldquo ; It was an immaculate dance . In my opinion , perfection , because it had to be . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;48000;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;48035;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was easily one of the more demanding movies Gassner has worked on in his five decades in the business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The last shooting day was the scene where George jumps into the river from the bridge . You go through the finish line and you fall over and you hug each other . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gassner was born in Vancouver in 1948 and lived here for five years before his parents took him and his brother to Portland , Ore . He was raised there and went to the University of Oregon at Eugene , where he was studying architecture . It&amp;rsquo ; s during that time that he saw David Lean&amp;rsquo ; s 1962 cinematic masterpiece Lawrence of Arabia and everything changed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I said , &amp;lsquo ; Now that&amp;rsquo ; s big . That&amp;rsquo ; s big and I want to do big . That is bigger than any building I could ever design and build , &amp;rsquo ; so it was about having a big imagination , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner , who moved to Los Angeles at age 21 and enrolled in the ArtCenter College of Design . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was while at the Pasadena , Calif. , college that he and a pal decided they were going to get a job working for Francis Ford Coppola on Apocalypse Now . And the rest , as they say , is history , as Gassner did go on to design the movie poster for the legendary Coppola film . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Always in demand , Gassner took the 1917 job over another James Bond film &amp;mdash ; he has done three already , two with Mendes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was the unknown , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner , when asked about that decision to go to war with Mendes . &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t know that much about the Great War and I wanted to explore , and hopefully tell the truest of the stories . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The story for 1917 came from Mendes&amp;rsquo ; s memories of the stories his grandfather , a First World War veteran , told him as a kid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was the most powerful script I have ever read , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And Gassner has seen some pretty great scripts . And he is part of one of cinema&amp;rsquo ; s most storied franchises &amp;mdash ; Bond , James Bond . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was exciting , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner about the Bond films ( Spectre , Skyfall and Quantum of Solace ) . &amp;ldquo ; There is a lot to do because there is a huge history &amp;hellip ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a huge , huge responsibility and something I have been lucky to do three times , and I will probably do again later on and down the line . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : The single shot , opening Day of the Dead scene in Spectre , directed by Mendes , is where the inspiration for 1917&amp;rsquo ; s one-shot look came from . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s where we got the idea to do 1917 , &amp;rdquo ; said Gassner. &amp;ldquo ; We figured out how to do it and it was actually pretty cool . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Gassner is asked about the amazing list of talented filmmakers he has worked with , he pauses and says , &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s always fun to be with friends . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; OK , but is there something else besides a good time with old pals that connects the dots between the projects of his impressive career ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Good storytellers . " data-portal-copyright= " Photo credit : Handout " **28;49151;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1190191 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Vancouver Short Film Festival&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Jan. 24-26 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Vancity Theatre &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : //www.vsff.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;vsff.com&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; After watching the film The Farewell , &lt;a href= " https : **30;49181;TOOLONG ? re ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Curtis Lum&lt;/a&gt; knew he , too , had a family story he wanted to tell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While director/writer &lt;a href= " https : **30;49213;TOOLONG ? re ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Lulu Wang&lt;/a&gt; &amp;lsquo ; s The Farewell is about a Chinese clan that keeps a big secret from the matriarch , Lum&amp;rsquo ; s film Grandma&amp;rsquo ; s 80th Surprise is a story about a Chinese family sharing information with the matriarch. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film , which Lum co-wrote and co-directed with his girlfriend &lt;a href= " https : **30;49245;TOOLONG ? re ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Fola **25;49277;TOOLONG , will be part of this year&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " http : //vsff.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Vancouver Short Film Festival&lt;/a&gt; . VSFF is a diverse offering of 46 films that do not get lumped into themes , leaving the event as a sort of cinematic tasting menu that is sure to satisfy curious film lovers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;49304;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;49340;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Lum&amp;rsquo ; s 10-minute long film tells the true tale of Curtis ( Lum ) introducing Ella ( Myrasol Martinez ) to his grandmother for the first time on the occasion of the grandmother&amp;rsquo ; s 80th birthday lunch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Right away from there I knew I wanted to do a film to honour my grandmother , and to share her with the world , but I also wanted to do a film that would make everyone want to immediately call up their mothers or grandmothers and want to give them a big ol&amp;rsquo ; hug , &amp;rdquo ; said Lum , who splits his time between Vancouver and Los Angeles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Interestingly , though at first the grandmother as drawn by the Curtis character gives you pause , it becomes clear that Curtis&amp;rsquo ; s concern is how his grandmother will react when she meets Ella and sees that she is black . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the film Curtis is a nervous wreck who has gone so far as to enlist his mother to talk to the grandmother and break the black ice before they break bread . Other family members fuel Curtis&amp;rsquo ; s anxiety and cause Ella to question what she is about to face . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t say she wasn&amp;rsquo ; t racist . I said she wasn&amp;rsquo ; t MAGA racist , &amp;rdquo ; a jittery Curtis says to Ella. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;49376;TOOLONG ... title= " Curtis Lum is the star and co-writer and co-director of the entertaining short film Grandma 's 80th Surprise . " alt= " Curtis Lum is the star and co-writer and co-director of the entertaining short film Grandma 's 80th Surprise . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;49412;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1188149 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like a birthday cake , you can cut the tension and angst in this story with a knife but , thankfully , there is a very healthy resolve &amp;mdash ; a resolve that actually occurred between Lum and his grandmother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All this time I thought my grandmother was racist , but in actuality it was all just one big miscommunication , &amp;rdquo ; said Lum. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This story , for me , was all about celebrating the miscommunication we have inter-generationally , and breaking out of our rigid culture and family tradition and celebrating a breakthrough I had with my grandmother , &amp;rdquo ; added Lum , who is a very busy actor and is also developing projects for his Arrival of the Fittest Entertainment production company . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Her and I now have a deeper , stronger relationship . I feel like we can talk about anything &amp;hellip ; Now she is so much more appreciative that I can be open and honest with her and vice versa , which is really nice . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;49442;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;49484;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? TV and film **29;49587;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;49618;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;49654;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the film , the grandmother is played by Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Lillian Lim . Lim ( Meditation Park ) , who said she didn&amp;rsquo ; t have to go far for inspiration for her character as her own mother was raised with cultural racism . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My mom was really like that , &amp;rdquo ; said Lim , adding that she is the middle child with a brother on either side . &amp;ldquo ; She told all three of us when we were growing up that &amp;lsquo ; if you marry anybody that is not Chinese , I will disown you . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lim , though , reports her mother softened that view as Lim grew older . In fact when she was 29 her mother told it was okay to widen her marriage net . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; At the time , to me , it was an insult . That I was in a desperate place , desperate to be married , &amp;rdquo ; said Lim with a big laugh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Lum ( who was also in Meditation Park ) asked Lim to do his film , Lim was excited but had one request &amp;mdash ; she wanted her character to speak Toisan ( Toisanese ) , a country village dialect spoken by her own mother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That was one of the wishes on my bucket list that I would do a film in Toisan , &amp;rdquo ; said Lim , &amp;nbsp ; who is currently working on a Disney + TV series . &amp;ldquo ; So my wish came true . It&amp;rsquo ; s kind of a dying language . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At its heart , Grandma&amp;rsquo ; s 80th Surprise is a story about love conquering all but that message is delivered through the lens of cultural biases and racism . Topics that are still very fresh today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Right now is the perfect time for a story like this , &amp;rdquo ; said Lum , who initially did the film as part of the Mighty Asian Movie Marathon competition . &amp;ldquo ; We still need to talk about these things . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lum&amp;rsquo ; s instincts were bang-on , as festival audiences of all cultures and backgrounds have embraced the sweet little movie . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was floored and overjoyed by the reaction we have got , &amp;rdquo ; said Lum about the film that premiered at the Vancouver Asian Film Festival in November . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We were in front of a predominantly Asian audience so I expected it to go over well , but surprisingly a lot of the people that have come up to us , that have stayed around after the screening to talk to us , a lot of them that it resonated with , weren&amp;rsquo ; t even Asian at all . That was what was the most beautiful for me as far as takeaway. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film , that has already earned awards at a handful of other festivals , is part of the exciting VSFF 10th anniversary program , a program that has been growing steadily since the festival started . This year organizers had 265 submissions to pick from . That number has doubled from four years ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s kind of crazy we are selling out screenings , we have rush lines to every program , &amp;rdquo ; said VSFF co-director Marena Dix. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think a lot of people are creating more in the city , and there has been a lot more opportunities for that . We&amp;rsquo ; re just really happy to have a place we can showcase what Vancouver independent talent has to offer . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;49681;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;49723;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? TV and film **29;49826;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;49857;TOOLONG ... latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;49893;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Short films are getting a lot more attention thanks to festivals like this , and streaming services and YouTube and Vimeo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Our festival is a great place to show what you want to do as a filmmaker and where you want to go as a creator , &amp;rdquo ; said Dix , who works in film and TV post production . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a melting pot of ideas . It&amp;rsquo ; s so fun . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those shorts can then become great calling cards for a filmmaker. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For me , an incredible opportunity to play and learn , &amp;rdquo ; said Lum who has produced two other short films . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As a producer , what I love about tackling a good short film is that it is easy to get eyeballs on the film . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To me , a short film is a great opportunity for people to have a chance to watch it and digest it , &amp;rdquo ; added Lum. &amp;ldquo ; People don&amp;rsquo ; t always have 100 minutes to watch a movie . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The short film is also an important part of building a career and continued professional growth for actors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love doing them , &amp;rdquo ; said Lim , who came to acting later in life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For all the other stuff you usually will never get a lead role , never . You&amp;rsquo ; re almost always background when you book anything . But for the short movies you get the lead role or the supporting lead role and , that&amp;rsquo ; s the only way you can showcase yourself as an actor , what you are capable of doing . That&amp;rsquo ; s why I love doing short movies . It&amp;rsquo ; s like a free acting class . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the VSFF , the program has been expanded from two to three days . Five-month Consul General Fabio Messineo attended the opening event . He returned later to introduce and discuss director Marco Bellocchio&amp;rsquo ; s Il Traditore ( The Traitor ) that was shot in his home island , Sicily . Audiences appreciate the festival&amp;rsquo ; s mix of new and old films , said Charity . The old included two screenings of La Dolce Vita by the late Federico Fellini who would be 100 on Jan. 20 . Recchioni welcomed the festival&amp;rsquo ; s new three-film component , Gialli ( Yellow ) , &amp;ldquo ; that is the Italian version of Noir with more sex , &amp;rdquo ; he said . The film , based on the lives of lifelong low-achieving Alberta headbangers Terry ( David Lawrence ) and Dean &amp;ldquo ; Deaner&amp;rdquo ; Murdoch ( Spence ) , spawned both a sequel , FUBAR 2 , and a spin-off Viceland TV series titled FUBAR Age of Computer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It also gave the world &lt;a href= " https : **33;51631;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **25;51666;TOOLONG . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A real-life band fronted by a fictional character , the group led by bass-playing singer Deaner is on tour supporting its latest concept album . Titled 3069 : A Space Sex Odyssey , the album about needing to insure the future of humankind by impregnating the universal Goddess with rock is out on Royal Mountain Records . To say this recording is a far cry from other label acts such as Orville Peck , Alvvays or Calpurnia is understatement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But as Deaner explained on the phone from Montreal , Nightseeker has always been about standing out from the crowd . He took time to talk to Postmedia about the band and its coming tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Following the fires in Fort McMurray and the loss of your home , instrument and more that was portrayed in FUBAR Age of Computer , it looks like you ca n't keep a good Deaner down ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **35;51693;TOOLONG : When your bass gets burned up , it might be seen as a sign to stop . But I&amp;rsquo ; ve got a hard head about things and there wasn&amp;rsquo ; t no way I was going to do anything after that but keep on given&amp;rsquo ; r . That&amp;rsquo ; s what it&amp;rsquo ; s all about . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : 3069 sounds like a lot of classic northern European concept albums from the ' 80s . Was it hard to complete ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;51730;TOOLONG : I like that you used the word concept because it&amp;rsquo ; s like a story , right . The listener who really digs music and focuses on the lyrics will understand how it starts with a guy who experiences a cataclysmic event in his world who is all alone but then ends up having to fight the Dragon Slayer , but he needs help and his buddies come along ( which is the band ) and then meets this woman who is the Queen of the Universe and everything works out in the end . All the songs tell a chapter of that story if you listen to them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;51762;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;51798;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What motivates your writing process , penning a catchy track like With Love on the Line ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;51834;TOOLONG : Is it a tune I want to crank on a Saturday night before I head out with my buddies to give&amp;rsquo ; r ? If the song meets that test , then we keep it . If it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t , me and the band get back to work and keep at it until we know that the song really can give&amp;rsquo ; r and just give it all we got . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Nightseeker is a long way from the garage duo you formed in FUBAR . What was your musical development ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;51866;TOOLONG : I began in a band called Quicksand , but that name was taken so we became Quakesand , and things were going pretty good . But the other three guys were all bricklayers , and one day on the job the scaffolding collapsed when she was a real windy day and they all had various band injuries and I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t wait a year or more for them all to get better . They did , which is good . Then my band in Calgary got hit by lightning and I lost the whole band that night , too , but I was OK . Something about having no testicles seems to make you immune from all those damages , I guess . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What can fans hope to hear in the set ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;51898;TOOLONG : Some old classics , for sure . Out of respect , we don&amp;rsquo ; t play Whale Hunter anymore , after Terry got married to &amp;mdash ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t want to say it &amp;mdash ; the person he married . Mostly , it&amp;rsquo ; s the new album because that&amp;rsquo ; s what everyone wants to hear us play . Most of the crowd is always super wasted , so we usually play about an hour to an hour and a half and then keep give&amp;rsquo ; n it with the fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;51930;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;51961;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;51999;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;52028;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;52059;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **31;52101;TOOLONG " &g; ... " data-portal-copyright= " Jasin Boland " **28;52686;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1185822 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A group of Aussie expats are throwing a Mad Max marathon at the &lt;a href= " http : //riotheatre.ca/ " &gt;Rio Theatre&lt;/a&gt; to help fight the fires back home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The day-long event at east Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s historic indie cinema , planned for later this month , will screen all four films in George Miller&amp;rsquo ; s beloved and bizarre action franchise , in addition to other entertainment , raffles and special guest appearances . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The benefit , which aims to raise $20,000 to send Down Under , is organized by actors Rhona Rees and Pauline Egan and event planner Tee Haynes &amp;mdash ; three Australians living and working in Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Although most of my friends and family are safe and out of the direct line of fire , so to speak , it&amp;rsquo ; s a strange sense of despair and helplessness that comes with being an ex-pat and reading about your home country from afar , &amp;rdquo ; said Rees . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s really strange . So I decided to try and direct that hopeless energy into something positive and made some inquiries at the Rio Theatre about putting on a movie marathon . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It turned out she wasn&amp;rsquo ; t alone . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; To my delight , a gentleman named Tee Haynes had already reached out to get the ball rolling , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; We have joined forces . That project was stopped but soon after LNG showed up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Despite protests the tanker traffic is green lit and , according to Wray , will begin in late 2023 or early 2024. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Noise pollution is huge , &amp;rdquo ; said Wray who has been working in the area for close to 20 years . &amp;ldquo ; It can interfere with them finding their prey , which is huge . She captured the connection between people and place , which I think is very important and she just caught those silent moments with the humpbacks , &amp;rdquo ; said Wray , who spends about eight months out of the year in the field . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I mean , look at the first scene where you come in with the drone and there is a humpback sleeping which is a very unusual thing for people to see . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of NFB " **28;56245;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1168775 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Burnaby filmmaker &lt;a href= " https : **33;56275;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Christopher Auchter&lt;/a&gt; can now add the famed &lt;a href= " https : **33;56310;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Sundance Film Festival&lt;/a&gt; to the list of events that have welcomed his short film Now is the Time this past year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 16-minute film tells the story of a totem pole raising in 1969 &amp;mdash ; the first one in a century &amp;mdash ; in &lt;a href= " http : **34;56345;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Old Masset&lt;/a&gt; in &lt;a href= " https : //www.gohaidagwaii.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Haida Gwaii&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Adding Sundance to a screening list that already includes &lt;a href= " https : //www.tiff.net/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;TIFF&lt;/a&gt; , the &lt;a href= " http : //viff.org " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Vancouver International Film Festival&lt;/a&gt; and a handful of other events was of course a cherry on the top of a great year for the Haida filmmaker . But what made the situation a little bit sweeter was the response Auchter got from a Sundance official when she told him Now is the Time is one of the 74 short films out of 10,000 plus submissions that made the cut for the prestigious Utah-based festival on Jan 23-Feb 2 , 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Sundance woman I talked to really liked the movie and she had never even heard of a totem pole or Haida Gwaii , &amp;rdquo ; said Auchter. &amp;ldquo ; The fact that the story still grabbed her is great . She said : &amp;lsquo ; now I know quite a bit about totem poles . &amp;rsquo ; That was quite special to hear . That she found the story so compelling was amazing for me. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " https : **34;56381;TOOLONG ... width= " 640 " height= " 360 " frameborder= " 0 " allow= " autoplay ; fullscreen " allowfullscreen title= " Now Is the Time ( Promo Clip 30sec - COMING SOON ) " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Along with the contemporary images , animation and interviews that Auchter shot , the film incorporates really fantastic footage from Eugene Boyko&amp;rsquo ; s 1970 NFB documentary This Was the Time that chronicled the carving and the raising of the pole . The new Auchter movie is the result of the NFB&amp;rsquo ; s inactive to get Indigenous filmmakers to create works using the Board&amp;rsquo ; s archives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Front and centre in both the archival and modern footage is First Nations master carver and international art star Robert Davidson . It was he and his brother Reg , who at the time were 22 and 14 respectively , worked on the pole six days a week for three-and-half months . The pole , Davidson&amp;rsquo ; s first ever , still stands in Masset these five decades later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was really special to meet them and learn about their story and interpret it through this film , &amp;rdquo ; said Auchter. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;56417;TOOLONG ... title= " Twenty-two-year-old Robert Davidson and his grandfather , Tsinii , discuss the raising of the first totem pole on Haida Gwaii in over a hundred years . " alt= " Twenty-two-year-old Robert Davidson and his grandfather , Tsinii , discuss the raising of the first totem pole on Haida Gwaii in over a hundred years . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of NFB " **28;56453;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1168773 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; That raising of the pole was considered a reawakening for the Haida people as many of the huge cedar poles&amp;nbsp ; that were all over Haida Gwaii&amp;nbsp ; a century and a half ago had been felled after missionaries&amp;nbsp ; deemed them&amp;nbsp ; sinful&amp;nbsp ; and tickets into hell . Government policies also allowed collectors and ethnologists to take poles away . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The pole raising attracted over 1,000 Haida people from the Raven and Eagle clans . Many of the elders that attended were wearing paper headpieces as their traditional wood-carved ceremonial masks , and most of their other artwork , had disappeared or was destroyed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There was really a void , but I didn&amp;rsquo ; t know the scale of the void , &amp;rdquo ; says Davidson in the film about the loss of art . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;56483;TOOLONG ... title= " Haida elders gather to celebrate the raising of the first totem pole on Haida Gwaii in over a hundred years . The destruction of the community 's totem poles was part of the systemic obliteration of Haida songs , ceremonies , and culture that had occurred over the previous decades . " alt= " Haida elders gather to celebrate the raising of the first totem pole on Haida Gwaii in over a hundred years . The destruction of the community 's totem poles was part of the systemic obliteration of Haida songs , ceremonies , and culture that had occurred over the previous decades . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of NFB " **28;56519;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1168776 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I didn&amp;rsquo ; t realize how much ceremony was connected to the art until that moment , &amp;rdquo ; says Robert Davidson in the film . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the Davidson&amp;rsquo ; s the carving of the pole was very much a deliberate act that managed to draw out the community&amp;rsquo ; s history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Their part was carving the pole and once they started doing that the elders in the community stepped in and started doing their part which was doing the potlatch and figuring out how to raise the pole , &amp;rdquo ; said Auchter. &amp;ldquo ; They were all trying to piece together pieces of knowledge that each other had from their grandparents or parents &amp;mdash ; the songs the dances . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The pole was so important not just because it was a big pole but because of all the things it triggered in the songs , the dances and the potlatch ( which was made illegal in 1884 and repealed in 1951 but still remained very rare ) . The protocols , &amp;rdquo ; added Auchter. &amp;ldquo ; It was like the keys to the ignition that started the engine again in terms of the Haida culture and the arts . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of Spinster production " **28;59068;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1158120 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Whistler Film Festival&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; on until Dec. 8 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Whistler &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;59098;TOOLONG ? gclid ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;59127;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When director &lt;a href= " https : //andreadorfman.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; Andrea Dorfman&lt;/a&gt; and screenwriter &lt;a href= " https : **30;59161;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Jennifer Deyell&lt;/a&gt; put the word out for a late thirty-something female actor to star in their new film Spinster it was clear they as filmmakers they were in a good position but sadly the film business itself still had a long way to go . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We connected with a casting agent in L.A. and sure enough there were a lot of people available , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman over the phone from Halifax recently . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That deep pool of available female talent comes as no surprise as it is well documented that over 30 means over the Hollywood hill . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;59193;TOOLONG ... title= " Filmmaker Andrea Dorfman 's fourth feature Spinster looks at one woman 's struggle to break free of the idea that she needs to get married and have kids . " alt= " Filmmaker Andrea Dorfman 's fourth feature Spinster looks at one woman 's struggle to break free of the idea that she needs to get married and have kids . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of Spinster production " **28;59229;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1158117 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t surprised at all , &amp;rdquo ; said the Halifax-based director before referencing a hilarious skit from the TV show Inside &lt;a href= " https : //www.amyschumer.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Amy Schumer&lt;/a&gt; . In the skit titled Last F&amp;amp ; *%able Day Tina Fey , Julia Louis-Dreyfus and Patricia Arquette are seated at a fully-stocked dining table in a clearing in the woods . While out walking Schumer comes across them and joins them at the table . The raise their glasses in a toast and Schumer asks if it is someone&amp;rsquo ; s birthday ? Nope , it&amp;rsquo ; s not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s kind of the opposite . We&amp;rsquo ; re celebrating Julia&amp;rsquo ; s last f$*k%ble day , &amp;rdquo ; says Arquette . Schumer asks what that means . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In every actresses life the media decides when you finally reach the point when you are not believably f$*k%ble anymore , &amp;rdquo ; says Dreyfus. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The skit was a big hit and a big knowing wink to the stark reality of female ageism in the entertainment business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s in the air . We know that women fall off of a cliff after a certain age . You have 50-year-old male actors getting together on camera with 25-year-olds . It&amp;rsquo ; s crazy . It&amp;rsquo ; s so in your face , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman before adding a sliver of hope to the discussion . &amp;ldquo ; I also think things are changing . More and more women are becoming directors and sticking as directors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think the more women telling stories and more different kinds of people telling stories ( will lead to ) definitely seeing more employment , I hope , for older women , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman who is also an animator , illustrator , documentary filmmaker and screenwriter. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While there is still a way to go to reach parity the discussion around the increase in female directors is very much a thing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here in North America names like Lulu Wang , Olivia Wilde , Annie Silverstein , Semi Chellas and Melina Matsoukas are just a handful of many up-in-coming female directors that have garnered attention recently and are poised to join the ranks of today&amp;rsquo ; s well established working Hollywood directors like Ava DeVernay , Greta Gerwig , Elizabeth Banks , Kathryn Bigelow , Patty Jenkins , Sarah Polley and others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the likes of Jenkins and Anna Boden aside , it seems the big tent pole pictures are still for the most part the purview of male directors . Where women directors are the norm is the indie film world . Those films get their first lives on festival screens like the ones operated by the Whistler Film Festival ( WFF ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now in its 19th year , the festival wraps on Dec. 8 after five days of top-notch cinema , events and programs , the WFF is pretty good in the non-male director department . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year 40 per cent of the festival&amp;rsquo ; s 86 films ( features and shorts ) are directed or co-directed by women , or non-binary individuals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dorfman is one of 13 women at the helm of a feature at this year&amp;rsquo ; s festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s amazing . That&amp;rsquo ; s fantastic . I love hearing that , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman. &amp;ldquo ; I see a lot of women make first and second features but I don&amp;rsquo ; t always see the stick to-it-ness that maybe our male colleagues have . That&amp;rsquo ; s what I would like to see . I would love to see what women make over their career . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spinster was co-conceived with Dorfman&amp;rsquo ; s longtime creative partner Deyell . About 15 years ago Dorfman and Deyell noticed that there was a discussion swirling around them and other women of a certain age . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In my mid 30s it was a time when all my friends were getting married and having kids and I was single , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman. &amp;ldquo ; She ( Jennifer ) also had a good friend who was single at that time and for both of us it was a really hard place to be . There was this mad race ( that lead ) to a lot of friends to settle just to make it happen . I was like I am &amp;lsquo ; not settling , &amp;rsquo ; and her friend was very much the same way . We would commiserate about this and talk about it endlessly and that I think was what the initial script was born out of . Just this idea that you are at the top of your game in many ways and still women can feel bad about being single which is absurd . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This film is product of lots of chat between Deyell and Dorfman not just as filmmakers looking for a good story , but as women looking and hoping to change the story . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I always say I want to see films I wish had been around when I was at a certain moment in my life , &amp;rdquo ; added Dorfman who has a boyfriend and two stepkids. &amp;ldquo ; Maybe this will be that film . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A character in the film was inspired by the friend of Jennifer&amp;rsquo ; s who Dorfman said was a scientist who studied bats in the Amazon and had &amp;ldquo ; this incredible life . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Even though she had this amazing life and was so successful her friends were still like : &amp;lsquo ; ahhhh she&amp;rsquo ; s not married . ahhhh she doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have kids . &amp;rsquo ; The fact that we do that to women over and over again is terrible . That we can give them praise for their lives then take it away from them because they don&amp;rsquo ; t have the marriage , the kids , the house ? Once again it is feeding into a fallacy because women have incredibly rewarding and successful lives while not being mothers and married . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Made for $1 million Spinster &amp;mdash ; which had its world premiere at the Whistler festival on Dec. 6 and will play again on Dec. 8 &amp;mdash ; is all about that pressure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Out of the deep talent pool of thirty-something actors that were available for work Dorfman and Deyell cast American comedian/actor Chelsea Peretti as Gaby the 39-year-old catering company owner who dreams of her own restaurant while navigating the sad sack looks and pity pouts she gets from those contemplating her singleness. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;59259;TOOLONG ... title= " Actors Chelsea Peretti and Jonathan Watton in a scene from the new film Spinster . " alt= " Actors Chelsea Peretti and Jonathan Watton in a scene from the new film Spinster . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy of Spinster production " **28;59295;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1158118 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I enjoy women in power so I wanted to be directed by Andrea , &amp;rdquo ; said Peretti via email . &amp;ldquo ; When I got the offer , I watched her films and thought they looked beautiful . She has a specific vibe and style and she made me fall in love with Nova Scotia . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What Dorfman liked about Peretti was her willingness and eagerness to get right into the mix of the film . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; She was a participant and collaborator , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman about Peretti ( Brooklyn Nine-Nine and Parks and Recreation ) adding that well received standup comedian asked if she could make some of the jokes her own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I know I&amp;rsquo ; m mouthy . I&amp;rsquo ; m irritable and I need to work on my core , &amp;rdquo ; says Gaby to guy who is leaving her after she has desperately and wrongly amped up a three-month relationship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shot over three week in Halifax in the summer of 2018 Spinster is a funny and sometimes melancholy look at one woman&amp;rsquo ; s evolution through and out of the archaic social structures that tell women they need a partner and kids to be truly happy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thankfully Gaby finally gets it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s weird marriage started as a contract of ownership and now it has kind of evolved into at best gross consumerism at worst a tax cut , &amp;rdquo ; says Gaby . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Peretti married filmmaker/comedian/actor Jordan Peele in 2016 when she was 38 . They had a son in 2017 but Peretti said her biological clock wasn&amp;rsquo ; t ringing and she wasn&amp;rsquo ; t facing down the pressure to get the partner and kid . She was lucky . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t sure what the future was going to hold for me &amp;mdash ; I really enjoyed my work and the community of comedians and actors I got to be around who are some of the funniest , most entertaining people in the world , &amp;rdquo ; said Peretti. &amp;ldquo ; I wasn&amp;rsquo ; t sure which way my life was going to go but felt like it was going to be exciting in whichever direction it went . I was right . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spoiler alert : this film doesn&amp;rsquo ; t get tied up with a big rom com bow and that makes for some fantastic post flick chat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think it is timely , &amp;rdquo ; said Dorfman. &amp;ldquo ; Jennifer and I have always felt we want to make films that people can go out for a coffee afterwards and talk about it . I think this is one of those films that people are going to have something to say about it , positive or negative . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Peretti added that she was thrilled to play the type of woman she wants to see on the big screen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I am honoured I was given the opportunity to embody this character , &amp;rdquo ; said Peretti. &amp;ldquo ; I hope women and anyone watching will leave emboldened to explore more new experiences . Romantic comedies never really resonated with me so I hope Spinster offers people an alternative model or vision . There is no one way to do life . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Put that last thought on a T-shirt . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **25;59325;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;59352;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/danagee " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;59386;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Dana GeeMon , 02 Dec 2019 19:00:53 **45;59417;TOOLONG ...
