" data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of WFF " **28;59535;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1152857 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Fall Back Down&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Dec. 5 at 8.30 p.m. , Dec. 6&amp;nbsp ; at 3 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Village 8 Cinemas , Whistler &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;59565;TOOLONG ? gclid ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;59594;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Director &lt;a href= " https : **33;59628;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;SB Edwards&lt;/a&gt; is a little anxious about premiering her new film &lt;a href= " https : **33;59663;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Fall Back Down&lt;/a&gt; at the 2019 &lt;a href= " https : **27;59698;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Whistler Film Festival . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What makes the Dec. 5 world debut of her new work even more memorable is that it is the first feature-length film from the Vancouver/Los Angeles based filmmaker. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I mean the barf emoji comes to mind , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards who also wrote the screenplay and was the lead producer on the project . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m trying not to be nervous . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Edwards is not alone in the newbie category , as 10 other directors will premiere their first features at Whistler this year . Edwards is also one of 13 female feature directors bringing work to the festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now in its 19th year , the five-day festival is showing 86 films from 15 different countries . It also boasts the largest Canadian content &amp;mdash ; almost 70 per cent &amp;mdash ; of any film festival in Canada . The festival also offers creative and professional development panels and events . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;59727;TOOLONG ... title= " SB Edwards . " alt= " SB Edwards . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of WFF " **28;59763;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1152856 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Fall Back Down marks a turning point for Edwards , she is no stranger to the filmmaking process as she has 10 years of movie/TV art department experience , short filmmaking and writing credits for TV on her resume . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But taking the reins of a full feature production , including launching it into the world , is another animal completely &amp;mdash ; something that is not lost on Edwards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; &amp;hellip ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t really know what I am doing so this whole process has felt like I am just in a constant state of about to be blindsided by something , which is a bit nerve-racking , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards . &amp;ldquo ; But I think it is going to be wonderful because I feel really proud of how the film turned out . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film&amp;rsquo ; s leading actor Andrew Dunbar , who is also a producer on the project , shares Edwards&amp;rsquo ; feelings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Nobody has seen it yet &amp;mdash ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve seen it a 100 times &amp;mdash ; so it&amp;rsquo ; s such an interesting place to be , &amp;rdquo ; said Dunbar , whose acting resume is a testament to a busy career in Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m so excited that it is going to be screened at the festival ; we&amp;rsquo ; ll get some sort of closure . We&amp;rsquo ; ll get to see it screened , and then it&amp;rsquo ; s the start of the next chapter for the film . It&amp;rsquo ; s nerve-racking . It&amp;rsquo ; s super exciting . It&amp;rsquo ; s all the feels , &amp;rdquo ; said Dunbar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;59793;TOOLONG ... title= " Actor Andrew Dunbar and director/screenwriter SB Edwards on set of Fall Back Down . " alt= " Actor Andrew Dunbar and director/screenwriter SB Edwards on set of Fall Back Down . " data-portal-copyright= " courtesy of WFF " **28;59829;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1152858 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Set in Vancouver , Fall Back Down is a romantic comedy with a punk rock pastiche . The story follows Nick , a heartbroken and listless activist who has decided to not invest himself in anything anymore . That leaden outlook has resulted in an employment record littered with firings from crummy jobs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally he manages to secure a gig at a garment sweatshop , and meets the bristly , quick-tempered Reena ( Aadila Dosani ) . &amp;nbsp ; At first the pair clash but all that changes when they discover a serious crime , a crime Reena is convinced that if they expose it they will become victims of the &amp;ldquo ; textile mafia . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nick&amp;rsquo ; s activism and the activists he is close to are familiar territory for Edwards . She called a &amp;ldquo ; punk rock house , &amp;rdquo ; home and has been an activist since she was young . She has been on the protest lines for a wide range of causes more times than she can count , and is still active in making her voice heard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For me , it started out being about the world I was in and the communities that I was in , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards , who began thinking about the story 10 years ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I felt the need to put us on screen and celebrate activists who protest . It&amp;rsquo ; s kind of interesting that the timing for that is more topical now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Without becoming too preachy &amp;mdash ; because I have seen many a film , an activist based film , go down with the preachiness &amp;mdash ; I wanted to paint everyone that I feel like are my people in this noble light , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another point that Edwards wanted to make in the film is how people react to big emotional upheavals and how the rest of society has a tendency toward wanting people to just get over things . That&amp;rsquo ; s not happening in this story as Nick really struggles after his radical and charming girlfriend ( Jacky Lai ) heads off on a humanitarian mission and never contacts him again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What I wanted to talk about , too , is how slow I think emotional recovery is , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In media something happens and people get better . It all gets wrapped up in an hour . I just wanted to look a little more at how long these periods are when we are mostly falling and then just slightly getting a little more healthier and a little more capable and then one day you kind of look up and you are over something you have been struggling with . When you finally reach a point when you can move in a new direction . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;59859;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;59901;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Check out our comprehensive event **29;59937;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;59968;TOOLONG ... North : The latest from the B.C. TV and film **29;60004;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;60035;TOOLONG ... the latest Metro Vancouver arts **25;60071;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Made for a very tight $200,000 , with $120,000 of that coming from a Telefilm Canada grant , the film focuses on Nick&amp;rsquo ; s bumpy journey . Played perfectly by Dunbar , Nick is one of those sad-sack characters that avoids coming off as a whiner thanks to some emotional depth and humour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For Dunbar , getting a character like Nick was a gift that every actor loves to unwrap. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t get to go out for roles like this . Casting directors don&amp;rsquo ; t see me as the punk activist , usually , &amp;rdquo ; said Dunbar who has also been named one the UBCP/Actra Stars to Watch at this year&amp;rsquo ; s festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Edwards knew Dunbar before this project , and she knew he could take some punk rock roughing up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I always knew he would do a good job , but I was shocked and thrilled and had that feeling , you know when something feels kind of magical . He is a star , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards who also gave big props to Dosani and Lai . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You don&amp;rsquo ; t worry . You don&amp;rsquo ; t worry his performance is going to fall apart at any point . You just get to settle in and be carried by this lovely human who goes through these various emotional challenges . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the film&amp;rsquo ; s spotlight is on Nick , there is plenty to watch in the surrounding characters who keep Nick from falling further into his pit of despair . It&amp;rsquo ; s these characters that Edwards hopes to give more to do in the future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My dream is that Fall Back Down magically turns into a spinoff TV show so I can write all the characters I didn&amp;rsquo ; t have time to explore in the movie , &amp;rdquo ; said Edwards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dunbar said that Edwards personal experience of life in a punk rock house is packed with plot ideas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Don&amp;rsquo ; t you just want to see that world ? You can dig so deep into it , &amp;rdquo ; said Dunbar , &amp;nbsp ; who just finished the Netflix film There&amp;rsquo ; s Someone Inside Your House . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The TV show idea aside , Edwards is busy working again with Fall Back Down executive producer Chris Moore ( Manchester by the Sea and Good Will Hunting ) on developing another TV show . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Called Nowhere , the show is about a fraternal male and female twins who were bullied growing up in small town . There is murder and mystery , says Edwards , who is the creator and head writer on the project . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;60098;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;60140;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? " data-portal-copyright= " Lost Transmissions " **28;60655;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1151907 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Whistler Film Festival&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Dec. 4-8 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Whistler &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;60685;TOOLONG ? gclid ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;60714;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **30;60748;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Simon Pegg&lt;/a&gt; was meant to star in the new indie film &lt;a href= " https : **33;60780;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Lost Transmissions&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was a perfect storm of reasons , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg over the phone from London recently . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I get scripts from my agents that say &amp;lsquo ; you may or may not like this . &amp;rsquo ; But this one said &amp;lsquo ; read this&amp;rsquo ; . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , something else caught the English actor/writer&amp;rsquo ; s eye . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I noticed it was directed by Katharine ( &lt;a href= " https : **30;60815;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Katharine O'Brien&lt;/a&gt; who also wrote the screenplay ) . I hadn&amp;rsquo ; t , until that point , been directed in a feature film by a woman , which felt remiss to me and indicative of the way the film industry is . So I was very happy when I read it and really responded to it , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg . &amp;ldquo ; I thought it was a really moving and interesting story . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The moviemaking experience worked out well , and Pegg felt right at home working on O&amp;rsquo ; Brien&amp;rsquo ; s production . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I live in a matriarchy . Everyone in my house is female , even the animals , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg , whose long list of film credits includes comedy &lt;a href= " https : **31;60847;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Shaun of the Dead&lt;/a&gt; and a handful of titles in the Mission Impossible and Star Wars franchises. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Lost Transmissions story revolves around Theo ( Pegg ) and Hannah ( Juno Temple ) as Hannah tries to help the schizophrenic Theo during a psychotic break . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Off his meds , the manic Theo races through an uneasy and sepia-toned Los Angeles with Hannah and other friends hot on his heels trying to get him to help . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;60880;TOOLONG ... title= " Simon Pegg and Juno Temple in Lost Transmissions " alt= " Simon Pegg and Juno Temple in Lost Transmissions " data-portal-copyright= " Lost Transmissions " **28;60916;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1151906 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Theo&amp;rsquo ; s story is based on a friend of O&amp;rsquo ; Brien&amp;rsquo ; s who she and other close pals helped to get back to his home in England where he could get health care and treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was a success story . I finally learned something this go around and I thought it was worth turning into a film , &amp;rdquo ; said O&amp;rsquo ; Brien , who has had others close to her with mental health issues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The film will be opening this year&amp;rsquo ; s Whistler Film Festival on Dec. 4 in its Canadian debut . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The festival , now in its 19th year , has 43 features and 43 shorts from 15 countries on 2019 program . The festival will also host various special events and industry conferences and meetups. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; O&amp;rsquo ; Brien and Pegg will both be at the festival and will be on hand for a Q&amp;amp ; A after the screening . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the most rewarding things about festivals is to connect to the audience after a screening , &amp;rdquo ; said O&amp;rsquo ; Brien over the phone from Los Angeles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So much gets built up around the red carpets and all the things that go around with it , and you know at the end of the day all that stuff is so fleeting and not really real , and it is way more rewarding to talk to people that come up and say they have a brother , a wife with schizophrenia and talk about how much the film meant to them . That&amp;rsquo ; s been great . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;60946;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;60982;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; O&amp;rsquo ; Brien is one of 13 female feature film directors at the festival . She is also in the class of 11 first-time feature directors showing work at Whistler . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think I had built up enough experience that it just felt like it was time , &amp;rdquo ; said O&amp;rsquo ; Brien , who has made many award-winning short films . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It is one of those things that , I think , as a woman you have to do so much more in order to prove to people that you are ready , so I felt when my time had come I definitely gained the experience and I felt prepared to do it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pegg , who has what the internet calls the holy trinity of sci-fi under his belt with his roles in the Dr. Who TV series and the Star Trek and Star Wars films , said O&amp;rsquo ; Brien had the 19-day shoot totally under control and looking back at the experience he is grateful the role gave him a chance to flex a creative muscles he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t often get to use . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was flattered and surprised that Katharine sent me the script because people don&amp;rsquo ; t tend to associate me with dramatic roles , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was touched because I really love doing dramatic roles . I wanted to be an actor I didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to be a comedian. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; O&amp;rsquo ; Brien , though , did not want Pegg to play Theo completely straight . The character is a charming bon vivant music producer until his illness takes over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He was written to be a certain way &amp;mdash ; extremely likable . He does so much pushing people away from him in the film that I knew I really knew I needed someone you were really rooting for the whole time , &amp;rdquo ; said O&amp;rsquo ; Brien. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s why Simon came to mind . It made sense to look for a comedic actor that could walk the line between something very serious that had these comedic accents , and Simon is so adept at doing that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;61018;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;61060;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Also the laws that are in place are outdated . The periods of observation are minimal , and it&amp;rsquo ; s just allowing a lot of people to just fall out onto the streets . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; O&amp;rsquo ; Brien said the people at the L.A. Mission in downtown Los Angeles told her they estimate 70-80 per cent of the people they see are mentally ill. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pegg , as well , sees the direct relationship between mental illness and homelessness. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have been in L.A. over the years , and Vancouver as well , and noted it there . The homeless problem and the mental health problem together form a really critical part of each city&amp;rsquo ; s social well-being , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg , who was well versed in the issue of the historical closing of mental health facilities in Vancouver as a component to the homeless crisis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over a handful of hectic days you see in this film how precarious life is for someone who is mentally ill . Theo at first has it all going on , but soon the cracks appear as the medications wear off . In turn regular daily activities go out the window as psychosis creeps in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Three bad days , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg with a sigh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s very tempting when you are walking down the street and you see someone on the corner just yelling at the sky as being insane . ( But ) insanity as it is , which is a sort of broad slightly reductive term , is the easiest way to marginalize anybody . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We do it all the time . You hear it all the time in politics and in art . People are branded as crazy then they&amp;rsquo ; re disqualified as human beings . But that person who is shouting might three days ago have been a perfectly functioning , well put together functioning member of society who just so happened could not afford their medication , or have been evicted from their apartment then just suddenly they&amp;rsquo ; re there and yet we just drive past them and think &amp;lsquo ; ahhh they&amp;rsquo ; re just mad . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pegg , who has suffered from depression , did his research to prepare for the role of Theo . He talked with patients , their caregivers and even the man the story is based on , who Pegg reports is on his medication and doing well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His work has paid off as his Theo is a complex character that one minute is charming and lovely then the next manipulative and scary . Your heart breaks when you see him descending , and it is stomped on even further when you see what awaits the mentally ill in America . This is not an easy film , and that&amp;rsquo ; s good because no one needs that old brilliant but mad artist trope. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For this film and his impressive and varied career Pegg will be honoured at this year&amp;rsquo ; s WFF with a Maverick Award . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They know how to tempt actors , &amp;rdquo ; said Pegg with a laugh . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They didn&amp;rsquo ; t need to do that ; I would have happily packed my snowboard and gone . " alt= " ? ine Coady is founder and director of the Irish Film Festival . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;62106;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1153462 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Vancouver Irish Film Festival&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Nov. 29-Dec. 1 &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Vancity Theatre &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **29;62136;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;virff.org&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Back for its second year , the Vancouver Irish Film Festival ( VIRFF ) is returning with solid list of features , documentaries , and a new shorts program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the Irish cinema culture is front and centre , the festival is also providing some non-film fun including traditional Irish music and dance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; You don&amp;rsquo ; t have to be one of the 675,000 self-identifying Irish folk ( Stats Canada 2016 ) in the province to enjoy this festival . The films are first and foremost good . Many events sold out last year , so keep that in mind . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Postmedia News spoke to festival founder and director &amp;Aacute ; ine Coady about the growing event . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;62167;TOOLONG ... title= " ? ine Coady " alt= " ? ine Coady " data-portal-copyright= " Irish Film Festival " **28;62203;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1153459 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What is new in 2019 ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; This year we have introduced a shorts program featuring the best Irish shorts over the past decade . Irish short films have been incredibly successful on the world stage , having achieved two Academy Award wins and 10 Academy Award nominations over the last 15 years . &lt;em&gt; ( You can see the shorts on Nov. 30 at 1 p.m. at Vancity ) . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What was the impetus to start the festival ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; I wanted to promote Irish film and Irish talent aboard and I saw an interest for a new film festival . There is such a wonderful Irish community in B.C. so I had brilliant support to launch it . We hope our schedule of programming will appeal not only to the growing Irish community in Vancouver but also to a broader audience . There are some amazing independent films in Ireland that , for a number of reasons , don&amp;rsquo ; t get seen in North America . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Storytelling and the Irish go hand in hand , so I imagine there was a lot of content to pick from . How did you decide on the lineup ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; The Irish have always had the gift of the gab and we love to tell a good story so it&amp;rsquo ; s little wonder that Irish talent have made some brilliant movies over the years . We started programming for this year&amp;rsquo ; s festival in July , choosing a mix of classic films and newer releases . As we are a new cultural festival , we could pick critically acclaimed films that had finished their distribution but may have not been seen in Canada . I was an independent filmmaker in Dublin before I moved here , so I know some crew who helped me with my indie programming . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How does the growing Irish population in B.C influence your programming choices ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; I wanted to appeal to all ages , so I feel the program at VIRFF 2019 has something for everyone : comedy , drama , fantasy , Irish Oscar shorts , documentaries , Irish-language cinema and family fare . I was delighted last year with the diverse audience of all generations , so we wanted to continue to grow on this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;62233;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;62269;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What film is you most excited to show to audiences ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; Our opening gala film A Bump Along the Way is a new release to Irish cinemas . This female written , directed and produced film set in Derry is a charming feel-good film and I can&amp;rsquo ; t wait to see how audiences in Ireland react to it . Other program highlights include acclaimed documentary Gaza from Garry Keane and Andrew McConnell , and Ireland&amp;rsquo ; s official entry for best international film at the 2020 Academy Awards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What are some of the other , non-film programming you have planned for this year ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; Festivalgoers can enjoy the &amp;ldquo ; craic , &amp;rdquo ; and watched live traditional Irish music and dancing performances . We have Irish food and drinks stalls , too , so everyone can enjoy an Irish cinema experience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All our volunteers ( including myself ) are Irish expats on a two-year working holiday visa , so we&amp;rsquo ; re working hard to bring Irish cinema to B.C. during our time in Canada . We don&amp;rsquo ; t have roots or family here but we wanted to leave an impact and establish a cultural film festival . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;62305;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;62347;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? It means leaving the North Pole to play private detective in Phoenix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Director Marc Lawrence ( Miss Congeniality , Two Weeks Notice ) wrote the story and took a lot of the inspiration for its look and feel from the thousands of holiday season images painted by American realist Thomas Kinkade . ArtsMoviesNetflix aims for the best stories in global animationhttp : **31;65611;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;65644;TOOLONG ... title= " A still from the Netflix animated holiday feature Klaus . " alt= " A still from the Netflix animated holiday feature Klaus . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;65680;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1131836 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Melissa Cobb is vice-president for original animation at Netflix . Before taking on her present position in September 2017 , the industry veteran held senior management positions at the Walt Disney Company , Fox Feature Animation , and DreamWorks , where she was the producer of the Oscar-nominated Kung Fu Panda trilogy. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The UCLA School of Management MBA and Stanford BSc of California was in Vancouver recently to receive a Women in Animation Diversity Award , presented in partnership with the Spark Computer Graphics Society ( Spark CG ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;65710;TOOLONG ... title= " Melissa Cobb , Netflix VP original animation . " alt= " Melissa Cobb , Netflix VP original animation . " data-portal-copyright= " STEPHANIE GIRARD " **28;65746;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1131840 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before receiving that honour on the opening night of the SPARK Animation 2019 conference , Cobb took time to discuss the slate of animated features and series that are appearing on Netflix , and the changing face of how products are delivered to a global viewership. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While she was in Vancouver , Cobb visited Burnaby-based BRON Studios , where the Kris Pearn and Cory Evans-directed animated feature the Willoughbys is being produced . Hollywood North animation houses such as BRON Studios , Atomic Cartoons and others are actively involved in the creation of content for Netflix&amp;rsquo ; s massive schedule . As more OTT ( over-the-top ) streaming services enter the market , it&amp;rsquo ; s a sure bet that local animation houses will be cranking out new programming . Cobb said that receiving the diversity award reinforced the conscious effort that she and Netflix have made to promote women into all positions of an industry that has been accurately described as a &amp;ldquo ; pirate ship . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From females in top jobs to an incredible amount of mobility , the times are really changing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There has a been a big difference lately , with women running Paramount , DreamWorks , Warner Brothers and Nickelodeon , &amp;rdquo ; said Cobb. &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a really cool thing to see these people that I grew up with , even if we are in competition , being in these sorts of positions . The business has never been as fluid as it is now , with so much mobility for artists and others to be going to work on projects that they are excited about . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The idea being that , rather than sticking to the past practice of staying at the same studio for decades on end , creatives today are able to pursue their passion and get a paycheque . It translates into better quality work when the team is genuinely into the project . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very international industry now , with new talent coming out of China , Ireland , Mexico , India and , of course , Canada , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; With the new models taking into account all the opportunities all over the world , the traditional route of coming through Hollywood to get a feature film made or be a serious creator is changing . There will be opportunities for new talent to emerge in regions and get supported in the country in which they live . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The decisions of what to program still roll out of Los Angeles , Calif. , but the amount of new , original content coming to the online broadcaster from other places is substantial . Talk to anyone at any major animation hub and they will tell you that the key to a really vital industry isn&amp;rsquo ; t in doing service work for others , but in creating your own intellectual property . Netflix has partnered with Hollywood North studios such as Atomic Cartoons to produce such popular original programs as Beat Bugs , The Last Kids , as well as service hits such as Hilda . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As well as North American products , Cobb has brought Mighty Little Bheem to Netflix . The first animated series from India follows the adventures of the baby version of the mythologically inspired character of Chhota Bheem , which has enjoyed multiple spinoff series . Nothing has been done to &amp;ldquo ; package&amp;rdquo ; the product for other markets either . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;65776;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;65812;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a non-verbal , preschool program that&amp;rsquo ; s entirely created in India that is now one of our biggest shows in that category globally , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; We don&amp;rsquo ; t judge what might work in a particular market , we make a piece of content , put it out everywhere , in every language and let the audience decide . We&amp;rsquo ; re finding that everybody gets it or doesn&amp;rsquo ; t , and what&amp;rsquo ; s the best is what rises to the top . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every major service provider is pursuing new content too . Competition for original new programming is fierce and that&amp;rsquo ; s translating into good jobs , more variety in shows and &amp;mdash ; best of all &amp;mdash ; what Cobb describes as a &amp;ldquo ; smarter kid space . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is a lot of really smart writing and interesting work going on in kid&amp;rsquo ; s programs , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Once you&amp;rsquo ; ve opened up the doors to more creators around the globe and you are no longer looking at &amp;lsquo ; this needs to be for the 10 a.m. time slot&amp;rsquo ; anymore , things become a lot more exciting . You can take more risks , diversify more and bring in many more and varied voices . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is also the bottom line behind Netflix bringing in someone with Cobb&amp;rsquo ; s considerable chops to helm the kids-and-family fare . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Disney+ launches Nov. 12 , and the children&amp;rsquo ; s entertainment juggernaut pulled all of its movies from Netflix last year . Other content is expected to go away as different entertainment companies launch their own streaming services . The Magic Kingdom is beyond a formidable challenger to any and all firms that pursue a piece of the profitable younger-viewer segment . Cobb&amp;rsquo ; s division needs hits now , as Variety.com reports that 60 per cent of Netflix customers &amp;mdash ; or about 83 million households &amp;mdash ; regularly watch kids-and-family content . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;65848;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;65884;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; First up is director Sergio Pablos&amp;rsquo ; s holiday adventure comedy Klaus . Mike Devlin , Victoria Times ColonistWed , 18 Mar 2020 20:25:04 **45;5605;TOOLONG ... things to know about Are You in Love , by Basia Bulathttp : **35;5652;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;5689;TOOLONG ... title= " Basia Bulat. " alt= " Basia Bulat. " data-portal-copyright= " RICHMOND LAM " **28;5725;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1237253 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Are You in Love&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Basia Bulat&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Secret City Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to believe that she was once known as an autoharp-strumming fresh face on the folk circuit . Because singer/songwriter Basia Bulat is now a full-on torch singer with serious pop sensibilities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her music has become a delightful hybrid of such &amp;rsquo ; 70s acts as &amp;mdash ; no , really &amp;mdash ; Captain &amp;amp ; Tennille blended with some cosmic southern soul and a dash of vintage new wave all thrown together to illuminate her instantly recognizable soaring vibrato. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Working once again with Jim James ( My Morning Jacket ) , who also helmed 2016&amp;rsquo ; s Good Advice , Bulat explores even denser textures and arrangements on the album&amp;rsquo ; s 13 tracks . Fans will be surprised &amp;mdash ; pleasantly &amp;mdash ; by the prog rock elements in songs such as Light Years , and it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to miss the arena-oriented feel of many of the songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are five things to know about Are You in Love ? : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 : Bowie influence&lt;/strong&gt; . Anyone listening to the title track , and album opener , is likely to get a sense of deja vu for David Bowie&amp;rsquo ; s classic Five Years from this song . It&amp;rsquo ; s got a similar ebb and flow in the drama of the delivery and one of only a few fist-in-the-air belters that Bulat has recorded . Her vocals are powerful throughout , but this song really was a good choice to introduce the album . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 : Your Girl&lt;/strong&gt; . Time to get your new wave on people . This bouncy tune has Cars-style keyboards , a totally defining bass line , and the surprisingly sad lyric is perfect juxtaposed against the happy music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 : Homesick&lt;/strong&gt; . This is classic Basia . Sparse strummed autoharp with just a smattering of what sounds almost like a toy piano accompanying her at first as she drops a vocal that could come right from a classic country tune . Then the whole thing blows up with a near wall of sound-style arrangement as she belts out &amp;ldquo ; I get homesick/Can you remember why&amp;rdquo ; to someone who &amp;mdash ; apparently &amp;mdash ; isn&amp;rsquo ; t listening . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 : No Control&lt;/strong&gt; . While the lead single is the poppy Your Girl , this funky mid-tempo ballad just might be a breakout track . The way the words &amp;lsquo ; no control&amp;rsquo ; are repeated , almost chant-like , just layers on the heartbreak while the backing band swings hard . By the end , it&amp;rsquo ; s exhilarating in the way that a soul ballad should be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Love is at the End of the World&lt;/strong&gt; . It&amp;rsquo ; s also at the end of the album&amp;rsquo ; s lengthy listen , as this song closes out the set . Yet another piano-driven mid tempo ballad that goes for that almost trancelike repetition of the song title , this one stands out for its slow , percolating electric piano backing and one of Bulat&amp;rsquo ; s breathiest vocals . She is in full power mode on most of Are You in Love ? It&amp;rsquo ; s nice to hear her drop back a bit too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;5755;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;5791;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Also out this week : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;African Head Charge&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Drumming is a Language : 1990-2011 Reissues Box Se&lt;/strong&gt; t &lt;em&gt;On-U Sound&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If ever there was perfect music for meditating away the long days of social-distancing and quarantine ahead , it&amp;rsquo ; s the avant-dub reggae pioneered by this seminal U.K. unit . Containing four heavily expanded versions of classic studio releases &amp;mdash ; Songs of Praise ( 1990 ) , In Pursuit of Shashamane Land , Visions of a Psychedelic Africa ( 2005 ) and Voodoo of the Godsent ( 2011 ) &amp;mdash ; as well as an album of unreleased tracks from the 1980s ( Churchical Chant of the Iyabinghi ) , this five-CD box set captures the collaboration between percussionist Bonjo Iyabinghi Noah and producer Adrian Sherwood . Without question , this is some of the deepest and most spiritual dub reggae ever crafted with songs from One Destination to Stoned Age Man still packing meaning and punch . Absolutely essential listening for anyone with a love of grooves , electronic beats and chanting to Jah. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;5827;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;5863;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Avishai Cohen&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Big Vicious&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;ECM Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trumpeter Cohen formed this experimental electronic fusion ensemble in 2013 after immigrating to the U.S. from Israel . Featuring Uzi Ramirez ( guitar ) , Yonatan Albalak ( guitar , bass ) , Aviv Cohen and Ziv Ravitz ( drums , live sampling ) , the 11 tracks range from the atmospheric ambient jams ( Honey Fountain , Moonlight Sonata , The Things You Tell Me ) to surprisingly rocking ( King Kutner ) . It&amp;rsquo ; s the kind of crossover sound that acts like Nils Petter Molvaer succeeded with decades back and it still resonates . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;5899;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;5935;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; **35;5971;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **39;6008;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt;Napalm Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is going to be a surprise to fans of Myrkur ( Amalie Bruun ) and her symphonic black metal . Not that the haunting and spooky sounds associated with the artist are absent on this new record , just that she has gone full-folky on this 12-track record . Droning hardanger fiddles , hand drums , choruses and glockenspiels are all brought together in a modern take on Scandinavian folk that is so near New Age Celtic-style music you could probably gift it to your Enya-loving relative or your Dead Can Dance-loving goth buddy and both would be delighted . It&amp;rsquo ; s quite beautiful and Fager Som En Ros should be used in an episode next season of The Witcher. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;6049;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;6085;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; **37;6121;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Violent Nature&lt;/strong&gt; **38;6160;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This Calgary crew plays classic old-school metal with clean , blues-tinged lead vocals , lots of harmonies and really big riffs . But , after only a few events , the orchestra cancelled live performances for the foreseeable future . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was an understandable and wise decision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After what must have been some intensely confusing days , the VSO made a bold call : To take two classic Beethoven works , the Fourth Piano Concerto and the Sixth Symphony and play them at the Orpheum March 15 as a livestream broadcast to interested listeners . ( View the concert at &lt;a href= " https : **33;7687;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **32;7722;TOOLONG ... ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7756;TOOLONG ... title= " Members of the VSO play to an empty Orpheum because of COVID-19 restrictions on March 15 , 2020. " alt= " Members of the VSO play to an empty Orpheum because of COVID-19 restrictions on March 15 , 2020. " data-portal-copyright= " Vancouver Symphony Orchestra " **28;7792;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1241393 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was invited to sit in rather splendid isolation in the empty theatre to watch . Downtown Vancouver was by no means deserted on this bright afternoon , but it certainly was subdued . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And although I&amp;rsquo ; m no stranger to the backstage world of classical music , it did feel decidedly odd to slink in by the stage door and wend my way through the Orpheum&amp;rsquo ; s unglamorous nether regions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The players were assembled in formal orchestra black . At 2 p.m. on the dot , maestro Otto Tausk was prepared to give the downbeat . The tech guys weren&amp;rsquo ; t quite ready , resulting in a few extra-long moments of pent-up tension . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was a unique experience and the orchestra members were well aware of its significance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , pianist Saleem Ashkar began the especially intimate opening measures of the concerto , a solo piano that was vulnerable in the emptiness. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a few moments , it was time for the orchestra to join in and the familiar , though still magical , concerto was truly underway &amp;mdash ; though with a certain distracted fragility. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By the recapitulation of the first movement , it was apparent that conductor , soloist and orchestra were all completely focused on the shared task of bringing Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s concerto to life . Circumstances were irrelevant . This was all about the music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7822;TOOLONG ... title= " Members of the VSO play to an empty Orpheum. " alt= " Members of the VSO play to an empty Orpheum. " data-portal-copyright= " Vancouver Symphony Orchestra " **28;7858;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1241394 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m a fan of Tausk&amp;rsquo ; s approach to classical-era repertoire , because he brings a 21st century awareness of early 19th century performance practices to his interpretations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To that end , he arranged the orchestra in a manner that Beethoven himself would have recognized : first violins on the left ; second violins on the right ; trumpets next to their percussion cousin , the timpani ; and a phalanx of seven double basses across the back of the stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This was no quest for novelty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There were immediate acoustic benefits from a rich , very present bass sound . For example , in the concerto&amp;rsquo ; s second movement &amp;mdash ; a sort of argument between a choleric orchestra and a more sanguine soloist &amp;mdash ; the empty hall added an extra measure of resonance to the orchestral outbursts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The reading of the Pastoral Symphony was no less persuasive , dozens of musicians playing with chamber music finesse and a truly collaborative spirit under the leadership of a fine conductor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A lot has happened in the last few weeks . In the great scheme of things , the cancellation of classical concerts is just a small part of our new , complicated reality . But as the performance unfolded , I realized that this was the first time that I had really considered the implications of how my life as a critic with a routine of two to three concerts a week has changed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a sobering realization . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before the event , I had quick chats with both Tausk and the VSO&amp;rsquo ; s new chief administrator , Angela Elster . With this exceptional event out of the way , Tausk plans to fly back to his family in The Netherlands ; Elster has the unenviable responsibility of keeping the VSO&amp;rsquo ; s home fires burning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both were adamant about the power of the great classics to speak to us in difficult times . The entirely unanticipated finale to the Beethoven festival said loudly and clearly : &amp;ldquo ; This is who we are . This is what we do . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;8567;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1229856 " /&gt; **31;8597;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Krystle Dos Santos&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **27;8630;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;8659;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mixing her time between music and acting , Vancouver-based artist Krystle Dos Santos has been steadily building towards her new album since her self-titled Western Canadian Music Award-winning 2008 debut . That acclaimed recording was followed by the even better Fame Fatale , which also received a WCMA nomination . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bloom/Burn deserves much more attention than that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over 10 tracks , this Edmonton-raised Guyanese musician pays homage to the sounds of Sixties and Seventies soul , classic Motown , and deep rhythm and blues . Backed by her quintet , Dos Santos&amp;rsquo ; voice soars , roars and delivers stories of love and devotion that sound like instant classics . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While there is no question that it&amp;rsquo ; s a hard row to hoe as a soul singer in Vancouver deserving national recognition , Dos Santos has what it takes to do it , as her past appearances at events such as the Honey Jam Toronto indicate . Here are five things to know about Bloom/Burn. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 : Bloom . &lt;/strong&gt; The album opens with a horn section intro that could have been on a Stax label Otis Redding session . Then the voice comes in with maximum impact at a low , bluesy pace that fits the riff perfectly . At around the 50 second mark , she does a little jump on the verse about &amp;ldquo ; the line through the clouds&amp;rdquo ; that just raises the hair on the back of your neck . That&amp;rsquo ; s what you want in a song . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 : Here 4 U&lt;/strong&gt; . A stunner of a funk groove built off of electric piano , pulsing clean bass and a some very nimble guitar picking bubbles underneath this song . Then the jazziness is paired up with more blasting horns and some hip-shaking percussion to hit that sweet spot of being both understated but impossible to not want to move to . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8691;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8727;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 : Buried Alive&lt;/strong&gt; . It would be a mistake to classify Dos Santos as a neo-soul act . Although she does appear to have an affinity for the stylings of a different era , she is also most certainly working with modern urban pop motifs as well . Nowhere is this better demonstrated than on this arena-sized tune . From its gigantic drum break to its fist-punching whoa-oh&amp;rsquo ; s , this is more Rihanna or Beyonc&amp;eacute ; than Aretha . Simply put , this is an artist who appears able to do it all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 : I Cry&lt;/strong&gt; . With it&amp;rsquo ; s reggae-rock rhythm and heavy arrangement , this is unlike any other piece on Bloom/Burn . It also demonstrates yet another side of Dos Santos&amp;rsquo ; considerable range . It&amp;rsquo ; s no surprise that she has been in so many musical theatre performances ranging from the Arts Club Theatre&amp;rsquo ; s Dream Girls to the Firehall Arts Centre&amp;rsquo ; s The Chelsea Hotel : The Songs of Leonard Cohen . The woman can deliver dramatically . She is working on a new cabaret musical titled Hey Viola ! about Canadian civil rights activist Viola Desmond with The Chelsea Hotel writer Tracey Power ( Miss Shakespeare , Glory ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Walk On Through&lt;/strong&gt; . OK , this is an obvious single to release from the record . A very Northern Soul-style rave-up with a chorus somewhat reminiscent of Spice Girls&amp;rsquo ; Stop . It&amp;rsquo ; s bold and brassy statement that can become something of a signature . You just know this is a killer in concert . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Also out this week : &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8763;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8799;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Anna Calvi&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **35;8835;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt;Domino Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Choosing to make her latest album a reworking of seven tracks from her acclaimed 2018 Mercury Prize-nominated release , Hunted seems a bit odd at first . But one need only listen to Calvi and Julia Holter&amp;rsquo ; s approach to Swimming Pool to appreciate just how utterly new the music is . This chorally orchestrated track is a standout , but so are the ethereal Eden ( feat . Charlotte Gainsburg ) , snarky Don&amp;rsquo ; t Beat the Girl Out of My Boy ( feat . Courtney Barnett ) , and others . Calvi&amp;rsquo ; s reframing of Indies or Paradise into something that sounds like it could have come off of PJ Harvey&amp;rsquo ; s Dry is fantastic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8872;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8908;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Chats&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;High Risk Behaviour&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Dine Alone Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From singer/guitarist Eamon Sandwith&amp;rsquo ; s tragic bowl cut/mullet hairstyle to having the viral video Succulent Chinese Meal Guy star in their Dine N Dash video , every thing that seems beyond stupid about this Sunshine Coast , Queensland , Australia punk trio probably isn&amp;rsquo ; t . Formed when the three members were in high school , the band&amp;rsquo ; s brand of young , loud and snotty music is delightfully cheeky , relentlessly entertaining and it&amp;rsquo ; s not hard to see why the group&amp;rsquo ; s odes to smoke breaks ( Smoko ) and local haunts ( Ross River ) and everyday Aussie occurrences ( The Clap , Heatstroke ) is killer . A hot album with those in the know for a year or more , it&amp;rsquo ; s now available in North America , doubtless in advance of a tour . Yay . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;8944;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;8980;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Jonathan Wilson&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Dixie Blu&lt;/strong&gt; r &lt;em&gt;BMG/Bella Union&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Playing David Gilmore to Roger Waters on Waters&amp;rsquo ; Us + Them tour left Wilson with some new tricks to approaching his easy going Seventies Laurel Canyon-era style songwriting . The opening of Just For Love has a keyboard passage that could be straight out of Shine On You Crazy Diamond , and his love of reverb-drenched pedal steel across the album echoes Pink Floyd guitar , too . But what really stands out is the many different vocal styles Wilson employs from a gentle whisper tone ( O&amp;rsquo ; Girl ) and a ringing country twang ( &amp;rsquo ; 69 Corvette ) to drawling roots rocker ( Enemies ) . At 14 songs , it&amp;rsquo ; s a bit long . But the songs all stand up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;9016;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;9052;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Spectres&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **38;9088;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt;Artoffact Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brian Gustavson&amp;rsquo ; s post-punk crew really knows how to conjure up the moody atmospherics of 1980s UK bands . The most obvious influence would have to be Joy Division/New Order , as the opening track The Head and the Heart makes clear . Over the course of the nine tracks , the group offers up everything from the addictive drive of When Possessed Pray to the downright dance-happy Fate . The production by ACTORS&amp;rsquo ; Jason Corbett deserves mention as it just crackles through the speakers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;9128;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;9170;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Riot is more a movement than a musical acthttp : **37;9476;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;9515;TOOLONG ... title= " Pussy Riot live in 2018. " alt= " Pussy Riot live in 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " IGNACIO ORREGO @FOTOROCK " **28;9551;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1229827 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Pussy Riot&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Cancelled &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Fortune Sound Club , 147 E. Pender St. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; $26 at Red Cat Records , Zulu and &lt;a href= " https : **33;9581;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **26;9616;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Rally with us in 2020 ! We encourage you to come to the performances with posters and banners , and with your face covered -- masks , balaclavas , scarfs , anything . Let 's riot ! &lt;/em&gt; &amp;mdash ; Pussy Riot Team &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to Nadezhda Tolokonnikova , Pussy Riot is a political movement first and a band after that . This poses the question of what exactly people are paying to see when whatever membership of the Russian anarcha-feminist collective steps on the Fortune Sound Club stage next week ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The co-founder of the Moscow-based agitprop collective explains it like this : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Music , obviously , but Pussy Riot came about as a movement for political statement and action first , &amp;rdquo ; said Tolokonnikova. &amp;ldquo ; We would stage unsanctioned performances with whoever was available to participate and the music was a vehicle to add impact . It was often samples of other bands mixed together , but as things have developed , the band has become a vehicle for presenting ideas with a somewhat more fixed membership and focus on the songs . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Formed in 2011 by Yekaterina Samutsevich , Tolokonnikova and her ex-husband Pyotr Verzilov , Pussy Riot has its origins in the anarchist art collective Voina , known for political and provocative **26;9644;TOOLONG actions . Made up of art-school students , academic activists and more , Voina mounted numerous art &amp;ldquo ; actions&amp;rdquo ; including a particularly memorable one on June 14 , 2010. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Titled Dick Captured by the FSB , the event included painting a 65-metre-long phallus on the surface of the Liteyny drawbridge leading to the headquarters of the Federal Security Service in St. Petersburg . The painting , titled Giant Galactic Space Penis , delivered a probing message to all who could see it when the drawbridge was raised . Anyone who thinks that there isn&amp;rsquo ; t radicalism in Russia would do well to read up on the past activities of groups such as this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The need to separate Russia and the Russian people from Putin , from the government , is so important , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; There are people actively opposed to the state putting themselves at great risk there like there are everywhere , and so many of the issues are the same as in the rest of the world . Pussy Riot is about getting together and doing something about it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pussy Riot formed out of the Moscow faction of Voina . From its beginning , the use of web-based technology was key to creating its enduring statements and spreading them throughout Russia and beyond . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group staged impromptu &amp;ldquo ; concerts&amp;rdquo ; at various sites in the city , typically dressed in loudly coloured dresses and leggings , wearing balaclavas and conducting interviews under pseudonyms . These events were intended to raise awareness around issues dear to the membership , which ranged from feminism and LGBTQ rights to social inequality and prisoner&amp;rsquo ; s rights . Underlying all the group&amp;rsquo ; s work is fierce opposition to autocratic and kleptocratic rule , particularly that of Russian President Vladimir Putin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Feb. 21 , 2012 , Pussy Riot catapulted into the international spotlight when they performed for 35 seconds inside Moscow&amp;rsquo ; s Cathedral of Christ the Saviour to create a video clip for the song Punk Prayer : Mother of God Drive Putin Away . This performance led to the later arrests of Maria Alyokhina and Tolokonnikova , who were charged with hooliganism and imprisoned without bail . Samutsevich was also arrested in conjunction with the event . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;All three were sentenced to two years in a penal colony , with Samutsevich lucky to get released on appeal . Tolokonnikova says it was a terrible experience , but it did n't lessen her progressive convictions . Upon release from prison in Krasnoyarsk , she flashed a victory sign to journalists , shouting " Russia without Putin. " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Prison in Russia is part of the program to oppress people and conditions are so bad , so brutal , that it&amp;rsquo ; s understandable why everyone is scared to do anything that could draw the attention of the authorities and put you at risk , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; I still have nightmares about being put back in prison . But you have no choice but to oppose what is happening , not only in Russia . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The conviction generated international outrage and the three women became the focus of attention from organizations ranging from Amnesty International to the German Bundestag . Even Hillary Clinton voiced support . By the time they were released from prison , Alyokhina and Tolokonnikova were global celebrities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After their prison release , books such as Words Will Break Cement : The Passion of Pussy Riot ( Riverside Press ) and documentaries such as director Mike Lerner&amp;rsquo ; s and Maxim Pozdorovkin&amp;rsquo ; s Pussy Riot : A Punk Prayer put the members in the spotlight . The timing couldn&amp;rsquo ; t have been better for spreading the Pussy Riot message . The putsch against Western democratic values taking place in Europe , the U.K. and the U.S. begged for a continued , international-level stance against state corruption , police brutality , prison conditions and the attack on women , immigrant , minority and LGBTQ rights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group certainly nailed the outcome of the 2016 American election , releasing its frightfully prophetic video titled Make America Great Again only a week before Donald Trump&amp;rsquo ; s triumphant presidential bid . Opening with Tolokonnikova acting as an anchor on &amp;ldquo ; Trump TV&amp;rdquo ; ( which now exists ) proclaiming that &amp;ldquo ; everyone&amp;rsquo ; s favourite , the great Donald Trump , has won the presidential election , &amp;rdquo ; the song then attacks and subverts many of the MAGA hatters&amp;rsquo ; favourite quotes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Did I wish that we had been wrong about that , yes , definitely , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; But there are so many similarities between Putin and Trump and the people behind them , that it&amp;rsquo ; s not that surprising . There is a strong sentiment in a certain part of society that the past was better , that we need to go back to the &amp;lsquo ; good old days . &amp;rsquo ; Somehow , this is going to fix the problems in the world ; it will not . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So Pussy Riot will be on the road doing its part &amp;mdash ; the band announced the tour would be postponed due to coronavirus concerns &amp;mdash ; playing its grinding electronic noise/punk songs such as the self-explanatory Police State and I Can&amp;rsquo ; t Breathe , written in honour of Eric Garner , who died after NYPD officer Daniel Pantaleo put him in a chokehold during an arrest . They have also dropped the fierce track Hangerz ( featuring Vic Mensa and Junglepussy ) , which challenges the continuing attacks against women&amp;rsquo ; s reproductive choice and rights around the world . Pussy Riot had plans to partner with PLUS1 to put $1 of every ticket sold to support &lt;a href= " https : **26;9672;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Action Canada for Sexual Health and Rights&lt;/a&gt; ( formerly the Planned Parenthood Federation of Canada ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tolokonnikova notes in a news release : &amp;ldquo ; Stop banning and punishing me . Treat me as truly equal . Talk to me . Listen to me . Help me when I need it . Planned parenthood and their affiliates are places where women can receive real support , and we , the women of Pussy Riot , cherish these unique safe places dearly . And we&amp;rsquo ; re seriously dedicated to continuously support them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Get the latest updates on &lt;a href= " https : **33;9700;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Pussy Riot&lt;/a&gt; news on Facebook and the &lt;a href= " https : **33;9735;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **27;9770;TOOLONG station on YouTube. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;9799;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;9835;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;9871;TOOLONG " **36;9902;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;9940;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;9969;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynFri , 13 Mar 2020 19:23:52 **45;10000;TOOLONG ... That&amp;rsquo ; s not to say there aren&amp;rsquo ; t big name classic rockers on the road &amp;mdash ; The Rolling Stones fit that bill better than any other act on the planet &amp;mdash ; but there appears to be plenty of new talent that can pack an arena , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As far as exciting new music goes , the decade is off to a good start . That so many emerging artists also happen to be women in a male-dominated industry is one more bonus . After growing up having to listen to how their granddads couldn&amp;rsquo ; t get no satisfaction , young women are demanding some now . It makes for more interesting music lyrically and emotionally than has been heard since the post-punk era saw a huge influx of all-female or female-fronted groups releasing rousing records . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After years of radio churning up variations of whining grunge , post-grunge , n&amp;uuml ; grunge , retro grunge bands , it&amp;rsquo ; s awesome to have something fresh sounding out . Prime examples of exciting sounds include Grammy ruler Billie Eilish , whose Vancouver show has been sold out for months , and Polaris Prize-winner Haviah Mighty , who is here for a limited club engagement . And if your taste runs towards gritty pub rock with classic punk influences , then Amyl and the Sniffers is a quartet you need to check out . Fronted by Amy Taylor , the group&amp;rsquo ; s sound mixes in elements of late &amp;rsquo ; 60s Detroit gutter rock , swaggering glammy &amp;rsquo ; 70s punk , and some decidedly Antipodean pub boogie . It&amp;rsquo ; s not that surprising the music is raw , given that the band&amp;rsquo ; s name is a play on local slang for street level club drug amyl nitrate . It&amp;rsquo ; s loud , brash and more than a little bit hooligan , right down to those tragic London bike courier haircuts some of the band members are sporting . The band&amp;rsquo ; s last show in town at the Fox Cabaret is still buzzed about . That means different things to different folks . Students of all ages revel in the respite from routine . Parents recoil in terror of what to do with all of them running free once more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Keeping the kids of all ages busy during the break is big business . Believe it or not , a likely majority won&amp;rsquo ; t be taking the time off to get caught up on coursework that could perhaps use some attention . The main assignment is to have fun . But what kind ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The new of the day isn&amp;rsquo ; t conducive to time-tested , spring break time fillers . Mounting concerns over the coronavirus find a lot of travel getting nixed . From camps , slopes and beyond , recreation and risk appear to be in a joust for dominance . But you can rest assured that artists will still be touring . It takes a lot more than a potential pandemic to keep musicians from money , and fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With that in mind , here is a mix of five concerts that looked well worth attending over the next 11 days . I can&amp;rsquo ; t offer any statistics , but once again this year March proffers an early spring bouquet of fine pianists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider Saleem Ashkar , artistic director of the Galilee Chamber , who will be part of the VSO&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;13083;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Beethovenfest **25;13118;TOOLONG &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; featured in the sublime Fourth Piano Concerto and the oft maligned Choral Fantasy in programs March 13 and 14 . The extra incentive here is that Ritter won the first Chopin Competition on Period Instruments in Warsaw in 2018 . He&amp;rsquo ; ll be playing lots of Chopin , but also Beethoven , Haydn , and two far more obscure figures from the generation before Chopin : Franciszek Lessel ( 1780&amp;mdash ; 1838 ) , and Jan V&amp;aacute ; clav Hugo Vor&amp;iacute ; &amp;scaron ; ek ( 1791&amp;mdash ; 1825 ) . ( See chopinsociety.org. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13174;TOOLONG ... title= " The one , the only Andr ? s Schiff . Photo credit : Joanna Bergin. " alt= " The one , the only Andr ? s Schiff . Photo credit : Joanna Bergin. " data-portal-copyright= " Joanna Bergin " **28;13210;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1233431 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then there are solo recitals by &lt;strong&gt;Sir Andr ? s Schiff&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;Benjamin Grosvenor&lt;/strong&gt; for the Vancouver Recital Society . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Schiff needs no introduction ; lucky for us , this performing giant of our age seems comfortable playing for Vancouver audiences . Over his regular appearances , he&amp;rsquo ; s given our audiences things that don&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily appear on the programs of other mid-sized towns . For example , we were the only place in Canada that got to hear his multi-concert Last Sonatas project , and before that we heard him do the entire first book of J.S. Bach&amp;rsquo ; s Well-Tempered Clavier. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For this visit Schiff focuses on Beethoven , six late middle period sonatas &lt;em&gt; ( March 24 at the Vancouver Playhouse ) &lt;/em&gt; . And two days earlier there&amp;rsquo ; s a special Vancouver Recital Society 40th birthday program at the Chan . It&amp;rsquo ; s an all-Bach program , with the Overture in the French Style and the Italian Concerto . Then ( fanfare , please ! ) the Goldberg Variations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadians take something of a proprietary interest in Bach&amp;rsquo ; s mega-masterwork . While Glenn Gould didn&amp;rsquo ; t exactly put it on the map , he did bring it widespread popularity . And now every player , young or old , famous or not , reveres it as one of the commanding landmarks of the keyboard repertoire , and wants to show what they can bring to its performance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Schiff&amp;rsquo ; s Well Tempered Clavier back in 2012 still resonates with me as one of the great performances in my reviewing career . I fully anticipate his reading of the Goldbergs will pack a similar punch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A ( very ) young Benjamin Grosvenor made his Canadian debut for the recital society back in 2013 . Still in his 20s , he&amp;rsquo ; s pushing boundaries as he seeks to carve out his own niche in the crowded world of piano players by demonstrating both personal taste and sustained musical growth . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Grosvenor&amp;rsquo ; s matinee on March 15 starts off with a keyboard work by Jean-Philippe Rameau . When was the last time we heard Rameau other than as an encore ? Grosvenor follows this with Schumann&amp;rsquo ; s Kreisleriana , an anthology of characteristic pieces that gives pianists plenty of scope for interpretive variety . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Grosvenor ends with another keyboard work : Liszt&amp;rsquo ; s gigantic , four-movements-in-one Sonata in B minor . Though Schumann and Liszt don&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily seem like the most complementary pair of composers , Grosvenor&amp;rsquo ; s done his homework : Liszt dedicated his exceptional , extravagant opus to Schumann &amp;mdash ; a quid pro quo for Schumann dedicating his Fantasy , Op. 17 to the 19th century&amp;rsquo ; s greatest keyboard showman a few years earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s going to be intense , but what month&amp;rsquo ; s worth of music ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;13240;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;13282;TOOLONG ... about classical **26;13318;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;13346;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? " data-portal-copyright= " Steve Rose " **28;13634;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1231280 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;A Bowie Celebration&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; March 13 , 8 p.m. ( subject to change ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Commodore Ballroom ( over 19 only ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets : &lt;/strong&gt; $72.25 ( inc. fees and taxes ) at &lt;a href= " https : **33;13664;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;13699;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; A roster of David Bowie alumni performs the entirety of the albums The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars , and Diamond Dogs . Special guest vocalists include Sass Jordan , Joe Sumner , and Corey Glover ( Living Colour ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brooklyn-born bandleader/keyboardist Mike Garson has been touring with A Bowie Celebration for four years . Postmedia News talked to him about Chris Hadfield , Evan Rachel Wood , and doing songs that even Bowie never performed live . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You 've played all over the world and had over 100 guest vocalists sit in . How much rehearsal time do they get ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; &amp;nbsp ; We usually just get a sound check with them . They do their homework , I send them the music , we talk about the keys and the songs . It&amp;rsquo ; s really shooting from the hip . But it&amp;rsquo ; s exciting because usually they&amp;rsquo ; re great singers . Over the last four years , we&amp;rsquo ; ve had everyone from Sting to Lorde to Perry Farrell to Simon Le Bon to Joe Elliott . It&amp;rsquo ; s endless . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : There 's at least one Canadian connection with Sass Jordan . Are there any other Canadian connections ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; In Toronto , we might have Commander ( Chris ) Hadfield the astronaut sit in . He loves to sing Bowie music . He did it last year and the first year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Actor Evan Rachel Wood has performed with the band as well . How did that come about ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; She&amp;rsquo ; s a good friend of mine , and she&amp;rsquo ; s sung with us two or three times over the last four years . This year she had a premiere of ( the HBO series ) Westworld so she couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be with us . But she&amp;rsquo ; s a gigantic Bowie fan . I&amp;rsquo ; ve recorded things with her , just myself on piano and her on voice . She loves David , she loves rock &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; roll and she can really put over a song . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What are her go-to tracks ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; She likes Moonage Daydream , she likes Rock &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; Roll Suicide . We did some esoteric stuff last year , like Slip Away ( from 2002&amp;rsquo ; s Heathen ) , which we recorded in my studio . She knows a lot of the music . She really grew up with it . She has the symbol from the Aladdin Sane album on her thigh , she had that done when she was 13. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Why did you decide to do these two albums in particular ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; Normally I just do hits and deep covers . This is the first year where I&amp;rsquo ; m doing a concept &amp;mdash ; Diamond Dogs for the first part and Ziggy for the second part . I chose Diamond Dogs because it never got its due as a complete album . Some of the songs have never been sung , even with David . I was in the studio with him when we recorded it in 1974 at Olympic Studio , but some of those songs never saw the light of day in performance . So doing those songs is really exciting . And with Ziggy , there are so many famous songs on there , like Suffragette City , but there are obscure ones like Soul Love and Star and It Ain&amp;rsquo ; t Easy , and they sound amazing . In the over 40 years I worked with David , he never sang those songs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What do you want people to get out of A Bowie Celebration ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; You know , what I noticed &amp;mdash ; even last night on the first show of the American tour &amp;mdash ; is that I look out there and there are three generations . There are people who saw me in &amp;lsquo ; 72 with David , and they have their children , and their children are there . And they&amp;rsquo ; re singing the words to every song . And they leave with great memories , because David was a great songwriter ; they&amp;rsquo ; re wonderful songs , they inspire people . I want them to leave not only having had a great time but that it remains in their hearts their whole life . That&amp;rsquo ; s really why I&amp;rsquo ; m doing it . We&amp;rsquo ; re paying it forward . I was sort of the closest to David , having been with him so much , and I have such respect for his music , that I feel it has to go on forever . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;13730;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;13772;TOOLONG ... for something to do ?
