NewsMusicClassical music : Discover the unsung women of Italian baroquehttp : **33;14624;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;14659;TOOLONG ... title= " Elektra Women 's Choir artistic director Morna Edmundson. " alt= " Elektra Women 's Choir artistic director Morna Edmundson. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;14695;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1227924 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Women of the Italian Baroque&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; March 7 , 7:30 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Pacific Spirit United Church &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;14725;TOOLONG : March 8 , 3 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Grosvenor Theatre , Kay Meek Arts Centre , &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;West Vancouver&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //elektra.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;elektra.ca &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Can we talk about our much overdue consideration of women composers ? Elektra Women&amp;rsquo ; s Choir offers a striking opportunity to sample music by seven composers in an impressive program with the Pacific baroque Orchestra . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;14760;TOOLONG ... title= " Alexander Weimann. " alt= " Alexander Weimann. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;14796;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1227922 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A collaboration by one of North America&amp;rsquo ; s pre-eminent women&amp;rsquo ; s voice ensembles , Elektra Women&amp;rsquo ; s Choir , guest conductor Alexander Weimann , and the authentic instrument/period performance practice musicians of the Pacific baroque Orchestra would be an event in itself . As a showcase for forgotten talents from the baroque era , it&amp;rsquo ; s something very special . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s always a whiff of affirmative action to 21st century events of this sort ; and each time all sorts of misguided objections are trotted out . High time to try to think it all through . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; First of all , there&amp;rsquo ; s the notion that if this music was any good , surely we would have heard it before . Not necessarily . Music history is fundamentally a 19th century concept . And the almost exclusively male musicologists who established the canon reflected the social attitudes of their age . They weren&amp;rsquo ; t out to deliberately exclude composers who were women ; but neither were they inclined to give women who composed much attention . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As this project amply demonstrates , lots of women were active in the baroque era . Many of the composers on the Elektra/PBO program worked in convents , unsung except in their particular communities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even a cursory contemplation of the seven life stories represented on the program gives us much to consider . Most came from privileged backgrounds , and received high-quality private musical education . Given the status of Italian music making in that era , this meant access to exceptional training . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But privilege came with a price . Women from this segment of society expected to be married off , complete with dowry . If an acceptable match could not be made , life in a nunnery was seen as an acceptable option , religious vocation or not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Convent life for those with musical aptitude and compositional talent had perks : ready performance opportunities &amp;mdash ; at least within their communities &amp;mdash ; and , presumably , some free time to create . Plus their music was often preserved in convent libraries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The idea of career building in any modern sense was not remotely an option . Even so , most of the women to be heard on the program did publish music , which presupposed professional stature and a measure of general interest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At this moment in time we are very much in the early stages of a more inclusive rewrite of music history . To begin with , treasures had to be rooted out and modern performing editions created . Much of that work has been done in recent decades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Next come projects like the Elektra/PBO collaboration : informed modern performers need to learn and to program these forgotten works . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last and most significantly , contemporary audiences need to hear the pieces . As we find out what we&amp;rsquo ; ve missed out on , we can then distinguish the exceptional from the remarkable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m going to bet that with Alexander Weimann&amp;rsquo ; s instinct for real quality and Elektra&amp;rsquo ; s artistic director Morna Edmundson&amp;rsquo ; s rigorous performing standards , Women Composers of the Italian baroque should win passionate advocates for these forgotten women of the 17th and 18th centuries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It just a shame we&amp;rsquo ; ve all had to wait so long . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;14826;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;14868;TOOLONG ... about classical **26;14904;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;14932;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? His 12th solo album , Ordinary Man , has topped the U.S. iTunes rock chart , hit the top 10 on the Billboard album chart and is on its way to being his highest charting solo release in the U.K. ever . The Andrew Watt-produced album follows on a number of very well-received singles &amp;mdash ; Under the Graveyard , Straight to Hell , Ordinary Man ( f . The truth is , that is less than five per cent of the audience , which is mixed of all backgrounds . I think K-Pop is something that sucks people in because it&amp;rsquo ; s open . I can do pop , EDM , rock , R&amp;amp ; B and it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t matter , K-Pop embraces them all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Plus , you crank the performance aspect up a lot do n't you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;16724;TOOLONG : There was a point when dancing to music became cheesy after the boy band era of NSync and Backstreet Boys , but there were always those who craved that kind of visual satisfaction . K-Pop really filled that void , because it&amp;rsquo ; s so geared to spectacle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you think you have paved the way to build a global career from your K-Pop position ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;A : &lt;/strong&gt; It hasn&amp;rsquo ; t really happened unless you are talking BTS &amp;mdash ; and they can do anything they want to because they are so big . For a solo singer/songwriter like me , it&amp;rsquo ; s new . But I have done a lot of collaborating with acts like Solange , Timbaland and others and made a point to mix English into my Korean songs . Yes , the new album was a risk , but I enjoy a challenge and pushing boundaries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;16756;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;16791;TOOLONG &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;16827;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;16869;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Promo shot for Miss Anthropocene release . 2020 PNG Merlin Archive " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17247;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1219584 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Miss Anthropocene&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **35;17277;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt;Grimes Creative Corporation/Crystal Math Music&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; In only a decade , Grimes ( a.k.a . Vancouver-born and raised Claire Boucher ) has gone from the eerie DYI of 2010&amp;rsquo ; s Halifaxa to 2012&amp;rsquo ; s confident and expansive critically acclaimed Visions right up to the wildly ambitious and successful sounds of 2015&amp;rsquo ; s Art Angels . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now Miss Anthropocene arrives at a time when Grimes is as much a global brand for her romantic affiliation with Elon Musk and shrewd manipulation of social media platforms as for her music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her fifth album is either a concept album about anthropomorphizing climate change into an evil entity , or another delightfully damming confusion of sounds and statements from an artist who is &amp;ldquo ; putting out her final earth album this year . &amp;rdquo ; This may very well be because she is fed up with all the attention being paid to her amorous adventures rather than her adventurous art . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spoiler alert : Repeated listenings won&amp;rsquo ; t divulge any grand statements about impending global chaos , save for the advice to gleefully &amp;ldquo ; f&amp;ndash ; k the world . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However the 11 tracks ( or 15 on the superior deluxe edition of the album ) are philosophically assembled , Miss Anthropocene lands as one of the first big releases of this decade and certainly one of 2020&amp;rsquo ; s most-anticipated records . Here are five things to know about it : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 . So Heavy I Fell Through the Earth&lt;/strong&gt; . A booming bass line haunts the back of the mix while leaden drums pound out echoing patterns until a vocal bursts forth to lets us all know what Enya huffing helium would sound like . The layers keep on stacking onto the six-minute song , until the lightest thing about it is Grimes repeating the tune&amp;rsquo ; s title . The sudden 360 turnaround at the 4:30 mark is quite brilliant , as she apparently falls clean through the planet and its gravity to float in some ambient expanse . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 . Violence ( with io ) &lt;/strong&gt; . This uptempo electro banger is one of the most straightforward songs on the record . But with lyrics such as You wan na make me bad , make me bad/ ( And I like it like that , and I like it like that ) , it turns the coquettish pop cluttering up the radio into something far darker and disturbing . Fans will be reading into the juxtaposing of violence , pain , partying and more as some kind of commentary on her relationship . Or Grimes is just eviscerating everyone&amp;rsquo ; s expectations in public . The video is well worth a peek. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;17314;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;17350;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 . New Gods . &lt;/strong&gt; Even someone used to making sense of the words on extreme black metal recordings could have trouble translating what Grimes is actually saying . Her voice is so often mutated past the point of comprehension , or pinging around the vast echoing background as it does in this song , that you are hard-pressed to pry any kind of meaning out of the music . Which works for a project that is meant to be both ethereal and personal . The mood is as , or more , important than the meaning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 . You 'll miss me when I 'm not around&lt;/strong&gt; . From not-fully-realized drum and bass tracks ( 4&amp;AElig ; M ) to the weirdly Taylor Swift-ish acoustic strumming in Delete Forever , the album mixes somewhat experimental approaches with mainstream songcraft . Nowhere is this more realized than in the full-on dance-rock of this hooky track . The heavy guitars coupled with the blasts of mega-manipulated vocal harmonies make this a likely single . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 . We Appreciate Power&lt;/strong&gt; . Available on the deluxe version of the album , this earlier collaboration with Hana came complete with press statements that it was influenced by everything from pro-A.I. pop bands to ideas of transhumanist desire . OK computer . What is clear is that the song&amp;rsquo ; s title is an accurate reflection of the artist&amp;rsquo ; s being . It&amp;rsquo ; s the kind of hard industrial rock track you might expect from Nine Inch Nails , but with a goofball spoken-word bit that could rival Madonna&amp;rsquo ; s bad rapping in Vogue . In other words , it&amp;rsquo ; s more fun than scary . The other remixes on the deluxe edition are of varying quality , with the Algorithm mix of IDORU particularly good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Also out this week : &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;17386;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;17422;TOOLONG &lt;h3&gt;Agnes Obel&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Myopia &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Universal Music Canada&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At some point , Obel&amp;rsquo ; s classical orientation is going to have to take shape in an opera . Here&amp;rsquo ; s your chance to prove it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spring applications are now being accepted for Granville Island&amp;rsquo ; s 2020-2021 busking program and you&amp;rsquo ; ll need to know more than just the chords to Wonderwall or that Green Day song . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , if you&amp;rsquo ; re a busker performing three days or more per week , you&amp;rsquo ; ll need to have at least three hours of repertoire on hand , with no song being played more than once in a set , among other requirements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Claire Diamond is the program coordinator for Granville Island&amp;rsquo ; s busking program and says there are about 150 applications each year , which is why specific requirements have been put in place to help whittle down the often overwhelming stack of resumes , as coordinators search for that elusive star quality to add to the Granville Island mix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They&amp;rsquo ; ve got something extra special that they bring to it , &amp;rdquo ; said Diamond , of what makes a performer stand out from a sea of aspiring guitarists , entertainers , and magicians. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s having that kind of persona and kind of engagement with people and being versatile and being able to be responsive to different groups , whether that be a school group visiting or local regulars , and engaging with people beyond just the music , the personality side of it as well . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The program was created to manage the myriad of busking opportunities on Granville Island , which draws some 10.5 million visitors annually from both near and far . Applicants must fill out an application and submit a video audition ; only applicants who meet the requirements and pass an invite-only live audition each year are issued a busking license , which permits the busker to perform at designated locations throughout the island . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In previous years , acts have ranged from musicians and performers of all genres and ages &amp;ndash ; including one busker , &lt;a href= " https : **33;19294;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Eugene Dudding&lt;/a&gt; , who last year&amp;nbsp ; celebrated 30 years of busking as an acoustic guitarist . That&amp;rsquo ; s not obligatory but it just gives us a better image as to how you work with an audience , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Don&amp;rsquo ; t get me wrong , we still have the odd living room video . At seven , she had penned a short opera based upon author Neil Gaiman&amp;rsquo ; s short story the Sweeper of dreams . Three years later , she produced Cinderella . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By that time , the world had taken notice of the confident young artist&amp;rsquo ; s prodigious talents , with many in the press dubbing her &amp;ldquo ; the next Mozart . &amp;rdquo ; Unwilling to wear that title , and noting that there already was a Mozart , the artist has gone on record stating she would prefer to be recognized for who she is : Alma. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Vienna is an incredibly inspiring place to grow up , it is really the city of music , &amp;rdquo ; said Deutscher , over the phone from her home in Austria . &amp;ldquo ; When I go to the vineyards with the amazing view of the city to skip around in the nature , or when I&amp;rsquo ; m sitting in the underground , I&amp;rsquo ; m constantly getting ideas . Also , having lived here awhile , I&amp;rsquo ; ve also composed a few Viennese waltzes. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These waltzes will almost certainly be imbued with the light and feathery touch that characterize the era when the House of Habsburg ruled the region . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critics writing about Deutscher&amp;rsquo ; s work have lit upon how it is very focused on melody , running counter to many of the atonal and arrhythmic facets of contemporary classical music . This somewhat tiresome argument bred in an academic circles that contemporary music must be ugly and dissonant to reflect these qualities in the world doesn&amp;rsquo ; t impress Alma. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her lush , symphonic music defies the critics . They certainly can&amp;rsquo ; t accuse her of failing to find inspiration in those same mechanics and technology of everyday life . Her recently composed Siren Sounds Waltz is informed by exactly what modernists say music should embrace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It just happens to be melodic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Viennese police siren is made in fourths&amp;nbsp ; and doesn&amp;rsquo ; t wail like most do in other places , so I decided to make it into a melody , &amp;rdquo ; Deutscher said . &amp;ldquo ; Then I also incorporated specific sounds such as local bus doors closing and other city noise and integrated them into a waltz . It begins very chaotically , with the orchestra playing like a street with horns and sirens , until it calms down and you enter into the imagination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;20031;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20067;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; That imaginary realm is where the &amp;ldquo ; ugly sounds of the modern world become something that is beautiful . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deutscher&amp;rsquo ; s imaginary realm is inseparable from her musical output . She has conceived a land she calls Transylvanian &amp;mdash ; never having been to Transylvania , she says she has no idea how that name entered her head &amp;mdash ; which is where she hears beautiful melodies that wind-up in finished works . These are often written by various uniquely-named composers in the land , such as Antonin Yellowsink. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All the composers in my imaginary country write a little bit differently , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Antonin is quite a melancholy character who writes sad melodies . Sometimes , when I&amp;rsquo ; m stuck in my compositions and don&amp;rsquo ; t know what to do , I show them to him and he often makes very good suggestions . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The strong female characters in her operas undergo adventures in Transylvanian too . Deutscher has always loved stories about girls who overcame difficulty through their talents and their determination . Due to this , she populates her works with them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s what I like , and it is also is a way for me to address how , in the past , there were talented female musicians who were denied the right to compose and have their works performed , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; That really made me rather quite angry . When I write a piece , working hard to develop the melodies into a something that makes senses , with a structure that makes sense ; I think of them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The more the interview continues , the more it becomes clear why Alma has enchanted everyone from Zubin Mehta to some of the classical music world&amp;rsquo ; s toughest critics and beloved British presenter Stephen Fry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her love of music is absolute , and completely impossible to separate from any other facet of her life . This artist was finding ways to note down the melodies that apparently come into her head constantly when she was six years-old and had no formal musical training to speak of . Her ongoing studying has , in large part , been about developing better techniques to transition what she hears to sheet music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deutscher went on the record at age 10 stating that she understood how it might be hard for some to take her music seriously because of her years . The 15 year-old on the other end of the line exudes a professional confidence coupled with youthful energy that begs the question : How far can it go ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m always composing , but it&amp;rsquo ; s a very hard and time-consuming process , taking those melodies that are constantly coming and organizing them , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; And for pieces such as the piano concerto I&amp;rsquo ; m doing in Vancouver , which I wrote when I was 12 , I am always doing little fixes and changes . I re-orchestrated almost the whole concerti to put in a big brass section , because I&amp;rsquo ; ve always wanted it to have a big crashing section that&amp;rsquo ; s really loud , and never felt that it worked quite right . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She says that the piano concerto holds a particular place in her heart , because she wrote a good deal of it on her grandmother&amp;rsquo ; s piano after she passed on . She says that it&amp;rsquo ; s one of the saddest things she has written , surprising to people who know what an incredibly happy person she is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So what does she do besides music ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I love ballroom dancing , and Vienna is a perfect place for that , and it&amp;rsquo ; s become a serious passion , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &amp;ldquo ; Twice a week , I get to go and learn the most amazing dances , and I&amp;rsquo ; m going to go to lots of balls this coming season with my dresses already picked out . And I also love the theatre . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alma Deutscher will play three performances with the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra under composer Stanley Dodds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " sderdeyn@postmedia.com " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;20103;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;20141;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;20170;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynFri , 21 Feb 2020 19:00:30 **45;20201;TOOLONG ... announcement : The Weeknd opens new world tour in Vancouverhttp : **31;20248;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20281;TOOLONG ... title= " The Weeknd play at the end of the H&amp;amp ; M STUDIO SS17 Spring-Summer 2017 ready-to-wear collection fashion show on March 1 , 2017 in Paris . Baker keeps dad Ginger 's beat alive with The Music of Creamhttp : **35;20733;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20770;TOOLONG ... title= " Kofi Baker , drummer , son of the late Ginger Baker and one of the forces behind The Music of Cream . " alt= " Kofi Baker , drummer , son of the late Ginger Baker and one of the forces behind The Music of Cream . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;20806;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1219583 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;The Music Of Cream : 50th Anniversary World Tour featuring Disraeli Gears&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;20836;TOOLONG : Sat . Feb. 29 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;20871;TOOLONG : Rickshaw Theatre , 254 E. Hastings St. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info&lt;/strong&gt; : From $25 at &lt;a href= " https : **33;20907;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **27;20942;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a band that was together only slightly more than two years ( 1966 to 1968 ) , Cream certainly left a legacy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The trio of drummer Ginger Baker , bassist/vocalist Jack Bruce and guitarist/vocalist Eric Clapton were the ultimate late-&amp;rsquo ; 60s power trio , responsible for taking the blues rock of the day into amplified zones of proto-heavy metal and jam band excess . Along the way , the group became the first supergroup to come out of the British Invasion . Each of the three musicians had served time in other popular bands of the day such as the Graham Bond Organization ( Baker , Bruce ) , the Yardbirds ( Clapton ) and John Mayall&amp;rsquo ; s Bluesbreakers ( Clapton , Bruce ) before coming together to form the far more popular trio . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the course of four studio albums and one live disc , the band produced such classic rock radio fixtures as Sunshine of Your Love , I Feel Free and Badge . Clapton went on to become an AOR legend . Baker and Bruce never attained near the same level of success again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , any music fan out there should check out Baker&amp;rsquo ; s excellent Air Force albums as well as 1990&amp;rsquo ; s Middle Passage . Ditto for Bruce&amp;rsquo ; s post-Cream output such as 1993s Somethin&amp;rsquo ; Else or his work with NYC underground composer Kip Hanrahan ( 1985&amp;rsquo ; s Vertical&amp;rsquo ; s Currency ; 1988&amp;rsquo ; s Days and Nights of Blue Luck Inverted ) . Bruce died in 2014 at age 71 , and Baker died last October at age 80. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Keeping the late player&amp;rsquo ; s music alive is the reason behind &lt;a href= " https : //www.musicofcream.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The Music of Cream&lt;/a&gt; . Not only does the band include Eric Clapton&amp;rsquo ; s nephew , Will Johns &amp;mdash ; the son of Led Zeppelin and Rolling Stones sound engineer Andy Johns &amp;mdash ; on guitar and vocals , but its beat is held down by Kofi Baker , Ginger&amp;rsquo ; s son . Musicians Sean McNabb and Chris Shutters round out the group , proving that it takes more than three musicians to recreate that distinctive Cream sound . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group is touring in memoriam to Baker , who died Oct. 6 , playing Cream&amp;rsquo ; s landmark 1967 second album , Disraeli Gears , in its entirety . Considered by many critics to be the best thing the band ever recorded , the album includes songs such as Sunshine of Your Love , Strange Brew , Tales of Brave Ulysses and more . The Music of Cream performs the entire album and rounds out the set with a selection of other material , including &amp;ldquo ; Clapton Classics&amp;rdquo ; such as Cocaine , Layla and Wonderful Tonight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kofi Baker chatted to Postmedia prior to the tour starting from his home in Chicago . The drummer , who has worked with such luminaries as jazz bassist Jonas Hellborg , started The Music of Cream following the original band&amp;rsquo ; s 2005 reunion show . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Postmedia : Obviously , you have a direct family connection to the music of Cream . But what made you decide that this project needed to happen at the time that you launched it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Kofi Baker&lt;/strong&gt; : I went to the Madison Square Garden show in 2006 when the band reformed and , at that time , I was doing mainly fusion jazz and hadn&amp;rsquo ; t really considered playing Cream music . But after the gig , my dad was saying he&amp;rsquo ; d never play with Jack again , had all the money he needed and that was that . So I decided to play it because people had always asked me to , it looked like a lot of fun and there was plenty of opportunity for improvisation and what I liked in music . Obviously , after my dad passed on , it took on a different feel as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Your press suggests that this project has experienced something of a similar up and down ride as that of the original band did ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;20971;TOOLONG : Oh yeah , every time things started to take hold , someone else came along with an idea that wrecked it and destroyed it and we had to regroup once again . One of the worst suggestions was having Malcolm ( Bruce , Jack&amp;rsquo ; s son ) join the band and being billed as the &amp;ldquo ; Sons of Cream . &amp;rdquo ; Unfortunately , Malcolm doesn&amp;rsquo ; t know any Cream songs , doesn&amp;rsquo ; t like playing them and he&amp;rsquo ; s not really a bass player . So that never worked and now he is out and we have much better musicians , a real bass player and it&amp;rsquo ; s a much better project . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;21003;TOOLONG ... title= " The band Cream in 1968 , its psychedelic heyday : Drummer Ginger Baker , guitarist Eric Clapton and bassist Jack Bruce ( left to right ) . " alt= " The band Cream in 1968 , its psychedelic heyday : Drummer Ginger Baker , guitarist Eric Clapton and bassist Jack Bruce ( left to right ) . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout/Postmedia News files " **28;21039;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1220038 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : So it takes four of you to do what the three of them did ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;21069;TOOLONG : Not at all , we just like to have the option of the larger band for the Clapton classics such as Layla and to flesh out the songs by Blind Faith and so on . Even Eric never plays Cream songs as a trio anymore , as he says he likes the larger sound . I&amp;rsquo ; m more of a full drummer than my dad , coming from the busier fusion side of things , so I tend to the more high-energy attack that Cream played with in the &amp;rsquo ; 60s than that super clean , stripped-down style that they brought to the material in the reunion . It was great , but it was kind of laid back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You 've played professionally since you were 17 , starting off with Steve Marriott ( Small Faces , Humble Pie ) and in groups with everyone from the late guitar genius Shawn Lane to Megadeth spin-offs . What did your father think of your work ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;21101;TOOLONG : Well , obviously he was there at the start teaching me things . But the last 10 years of his life , a man who was never that easy to deal with , had become someone we thought was so much worse . We were completely estranged . But when I went to see him in hospital , I came to realize that it was his wife who was really the reason that he wasn&amp;rsquo ; t communicating with the rest of the family , making him write us out of his will and so on . None of us was even invited to the funeral until the last minute , so most of us couldn&amp;rsquo ; t make it . But I knew that was all because of her , which makes it better . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : All the more reason to have this project take shape and keep the family legacy going . Are there any songs that you find really stand out for you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;21133;TOOLONG : It&amp;rsquo ; s interesting , because I like pretty much all of it . White Room and Tales are kind of the same song , and Badge is pretty straight-ahead pop . But the rest is unique , falling somewhere in between jam bands , heavy metal and even aspects of fusion . To my hearing , no one seems to have done that since with both that level of musicianship as well as keeping it heavy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;21165;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;21200;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;21236;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;21267;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;21305;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;21334;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;21365;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;21407;TOOLONG ... From the moment the curtain rises &amp;mdash ; after , for once , an overture played as an overture with no superfluous stage action &amp;mdash ; we are presented with an environment that signals &amp;ldquo ; Comedy Tonight ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ken MacDonald&amp;rsquo ; s set is gloriously daffy but sophisticated . Her approach is inventive and loaded with details , both broad and fine , that should have served the production well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Barber&amp;rsquo ; s big numbers are democratically handed out to a generally strong ensemble cast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As Count Almaviva , Victoria tenor Isaiah Bell was uneven . Baritone Taehyun Jun was delightful in the role of Don Basilio , vocally first rate and entirely prepared to enter into the comic spirit of his part and the production . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lyric baritone Edward Nelson made a very fine Figaro indeed , a congenital schemer who&amp;rsquo ; s always a step , or three , ahead of everyone else . Confident yet not bombastic , Nelson makes it clear that Figaro is well aware that clever counts for only so much in a world of privilege and power . And he was able to sail through all the nimble moves demanded by Corcoran with ease . He was a joy to watch every second he was on the stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;21908;TOOLONG ... title= " California baritone Edward Nelson sings Figaro in Vancouver Opera 's Barber of Seville . " alt= " California baritone Edward Nelson sings Figaro in Vancouver Opera 's Barber of Seville . It&amp;rsquo ; s all about timing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadian conductor Nathan Brock , back in this country after stints in Europe , flattered his singers and rarely pushed his orchestra out of its comfort zones . This wasn&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily a problem in arias and ensemble pieces , but in the copious recitatives that drive the story , an overriding desire for vocal beauty was at odds with pacing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Comfort also killed the comedy . ( Do we really need a whiff of Wagner&amp;rsquo ; s Treulich gef&amp;uuml ; hrt in the fortepiano to underscore an impending marriage ? How to Dress Well ) and the title track . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Greene was clearly an artist who could expand the sonic range of dance music to include emotion and introspection more commonly sourced in soul and urban pop . But he never lost the train of thought that says keep the party bumping . His latest release , Dawn Chorus , is an equally engaging and emotional collection loaded with guests and collaborators ranging from Lost in Translation film composer Brian Reitzell to rapper Cadence Weapon and ambient vocalist Julianna Barwick. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a big leap in arrangements , production and pulse for the artist , who has moved from expertise in cutting and pasting collages of samples to working from a live musician base to reconfigure into something new . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Green took time to chat from his Toronto studio prior to heading across Europe and North America on tour , noting that new material such as Serenity was &amp;ldquo ; pulling off the magic trick&amp;rdquo ; of keeping audiences entranced. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;22559;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;22595;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : I 've read about five different reviews of Dawn Chorus , and each talks about how you have " updated " house music . Why is that , and has house become the heavy metal of electronic music , that just never goes away ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;22631;TOOLONG : At this point house music can be more of a catch-all word for any and all dance music that isn&amp;rsquo ; t grim or very minimal and cold sounding . Along with acid house , which is still around as well , it&amp;rsquo ; s a type of updated disco and it keeps coming back around . When done right , it&amp;rsquo ; s grooves in pockets with nice melodies that are fun . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : It 's also the electronic music genre that lends itself best to the formation of actual songs rather than just tracks , is n't it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;22663;TOOLONG : Yep , the most exciting house music is when it hovers between song and track in its complexity . A classic Chez Damier or Little Louie gives you a little more than just a bass line and a rimshot pattern . My ear is drawn to things with a few more of those elements of melody and hints of structure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Besides composing your own original material , you have a lengthy resum ? remixing artists ranging from Radiohead to Ciara and others . What makes a great remix in your mind ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;22695;TOOLONG : I think you need to study the parts of the original as hard as you can and focus in on one section that you really hook on , like the way the vocal sounds in the pre-chorus break , or something . Not that it has to be one eight-second loop , but more that one section that you can extend and expand upon until it really catches your ear and almost trying to drive someone insane with it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Dawn Chorus is a different thing from what you just described , involving a lot more input from musicians and singers . Do you think that recording at Hudson Mohawke 's L.A. studio got under your skin and inspired some of these changes , bringing kind of an L.A. vibe ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;22727;TOOLONG : Yeah , that place is infectious and gets right under your skin . Part of the genesis of the album was , how could I use the tools &amp;mdash ; drum machines and such &amp;mdash ; that belong to the culture of the genre , but make it so if you were blindfolded and listened , you might file it under alternative pop rather than dance music . I wrote the album in my 29th year ; now I&amp;rsquo ; m 30 and not a young gun anymore , but still working in a hedonistic , youth-obsessed ecosystem . What music would make me comfortable where I&amp;rsquo ; m at now ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : A very sizable demographic that came of age in the ' 90s with the explosion of electronic music and raves is in that same place you describe now . Unlike classic rock , where you can play your hits from a walker , electronic music has never been about staying in the same place . Do you think you are paving the way for where the music can be for changing tastes ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;22759;TOOLONG : There are definitely veterans that are resting on their laurels in dance music too , but that&amp;rsquo ; s not where I&amp;rsquo ; m at . Since 2014 , I&amp;rsquo ; ve been really invested in using a lot of visuals in my sets , but trying to avoid the massive projections and LED lights that can be somewhat distracting and take you out of the experience . So I&amp;rsquo ; ve been developing my lighting set with a designer from Glasgow named Shaun Murphy to take almost standard club lighting and turn it into something new that keeps the black space there too . NewsMusicClassical music : Maria Callas hologram to perform with Vancouver Symphony Orchestrahttp : **31;23576;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;23609;TOOLONG ... title= " The one , the only Maria Callas. " alt= " The one , the only Maria Callas. " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;23645;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1215842 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Callas In Concert -- The Hologram Tour&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When : &lt;/strong&gt; Feb. 22 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Orpheum Theatre &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Info and tickets : &lt;/strong&gt; From $40 at &lt;a href= " https : **33;23675;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;23710;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nostalgia meets state-of-the-art 21st century technology in a surprising new initiative at the Vancouver Symphony : a program focused on that most 20th century of divas , Maria Callas. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not just a tribute concert , nor a program of great hits from her characteristic repertoire . This is a technological evocation of Callas in holographic form , a ghost in the machine , mounted by production company BASE Hologram. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23742;TOOLONG ... title= " Maria Callas in 1968 " alt= " Maria Callas in 1968 " data-portal-copyright= " ALFREDO MICCOLI " **28;23778;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1218452 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hologram shows devoted to dead performing artists have been around for a while . Events built around Frank Zappa , Buddy Holly , and Roy Orbison have done well at the box office , despite some audience pushback over the ethics involved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it&amp;rsquo ; s a startling idea to build a show around an operatic diva . And what greater opera legend is there than Maria Callas ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born Maria Anna Cecilia Sofia Kalogeropoulos in Manhattan in 1923 , Callas was educated in Athens , then began singing professionally in 1941 . At first she sang almost everything , even Wagner . But , under the watchful eye of Italian industrialist ( and Callas&amp;rsquo ; first husband ) Giovanni Battista Meneghini , and mentored by conductor Tullio Serafin , she reinvented herself as a bel canto specialist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was always controversial , always in the news . But she was remarkable . In her prime , her acting style was as inimitable as her voice . The late Alan Aberbach , founder of Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Opera Club , told me about seeing all of her Met performances as Tosca one season . Each was memorable , but on one particular evening the stars aligned and Aberbach witnessed the opera performance of a lifetime as Callas took extraordinary risks and triumphed utterly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23808;TOOLONG ... title= " Maria Callas performing in Vincenzo Bellini 's Norma in Paris in 1964. " alt= " Maria Callas performing in Vincenzo Bellini 's Norma in Paris in 1964. " data-portal-copyright= " - " **28;23844;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1218456 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her private life &amp;mdash ; not that someone as newsworthy as Callas could ever be private &amp;mdash ; could be the grist for a fine opera libretto : she left Meneghini to become the mistress of Aristotle Onassis from 1959 until 1968. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then Onassis married Jacqueline Kennedy . A humiliated Callas tried film acting , then teaching ; her sessions at Juilliard became the subject of Terrence McNally&amp;rsquo ; s play Master Class . There was a profitable comeback tour ( including a March 1974 date at the Queen Elizabeth Theatre ) , but the glory days were over . She died in Paris in 1977 , aged just 53. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Talking with the VSO&amp;rsquo ; s Neil Middleton , I got a tangible sense of the orchestra bravely attempting something far outside the usual concert model . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; BASE Hologram developed the Callas show to get into the classical world with an iconic artist , and approached the orchestra . The logistics are sophisticated , explains Middleton . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a little bit magical : proprietary technology from the company uses multiple projectors to create a 3-D image of Callas standing on the stage . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Recordings of the singer are used ; her vocal part is extracted and played back while the orchestra performs live , similar to the VSO strategy for its wildly successful movie nights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;23874;TOOLONG ... title= " Irish conductor and composer E ? mear Noone . " alt= " Irish conductor and composer E ? mear Noone . " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;23910;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1215841 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; This demands a conductor perfectly comfortable not just with tailoring an orchestral accompaniment , but also a specialist not spooked by technology . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Middleton believes the project has just the right fit with Irish conductor and composer E&amp;iacute ; mear Noone , who crafted soundtracks for video games like Overwatch and World Of Warcraft , and recently received accolades for being the first woman to conduct the orchestra at the Oscar&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While the VSO is chuffed to debut the Canadian presentation of a classical holographic project , trying out new technology is a complicated endeavour with more than a few risks involved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To assure everyone in the audience gets the best possible experience , some Orpheum seats will be off limits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Seats have to be limited because the hologram is not perfectly visible from every point in the theatre , &amp;rdquo ; says Middleton . &amp;ldquo ; This is definitely a suspense of disbelief proposition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a chance for my generation to discover an rare talent in the only way still possible &amp;mdash ; to experience what made Callas such an iconic figure . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;23940;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;23982;TOOLONG ... about the VSO&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;24018;TOOLONG ... about classical **26;24054;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;24082;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? The FOC has planned an ambitious end to its 72nd season : the Tak&amp;aacute ; cs Quartet playing all six Bart&amp;oacute ; k quartets over two evenings , April 26 and 28. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Pavel Hass Quartet will be heard March 8 in a program featuring quartets by Cekovsk&amp;aacute ; and Tchaikovsky , plus a quintet including pianist Boris Giltberg . Giltberg made his Vancouver debut in 2011 , and you can be sure that his passionate playing will be welcome in Dvor&amp;aacute ; k&amp;rsquo ; s 1887 Piano Quintet. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And there&amp;rsquo ; s some new music as well with a performance &amp;mdash ; surely a Vancouver first &amp;mdash ; of A Midsummer Quartet ( 2016 ) by Lubica Cekovsk&amp;aacute ; . Born in 1975 , the Slovakian composer studied at London&amp;rsquo ; s Royal Academy of Music and created quite a stir with her operatic treatment of The Picture of Dorian Gray . She also did the music for the 2016 computer game The Mandate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Vancouver Recital Society hosts string quartets less frequently , but when founder Leila Getz finds a group she admires , you can be sure that Vancouver audiences will hear them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Doric Quartet returns to town on Feb. 16 to play quartets by Dvorak and Sibelius , plus a new composition &amp;mdash ; the Canadian premiere of Mark-Andr&amp;eacute ; Hamelin&amp;rsquo ; s Piano Quintet , with the composer at the keyboard . Hamelin is well known to Vancouver as a piano virtuoso as &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;VRS audiences know him as a composer from his demonically difficult Toccata on L'homme arm ? and a short curtain-raiser commissioned for the its 40th anniversary . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; VRS brokers the Vancouver debut of the Schumann Quartet on March 1 as brothers Mark , Eric and Ken Schumann include violist Liisa Randalu in their family enterprise . The young quartet captured the 2016 Newcomer Award at the BBC Music Magazine Awards and hopes to captivate the VRS audience with Mozart&amp;rsquo ; s K. 499 &amp;ldquo ; Hoffmeister&amp;rdquo ; Quartet , Mendelssohn&amp;rsquo ; s Quartet in E minor , Op. 44 , No. 2 , and Shostakovich&amp;rsquo ; s intense Ninth Quartet ( 1964 ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The programming of these three ensembles defines how chamber music ensembles are adapting for today&amp;rsquo ; s audiences . The Doric and Pavel Hass groups both seek to expand their range through the addition of guest artists and the inclusion of very recent work , belying the notion that chamber music audiences are stuck in the past . The Schumann ensemble is still establishing its reputation and wants to be heard in classics but , as younger performers , they consider the mid-century work of Shostakovich as &amp;ldquo ; classic&amp;rdquo ; as Mozart or Mendelssohn. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , there&amp;rsquo ; s a special quartet project at the end of March . Though local fans associate chamber music with the Vancouver Playhouse , presenters are always on the lookout for new spaces that are attractive , accessible , and acoustically good . On a golden day last fall a little delegation made a visit to the beautifully renovated Congregation Beth Israel synagogue on Oak Street . It didn&amp;rsquo ; t take long to confirm that this could be a wonderful new space for music as well as worship . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then it turned out that the Jerusalem Quartet , who have a long-standing invitation to town from the VRS &amp;mdash ; and who will be essaying all of the Beethoven string quartets in the fall &amp;mdash ; were coincidentally on the West Coast . Fresh Laundry , Rings A Bell , Regulars , Love Me Wrong and Devil I Know all hone in on different aspects of her soprano range and the buzz around the release is building . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are five things to know about the album : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 : Fresh Laundry&lt;/strong&gt; . With its big booming beat , spooky vocal and splashy keyboard hook , the opening tune to the 12 track record is a strong intro . The way the song builds to the point where the singer proclaims &amp;ldquo ; something has to die , &amp;rdquo ; and then just drops off into near silence before a keyboard hook that could be from a vintage UK nineties dance pop pulses her back into action is very nice indeed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 : Sarah Come Home&lt;/strong&gt; . There is something quite addictive about this heartfelt declaration to an absent girlfriend to return to the nest . What went wrong is never made clear , but the tune dances around on a hook that wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t sound out of place on a Carly Rae Jepsen record , which is high praise . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;28866;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;28902;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 : Super Duper Party People&lt;/strong&gt; . The Donna Summer-redux synthesizer line is hard to resist , but the rap-speak lyric is tragic . Plus , does anyone really think the elementary school rhyming of lines like we&amp;rsquo ; re super duper/we&amp;rsquo ; re the party troopers/uh-huh deserves to make it to a record ? It&amp;rsquo ; s a shockingly weak track on an album with a majority of solid ones . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 : Guests&lt;/strong&gt; . Troye Sivan turns up on the bluesy ballad Love Me Wrong to wax romantically , while Mitski makes an appearance on Susie Save Your Love . This latter tune is the better of the two , with a slinky R&amp;amp ; B arrangement complete with a distorted guitar solo that sounds like it was recorded in a tin can . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Learning in Public&lt;/strong&gt; . The album closer shuffles out on a songs loaded with back up vocals , doo doo do do do&amp;rsquo ; s , a simple handclap and snare beat and reverberant piano plinks . It&amp;rsquo ; s both sparse and lush at the same time , which is a pretty brilliant production trick . Of course , the sound of the entire album is always pristine and carefully constructed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Allie X , March 27 , 8 p.m . Venue , 881 Granville . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;29754;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206809 " /&gt; **29;29784;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; **33;29815;TOOLONG : Feb. 15 , 7 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;29850;TOOLONG : The Fox Cabaret &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets and info&lt;/strong&gt; : $18 at &lt;a href= " https : //www.livenation.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **28;29886;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Montreal electro soul singer Geoffroy lost his mother in 2017 . He doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mince his words describing the effect her death had on him . Even after a lengthy illness , it was a jarring loss for the man born Geoffroy Sauve. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To work through his grief , he set about writing an album that explored the nooks and crannies of childhood memories , adult longings and &amp;mdash ; most important &amp;mdash ; the sense of place that parents provide . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Revisiting his youth in Montreal&amp;rsquo ; s **26;29916;TOOLONG ; ce , or NDG , neighbourhood in the city&amp;rsquo ; s West End , he penned the material that makes up his new album , 1952. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The title was the year of his mother&amp;rsquo ; s birth , and many songs relate directly back to her passing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was very close to my mother , and as an only child I stayed home until I was 27 , &amp;rdquo ; said Geoffroy. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My work means I travel a lot and , when I was home , being close to my mom in her condition was important . She lived for a decade longer than was expected and that meant there was time to actually talk about death , about all the things you have on your chest , so there was luck in this bad luck . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;29944;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;29980;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The opening tune Fear of Falling Apart directly addresses personal loss . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over washes of vintage keyboards and distant echoing wooden percussion , the song outlines how hard the long demise of his mother was and its effects on him : &lt;em&gt;Got me scared of getting older / But my luck got stolen / Lost my mother to the devil , I 'll get by / But lost a part of my soul / And it feels like I 'm wandering off . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; About five or six songs on the album really are about the effects of her passing , with none as direct as the Fear of Falling Apart , &amp;rdquo ; Geoffroy said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The after-effects are there in When Everything Is Gone and Talking Low , but I didn&amp;rsquo ; t want anything to be directly evident or obvious for the listener who didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to go deeper . That&amp;rsquo ; s why I liked the name 1952 ; it&amp;rsquo ; s evocative without being obvious . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The captivating cover art , designed by Montreal tattoo artist Dan Climan and based on an old photo of Geoffroy&amp;rsquo ; s mother , also manages to be beautiful and evocative without being obvious . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;30016;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30058;TOOLONG ... for something to do ? Check out our comprehensive event **29;30094;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;30125;TOOLONG ... latest music **25;30161;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finding the positive in the negative goes a long way to explaining how 1952 manages to possess a sonic stoicism and make you want to dance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That a former contestant on La Voix ( the Qu&amp;eacute ; bec franchise of The Voice TV singing competition ) would go on to make music as smart and non-obvious as what appears on 1952 is surprising . This critic would even consider the word stealthy to describe the way the songs work their way into your consciousness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Geoffroy stresses that he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t like being &amp;ldquo ; in your face&amp;rdquo ; as a person or in his music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His goal with 1952 was to grind through emotional issues and create emotionally reactive material . Judging from the reception to singles such as 21 Days or Woke Up Late , fans are hungry for more of Geoffroy&amp;rsquo ; s round , breathy vocals , classic instrumentation and tasty arrangements . 1952 features the same production teams as 2017&amp;rsquo ; s Polaris Prize long-listed debut Coastline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That album garnered over 25 million streams and established Geoffroy as a bonafide star in Quebec and in Europe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now the mix of layered percussion , jazzy guitars , cool woodwinds and plentiful analog synthesizers and keyboards that Geoffroy , Gabriel Gagnon , Cl&amp;eacute ; ment Leduc and Max Gendron have crafted is getting its &amp;ldquo ; rest of Canada&amp;rdquo ; rollout . Fans may be surprised how the sounds aren&amp;rsquo ; t generated by pushing a button . This is live music performed by live musicians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m not a computer geek and I don&amp;rsquo ; t engineer much , and I just love the warm , soft sounds that comes with using analog , &amp;rdquo ; Geoffroy said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the long way to go to get to the end product , but I think that you can hear when the results are reached with the digital shortcuts . I guess it&amp;rsquo ; s just another layer of professionalism , and I&amp;rsquo ; m a firm believer that if you are going to do it at all , do it right . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This opinion is shared by his studio collaborators . Leduc is a member of the touring band . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Having Cl&amp;eacute ; ment in the band allows us to easily export the sound we&amp;rsquo ; ve done in studio to the live arena , &amp;rdquo ; said Geoffroy. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He brings along a big station and will play the Moog , the Prophet , the bass and as many other instruments as he can to make the music full . I usually bring a skeleton with ideas of where I want it to go to the guys , and then we flesh it out in studio and determine where it&amp;rsquo ; s really going to go . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides Leduc and Geoffroy , the band for this western Canadian tour also includes a live drummer . The singer says this configuration adds so much to the sound that he can&amp;rsquo ; t imagine doing it any other way . Larger shows are fleshed out to a five piece with an additional guitarist and vocalist. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the immediate draws in the music is that while it is soft , there are layers of active percussion throughout . Given the rabid embrace of all kinds of drum-crazy styles in the Quebec electronic scene , is it safe to say that Geoffroy raved in his youth ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Not really , I&amp;rsquo ; m just a big fan of all musics and genres , drawing inspiration from African and Haitian rhythms as well as deep house and even folkies , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Most of the material starts with a traditional singer-songwriter guitar and voice approach . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Geoffroy is &amp;ldquo ; happily surprised&amp;rdquo ; to see sell-out shows in markets across Canada where he hasn&amp;rsquo ; t performed before . Even though he chooses to write in English rather than French , there are challenges for Quebec artists to break into the rest of Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many of the excellent acts that are on the Bonsound label he records for have massive followings in their home province and across the world , but they couldn&amp;rsquo ; t sell out Saskatoon , let alone Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Streams are one thing , but no one has any idea how well things are working until you are actually selling tickets and going to those places , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I can tell you that eight million streams for a new song won&amp;rsquo ; t fill my pocket , or anyone else&amp;rsquo ; s , once you split it all around . You have to tour . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Geoffroy will accept that the music on 1952 is informed by &amp;ldquo ; hard nostalgia , &amp;rdquo ; he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t agree that his music is brooding , pensive or sad . He says he&amp;rsquo ; s a happy , positive person who makes music that is ultimately intended to hit the listener in those places , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s very important to differentiate softness , or melancholy , and sadness , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; Damien Rice makes sad music . " data-portal-copyright= " Francois Nel " **28;30712;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1211520 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The iconic Janet Jackson &amp;ndash ; Miss Jackson if you&amp;rsquo ; re nasty &amp;ndash ; will bring her Black Diamond World Tour to Vancouver in August . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The tour will feature all-new production , new music from her upcoming album Black Diamond and , of course , a steady stream of greatest hits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jackson&amp;rsquo ; s outing comes as her iconic Rhythm Nation 1814 recently celebrated its 30th anniversary in September 2019. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Black Diamond tour will kick off in late June in Miami and make its way across the U.S. and Canada , with European dates to be announced at a later time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jackson , who is also the sister of late King of Pop Michael Jackson , is one of the most influential figures in pop history and dance , with two Grammy Awards , two Emmy nominations , a Golden Globe Award and an Academy Award nomination , along with dozens of American Music Awards , MTV Video Music Awards and Billboard Music Awards . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jackson will perform at Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Rogers Arena on Aug. 22 , 2020 , with tickets on sale this Thursday through &lt;a href= " https : //www.livenation.com/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;LiveNation&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " mailto:sip@postmedia.com " **31;30742;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **25;30775;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;30802;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;30835;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;30871;TOOLONG Stephanie IpMon , 10 Feb 2020 16:27:08 **45;30907;TOOLONG ... NewsMusicFive things to know about U kin B the Sun , by Frazey Fordhttp : **36;30954;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;30992;TOOLONG ... title= " Vancouver singer/songwriter Frazey Ford . " alt= " Vancouver singer/songwriter Frazey Ford . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;31028;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1200781 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;U kin B the Sun&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Frazey Ford&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Arts &amp; Crafts&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s been six years since Indian Ocean . The second album by former Be Good Tanyas singer Frazey Ford found the Vancouver-based soul/folksinger pairing her instantly recognizable voice with backing from no less than the Hi Rhythm Section , the Reverend Al Green&amp;rsquo ; s band . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a perfect fit for her unique delivery , which includes the kind of drawled diction and half-finished phrasing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like blues or R&amp;amp ; B greats , it&amp;rsquo ; s all about the feel as much as the meaning in the lyrics , although hits such as Done from Indian Ocean hit with both groove and message about having had enough of the dysfunction and violence in society . The same is true of The Kids are Having None of it on the new album , which holds out hope for the younger generation fixing the mess that is the world today . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Once again , the music is in a classic &amp;rsquo ; 70s soul vein and works its way into your brain slowly . Here are five things to know about the album : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 : Azad&lt;/strong&gt; . The opening song is proof of how less is more in the world of pop music . Rolling in on a superb bass line and simple snare and hi-hat beat , the tune slowly builds the whole way through , gaining simple organ , smooth backing vocals and then a funky-as-can-be keyboard vamp right out of Stevie Wonder&amp;rsquo ; s Superstitious . It&amp;rsquo ; s a killer first tune . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 : Money Ca n't Buy&lt;/strong&gt; . &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; ve got a life that money can&amp;rsquo ; t buy . &amp;rdquo ; Ford repeats this line repeatedly , almost chanting it , as she outlines how the subject of the song has blown it again . Presumably , this is due to hubris . But it&amp;rsquo ; s not an angry song as much as a regretful statement about someone you sense that she cares/cared about . It&amp;rsquo ; s very moody . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 : Let 's Start Again&lt;/strong&gt; . This could be the most straight-ahead , blues tinged tune Ford has ever recorded . A loving plea to do as the title declares , the song is pleading for more . But , ultimately , it ends on a descending piano scale that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t sound hopeful at all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 : The Kids are Having None of it&lt;/strong&gt; . Ford notes in the news release for the album that the album&amp;rsquo ; s songs came out in a much more direct way than her previous work , and it&amp;rsquo ; s far more direct . Nowhere is this more clear than in this single where she sounds like she is warning those in power to take notice of what the future may hold if they don&amp;rsquo ; t listen to the youth of today . The singer mentions being &amp;ldquo ; more in touch with the wholeness of anger , &amp;rdquo ; and this track certainly is. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Golden&lt;/strong&gt; . One of the most upbeat songs of the set , U kin B the Sun might have benefited from a few more like this song to shuffle up the overarching mood of resignation and melancholy that pervades the 11 tracks . Sometimes , being able to punch air and be &amp;ldquo ; happy to jump in the sea&amp;rdquo ; over a sweet guitar solo really is enough . This is sure to be an in-concert hit when Ford hits the road again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;31058;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;31094;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Also out this week : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Alabaster DePlume&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;To Cy and Lee : Instrumentals Vol. 1&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt; International Anthem&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; London-based singer/instrumentalist DePlume collects 11 instrumentals recorded over the past eight years onto one standout album . Opening with the gorgeous Visit Croatia , featuring a haunting clarinet soaring over scant piano and echoing keyboards , the album ventures into terrain as different as Song of the Foundling , which sounds like Tinariwen interpreted by avant-garde classical musicians , to Why , Buzzardman , Why , with its classical piano flourishes . An unusual , and completely rewarding , record whose only shortcoming is a bit too much tempo consistency in the writing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **33;31130;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;31165;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Last Wild Sons&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;East Side of Midnight&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;31201;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;31236;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From 1987 to 1991 Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s Last Wild Sons were regulars on the exploding roots-rock scene . Brothers Gene , Darren and Shaun ( Butch ) Murphy and buddy Al Black Davidson formed Version 1 of this band and recorded one album that saw its release and a collection of other tracks . These were consigned to the closet for a few decades , but are finally getting out there and it&amp;rsquo ; s crazy that songs such as the excellent , chiming Tell Em What I Was and title track didn&amp;rsquo ; t hit back in the day . If you like bands like the Blasters , X or Jason and the Scorchers , you will want to hear this . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;31267;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;31303;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Sons of Apollo&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;31339;TOOLONG &lt;em&gt;Inside Out Records&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Supergroups usually don&amp;rsquo ; t live up to their billing . However , the pairing of former Dream Theatre members Mike Portnoy and Derek Sherinian with Ron ( Bumblefoot ) Thal ( ex-Guns N Roses ) , Billy Sheehan ( ex-David Lee Roth ) and Jeff Scott Soto ( ex-Journey ) appears to be one that delivers the kind of progressive metal that Dream Theatre were beloved for . If you want complex-but-heavy workouts full of plenty of solos , then King of Delusion , or the nearly 16-minutes-long New World Today , won&amp;rsquo ; t disappoint . But it&amp;rsquo ; s also pretty accessible on other tracks , explaining why the album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Current Hard Rock chart . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;31374;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;31410;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tami Neilson&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Chickaboom ! &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;em&gt;Outside Music&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cover declares &amp;ldquo ; the hot rockin&amp;rsquo ; lady of country , rockabilly and soul sings &amp;hellip ; &amp;rdquo ; And she does . From the slinky opener Call Your Mama , with its constant cowbell and percussion driving home the message that the fella can go home as his days of being a useless mooch are over , to the raucous jam of Tell Me that You Love Me , Neilson lives up to her mile-high bouffant and fringe-jacket &amp;rsquo ; 50s vibe . Great production , particularly on the Everly Brothers-esque closer Sleep . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;31446;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;31481;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;31517;TOOLONG " **36;31548;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;31586;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;31615;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynFri , 07 Feb 2020 19:07:55 **45;31646;TOOLONG ... announcement : The Rolling Stones play B.C. **28;32159;TOOLONG " &gt;&lt;/sc ... &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s always a pleasure to return to North America and play for some of the biggest and best crowds in the world , &amp;rdquo ; Prices haven&amp;rsquo ; t yet been released . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fans can register for presale at &lt;a href= " https : **33;32189;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Rollingstones.com. &lt;/a&gt; ... &lt;/p&gt; Scott BrownFri , 07 Feb 2020 06:53:03 **45;32224;TOOLONG ... review : 5 things to know about Temples and Art d'Ecco at the Foxhttp : **37;32271;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;32310;TOOLONG ... title= " Temples . UK psychedelic pop band 2017 . PNG Merlin Archive " alt= " Temples . UK psychedelic pop band 2017 . PNG Merlin Archive " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;32346;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206810 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Temples and Art d'Ecco&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;32376;TOOLONG : Feb. 4 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **34;32411;TOOLONG : Fox Cabaret , 2321 Main &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kettering , UK , quartet Temples has six years of touring and recording under its belt now and it shows . The group&amp;rsquo ; s performance at the Fox Cabaret on a snowy/rainy Vancouver night was as polished and paced as the latest single Holy Horses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Adding to the buzz around the gig was the presence of rising gulf island act &lt;a href= " http : //artdeccomusic.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Art d'Ecco&lt;/a&gt; , whose album Tresspasser is an absolute joy of glammed-up swagger . Having played a number of high profile gigs such as the Squamish Music Festival , the singer and his tight backing band are really taking shape . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are five things to know about the show : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;1 : The Howl&lt;/strong&gt; . The band opened with the fourth tune from its most recent album , Hot Motion . With its fuzzed out lead riff , airy keyboards ( courtesy of rhythm guitarist Adam Smith ) and chanting vocal hook , the song is a perfect example of what the band does right . Blending classic &amp;rsquo ; 60s style psychedelic pop with some flourishes that could only come from players who lived through the Brit Pop era , the tune is a pulsing gem . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;2 : You 're Either on Something&lt;/strong&gt; . One of the best songs the band has written to date just slays live . With its chiming harmonies and rising break , it is totally suited to lead **27;32447;TOOLONG James Bagshaw&amp;rsquo ; s high voice . Straight and to the point . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;3 : Holy Horses&lt;/strong&gt; . And this could be the second best song the band has produced . It&amp;rsquo ; s like a snarling mix of Beatles and Oasis with a bouncing bass line broken up by one of the hardest rocking hooks in the group&amp;rsquo ; s repertoire . At a time when lengthy guitar jams are &amp;mdash ; fairly &amp;mdash ; consigned to the jam band heap , Temples will still take an occasional workout and let their trippy hair fly . They did a nice job on doing that on this one , with Bagshaw laying down some razor sharp leads . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;32476;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;32512;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;4 : The drums&lt;/strong&gt; . The band is on its third drummer , and they may still not have the right one . Rens Ottink did a great job keeping time and keeping it really thudding and straight-ahead . The thing is , the songs could stand a bit of breathing room that a more light touch could bring . Temples leans much more to the pop side than the rock side on a lot of the material and the four-on-the-floor pounding might be holding back the songs from soaring . Let Ottink swing a bit and see what happens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;5 : Art d'Ecco&lt;/strong&gt; . It&amp;rsquo ; s always great to see a local warm-up act really bring it . With a set of solid songs , good stage look and vibe and a really fine singing voice , d&amp;rsquo ; Ecco made Temples have to bring its A-game . Veering from glam rock to some jumpy dance pop , the sound is seductive , if not quite as outrageous as it could be . Fans are looking forward to hearing the next album . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;32548;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;32584;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;32620;TOOLONG " **36;32651;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **27;32689;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;32718;TOOLONG &l; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; Stuart DerdeynThu , 06 Feb 2020 02:05:18 **45;32749;TOOLONG ...
