We consider the relevance of this issue below . <h> DISCUSSION <h> Egyptian history and 14C offsets <p> Our findings identify and highlight the relevance of a recurring variable growing season positive 14C offset for the lower-elevation Mediterranean . This recurring phenomenon , with offset episodes variously from 13 to 31 14C years ( Fig. 2A ) , undermines the relevance of the generic midlatitude NH 14C calibration curve for high-resolution chronology in the Mediterranean and especially during these offset episodes . As an example , we may highlight and confirm the relevance of these periods of difference by comparing the time series of 14C data from the historically sequenced New Kingdom Egypt dataset ( 23 ) placed against IntCal04 versus the Hd GOR 14C record from Fig. 2A , as shown in Fig. 4A . There are several periods where the 14C dates on the Egyptian samples , in fact , appear to fit the pattern of the Mediterranean-relevant Hd GOR record much better than the IntCal04 ( 2 ) record , as well as without application of a static correction factor ( 16 , 23 ) . The dates for samples from the tomb of Tutankhamun at Thebes offer a good test case ( 23 , 24 ) . Mainstream assessments of historical sources place the time range for the accession of Tutankhamun ( the king and his court subsequently leave Amarna for Memphis early in his reign ) and his death likely in his 9th or 10th year , somewhere between 1336/1325 and 1327/1316 BCE ( 23 , 24 , 49 ) . The coherent weighted average 14C date from a set of samples ( using six of seven available dates ) from the funerary context of Tutankhamun is 3117 ? 12 14C years B.P. If we compare the intersection of these calendar and 14C ranges , we see a better fit with the Hd GOR calibration range ( Fig. 4A ) . The placement of the Tutankhamun data set rerunning the analysis in ( 24 ) against IntCal13 and comparing against IntCal04 and Hd GOR similarly shows a likely best fit versus the Hd GOR range ( Fig. 4A , inset ) . <p> Fig. 4Two example chronological ramifications from the Mediterranean 14C record and offsets indicated by the Hd GOR dataset . <p> ( A ) Egyptian date series as reported and placed against IntCal04 ( 23 ) compared with Hd GOR curve from Fig. 2A ( curves are shown as 1 SD bands , and data were plotted as 1 SD ranges of 14C ages and modeled calendar age ranges ) . Data that are almost certain to be outliers ( 23 ) have white center points . Cyan box indicates weighted average 14C ( 1 SD ) and calendar range for Tutankhamun ( Tut ) . Inset : Modeled placement 68.2 and 95.4% highest posterior density ( hpd ) of Tut against IntCal13 ( 4 ) from the OxCal model in ( 24 ) and compared with IntCal04 ( 2 ) and Hd GOR ( Fig. 2A ) . ( B ) The difference in 13th century BCE dating probability comparing the calendar age probabilities for 3035 ? 15 14C years B.P. from the Hd GOR data ( Fig. 2A ) versus IntCal13 calibration curve ( 4 ) . Data from OxCal ( 59 ) with curve resolution set to 1 year . <h> Eight apparent offset intervals for attention <p> Within our study , eight periods are noted where substantive offsets likely associated with a typical Mediterranean growing season are evident . These periods for further attention are indicated in Fig. 2A and table S2 the grand solar minimum period 750 ? 60 BCE ( 50 ) likely reflects a different process ( 15 ) . Some of these periods of reversals and plateaus in the atmospheric 14C record are moreover likely associated with climate change episodes since marked changes in 14C production and availability in the troposphere in the Holocene reflect changes in solar activity and ocean systems ( 51 , 52 ) and , thus , may sometimes be associated with periods of cultural transition . For example , the time intervals around the termination of the Late Bronze Age ( mid -- later 13th century BCE ) and during the earlier Iron Age ( 11th century BCE ) stand out as two culturally important time intervals when major transformations or reorientations in historical trajectories are often linked with climate perturbations ( 19 , 52 , 53 ) . These transitions are coeval with periods in the GOR record that are offset from the IntCal records ( Fig. 2A ) , and hence , small but potentially important revisions to chronology might be suspected and will be crucial to defining and interpreting historical narratives ( 18 , 19 , 53 ) . We give a specific example and illustration of how the calendar time range to be associated with a given 14C date can change . A hypothetical 14C date of 3035 ? 15 14C years B.P. has double the calendar probability ( 37.9% versus 18.7% ) for the critical date range between 1260 and 1200 BCE when contrasting the Hd GOR versus IntCal13 14C calibration datasets ( Fig. 4B ) . <h> Thera/Santorini eruption date <p> The earlier 16th century BCE Mediterranean offset identified above in the Hd GOR and GrM NOC datasets is particularly relevant to a long-running controversy : the dating of the Minoan eruption of the Thera ( Santorini ) volcano and associated debates around its impacts and the chronology of the beginning of the Aegean Late Bronze Age ( 13 , 19 , 54 -- 58 ) . Scholarship until now has used the various versions of the NH IntCal 14C calibration curve . Although the 16th century BCE reversal in the calibration curve has long been noted as potentially creating a dating ambiguity for the Thera eruption between the later 17th century BCE and the earlier mid -- 16th century BCE , the weight of probability has supported the older age range in the later 17th century BCE and , thus , a date over 100 year earlier than the pre-radiocarbon archaeological estimates 1500 BCE ( 57 ) . A recent contribution , seeking a compromise , is a proposal to revise the IntCal 14C calibration curve 1660 to 1540 BCE based on measurements of BCP and IrO at AA , which yield older 14C ages for this interval than IntCal13 ( 13 ) . However , the identification of a specific Mediterranean offset in the earlier 16th century BCE ( Figs. 2 , A and B , and 3A ) indicates that the correct date will not solely derive from IntCal nor do these BCP and IrO samples reflect the typical Mediterranean growing season ( see above ) . There is instead a specific Mediterranean context for this controversy . Thus , rather than ( or in addition to ) adjusting the overall IntCal calibration curve ( important although this is , in general , when justified ) , instead , it is the effect of the Mediterranean offset at this period that is relevant . In particular , as evident in Figs. 2 ( A and B ) and 3A , the Hd GOR and GrM NOC data indicate that Mediterranean 14C ages in the earlier 16th century BCE are older than the IntCal values and , thus , are potentially approximately contemporary with 14C ages for the last decades of the 17th century BCE . This could exacerbate the dating ambiguity between the later 17th century BCE and the earlier mid -- 16th century BCE . At the same time , the absence of elevated 14C ages for the Mediterranean Hd GOR and NOC samples 3600 to 3555 cal B.P. , contrary to the AA BCP and IrO dataset ( Fig. 3A ) ( 13 ) , is also important for this topic . <p> We can assess the implications and remaining uncertainties . The calibrated calendar probabilities for dating the Santorini eruption following two published methods ( 55 , 56 ) can be compared with the Hd GOR scenario . If we rerun these analyses with the Hd GOR calibration dataset ( as in Fig. 2A ) with its revision of the earlier mid -- 16th century BCE 14C values to reflect Mediterranean conditions and regional offset , we find that the results support a later 17th century BCE date range for the Thera eruption , including the entire most likely 68.2% highest posterior density ( hpd ) ranges ( Fig. 5 , A and B ; 1649 to 1617 BCE and 1680 to 1613 BCE , respectively ) . We may also reconsider the dating of the Thera olive branch sample , found buried in the Thera eruption pumice ( 58 ) , modeled as an ordered sequence of older to more recent wood to obtain a dating estimate for the outermost dated sample ( 13 , 54 ) against the Hd GOR dataset ( Fig. 5C ) . This places all the 68.2% hpd range in the 17th century BCE and most ( 76.6% versus 18.7% ) of the 95.4% hpd range at or before 1610 BCE and hence again likely indicates a later 17th century BCE date range . Thus , the Mediterranean-relevant Hd GOR dataset does not indicate the ambiguous 17th or 16th century calibrated ranges for the Thera eruption proposed in ( 13 ) from the AA BCP and IrO data . In the case of the olive branch , we may note one additional important element : The dates on the sample were run as LLGPC measurements at the Hd 14C laboratory ( 58 ) . Hence , there is no possible AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC issue in this case . Instead , we have comparable Mediterranean Hd measurements against Mediterranean Hd measurements . The finding is most likely a later 17th century BCE date range for this sample ( 19 ) . <p> ( A to C ) With Hd GOR calibration dataset in Fig. 2A . ( D and E ) Application of a hypothetical addition of +10 14C years to Hd GOR to reflect a putative AMS 14C offset to LLGPC measurements . ( F and G ) Application of a hypothetical +15 14C years . ( H and I ) Application of a hypothetical +20 14C years . ( J and K ) Application a hypothetical +25 14C years . Main hpd regions are those contiguous intervals identified within the overall 95.4% hpd ranges . <p> The remaining caveat is the issue of whether there is , in addition , a typical AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC offset that we should take into account when considering AMS 14C dates . As discussed above , the evidence is mixed . Nonetheless , consideration above of some Mediterranean AMS 14C cases suggested that perhaps an additional factor of =10 14C years might apply to the LLGPC Hd GOR dataset versus AMS 14C dates . These comparisons especially including OxA AMS 14C data are particularly relevant to the Thera case since OxA AMS 14C data , or the demonstrated very comparable Vienna ( VERA ) AMS 14C data ( 23 , 46 , 55 ) , comprise 79% and 75% of the two datasets ( 55 , 56 ) for the Thera volcanic destruction level . If we rerun the analyses in Fig. 5 ( A and B ) with an additional hypothetical +10 14C years adjustment to the Hd GOR dataset , then we do not find a substantial change ( Fig. 5 , D and E ) . The dating probabilities still continue to indicate the later 17th century BCE as the most likely date range . To effect substantive change , a putative AMS to LLGPC offset would need to be rather larger . If it were to reach around 15 14C years , then the date of the Santorini eruption starts to become more ambiguous . There is still greater probability in the later 17th century BCE , but moderate probability now lies in the earlier mid -- 16th century BCE ( Fig. 5 , F and G ) . Only if the hypothetical adjustment is 20 or 25 14C years , does the dating probability switch to indicating that an earlier mid -- 16th century BCE date range is more likely ( Fig. 5 , H to K ) . However , despite some data suggesting larger AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC differences of around this level ( 10 , 12 , 13 ) , the Mediterranean cases reviewed above only suggest a difference of about half this level ( or less ) , other comparisons are mixed , and some are even close to zero ( see above ) . Much of the current observed variation is as likely to relate to interlaboratory variations in methods and instruments an ever-present issue ( 8 , 11 , 48 ) , something only more evident as AMS 14C approaches the precision of LLGPC and LSC datasets . The conclusion at present is that more work is needed to clarify and quantify the status of any typical AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC 14C offset on comparable samples , that is , an offset that is common across multiple AMS 14C laboratories and not cases of individual interlaboratory variations ( up and down ) within an overall range of values . In the case of the Thera olive branch sample , this avoids any possible AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC issue since it was measured at Hd using LLGPC ( 58 ) . Here , comparison with the Mediterranean relevant Hd GOR dataset indicates a most likely later 17th century BCE date range ( Fig. 5C ) , which is consistent with the analysis of sets of AMS 14C data against the Hd GOR dataset ( Fig. 5 , A and B ) . This suggests the reality of an additional AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC contribution of no more than about =10 14C years , as discussed above . <p> The situation could change if future work can , to the contrary , robustly demonstrate a much larger standard AMS 14C -- to -- LLGPC offset . We also need to better define ( and enlarge the database concerning ) the Mediterranean offset independent of these questions of interlaboratory and intermethod variations . Already , we can likely set the parameters of the extreme alternative scenario with respect to the Santorini eruption case using the available data and the same models ( 13 , 54 -- 56 , 58 ) . The BCP record of ( 13 ) likely exhibits a maximum alternative case for a revised AMS 14C IntCal summer NH baseline ( Fig. 6 , A to C ) ( 19 ) . We can then , in addition , consider the possible relevance of the positive average offset of 21 14C years between the Mediterranean and NH in the period 3550 to 3486 cal B.P. ( 1601 to 1537 BCE ) as identified from the comparison of the Hd datasets ( Fig. 2B ) and apply this adjustment to the AA BCP data ( Fig. 6 , D to F ) . In this hypothetical experiment , we treat the remainder of the period 3600 to 3450 cal B.P. ( 1651 to 1501 BCE ) as not being substantively offset ( Figs. 2B and 3A ) . The probability distributions in Fig. 6 illustrate the extreme alternative dating scenarios . The published AA BCP record ( Fig. 6 , A to C ) creates an ambiguous situation : A clear probability region remains in the late 17th century BCE to early 16th century BCE , but there is also considerable probability in the mid -- 16th century BCE . However , were the approximate range of the AA BCP data to form a new IntCal baseline and a Mediterranean positive offset to also apply in addition ( a logical implication , but needing empirical testing ) , then the dating probability starts more strongly to support an early to mid -- 16th century BCE date . Such a scenario or the hypothetical large LLGPC to AMS 14C adjustments considered in Fig. 5 ( H to K ) , interestingly , does not , however , return us to the traditional " low " archaeological chronology ( 19 , 57 ) . Instead , it would point to a possible alternative between the current " high " and low scenarios : a shortened " compromise early chronology " for the date of the Santorini eruption and the earlier Aegean Late Bronze Age ( 19 , 56 ) . Even at the extreme hypothetical adjustment range ( Figs. 5 , H to K , and 6 , A to F ) , the traditional date range of the Santorini eruption 1500 BCE ( 57 ) , or any date after 1530 BCE , appears highly improbable . <p> ( A to C ) With AA BCP calibration dataset ( 13 ) with a curve resolution of 5 years ( smoothing the noisy 1-year data ) . ( D to F ) Application of a hypothetical further addition of +21 14C years 3550 to 3486 cal B.P. ( 1601 to 1537 BCE ) to reflect the positive Mediterranean offset ( Fig. 2B ) ; curve resolution , 5 years ( smoothing the noisy 1-year data ) . Main hpd regions are those contiguous intervals identified within the overall 68.2 and 95.4% hpd ranges . <p> Overall , our findings , both the periods of positive 14C offsets that we focus on in this paper , as well as the instances of periods of negative offsets noted above , in addition to other indications of similar Mediterranean or seasonal 14C offsets ( 8 , 14 -- 19 ) , highlight the relevance of these recurring offset elements to high-resolution absolute dating for Old World prehistory . This topic assumes greater and greater importance as 14C dating and chronometric aspirations become ever more accurate and precise . We may draw two key conclusions . First , there is now clearly a need going forward for the development of a detailed consensus Mediterranean 14C time series to secure an appropriate closely defined Old World archaeological time scale . No simple static adjustment is possible as a satisfactory solution for the recurring , periodic offsets observed in both the BCE and CE windows reported in works to date . Second , it is necessary to establish greater temporal and spatial delineation of seasonal/growing season variations for accurate high-precision 14C dating worldwide . <h> MATERIALS AND METHODS <h> Experimental design <p> The main aim of this study is to compare time series of radiocarbon ( 14C ) measurements on tree ring samples and , in particular , to compare data from trees with typical lower-elevation Mediterranean growth contexts versus those from central and northern Europe , which comprise most of the midlatitude NH international radiocarbon calibration curve IntCal , through different iterations ( 1 -- 4 ) . We sought to investigate whether a likely growing season -- related offset occurred periodically in the past , as has been reported in a more recent period ( 18 ) . In particular , a key aim of the study is to compare data from a central European time series ( GeO from southern Germany ) versus data from a Mediterranean time series ( Juniperus sp. from central Anatolia ) , which were measured in the same laboratory ( the LLGPC facility at Hd ) under the same conditions . This parallel dating strategy circumvents the problem of being unable , otherwise , to extract signal from the noise of interlaboratory variation , which is often the cause for any apparent differences . Thus , regardless of the absolute dating accuracy of the Hd laboratory over this period , the relative similarities or differences observed between the two Hd time series are real . We then tested one period where a difference in values was observed with an additional series of measurements on wood from Italy at another laboratory using a different method ( AMS 14C ) , and we investigated and compared another period where a more modest difference was observed with wood from northern Anatolia using data from three AMS 14C laboratories . For details on the laboratory procedures at each 14C laboratory and the tree ring samples used , see the Supplementary Materials ( 19 ) . We note that three 14C measurements were excluded as unexplained too old outliers and remeasurements of these samples are used instead ( see table S1 ) . <p> The tree ring series wiggle matches ( 39 ) and calibrated calendar dating probabilities shown in Figs. 2 to 5 were obtained using the OxCal software ( 59 ) . OxCal version 4.3.2 was used , except for the analysis in Fig. 4A , which used version 4.1.7 as did the reruns of the model in ( 23 ) mentioned in the main text ( Results ) . Curve resolution of 1 year was used . For discussion and information about the use of OxCal and the specific outlier models and coding , see the Supplementary Materials ( 19 ) . <h> Statistical analysis <p> Radiocarbon calibration and wiggle matching used the OxCal software ( 19 , 59 ) as noted . Interpolation of 14C time series to 1-year increments used linear extrapolation . Where 10-year tree ring blocks are involved , the midpoint is treated as year 5.5 of the series , and 0.5-year increments were interpolated as necessary . In cases of 14C dates run on the identical ( same age ) tree ring years , these were combined into weighted averages and errors ( 19 ) . Differences between 14C time series were calculated from the set of paired comparisons ( either corresponding 1- or 0.5-year interpolated intervals or paired data ) and their combined ( propagated ) errors . <p> Fig . " <p> Right now the company is focused on five industries : manufacturing , transportation , apparel and retail , food and beverage and real estate . <p> " The building blocks of a carbon journey are : create carbon emissions inventories ( footprint ) , build a low-carbon scenario by selecting options that will reduce emissions , set up a carbon reduction target ( science-based or not ) , calculate their carbon budget , analyze potential carbon taxes , define an optimal carbon price and finally @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ international policies compliance ) , " the company said in a statement . <p> Joining Fujihara is Alain Rodriguez , one of the first 20 engineers at Uber who is now focused on the climate issue . <p> " Basically , we combine climate finance methodologies , to manage emissions reductions and costs related to the implementation of low-carbon technologies ( ultimately , this is what a carbon price means for a company ) . The delay in closing the Canada-U.S. border may well have been one of those . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For now , we&amp;rsquo ; re still at the stage where suppressing the spread of COVID-19 &amp;mdash ; keeping the number of infections as low as possible for as long as possible by social distancing , along with the closure of schools , bars and restaurants &amp;mdash ; could halve the number of COVID-19 deaths and cut peak demand for critical care by two-thirds . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even with those sharp reductions , our troubles will still be far from over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is likely to be an eight-fold increase in the demand for critical care beds beyond available capacity , based on modelling done by the Imperial College COVID-19 Response Team using data from China and South Korea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The &lt;a href= " https : **33;6480;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;study&lt;/a&gt; released earlier this week laid out scenarios for Britain and the United States . No one has yet predicted how many Canadians might die . But the modelling suggests that half of all those needing critical care will . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Using expert clinical opinion , the Imperial College team estimated the infection fatality rate for those over 80 at 9.3 per cent . The rate drops to 5.1 per cent for people aged 70 to 79 , and 2.2 per cent for those 60 to 69 , declining to 0.002 per cent for children under nine . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As absurdly simple as it seems to suppress a pandemic by staying on the couch , it is still economically devastating . Canadians got a glimpse of its cost on Wednesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Phase One of the federal government&amp;rsquo ; s response is $52 billion &amp;mdash ; three per cent of our gross domestic product &amp;mdash ; to mitigate the damage caused by extraordinary job losses and business closures . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That $52 billion only covers four months . Wrestling this virus to something approaching manageable is going to take much longer and is dependent on finding a vaccine , which could take up to 18 months . It is also yet to be determined whether anyone who has had the infection will have immunity when the next wave of the virus hits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For those who resent any restrictions placed on their freedom , these are difficult times . For those who thrive on social contact , it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to accept your friends declining invitations as being in your best interest as well as their own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s distressing to all but the most introverted of introverts to witness the life being sucked out of our neighbourhoods as restaurants , cafes , gyms , yoga and Pilates studios , hairdressers , theatres , music venues , museums , libraries are shuttered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For those of us who live in condos and apartment buildings , it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to know where social distance begins and ends . Do you share the elevator ? Or wait ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those , of course , are problems that pale next to the difficulties faced by women living in abusive situations , the homeless and the poor who rely on public spaces for warmth , bathrooms , and even food . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; re learning what this new normal looks like with the hope that we may get a reprieve in the summer if the spread of infection subsides , before it is expected to rage back to life in the fall and we will be asked once again to make a few sacrifices for the greater good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But this is marathon , not a sprint . It may test the degree to which we are willing to sacrifice for the greater good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Monday , civil libertarians warned not to overstep Canadians&amp;rsquo ; rights and freedoms in response to the prime minister&amp;rsquo ; s statement that the government would be looking at the Emergencies Act to see whether amendments were needed to &amp;ldquo ; enable us to take the actions needed to protect people . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Wednesday , the B.C. government joined other provinces in declaring a state of emergency in addition to the previously declared public health emergency . It now has wide powers to enforce a wide range of orders , including its use of private property , entry without warrant , quarantines and rationing of food , fuel , medical equipment or other essential services . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So far , we&amp;rsquo ; ve only been asked to be our best selves , good citizens and neighbours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most Canadians have responded as expected , with kindness and care , even in long grocery lineups. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the opportunity to suppress this pandemic is rapidly closing and we&amp;rsquo ; ve been put on notice that we can do this the easier way . We can wash our hands , keep our distance and stay home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Or we can do it the harder way , with more sickness , more deaths , and police officers pulled away from more pressing duties to enforce those orders . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;6515;TOOLONG " **36;6546;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamFri , 20 Mar 2020 02:09:13 **45;6584;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildHealthLifeLocal HealthLocal **45;6631;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Sang Tan " **28;7316;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1243119 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Keep Calm and Carry On . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That was the message on the 1939 posters aimed at lifting the morale of the British public before the outbreak of the Second World War , which was about to bring mass air attacks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The world is not now at war , militarily . But an invisible &amp;ldquo ; enemy&amp;rdquo ; has infiltrated in the form of a novel coronavirus . It has infected hundreds of thousands of people and killed several thousand around the world ( mostly in China and Italy ) , with several deaths in Canada ( many of whom were in the same North Vancouver seniors home ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The world is on high alert . And it&amp;rsquo ; s an especially nerve-wracking time for the hundreds of millions of people &amp;mdash ; roughly one in eight people in the West &amp;mdash ; who struggle with chronic anxiety , which makes them prone to bodily distress and constant feelings of dread . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This COVID-19 outbreak is a reminder that , even at the best of times , &lt;a href= " http : **34;7346;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;life is risky . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The regular seasonal flu normally kills 3,500 a year in Canada , almost all of whom have compromised health systems . Yet that never makes front-page headlines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nor do the 92,000 Canadians who are diagnosed each year with heart failure , the almost 2,000 Canadians who die in automobile accidents or the &lt;a href= " http : **34;7382;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;1,000 who die annually on the job . &lt;/a&gt; The list of risks goes on and on . We should never try to convince ourselves that our leaders &amp;mdash ; or anyone &amp;mdash ; can make us absolutely safe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet with governments around the world making extraordinary moves to ramp up preventative measures against COVID-19 , leading to many suffering financially , the public has a right to be concerned . We have a duty to take precautions , for the sake of ourselves and , as in war , the common good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7418;TOOLONG ... title= " ' Actual panics are rare , ' says Baruch Fischoff , an expert in risk analysis . ' You 'll see them in movies more than in real life . Under crisis situations , people typically rally around one another , they support one another , they act bravely . ' " alt= " ' Actual panics are rare , ' says Baruch Fischoff , an expert in risk analysis . ' You 'll see them in movies more than in real life . ' " data-portal-copyright= " cmu.edu " **28;7454;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1243148 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Panic is not an option , however . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And , fortunately , few do actually panic in times of pandemic or other widespread crises , says Baruch Fischhoff , an expert in risk analysis whose work is being &lt;a href= " https : **33;7484;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;highlighted by the American Psychological Association&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Actual panics are rare . You&amp;rsquo ; ll see them in movies more than in real life . Under crisis situations , people typically rally around one another , they support one another , they act bravely . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean a few aren&amp;rsquo ; t behaving badly , though . They include the opportunists from Vancouver , Kelowna and various corners of the planet getting their clutches on stacks of toilet paper , cleansers and meat to sell for an inflated profit . In times of war a small number of carpet-baggers always appear . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And China&amp;rsquo ; s foreign ministry spokesman &lt;a href= " https : **33;7519;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Zhao Lijian did not do anyone any favours&lt;/a&gt; last week when he spread an unfounded conspiracy theory that the U.S. military caused the COVID-19 outbreak in the city of Wuhan , where Chinese authorities initially tried to cover it up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadians have had a rough start to 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;7554;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;7596;TOOLONG ... Todd : Free psychotherapy is just good **30;7758;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The year began with a handful of Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary chiefs and various activists joining forces to **25;7790;TOOLONG ; by blockading railways and roads . Then COVID-19 arrived in this cosmopolitan country , with 87 per cent of our cases linked to travel . It&amp;rsquo ; s paradoxical that worried politicians have responded by , in many ways , shutting down Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year has not been a lot of laughs for Canadians . Still , in the midst of these larger troubles , old-fashioned stoicism can go a long way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are many things one can do to stop dread and anxiety becoming overwhelming : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Keep things in perspective&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Don&amp;rsquo ; t be too hard on yourself if you&amp;rsquo ; re experiencing more nervousness than usual . Give yourself credit for tolerating the current uncertainty , says Anxiety Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Assess the facts&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; With a few hundred Canadians having confirmed or presumptive COVID-19 , it means the current odds of being among such known cases in this country are , roughly speaking , only about 70,000 to one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And &amp;ldquo ; take a deep breath and remind yourself that most people who contract COVID-19 will only experience mild symptoms , &amp;rdquo ; adds the American Psychological Association . Fewer than one in 100 will die , and they&amp;rsquo ; ll mostly be those who are already ailing . The average age of the Italian fatalities has been 81. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Monitor your news intake&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadian journalists are largely being responsible in their coverage of COVID-19 . But the avalanche of news stories , which the public is devouring , can give the impression things are spinning out of control . They&amp;rsquo ; re not . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;7817;TOOLONG ... title= " Anxiety Canada 's Mindshift app. " alt= " Anxiety Canada 's Mindshift app. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;7853;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1243174 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Take an analytical approach to the news . Treat reports from social media and even friends with healthy skepticism . Exaggeration can slip into even the most earnest news stories , put together by journalists who are themselves excitable . Verify where information is coming from , with health agencies being among the most trusted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As we think about and focus more on coronavirus , the perception of threat increases , not the actual risk , but our perception of it , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;7883;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;says Anxiety Canada&lt;/a&gt; , which has long produced a helpful mobile app for dealing with anxiety called &lt;a href= " https : **33;7918;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Mindshift. &lt;/a&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s based on the proven principles of &lt;a href= " http : **34;7953;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Cognitive Behavioral Therapy&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; By limiting or eliminating contact with the media you can help yourself manage your own anxiety &amp;hellip ; Commit to only checking in a couple of times a day . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Anxiety Canada goes further and says &amp;ldquo ; stop talking about coronavirus , &amp;rdquo ; including at the proverbial water cooler . &amp;ldquo ; To keep thinking about it influences our sense of threat/risk . To counteract this , don&amp;rsquo ; t initiate the conversation and change the subject if it does come up . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Protect yourself&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most important advice might be the most basic , which we all now know . Wash your hands often . Try to stop touching your face , since viruses enter our bodies through our eyes , nose and mouth . &amp;nbsp ; Avoid handshakes and hugs and keep a distance of one metre from anyone exhibiting symptoms . If you have a cough or fever stay home . Et cetera. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , even though risk-analyst Fischoff says the normal seasonal flu is currently a greater threat to North Americans than he hopes COVID-19 will ever be , he realizes many people are worried about loved ones who might be in tougher situations than themselves , either because they already struggle with anxiety or because they&amp;rsquo ; re being hit financially . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Be supportive of people who are under greater stress , &amp;rdquo ; Fischoff says . It&amp;rsquo ; s what we always hope we would do anyways. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But don&amp;rsquo ; t let your concern for others trick you into believing things are worse than they are . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;7989;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **33;8017;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **25;8052;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;8079;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;8112;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? A query to the U.S. Customs and Border Protection agency did not receive a response . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Essential travel will be allowed to continue to preserve critical supply chains , Trudeau said , which means trucks will continue to cross the border to deliver food , fuel and medicine , and essential workers such as health-care professionals who live and work on opposite sides will also be permitted to cross . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Government officials also said exemptions will remain in place to ensure Canadians who are now in the U.S. are able to return home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; James Brander , an economics professor at the University of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s Sauder School of Business , said there is tremendous uncertainty surrounding everything that involves the coronavirus , including how the border restrictions will work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said the decision about whether everyday cross-border business activity that is not necessarily related to supply chains will be considered essential will be an important one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If all this business service-related activity is shut off , then I think that will be yet another significant or noticeable reduction to economic activity in both places , &amp;rdquo ; Brander said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although trade will not be affected , businesses on both sides of the border will feel the pinch of fewer visitors . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; According to licence plate survey data from the Border Policy Research Institute , at specific retail locations in Whatcom County , Canadians constitute an average of 17 per cent of weekend customers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trautman said big retail stores like Ross , Trader Joe&amp;rsquo ; s and Costco are popular with Canadian shoppers , but she believes those big corporations will be able to prevail more easily than smaller retailers . For instance , border gas stations and mailbox outlets rely primarily on Canadians who pop over for a quick visit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Those are going to struggle , I think , to weather this storm . Depending on how long those restrictions are in place , those places will not bounce back as quickly , if at all . We&amp;rsquo ; ll see , you know , it&amp;rsquo ; s just so unprecedented , &amp;rdquo ; Trautman said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She said although it is speculative at this point , if the restrictions go on for a long time , Canadians could alter their consumer behaviour , as they have done when the dollar has dropped significantly , and that could take a long time to bounce back once it&amp;rsquo ; s entrenched . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Walt Judas , CEO of the Tourism Industry Association of B.C. , said the travel restrictions that have been implemented in recent weeks and days have had an immediate impact on tourism across the province . He said some hotels are already at less than five-per-cent occupancy , and others are closed or on the brink of closing because they have no guests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Any additional measures are going to add to what&amp;rsquo ; s already happened , but most of the damage has already been done , &amp;rdquo ; Judas said . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re following the lead of health authorities and recognizing , of course , that the industry is reeling as a consequence , but everybody understands and knows it&amp;rsquo ; s the right thing to do . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Merv Korolek responded to the scene , the three officers searched the car . That&amp;rsquo ; s when the dispatcher told him , 15 minutes after he&amp;rsquo ; d first asked for the plates to be run , that the suspects&amp;rsquo ; vehicle had been stolen in California . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He alerted the other two cops and then walked over to the group of suspects standing on the sidewalk . Buis , who had not pulled his service revolver out of his holster , explained to one of the passengers , a nervous-looking Gustave Gyulay , that he didn&amp;rsquo ; t want any trouble . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Just walk over to the car and put your hands on the roof , &amp;rdquo ; Buis said , while placing his hand on the 26-year-old suspect&amp;rsquo ; s shoulder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gyulay suddenly stepped backwards , put his hand into the back of his pants , and pulled out a sawed-off shotgun . &amp;ldquo ; Come here , I want you , &amp;rdquo ; he told Buis , according to the police reports . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The young cop backed up quickly but Gyulay ran toward him , firing the shotgun at very close range . The bullet tore into Buis&amp;rsquo ; s thighs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buis remembers floating in the air and hitting his head on the ground , his ears ringing from the loud blast . Disoriented and in shock , he lay so still , face-down on the sidewalk , that his co-workers didn&amp;rsquo ; t know if he were dead or alive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His partner , Robinson , fired one shot at the suspect , then ran to the cruiser to hit the radio emergency button . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Korolek , who was behind the suspects&amp;rsquo ; car , shouted at Gyulay , &amp;ldquo ; Hold it right there . &amp;rdquo ; The Mountie unleashed five bullets , one that went through Gyulay&amp;rsquo ; s right arm and lodged in his liver , the RCMP report says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Robinson blasted two more shots at Gyulay , who was struck in the knee and ankle before he reached into Buis&amp;rsquo ; s holster and pulled out the cop&amp;rsquo ; s revolver , using it to fire at the other officers . &amp;ldquo ; The gun was shooting over my left ear as he is using me as a barricade , &amp;rdquo ; Buis recalled . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gyulay then rammed Buis&amp;rsquo ; s own revolver into the back of his head , and told the other officers to drop their guns or he would kill their colleague . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buis can still remember the hot muzzle burning his neck and the sound of his revolver being cocked , knowing a bullet was live in the chamber . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The harrowing incident unfolded two years after Buis graduated from the RCMP training depot in April 1977 and began working in Burnaby . As he lay on the ground , he thought of his wife Kellie , a 23-year-old Delta school teacher . He thought of his parents &amp;mdash ; he&amp;rsquo ; d had dinner with them earlier that evening to celebrate his birthday . He thought about the safety of his fellow cops . He thought about the short life he&amp;rsquo ; d had . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Robinson kept his revolver pointed at Gyulay , telling him to drop the gun and not add murder to the mounting number of charges against him . Crouching on the ground , Gyulay tried to get the bullets out of the pouch attached to Buis&amp;rsquo ; s belt , but he dropped the ammunition onto the sidewalk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As more officers arrived , Gyulay slowly put the revolver to his own head before throwing it onto the nearby grass . He was arrested for attempted murder , and the following year was sentenced to life in prison . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The shooting was over in a matter of minutes , but for Buis the healing would take a lifetime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His right leg was badly damaged &amp;mdash ; his wife said the wound was larger than her two fists held together &amp;mdash ; and his left leg was injured as well . He spent 26 days in the hospital , undergoing two surgeries , including a skin graft , and was off work for 2&amp;frac12 ; months . Since then , he&amp;rsquo ; s had seven more leg surgeries and several knee surgeries to address aftermath injuries , remove dozens of pellets embedded in his skin , reduce his pain and minimize the scarring. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10094;TOOLONG ... title= " The scars on RCMP officer John Buis 's right leg , two years after the shooting . " alt= " The scars on RCMP officer John Buis 's right leg , two years after the shooting . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;10130;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239664 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Injuries far from just physical&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The shooting , though , would not be the last trauma in Buis&amp;rsquo ; s 43-year career . Two of his depot troop mates were killed on the job , his emergency response force boss committed suicide , a young constable on his watch was killed by street racers , and he participated in two peacekeeping tours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When people think someone gets shot , they think he recovers and goes back to work . I thought I had dealt with it pretty well , the emotional , psychological stuff . But it is the cumulative things over the years , &amp;rdquo ; said Buis , who is now a staff-sergeant major . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He thought he had held his life together with tough-guy bravado , but things started to come unglued in 2017 and totally fell apart last year , when psychologists diagnosed him with post-traumatic stress disorder , or PTSD , and a dependency on opioids and alcohol that he had used to try to self-medicate his pain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He sought help at Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s &lt;a href= " http : **34;10160;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Operational Stress Injury Clinic&lt;/a&gt; , which caters to police and soldiers , and from there attended a nine-week residential treatment program in Saanich. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He is speaking out today to encourage a larger conversation about mental health among first responders , who are often hesitant to ask for help . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think there are a lot of people , particularly members of the RCMP , who if they get into this type of situation don&amp;rsquo ; t really know where to turn . And hopefully we can start talking about the services that are out there for people who may end up in a similar situation to me , &amp;rdquo ; said Buis , who has been on medical leave since October 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I have a son and his girlfriend in the RCMP and do not want to see either of them go through what I have gone through . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buis believes he was able to find help because his leg surgeries meant he was already in contact with medical personnel who work with Mounties. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There has been much debate , though , about whether the RCMP and other first-responder agencies have put enough resources into dealing with PTSD. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10196;TOOLONG ... title= " IHIT 's Staff Sgt. " data-portal-copyright= " Gerry Kahrmann " **28;10232;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239737 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Some officers did n't get help&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Former high-profile RCMP spokeswoman &lt;a href= " https : **29;10262;TOOLONG ? pag ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Staff Sgt. Jennifer Pound maintains a raw blog&lt;/a&gt; that documents her struggle with PTSD , and insists she has not found the help she needs from the Mounties or the health care system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; One of the most gutting realizations of this journey for me is that once I became injured , the RCMP family I once bought into appeared to no longer value me , &amp;rdquo ; she wrote last September . &amp;ldquo ; If funding is not provided to create more positions for health care employees , then injured first responders will continue to sit on wait-lists with the risk of their injury becoming more difficult to treat . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The assistance offered to former B.C. RCMP spokesman Sgt. Pierre Lemaitre was analyzed at the 2018 &lt;a href= " https : **33;10293;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;inquest&lt;/a&gt; into his 2013 suicide . She was also unable to provide information on the type and number of officers accessing the support , &amp;rdquo ; the coroner&amp;rsquo ; s report said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the jury&amp;rsquo ; s recommendations was that the RCMP should include mental health assessments as part of mandatory three-year physical assessments for all officers . " data-portal-copyright= " Colin Price " **28;10400;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239729 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also in response to the coroner&amp;rsquo ; s recommendations , the RCMP said it would hire 14 new staff psychologists . Spokesman Daniel Brien said this week that will bring the number of staff psychologists up to 27. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said PTSD is &amp;ldquo ; an increasing concern&amp;rdquo ; within the RCMP , but could not say how many members have that diagnosis because that would require delving into private medical files . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brien said the RCMP is taking many steps to address work-related stress , including tracking the mental health of cadets after they start working , and an online suicide prevention course . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There were 25 documented RCMP suicides between January 2014 and December 2019 , involving 15 active members and 10 retirees , Brien said . &lt;a href= " https : **33;10430;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Postmedia has reported&lt;/a&gt; &amp;nbsp ; that between 2006 and 2014 , there were 31 suicides by serving or retired Mounties. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Certainly , the RCMP is not the only agency grappling with mental health issues . WorkSafeBC has seen a large increase in accepted PTSD-related workplace claims , 641 in 2019 , up from 266 in 2017 . Of the 2019 claims , 21 were for municipal police officers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; WorkSafeBC created an anti-stigma campaign , &lt;a href= " https : **33;10465;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Share It , Do n't Wear It&lt;/a&gt; , and held a mental health conference for first responders last year , which was attended by 300 people , 81 of them police officers . A second conference is being planned for January . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another former Mountie , retired superintendent Russ Grabb , told Postmedia this week that he believes he developed PTSD during his long career , which included an attempt on his life by &amp;mdash ; coincidentally &amp;mdash ; one of the suspects in the Lincoln Continental just days before Buis pulled the same car over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Grabb is also haunted by the image of the charred bodies of two little girls killed in a Lions Bay house fire in 1977. &amp;ldquo ; The gruesome sights and penetrating smells of that double autopsy haunted me for over 40 years , &amp;rdquo ; Grabb said this week . &amp;ldquo ; ( But ) it was the 1970s , and we were conditioned to just &amp;lsquo ; suck it up&amp;rsquo ; or face eternal derision and shame . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10500;TOOLONG ... title= " RCMP media relations officer Sgt. " data-portal-copyright= " David Clark " **28;10536;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239722 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;Demand for help ' growing quite significantly ' &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The residential program that Buis attended for nine weeks last fall was at Homewood Ravensview in Saanich , which opened in June to address &amp;ldquo ; an unmet need&amp;rdquo ; in Western Canada for in-house treatment of trauma and PTSD among &lt;a href= " https : **33;10566;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;first responders , soldiers and veterans&lt;/a&gt; , said staff psychologist Michael Berry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A lot of first responders and military members are coming in with occupational stress injury , which means that they&amp;rsquo ; ve had trauma in the workplace , &amp;rdquo ; Berry said . &amp;ldquo ; The need and the demand for services and treatment is growing quite significantly . I think there is still stigma in those communities . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He believes the RCMP and other first-responder organizations are moving in the right direction to better address mental health , but there&amp;rsquo ; s still more work to do . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think there is still a ways to go yet , &amp;rdquo ; Berry said , but added senior Mounties like Buis speaking publicly will assist others . &amp;ldquo ; To help them feel like it is valid and it&amp;rsquo ; s OK to seek out supportive help . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10601;TOOLONG ... title= " RCMP Const . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;10637;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239715 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Through a series of interviews , it was clear that sharing his story has not been easy for Buis , who is approaching retirement . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve had a number of traumatic situations that changed me , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In March 1985 , six years after his shooting , Buis heard over the police radio that Mike Buday , his &amp;ldquo ; pit partner&amp;rdquo ; at training depot , had been fatally shot on the job near Teslin Lake in northern B.C. &amp;ldquo ; He was a great young man and when I found out he had been killed , it was very devastating , &amp;rdquo ; he recalled . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two years later , Buis was a member of the Burnaby RCMP emergency response team when the team leader , Const . Lee Rumball , shot himself in the ERT van parked at the detachment . Earlier in the evening , Rumball&amp;rsquo ; s wife had phoned Buis to ask if he knew where her husband was , and later that night he drove to Abbotsford to deliver the crushing news . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10667;TOOLONG ... title= " John and Kellie Buis with the RCMP honour guard at their 1977 wedding . Rumball was the fifth of six suicides with ties to the Burnaby detachment between 1982 and 1988 , he added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In September 1991 , Buis was on a ferry returning from Tofino when he read in the newspaper that Const . Chris Riglar &amp;mdash ; another depot friend who had also been in his wedding party &amp;mdash ; had been killed by a drunk driver outside Victoria . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very awful experience , &amp;rdquo ; said Buis. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So too was the senseless 2002 death of Richmond Const . Jimmy Ng , killed by two street racers. &amp;ldquo ; It was a very , very tragic incident , &amp;rdquo ; said Buis , who was Ng&amp;rsquo ; s watch commander . &amp;ldquo ; It really hit the people on my watch hard . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10733;TOOLONG ... title= " Dr. Chris Ng and Therese Ng , the parents of Const . " data-portal-copyright= " Jason Payne " **28;10769;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239696 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the memories that Buis finds the hardest to shake was an experience during one of his two tours working with peacekeepers in the former Yugoslavia in 1994 and East Timor in 2003-04 . He is haunted by his crew&amp;rsquo ; s sudden evacuation out of Yugoslavia to escape the violence , and his inability to help the citizens he had been protecting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We were leaving them behind . And I didn&amp;rsquo ; t realize how much of a dilemma that would be for me , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10799;TOOLONG ... title= " Const . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;10835;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239686 " /&gt; &lt;h3&gt;'I said , " I need help " ' &lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Buis said he&amp;rsquo ; s had a remarkable career , with many accomplishments of which he is proud . But in 2017 , he developed a serious infection following yet another surgery on his right leg . He was prescribed the powerful opioid Dilaudid for the pain and spent two weeks in isolation , during which memories of his last long stay in hospital in 1979 brought flashbacks of the shooting . Later , both his knees were replaced as a result of injuries from the shooting , and he also had several unrelated surgeries , which all brought more opioid prescriptions for pain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In March 2019 , a surgeon told Buis his daily dosage of Dilaudid was frighteningly high . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I quit cold turkey . But the pain was still there , so I started drinking . I was still hurting and it was ruining my relationship with my wife . I was just sitting at home feeling sorry for myself , &amp;rdquo ; he said with blunt honesty . &amp;ldquo ; I said , &amp;lsquo ; I need help . &amp;rsquo ; And for me to say that , it was difficult . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the end of May 2019 , he stopped drinking and reached out to the &lt;a href= " http : **34;10865;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Operational Stress Injury Clinic&lt;/a&gt; . The ensuing assessment from the staff psychologist shocked him : He had PTSD , anxiety , depression and alcohol use disorder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was like cold water being thrown in my face , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In recommending he attend in-patient therapy , the doctor wrote : &amp;ldquo ; The cumulative effect of his many traumatic experiences have caused symptoms that have lasted decades . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;10901;TOOLONG ... title= " RCMP Staff Sgt. Major John Buis is on medical leave because of PTSD , which he developed over his 43-year policing career . " data-portal-copyright= " Francis Georgian " **28;10937;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1239679 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; He agreed to go to Ravensview , but even as Buis drove through the gates last September , he heard a nagging voice asking : &amp;ldquo ; Do I really need this ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It turns out he did . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was able to confront the demons from his past and some pent-up disappointments , such as the two officers who saved his life in 1979 never receiving recognition for their actions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When he completed the program in December , his discharge papers noted that &amp;ldquo ; during his career with the RCMP , the culture was to not express weakness . It&amp;rsquo ; s to calibrate his ability to be out in public so that they can figure out what the eventual end goal is , where is he in the context of our hope based on the law that we have to get him ready to re-integrate him into society ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born in Winnipeg , the second of three kids , Schoenborn&amp;rsquo ; s childhood was unremarkable &amp;mdash ; his parents divorced when he was about 11 and he initially moved to the Lower Mainland with his mother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At 14 , he moved to Camrose to live with his father . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He completed Grade 9 , developed a thirst for alcohol and a taste for drugs , and became a roofer with a history of petty crime &amp;mdash ; B&amp;amp ; Es , mischief , assault , drunk driving , and flouting legal orders &amp;mdash ; until 1993 when he met his wife . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Schoenborn came to fear she was unfaithful and frequently questioned the paternity of his children &amp;mdash ; signs of his growing psychiatric illness . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1987 when he was 19 , Schoenborn had been hospitalized with auditory hallucinations in Camrose and claimed to have spoken to Jesus . He was discharged but received no psychiatric follow-up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1999 , he crashed his car while rushing his 15-month-old daughter to hospital for fear she had been sexually assaulted by his wife and her supposed lover . As a result , he was admitted to Royal Columbian Hospital for more than a month of psychiatric care before he left , against medical advice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just before the slayings , Schoenborn was again suspicious about his children being groomed for prostitution , was hearing voices and becoming more and more paranoid . He was living in a tent or his car in the Lower Mainland , bankrupt . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prosecutors insisted he killed the children to get revenge on his wife , Darcie Clarke , who died of undisclosed causes on May 30 last year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2011 , escorted absences were approved for Schoenborn , but the Crown had the decision revoked. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Escorted absences were again approved by the board in 2015 , triggering a two-year fight by prosecutors to have him declared a &amp;ldquo ; high-risk . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But then-B.C . Supreme Court Justice Martha Devlin concluded Schoenborn&amp;rsquo ; s progress , mental condition and the opinions of experts provided no reason to believe he posed a serious enough threat to warrant the label . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , he was not approved for an escorted pass because of anger management and interpersonal challenges until last year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since then , Schoenborn has had &amp;ldquo ; staff supported&amp;rdquo ; trips , at first to parks , then coffee shops and shopping centres . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Robert Lacroix , a forensic psychiatrist , said that reflected his progress . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the last year , Schoenborn has started counselling for substance use , completed a &amp;ldquo ; Social Communications Skills&amp;rdquo ; course and he has attended a Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Psychosis program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although forensic security officers initially accompanied Schoenborn&amp;rsquo ; s designated staff , now they occur without security and with other patients . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Potential destinations for unescorted leave could include community rehabilitative programs , recreational outings or occupational programs , the therapists said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While at times irritable and abrasive , Schoenborn is said to cooperate with ward routine and rules , but remains a lightning rod for some patients who taunt and target him . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Imagine if you were under this level of scrutiny , would you only have a handful of incidents in a year where you wished you&amp;rsquo ; d acted differently ? &amp;rdquo ; Gill said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Schoenborn&amp;rsquo ; s illness is apparently in &amp;ldquo ; full remission&amp;rdquo ; and he reputedly has improved personal insight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His team worries about two situations if he is released . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first involves violence resulting from a psychotic episode triggered by delusions of jealousy or paranoia if Schoenborn stopped taking his meds or relapsed into substance use . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But such symptoms , the experts assured , would evolve over a period of months and were not likely to go undetected in a structured setting or with regular psychiatric follow-up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The second scenario involved violence sparked by his &amp;ldquo ; reactive anger&amp;rdquo ; when provoked . Schoenborn is engaged in psychotherapy to help exert self-control . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But his only support is his mother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At best , the review was told he will require a gradual progression toward community reintegration during which his coping skills will need constant evaluation and support . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is the healthiest I&amp;rsquo ; ve ever seen him and I&amp;rsquo ; ve known him for 12 years now , &amp;rdquo ; Gill said . &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s not ready for release , but we&amp;rsquo ; re not asking for that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Dave Teixeira , a family spokesman who attended the review with Darcie&amp;rsquo ; s brother Mike , said : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The family and I are hopeful there will be no more additional privileges , but we&amp;rsquo ; re also somewhat understanding that this may go through , and so what could happen is over the next three , six , 12 months the director here at Colony Farm could allow Schoenborn into our community in about a 15-minute radius of this hospital &amp;mdash ; so that means elementary schools , soccer pitches , Coquitlam Centre Mall , downtown Coquitlam , where he will be allowed to roam about . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The panel reserved its decision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;11750;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;11781;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;11819;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; Ian MulgrewFri , 13 Mar 2020 01:25:45 **45;11852;TOOLONG ... Mulgrew : Money probe requires secrecyhttp : **33;11899;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;11934;TOOLONG ... title= " The commission of inquiry into money-laundering in B.C. is being led by Austin Cullen . " alt= " The commission of inquiry into money-laundering in B.C. is being led by Austin Cullen . " data-portal-copyright= " Jason Payne " **28;11970;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1237338 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; An inscrutable B.C. Court of Appeal decision closing the door on the public in a securities investigation has raised a legal quandary that will face the Cullen Commission into money-laundering. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The province&amp;rsquo ; s high bench took the rare step on March 4 of sealing and anonymizing a case because of the nature of financial investigations and the potentially devastating effects on targeted but innocent individuals and companies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is called &amp;ldquo ; Party A v. British Columbia ( Securities Commission ) &amp;rdquo ; , although it involves the full Sesame Street gang &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; Party A , Party B , Party C , Party D , and Party E , &amp;rdquo ; which is about all I can tell you . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the opaque &lt;a href= " https : **33;12000;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;oral judgment&lt;/a&gt; published Wednesday , Justice Mary Saunders explained why the unusual cloaking procedures were necessary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These are the same conundrums that will dog former B.C. Supreme Court associate chief justice Austin Cullen later this year at his inquiry&amp;rsquo ; s evidentiary hearings &amp;mdash ; trying to get to the bottom of misconduct in public is fraught with difficulty because of the damage that can be done to innocent parties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From the start , Cullen has maintained he is strongly committed to ensuring the commission respects the rights of individuals , companies and agencies and protects their privacy , legal interests and reputations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But those issues are not easily addressed , as shown in this appeal that arose out of a 2019 Securities Commission investigation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Under the financial policing system , an investigation precedes a &amp;ldquo ; notice of hearing , &amp;rdquo ; an indictment outlining specific allegations parties must answer and explain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Investigations can be carried out without a notice of hearing ever being issued , just as police investigations can end without charges being laid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And like a police inquiry , just the fact the investigation occurred may harm individual reputations and the capital markets in situations where no wrongdoing may ever be alleged . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a result , not surprisingly , people who think they might be mentioned at the Cullen Commission have already lawyered up &amp;mdash ; an apparently wise move given that at its public meetings , half-baked accusations were flung around without censure or correction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In this case , the alphabet cartel wanted the securities investigation and any mention it took place sealed and anonymized &amp;mdash ; and the commission agreed . So did Saunders . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Proceedings in the Supreme Court dealing with a constitutional issue arising from the same investigation , Saunders noted , are not &amp;ldquo ; sealed&amp;rdquo ; because that file itself does not involve inherently sensitive information . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nonetheless , efforts have been made to anonymize those proceedings , too , she added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is always concern on the part of this court when orders are sought that would seal a file , &amp;rdquo ; Saunders acknowledged . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; The principle of the open court is important and we do not lightly seal a file , the act of which has the effect of foreclosing public knowledge of the contents of the file . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Quoting a financial regulatory expert , the justice said public knowledge that an investigation was conducted would significantly harm a venture capital business and the personal reputations of those involved : &amp;ldquo ; It is also possible that persons could draw connections to other companies and individuals related to the applicants and damage the business or reputations of those other companies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What heightens the unfairness , in this case , is that the disclosure of the issuance of a freeze order will leave the public with the erroneous impression that the applicants have engaged in some kind of wrongdoing when no such inference can or should be drawn at this stage . In addition , in my experience , there is almost nothing the applicants&amp;rsquo ; will be able to say or do to counteract the prejudice they will undoubtedly suffer by this premature and misleading disclosure . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In my opinion , the integrity of this investigation , the capital markets in general and the applicants , in particular , will all unfairly suffer harm from premature disclosure of this investigation . To that extent , in my opinion , it would be contrary to the public interest in the capital markets for these proceedings to proceed in a public setting . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She issued the extraordinary sealing order . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Cullen has a similar Gordian knot &amp;mdash ; the mere accusation of money-laundering tarnishes , no matter the reality , while marketplace repercussions and the damage to the innocent can&amp;rsquo ; t be ignored . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But since he is charged with conducting a public inquiry , I don&amp;rsquo ; t think Cullen&amp;rsquo ; s got the same leeway as Saunders to respect the presumption of innocence . It&amp;rsquo ; s going to be harder for him to close the door on the hearsay and speculation that has permeated the money-laundering discussion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Especially given the **26;12035;TOOLONG ; s and the public&amp;rsquo ; s desire for identifiable culprits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;12063;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;12094;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;12132;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; Ian MulgrewWed , 11 Mar 2020 23:32:58 **45;12165;TOOLONG ... drop hits bottom line for Vancouver airport , businesseshttp : **30;12212;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;12244;TOOLONG ... title= " Amy Wilson of the Lattimer Gallery at Vancouver International Airport . CLARY " **28;12835;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1234965 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; VICTORIA &amp;mdash ; The worldwide economic crunch caused by the coronavirus epidemic will eventually drag down B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s budget , but business and labour leaders are urging the province to push through the downturn and spend whatever is necessary in the crisis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Steep losses this week in stock markets , the collapse of oil prices , and the curtailment of cruise ships and travel will hit B.C. through reductions in corporate and personal tax revenues , in hotel tax revenue , and in export revenue , said Ken Peacock , chief economist at the B.C. Business Council . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The business council has revised its&amp;nbsp ; projected growth of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s gross domestic product to 1.4 per cent for 2020 , down from two per cent projected in January . The provincial budget pegged GDP growth at 1.9 per cent , meaning the province is already off target . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s really no data on economic impact so far , &amp;rdquo ; said Peacock , citing the risk of cancellations of conferences , sporting events and other large-scale public gatherings . &amp;ldquo ; But we will almost certainly be revising our look down again . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Premier John Horgan said the province will face &amp;ldquo ; significant challenges&amp;rdquo ; to its economy in the short-term as a result of the coronavirus , especially because of to B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s close economic ties to Asian countries hardest hit by the COVID-19 disease . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have what is now a pandemic and we have extraordinary challenges within markets around the world , &amp;rdquo ; Horgan told the Surrey Board of Trade on Tuesday . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; ve seen catastrophic falls within the Dow and Toronto exchanges . But all governments can do is prepare for the worst and hope for the best . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; British Columbia is an open economy with a diverse population , so it&amp;rsquo ; s not a surprise we would have a significant number of cases here , among the highest in the country . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 2020 provincial budget , which begins April 1 , projects a $227 million surplus on $60 billion in spending , with a $300 million forecast allowance and $600 million contingency fund . That $900 million fiscal cushion is &amp;ldquo ; very prudent , &amp;rdquo ; said Horgan . However , government also draws money to fight seasonal forest fires from the same contingency fund . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The budget earmarked billions more for new capital spending , bringing the three-year plan to $22.9 billion in projects &amp;mdash ; some of which could be fast-tracked to stimulate the provincial economy and generate jobs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We can anticipate economic disruption , &amp;rdquo ; said Horgan. &amp;ldquo ; The challenge from government is we can&amp;rsquo ; t predict from moment to moment where those consequences will be . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finance Minister Carole James had to introduce new taxes and cut spending to achieve the small surplus projection. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " visualisation/1296452 " &gt;&lt;/iframe&gt; ... &lt;p&gt; With the economic downturn , and pressure on the health care system , the government should stop worrying about trying to post a surplus , said Peacock . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Right now is not the time to be worried about deficits , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; And fortunately for B.C. we are in a very strong fiscal position . We have low debt loads , and government absolutely can borrow some money and run a deficit for 2020 if it requires devoting money to health care . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The province should also use that fiscal room to help pay for sick days for employees who are being told by public health experts not to come to work when ill , said Laird Cronk , president of the B.C. Federation of Labour . Some workers have paid sick days in collective agreements or contracts , but thousands more do not and need government help , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What we don&amp;rsquo ; t want is workers having the untenable decision of saying do I self-isolate and disclose I&amp;rsquo ; m not feeling well and not go to work and risk possibly not having not having a job to come back to , &amp;rdquo ; said Cronk. &amp;ldquo ; Or even if I do have a job to come back to I&amp;rsquo ; d lose 14 days of pay and lose my rent . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau is expected to announce federal support measures for the economy and unemployment insurance on Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. has little revenue in the budget from oil production and is far less hurt by the collapse in oil prices than Alberta . The $40 million projected for oil production in B.C. in 2020 is based on an American spot market price that had dropped almost in half as of Tuesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , natural gas is a major economic driver for B.C. Every 25 cent drop in the price of natural gas on the global energy market costs B.C. $30 to $40 million in lost revenue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tourism is also a significant part of the provincial economy . Health Minister Adrian Dix has urged people to reconsider travel on cruise ships , which account for more than $3.2 billion in economic activity annually in Canada &amp;mdash ; much of which is centred on popular ports of call like Vancouver and Victoria . On Tuesday , B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s chief medical health officer , Dr. Bonnie Henry , said the start of the cruise ship season should be delayed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; A few channels the economy will be impacted through most immediately are airlines , tourism and the related accommodation sector , &amp;rdquo ; said Peacock . &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s going to a big hit . It was a big hit in SARS and it will be a big hit now . Tourism is even more important to the B.C. economy than it was in 2003 . It&amp;rsquo ; s a growth engine . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The extent of the economic impact to B.C. also depends on any drop in household income , jobs and spending caused by the virus . A one percentage point drop in 2020 B.C. household income growth costs the provincial treasury up to $115 million , and one percentage point drop in provincial sales tax equates to $25 million in lost revenue , for example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The B.C. government could stimulate the economy by rolling back some of its taxation penalties on real estate and property ownership , allowing that sector to rise again and buffer the province from declines elsewhere , said Andrey Pavlov , a professor of finance at the Simon Fraser University&amp;rsquo ; s Beedie School of Business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Roll back all these measures , roll back the speculation and vacancy tax , the school tax , rent controls , rental only zoning , roll that back so that we can allow arguably the most important sector in our economy to flourish and that will help protect and insulate us from overall economic declines , &amp;rdquo ; said Pavlov. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Short of that , Pavlov urged people to not overreact to the economic declines caused by the virus . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It has been said time and time again , do not sell in a panic , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finance Minister James was not available for an interview Tuesday but in a statement her ministry said it is continually monitoring the effect of the virus and working with other provinces to mitigate the impact . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; At the moment we expect that the economic impacts will be temporary , and we know that B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s economy is well diversified and resilient as we continue with the largest infrastructure investment in the province&amp;rsquo ; s history , &amp;rdquo ; said her ministry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s economy is well diversified but not immune to any slowdown in the global economy . The full extent and impact felt from COVID-19 may not be known for a while , but we are monitoring the situation and working with economic partners across the country . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;12865;TOOLONG " **33;12893;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;12928;TOOLONG " &gt;t ... &lt;/p&gt; Rob ShawWed , 11 Mar 2020 00:35:59 **45;12957;TOOLONG ... **26;13004;TOOLONG Bramham : Canada 's other public health crisis also needs urgent attentionhttp : **31;13032;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;13065;TOOLONG ... title= " Sharene Shuster 's son , Jordan Hunter Carhoun , died of a fentanyl overdose in August 2018 .
