" data-portal-copyright= " Francis Georgian " **28;13101;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1233640 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is a very real and deadly health crisis in B.C. from which two people died yesterday and two more will likely die today , tomorrow and the days after that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not COVID-19 , and no news conference was hastily called to talk about it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most of those dead and dying are blue-collar guys in what should be the prime of their lives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is the reality as B.C. lurches into the fifth year of an opioid overdose crisis . It&amp;rsquo ; s a seemingly unending emergency that by the end of 2019 had already killed 5,539 people here and more than 13,900 across Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Five years in , this crisis has become normalized , with the only certainty as we face another day is that first responders are now better at resuscitating victims because , year over year , the calls have only continued to increase . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last week , Prime Minister Justin Trudeau appointed his top ministers to a committee tasked with responding to the COVID-19 crisis . At that point , Canada had only 30 confirmed cases . Of the 21 B.C. cases , four of the patients have fully recovered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not to belittle the concerns about COVID-19 becoming a global pandemic , but with nearly 14,000 dead already , no committee &amp;mdash ; high-level or otherwise &amp;mdash ; has yet been struck to devise a national addictions strategy that would deal not only with opioids , but also the biggest killer , which is alcohol . A 2019 report by the Canadian Institute for Health Information found that 10 Canadians die every day from substance use , and three-quarters of those deaths are alcohol-related. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the 2019 election , the issue flared briefly after Conservatives placed ads &amp;mdash ; mainly through ethnic media &amp;mdash ; claiming that Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s Liberals planned to legalize all drugs , including heroin . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Already beleaguered , Trudeau not only denied it , he quickly disavowed the resolution overwhelmingly passed at the party&amp;rsquo ; s 2018 convention that called on the Canadian government to treat addiction as a health issue , expand treatment and harm reduction services , and decriminalize personal-use possession of all drugs , with people diverted away from the criminal courts and into treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trudeau disavowed it again this week when a Liberal backbencher&amp;rsquo ; s private member&amp;rsquo ; s bill was put on the order paper . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13131;TOOLONG ... title= " Liberal member of Parliament Nathaniel Erskine-Smith ( in front ) pictured in 2018. " alt= " Liberal member of Parliament Nathaniel Erskine-Smith ( in front ) pictured in 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press " **28;13167;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 919119 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Depending on how you read Bill C-236 , it&amp;rsquo ; s either calling for decriminalization or legalization . Regardless , the fact that Nathaniel Erskine-Smith&amp;rsquo ; s bill will be debated at least gets it on the political agenda because unless there are some major changes , Canadians are going to continue dying at these unacceptably high rates that have already caused the national life expectancy to drop . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Erskine-Smith , an Ontario MP from the Beaches-East York riding , favours a Portugal-style plan of which decriminalization plays only a small part . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But parliamentary rules forbid private member&amp;rsquo ; s bills from committing the government to any new spending , so he said his bill could only narrowly focus on decriminalization. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The slim bill says charges could be laid &amp;ldquo ; only if &amp;hellip ; the individual can not be adequately dealt with by a warning or referral ( to a program agency or service provider ) &amp;hellip ; or by way of alternative measures . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Erskine-Smith disagreed with the suggestion that it gives too much discretionary power to police &amp;mdash ; especially since in B.C. , it&amp;rsquo ; s prosecutors , not police , who determine whether charges are laid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , what he proposes is quite different from what happens in Portugal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There , police have no discretionary power . People found with illicit drugs are arrested and taken to the police station where the drugs are weighed , and the person is either charged with possession and sent to court or diverted to the Commission for the Dissuasion of Drug Use to meet with social workers , therapists and addictions specialists who map out a plan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since private members&amp;rsquo ; bills rarely pass , Erskine-Smith doesn&amp;rsquo ; t hold out much hope for his . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It created a firestorm on social media , with some recovery advocates pitted against advocates for harm reduction , including full legalization. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;13197;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;13239;TOOLONG ... deaths decrease in B.C. , but officials say safer drug supply **27;13274;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;13303;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;13820;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1231222 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Inequality is bad for your mental health . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Famed British epidemiologist Richard Wilkinson couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be coming to a more appropriate city to deliver his message that material inequality has powerful , negative psychological effects . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Metro Vancouver could be the poster child for a society with sharp disparities in wealth , which Wilkinson has shown makes people more prone to such things as heart disease , anxiety and drug use . The rich or established in this city have sparkling homes while the rest agonize over getting by in one of the most unaffordable housing markets in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Exacerbating the wealth gap , Metro Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s median wages are ninth worst of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s 10 largest cities . Metro Vancouver ranks a dismal 50th for wages when compared to North American cities , according to Andy Yan , head of Simon Fraser University&amp;rsquo ; s City Program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , despite the struggles of the city&amp;rsquo ; s lower and middle classes , Metro Vancouver has won the dubious honour of being dubbed the &lt;a href= " http : **34;13850;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; " supercar capital " of the world&lt;/a&gt; , with the number of Aston Martins , Bugattis and Rolls Royces running far out of proportion to the population . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The influential co-author of the &lt;a href= " https : **33;13886;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The Inner Level : How More Equal Societies Reduce Stress , Restore Sanity and Improve Everyone 's Well-Being&lt;/a&gt; has worked with Kate Pickett for more than a decade to map out just how much the realities and perceptions of inequality contribute to fragile egos , addiction , depression , obesity and violence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Compared to other democratic countries , Wilkinson&amp;rsquo ; s research shows , Canada is in the middle of the pack in the gap between rich and poor , less divided by money than the U.S. , but &lt;a href= " http : **34;13921;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;far less equal than Norway , Denmark , Austria and Japan&lt;/a&gt; . Still , the Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives says Canada&amp;rsquo ; s wealthiest 87 families collectively own the same amount as the lowest-earning 12 million Canadians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;13957;TOOLONG ... title= " Narcissism levels rise in unequal societies , says British epidemiologist Richard Wilkinson , yet low self-esteem is more likely , including feeling compelled to self-medicate with alcohol and drugs . " alt= " Narcissism levels rise in unequal societies , says British epidemiologist Richard Wilkinson , yet low self-esteem is more likely , including feeling compelled to self-medicate with alcohol and drugs . " data-portal-copyright= " JohnHoulihan.com " **28;13993;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1231368 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Metro Vancouverites will be able to hear about the wide-ranging downsides of economic hierarchies when Wilkinson , professor emeritus at the University of Nottingham&amp;rsquo ; s Medical School , gives a free lecture at the Queen Elizabeth Theatre at 7 p.m. on April 2 , as part of SFU&amp;rsquo ; s Public Square Community Summit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Both Wilkinson and Pickett , a professor of epidemiology at the University of York , have been in-demand speakers since their bestseller The Spirit Level was published in 2009 , winning multiple awards . It provided devastating evidence that both those on low incomes , and perhaps surprisingly the rich , are all hurt by inequality . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In a telephone interview from his home in York , England , Wilkinson said he&amp;rsquo ; s been to Canada and Vancouver several times and generally finds the country &amp;ldquo ; clean and modern and not as hard-edged as the U.S.&amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilkinson talked about how the &lt;a href= " http : **34;14023;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;prevalence of luxury sports cars&lt;/a&gt; in Metro Vancouver and elsewhere can be excruciating for those who witness them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;14059;TOOLONG ... title= " Despite many displays of opulence in Metro Vancouver , this chart shows that median household incomes in the city rank a dismal 50th among North American cities . ( Source : Andy Yan , Simon Fraser University City Program ) " alt= " Despite many displays of opulence in Metro Vancouver , this chart shows that median household incomes in the city rank a dismal 50th among North American cities . ( Source : Andy Yan , Simon Fraser University City Program ) " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;14095;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1231063 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are studies that show that people in more unequal areas are more likely to spend money on flashy stuff , particularly flashy-looking cars , &amp;rdquo ; Wilkinson said , noting supercars are few and far between in his hometown , located two hours north of London . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I remember reading how sports cars are a bit of a nuisance , because you can&amp;rsquo ; t park them by the side of the road because people deliberately scratch them . That shows resentment . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The perception of &lt;a href= " http : **34;14125;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;extreme inequality&lt;/a&gt; that goes along with everything from high-end cars to glittering jewellery outlets to overbuilt mansions , Wilkinson said , can cause people to feel inferior and lack in confidence , which can lead them to withdraw and feel depressed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; However , others , as we argue in the book , pick themselves up . For their own self-advancement they start to flaunt their professional achievements , instead of being modest about them , &amp;rdquo ; said the expert in the so-called social determinants of health . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If you&amp;rsquo ; re worried about how you&amp;rsquo ; re seen and judged in terms of status , then you either feel overcome with insecure self-worth or you respond the opposite way and try to show yourself off in a very positive light , like by buying expensive cars . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **34;14161;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Narcissism levels rise in unequal societies&lt;/a&gt; , says Wilkinson , yet low self-esteem is more likely , including feeling compelled to self-medicate with alcohol and drugs . Which makes one wonder whether it&amp;rsquo ; s more than a coincidence that Metro Vancouver is one of the centres of the opioid crisis . The city accounts for more than its share of the 2.5 people in the province dying each day of overdoses , &lt;a href= " http : **34;14197;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;four out of five being men . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Wilkinson finds Canada&amp;rsquo ; s little-discussed gender breakdown on overdose deaths intriguing , since the current focus in Britain is on the rising number of drug fatalities among women . The grim subject deserves further research , he suggested , since evidence suggests it is more common for women who are stressed to &amp;ldquo ; eat for comfort . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;14233;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;14275;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " JONATHAN HAYWARD " **28;15260;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1228971 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; British Columbia Indigenous Relations Minister Scott Fraser acknowledged there was a disagreement over the natural gas pipeline going through traditional territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are developing a protocol here &amp;hellip ; to recognize rights and titles for the future , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I ask for some space and calm to continue that good work , and allow the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en people to review the arrangement and to endorse it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chief Woos , one of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary leaders , called the draft a milestone for everyone involved but said the &amp;ldquo ; degree of satisfaction is not what we expected . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He stressed that the hereditary chiefs remain opposed to the pipeline in their traditional territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We are going to be continuing to look at some more conversations with B.C. and of course with the proponent and further conversation with the RCMP , &amp;rdquo ; Woos said . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not over yet . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A joint statement released by representatives of Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en Nation , the province and the federal government acknowledged that they had not come to an agreement on the pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shortly after the proposal was announced , Coastal GasLink issued a statement saying it would resume construction activities in the Morice River area , which is near the Unist&amp;rsquo ; ot&amp;rsquo ; en Healing Centre , on Monday . It also said the company is committed to talking with all Indigenous groups along its route . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The company had agreed to pause construction during the talks between the hereditary chiefs and the ministers , which began Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RCMP had also pledged to cease patrols along the Morice West Forest Service Road during the discussions . The Mounties did not respond to requests for comment Sunday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The dispute over the pipeline has spurred solidarity protests across the country that have disrupted passenger and freight train service over the last three weeks . Police have recently moved to dismantle some of the blockades. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en are governed by both a traditional hereditary chief system and elected band councils . A majority of its councils have approved the pipeline , but some of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary chiefs oppose it running through their traditional territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gary Naziel , a Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary subchief who wants the pipeline built , said he hasn&amp;rsquo ; t seen the proposed arrangement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What&amp;rsquo ; s done behind closed doors hasn&amp;rsquo ; t been shared yet , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; But it will be settled in the Feast Hall &amp;mdash ; all this stuff that&amp;rsquo ; s been going on has to come to Feast Hall . We will deal with it there . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naziel said no date has been set to discuss the proposal , but he noted it&amp;rsquo ; s a good first step and he&amp;rsquo ; s satisfied that the pipeline is going ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The projects are going forward , so that way we can get the benefits for our education and language , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; If everybody is satisfied , that&amp;rsquo ; s fine by me . Internally we need to fix things in the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en Nation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We already know we had titles and rights to this land . We know we own this land . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The dispute also involves other unsettled land rights and title issues , including who has the right to negotiate with governments and corporations , the fact that the land is not covered by a treaty and remains unceded , and a 1997 court case that recognized the hereditary chiefs&amp;rsquo ; authority and the exclusive right of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en peoples to the land but did not specify the boundaries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lawyer Peter Grant , who represented the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en and neighbouring Gitxsan First Nation , said the proposal is not a treaty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a draft arrangement , but I think it&amp;rsquo ; s very powerful , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The secretary of the Mohawk Nation of Kahnawake said activists have decided to maintain their rail blockade on the territory south of Montreal , at least for now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kenneth Deer said the Mohawks want more clarification on the agreement between the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary chiefs and the federal government before making a final decision . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a big decision to decide to take down the barricade or not , and they want to make sure they have everything before they make a decision , &amp;rdquo ; he said Sunday outside the entrance to the barricade , where Mohawk flags flew from a tent and pointed wooden shelter protected by low concrete barriers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Deer , who said he&amp;rsquo ; s been in contact with hereditary chiefs , said good things came out of the meeting in B.C. , as well as &amp;ldquo ; some things that were not so good . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said the agreement includes discussions on who are custodians of the land , as well as a recognition of the hereditary chiefs , which he described as &amp;ldquo ; significant . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; However , the pipeline is not resolved , and that&amp;rsquo ; s a very big issue , not only for the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en chiefs but for everybody , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; -- With files from Colette Derworiz in Edmonton and Morgan Lowrie in Kahnawake&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;15290;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; " data-portal-copyright= " Jenelle Schneider Jenelle Schnei " **28;15583;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1224981 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The interminable constitutional trial over the provision of private health care in B.C. &amp;mdash ; dubbed The Flying Dutchman of the B.C. Supreme Court by lawyers &amp;mdash ; finally made it back to harbour Friday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In many ways , what should have been an intellectual cruise involving a few months of written argument and data from the medical system became a veritable Royal Commission that has generated a library of evidence . It involved 194 days of proceedings over 3 1/2 years that mocked timely justice and badly bruised the belief that the courts can act as an effective brake on bad government by providing a remedy to unconstitutional law-making. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The length of time and cost of the case are an argument that the courts are no longer capable of efficiently resolving such thorny questions of social policy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As intervener lawyer Joseph Arvay said : &amp;ldquo ; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;This case would appear to be , at least in my experience , the most complex Charter case I 've ever seen . And one that truly does test the institutional competence of the court . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At a time when more and more Canadians think the country isn&amp;rsquo ; t working , the dysfunctional legal system must be considered a primary reason . Indigenous people have run into the same problem trying to hold governments to account through litigation &amp;mdash ; they too have found themselves bogged down in endless process that pours millions-of-dollars into lawyers&amp;rsquo ; pockets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The duration brought its own risks and demands on memory &amp;mdash ; the constitutional challenge of two provisions of the Medicare Protection Act was nearly derailed late last year when B.C. Supreme Court Justice John Steeves required health care . This week Steeves couldn&amp;rsquo ; t remember what prevented the government from enforcing the law . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There is in place a consent order allowing private surgical services to continue , &amp;rdquo ; plaintiffs&amp;rsquo ; lawyer , Robert Grant , explained &amp;mdash ; issued by Justice Janet Winteringham following an injunction she granted in November 2018 after Victoria amended the law and planned enforcement , though its validity was in question . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Did I sign ? that ( order ) ? &amp;rdquo ; the justice asked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; No , it carries on from Justice ? Winteringham , &amp;rdquo ; Grant replied . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So , it has to do with the amendments , as I say , that occurred during my trial , &amp;rdquo ; Steeves said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;15613;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;15655;TOOLONG ... health care battle in judge 's hands but expected to land in Canada 's top **26;15690;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Exactly , &amp;rdquo ; Grant said . &amp;ldquo ; And what it did is effectively to ? confirm they won&amp;rsquo ; t be employed until your lordship ? ruled , so that allowed the status quo to continue . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Maybe ( government lawyer Jonathan ) Penner can give the minister my ? compliments for making my job easier , &amp;rdquo ; the justice quipped. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two private clinics and a handful of patients launched the litigation roughly a decade ago because the constraints on dual practice by doctors and private health insurance would force private clinics and diagnostic centres across the province to close . No evidence or data was offered by either government to support the assertion that the private clinics cause harm to the public system and B.C. has not measured the impact or effect of the clinics that have existed for a generation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; They would have welcomed an opportunity for an impartial objective empirical study , &amp;rdquo ; Grant said . &amp;ldquo ; It might have made this litigation unnecessary as it would have confirmed that private surgeries did not have any adverse effects on public surgeries . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Vancouver lawyer accused the government of grossly mischaracterizing and misrepresenting evidence in closing statements he said were little more than fearmongering . He pointed out B.C. has had de facto private health care for 20 years and the sky hasn&amp;rsquo ; t fallen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To end that status quo , he added , would make the public health system even more overcrowded as the 65,000 private surgeries done annually join already historically long waiting lists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Nobody gets ? ahead in the public queue by having private ? surgery , &amp;rdquo ; Grant explained . &amp;ldquo ; What happens is you leave the queue . ? You&amp;rsquo ; re not jumping the queue , you&amp;rsquo ; re leaving the ? queue . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead of relevant data , the federal and provincial governments resorted to fervid rhetoric about the prospect of U.S.-style health care and the poor languishing in dirty beds at the mercy of greedy , unscrupulous physicians . At one point they accused a respected neurosurgeon of having &amp;ldquo ; scaled back public work because he wanted more time to smell the roses and read a book . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is an egregious mischaracterization of the evidence , &amp;rdquo ; Grant told Steeves. &amp;ldquo ; In fact ( the doctor ) suffered a family tragedy . His wife developed terminal cancer &amp;mdash ; and he needed to scale back his public on-call commitments as he couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be operating all night due to his family&amp;rsquo ; s needs &amp;hellip ; With his wife&amp;rsquo ; s illness and passing , he could not do this with four children . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Grant swept the broader accusations aside too : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If there was one shred of ? evidence that doctors practising ? in the private system , just one piece , one example ? of a doctor performing private pay surgery , ? shirking a commitment to the public system or ? causing any problem at all for the public system , ? we can be certain they would have called that ? evidence , but they didn&amp;rsquo ; t. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He urged Steeves to draw an adverse inference from the government&amp;rsquo ; s failure to call a single doctor or senior administrator to give evidence about problems the public system had experienced as a result of private surgeries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The evidence in this trial shows thousands of British Columbians wait too long past government-mandated medically maximum acceptable waits for their condition , risking progression of disease and in some cases shortened lifespan or death , &amp;rdquo ; Grant concluded . &amp;ldquo ; In evidence in this trial , is the fact that in one year , in just one health region in B.C. , Fraser Health , 308 patients died waiting for medically necessary surgery . B.C. patients need a &amp;lsquo ; safety valve&amp;rsquo ; . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before the courtroom emptied , Steeves said : &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m looking forward to completing my judgment and setting my name on it , and , once I&amp;rsquo ; ve done that , I&amp;rsquo ; ll join the rest of the world watching the progress of this case with great interest . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He is expected to take several months , perhaps longer , on his ruling . Appeals are expected to follow , which means a final decision could be two , three or more years away . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Outside of court , Dr. Brian Day , the face of the litigation , said he was relieved that the trial was over . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Suffering patients -- the more than 30,000 a year who wait past the government 's own maximum acceptable wait times , and the 18-a-week who die on public wait lists in B.C. -- need the justice system to rescue themselves from their plight , " he said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " It 's astonishing that we are the only country on earth that outlaws private health insurance . " data-portal-copyright= " STAN HONDA " **28;15970;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1225500 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;16000;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Greater Toronto and Metro Vancouver are growing far faster through immigration than any other North American city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The two Canadian metropolises are absorbing many more immigrants per capita than the United States&amp;rsquo ; top immigrant-receiving cities , such as New York , Miami , Los Angeles and Washington , D.C. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rapid growth of &lt;a href= " http : **34;16036;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Toronto and Vancouver&lt;/a&gt; through immigration comes as the federal Liberals in 2019 welcomed the largest number of new immigrants to the country in more than a century at 341,000. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The concentrated flow into Toronto and Vancouver is occurring as the province of Quebec has reduced its immigration levels by 20 per cent , leading to fewer moving last year to Montreal ( 34,620 ) . The two Canadian cities&amp;rsquo ; immigration numbers also coincide with tightening border rules in the U.S. , which has long allowed in &lt;a href= " http : **34;16072;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;three times fewer immigrants per capita than Canada . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Greater Toronto and Metro Vancouver , the latter of which experienced a record 13-per-cent rise in new immigrants in 2019 , are proving to be distinctly powerful magnets for foreign-born newcomers , even within their own provinces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although it&amp;rsquo ; s often said Canada is a &amp;ldquo ; big country , &amp;rdquo ; most immigrants focus on heading to the country&amp;rsquo ; s biggest cities . Sixteen of 20 newcomers to British Columbia in 2019 headed directly for Metro Vancouver , while one of 20 set up home in the Greater Victoria region . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver real-estate marketer Bob Rennie and associate Andrew Ramlo told the Independent Contractors and Businesses Association last week that a projected &lt;a href= " http : **34;16108;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; " demographic crunch " &lt;/a&gt; involving immigrants will bring one million more people into Metro Vancouver in the next 20 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That will require building 450,000 new homes &amp;mdash ; the equivalent of &amp;ldquo ; another Vancouver , Burnaby , New West and Coquitlam , &amp;rdquo ; said the real-estate marketers . Other analysts say it&amp;rsquo ; s worth monitoring the impact of such high in-migration on not only local housing , but on transit and the labour market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16144;TOOLONG ... title= " The Vancouver skyline . The Independent Contractors and Businesses Association was told last week that a projected ' demographic crunch ' involving immigrants will bring one million more people into Metro Vancouver in the next 20 years . " data-portal-copyright= " Francis Georgian " **28;16180;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1225730 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jack Jedwab , president of Metropolis Canada , says Metro Vancouver , despite its relatively small size of 2.6 million , is projected to be the fifth highest immigrant-receiving city in North America in total numbers after only New York , Toronto , Miami and Los Angeles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A Postmedia analysis of Jedwab&amp;rsquo ; s data on North American cities revealed that Metro Vancouver and Greater Toronto take in a much higher per capita proportion of immigrants each year than any major U.S. city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The record number of new immigrants to Greater Toronto in 2019 ( 117,000 ) boosted the city&amp;rsquo ; s population by 1.9 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The rising immigrant population of Metro Vancouver ( 40,020 ) hiked the West Coast metropolis&amp;rsquo ; s population by 1.6 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The recent arrival of 168,000 immigrants to New York City in one year makes the Big Apple the top immigrant-receiving city in North America in gross numbers . But the population of the New York census region of 20 million grew through immigration by only a small margin compared to Vancouver and Toronto : 0.8 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The second-largest immigrant-receiving metropolis in the U.S. , the Miami region of 6.2 million , grew by just 1.2 per cent in a year via 80,000 new immigrants . Los Angeles , with more than 12 million people , grew by a tiny 0.6 per cent through the arrival of 70,032 new immigrants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The U.S.&amp;rsquo ; s other top immigrant-receiving metropolises &amp;mdash ; Washington , D.C. , Chicago , Houston , the San Francisco area and Dallas/Fort Worth &amp;mdash ; all also expanded by less than 0.6 per cent annually as a result of immigrants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The speedier rates of immigration growth for Toronto and Vancouver were achieved without taking into account the arrival of temporary foreign-born newcomers to each city , particularly international students , whose overall numbers in 2019 ( 642,000 ) have doubled since 2015. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16210;TOOLONG ... title= " The Toronto downtown skyline . " data-portal-copyright= " Ernest Doroszuk " **28;16246;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1225734 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Greater Toronto and Metro Vancouver took in far more new international students and &lt;a href= " http : **34;16276;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;foreign guest workers&lt;/a&gt; in 2019 than they did immigrants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Metro Vancouver , the volume of &lt;a href= " https : **33;16312;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;non-permanent foreign-born residents&lt;/a&gt; who moved in ( 101,000 ) was more than double the number of immigrants . Yet analysts point out both permanent and non-permanent newcomers have an impact on housing , transit , wages and &lt;a href= " http : **34;16347;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;rental accommodation&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another geographical imbalance in immigration patterns reveals itself when figures are broken down by territory and province . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C ( mostly Metro Vancouver ) took in as many immigrants last year as all of Saskatchewan , Manitoba , Nova Scotia , Nunavut , Yukon , Prince Edward Island , Newfoundland and New Brunswick combined . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New Brunswick officials are lamenting they can not hold onto the meagre 5,000 to 6,000 or so a year who initially move to their Maritime province . A team of researchers this month &lt;a href= " https : **33;16383;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;found 50 per cent of immigrants leave New Brunswick&lt;/a&gt; after five years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Data on 2019 immigration levels also reveals striking changes in the origins of the 341,000 immigrants who arrived in Canada this year , compared to the 271,000 who came in 2015 , the first year of Justin Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Jedwab&amp;rsquo ; s data shows the proportion of immigrants coming to Canada from India has doubled since 2016 , to the point that that giant South Asian country&amp;rsquo ; s citizens now account for one in four of all new immigrants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;16418;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;16460;TOOLONG ... site graphically shows immigration and foreign-student trends in Vancouver and **28;16495;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;16525;TOOLONG ... Some are highly skilled . Since 2015 there has been a four-fold increase in &amp;ldquo ; software engineers and designers&amp;rdquo ; moving to B.C. ( 1,045 came last year ) , according to data obtained by Jedwab. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There have also been big jumps in immigrants arriving through semi-skilled and low-skilled immigration categories . In the past four years B.C. , particularly Metro Vancouver , has had increases of more than 300 per cent in &amp;ldquo ; restaurant and food service managers , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; retail managers , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; public relations managers , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; transport truck drivers , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;ldquo ; administrative officers&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; administrative assistants . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The number of Metro Vancouver immigration stories that can be mined from such data is unlimited . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;16658;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **33;16686;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **25;16721;TOOLONG &lt;a href= " https : **25;16748;TOOLONG " class= " twitter-follow-button " data-show-count= " false " &gt;Follow @DouglasTodd&lt;/a&gt; **25;16775;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;16802;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? NewsNationalStaff BlogsWorldIan Mulgrew : Reconciliation in danger of derailment by a minority opposed to rule of lawhttp : **37;16945;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;16984;TOOLONG ... title= " Police officers make an arrest during a raid on a Tyendinaga Mohawk Territory camp next to a blockaded railway crossing in Tyendinaga , Ont. , on February 24 , 2020. " data-portal-copyright= " CARLOS OSORIO " **28;17020;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1225196 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;17050;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; The mob opposing the Coastal GasLink pipeline refuses to acknowledge the complicated legal reality of First Nations reconciliation or Aboriginal rights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , our politicians look like they don&amp;rsquo ; t have a clue or any confidence in what is being done to settle Indigenous grievances and the cops appear more interested in filing overtime than clearing blockades so the country can function and people get to work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In its &lt;a href= " https : **33;17086;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;latest ruling&lt;/a&gt; on Aboriginal rights involving the Innu in Labrador , the Supreme Court of Canada reiterated on Friday its past pronouncements , but few noticed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The court has made it clear &amp;mdash ; Indigenous sovereignty was extinguished and the federal government calls the shots in Canada , even for Aboriginal people . &amp;nbsp ; Still , the high bench emphasized Section 35 of the Constitution specifically recognizes Aboriginal and treaty rights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are about one million First Nations people across the country ( not counting the 65,000 Inuit or 600,000 M&amp;eacute ; t is ) &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; and most are covered by a treaty that together with the constitution defines their relationship with governments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In B.C. , however , the colonial administration stopped signing treaties , leaving most of B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s roughly 250,000 First Nations today without a deal . &amp;nbsp ; Worse , politicians for most of B.C. history supported Indigenous policies that could have been drafted by the U.S. 7 **25;17121;TOOLONG Cavalry under Custer. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I think that era ended in 1991 when B.C. Chief Justice Allan McEachern rejected the Gitxsan and Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en Aboriginal claims in a 400-page judgment that was staggering in its tone-deaf condescension. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McEachern cribbed a Thomas Hobbes quote to describe Indigenous lives as &amp;ldquo ; nasty , brutish , and short . &amp;rdquo ; He then pointed out they didn&amp;rsquo ; t invent the wheel or have horses . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indigenous people had many reasons to be angry at how they were being treated ; McEachern was a lightning rod . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Within a year , a new NDP government precipitated a sea-change in Victoria . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It abandoned the long-held anti-Indigenous-rights stance , leading the B.C. Court of Appeal to reject McEachern&amp;rsquo ; s decision and order a new trial . And premier Mike Harcourt launched a process to sign modern treaties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1997 , the Supreme Court of Canada also &lt;a href= " https : **33;17148;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;tossed McEachern 's insulting ruling&lt;/a&gt; &amp;nbsp ; and sent the Gitxsan and Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en case back for a retrial . A generation later , that retrial has not taken place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , the Gitxsan and Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en bought into the promise of the nascent reconciliation movement . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unfortunately , the &lt;a href= " http : //www.bctreaty.ca/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;B.C. treaty-making process&lt;/a&gt; has not been as successful as hoped &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; some of the province&amp;rsquo ; s 200 bands refused to participate or angrily withdrew and there have been too few agreements given the hundreds of millions in tax money incinerated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The lack of progress has been frustrating because of the cost and years it takes to reach a pact or get a legal decision involving Indigenous rights . The discontent is exacerbated when most rulings are hard to fathom . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Supreme Court of Canada says Aboriginal title isn&amp;rsquo ; t the same as owning property ; Aboriginal title belongs to a group , not an individual . &amp;nbsp ; It&amp;rsquo ; s also for the benefit of future generations , not just the current one . So it can&amp;rsquo ; t simply be sold and individuals can&amp;rsquo ; t make decisions about it , except maybe in circumstances the court hasn&amp;rsquo ; t envisioned yet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In other words : &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s complicated ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet the treaty-making continues and both sides are still pursuing solutions outside the courtroom so the politicians and Indigenous people shape the future , not some judge . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As everyone knew it would be , the process of negotiating reconciliation has been fraught with difficulty , failure and false starts , especially in B.C. given its despicable record of First Nations relations and the lack of treaties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The issues we confront are not new &amp;mdash ; they were before the Supreme Court in 2013 , in a B.C. logging dispute . &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;In that unanimous decision , the high bench said Indigenous individuals could not exercise " community " rights by blocking a road without authorization from their band . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( R ) ights may sometimes be assigned to or exercised by individual members of Aboriginal communities , and entitlements may sometimes be created in their favour , &amp;rdquo ; Justice Louis LeBel wrote for the court . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To legitimize civil disobedience , he wrote , would be &amp;ldquo ; tantamount to condoning self-help remedies and would bring the administration of justice into disrepute . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It may well be , &amp;rdquo ; LeBel added , &amp;ldquo ; that , in appropriate circumstances , individual members can assert certain Aboriginal or treaty rights , as some of the interveners have proposed . But I would not , on the occasion of this appeal and at this stage of the development of the law , try to develop broad categories for these rights and to slot each right in the appropriate one . This is an important issue , but a definitive pronouncement in this regard can not be made in the circumstances of this case . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s why it&amp;rsquo ; s complicated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; LeBel believed that some community members might &amp;ldquo ; have a greater interest in the protection of the rights on their traditional family territory than do other members of the First Nation , and that this connection gives them a certain standing to raise the violation of their particular rights . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some might argue that opens the door for , say , a handful of hereditary chiefs to assert their clan interests to block a pipeline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Perhaps , but all the judges insisted that if Indigenous people believed their rights were being breached , they should ask for a judicial review rather than mounting barricades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the 8-0 , landmark 2014 &lt;a href= " https : **33;17183;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Tsilquot'in judgment , &lt;/a&gt; now-retired chief justice Beverley McLachlin confirmed that First Nations had rights , though government could still expropriate or place easements on Indigenous land . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Tsilquot&amp;rsquo ; in did not win their claim lock , stock and barrel , but rather a much smaller area of about 1,700 square kilometres &amp;mdash ; less than the size of Metro Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indigenous control of the land , insofar as they can benefit from it , the court explained , was constrained by the community nature of their rights and the need to look after the interest of future generations , which again was subjected to judicial review given the fiduciary obligations involved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As long as the government negotiated in good faith , carried out meaningful consultation and , presumably , was willing to cut a reasonable cheque &amp;mdash ; a mine , pipeline or industrial development could proceed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most importantly , although tortoise-like and expensive , the Tsilquot&amp;rsquo ; in decision indicated the process could work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; McLachlin called it the new &amp;ldquo ; governing ethos &amp;hellip ; of reconciliation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the last few weeks , the protesters have mocked that hope and the authenticity of the country&amp;rsquo ; s difficult but progressing reconciliation efforts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The majority of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en say they back the GasLink pipeline , are satisfied with the consultations and happy with the outcomes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet their rights are being ignored , ordinary commuters are having their lives disrupted , court injunctions are being flouted and the economy bruised . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These blockades are not just an inconvenience &amp;mdash ; they are an insidious attempt to derail reconciliation by a minority opposed to the rule of law . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;17218;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;17249;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;17287;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; Ian MulgrewWed , 26 Feb 2020 21:00:44 **45;17320;TOOLONG ... Bramham : It 's not enough to just keep overdose victims alivehttp : **35;17367;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17404;TOOLONG ... title= " Paramedics transport a woman suspected of an overdose. " alt= " Paramedics transport a woman suspected of an overdose. " data-portal-copyright= " Dan Janisse " **28;17440;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1224488 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There was some good news in the 2019 data from the B.C. Coroners Service . Overdose deaths in the province declined for the first time since fentanyl-tainted drugs hit the streets and a public health emergency was declared in 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The decrease was significant &amp;mdash ; down 36 per cent from 2018 &amp;mdash ; even though the death toll remains heartbreakingly high . As B.C. enters its fifth year of the crisis , nearly three British Columbians are dying every day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It does mean that all of the money poured into this crisis &amp;mdash ; for naloxone kits , the training for paramedics , medical professionals and laypeople in how to use naloxone , more supervised consumption sites , and more people now on prescriptions for drugs like methadone and Suboxone to staunch addicts&amp;rsquo ; opioid cravings &amp;mdash ; is keeping more people alive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But that&amp;rsquo ; s really where the good news ends . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alarmingly , the number of 911 calls has continued to climb . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Paramedics and other first responders took more than 24,000 calls last year , with calls spiking to more than 130 overdose alerts on &amp;ldquo ; cheque days&amp;rdquo ; or &amp;ldquo ; welfare Wednesdays. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Being revived from an overdose or living with an opioid addiction comes at a high cost . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Opioids affect the receptors in the brain , causing breathing to become dangerously slow , which in turn slows the heart and sometimes causing cardiac arrest . When the hearts doesn&amp;rsquo ; t pump at capacity , less oxygenated blood makes it to the brain . Without oxygen , brain cells die &amp;mdash ; and they don&amp;rsquo ; t regenerate. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s called toxic brain injury . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Within the coming weeks or months , the B.C. Centre for Disease Control will release data on the prevalence of brain injury among opioid users , including those who have been successfully restored to life with naloxone. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We know that many hundreds of people will need a lifetime of care , &amp;rdquo ; said Dr. Perry Kendall , who raised the alarm during the coroner&amp;rsquo ; s news conference earlier this week . &amp;ldquo ; It will be a tremendous burden . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s far from the only one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The burden carried by first responders is different and no less costly . They are burning out and checking out of the system , unable to cope physically , mentally or emotionally with the constant stress of being called to deal with all the overdoses. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;17470;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;17512;TOOLONG ... overdose deaths decrease , but officials say safer supply **27;17547;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not to say that harm-reduction measures aren&amp;rsquo ; t working . No one disputes that they are keeping many people alive . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But until now , little attention has been focused on the quality of their lives , post-overdose. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Five years into the public health emergency , Chief Coroner Lisa Lapointe said B.C. still doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have a comprehensive system that includes prevention , treatment and recovery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The lack of a seamless system is particularly problematic and even deadly for people in rural areas and those coming out of jails and prisons , according to Dr. Nel Wieman , senior medical officer at the First Nations Health Authority . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The numbers back that up . The death rate in the Northern Health Authority , at 22.5 per 100,000 , trails Vancouver Coastal , which has the highest rate , by a mere half a percentage point . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regardless of where they live , Lapointe said families frequently tell coroners how their loved ones managed through detox only to come out and die while on the waiting list for a recovery bed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The problem isn&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily that there aren&amp;rsquo ; t enough treatment beds . On most days , some lie empty because the government only funds treatment for welfare recipients . Everyone else has to pay their own way . And except for those with generous employee benefits , many can&amp;rsquo ; t afford treatment that comes at a cost of $900-plus a day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lapointe also decried the lack of provincial treatment standards . Different operators have different approaches . Some aren&amp;rsquo ; t evidence-based . Some are strictly abstinence-based and refuse to accept people on drug therapies such as methadone and Suboxone , even though without that , they are more vulnerable to overdose if they relapse. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Decriminalization is touted by some as the answer . Without fear of criminal charges , the theory is that people would be more willing to seek help . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They point to Portugal , where decriminalization was brought in as part of a massive overhaul of its drug treatment system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But decriminalization has only worked there because Portugal also boosted spending on the other three pillars &amp;mdash ; prevention , enforcement and treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here , the crucial elements are missing . With a minority government in Ottawa , the Liberals already have enough problems on their plate to risk raising the controversial idea of decriminalization. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meanwhile , most provinces , including B.C. , haven&amp;rsquo ; t invested enough in the infrastructure to put a Portugal-style model in place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This week , Mental Health and Addictions Minister Judy Darcy agreed that there are enormous gaps in B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s fragmented system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When the New Democrats were elected less than three years ago , she said the drug treatment system had been neglected for so long that it was not able to cope with regular tasks , let alone a public health emergency . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government is taking steps to fix that . But whether it&amp;rsquo ; s moving fast enough is a conversation that both the coroner and chief medical health officer are pushing British Columbians to have because the lives of many loved ones depend on it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;17576;TOOLONG " **36;17607;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamWed , 26 Feb 2020 00:12:09 **45;17645;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildHealthLocal HealthLocal **42;17692;TOOLONG Mulgrew : Home is more than where the heart ishttp : **38;17736;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;17776;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " PhotoMelon/Getty Images/iStockphoto " **28;17812;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1221941 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Home may be where the heart is , but ask a lawyer and you&amp;rsquo ; ll get a complicated answer and a six-figure bill . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , a B.C. Court of Appeal registrar , Tim Outerbridge , slashed Helen Sato&amp;rsquo ; s legal bill by 30 per cent &amp;mdash ; rolling back her legal costs to about $89,000 from $135,000 in a dispute about where her late brother Hiroyuki considered home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In &lt;a href= " https : **33;17842;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;his assessment&lt;/a&gt; of the invoices , Outerbridge said Helen Sato was overcharged in the appeal of a five-day inheritance trial that turned only on the question of where her brother Hiroyuki Sato was &amp;ldquo ; domiciled&amp;rdquo ; when he died . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In making this reduction , I recognize that this was an appeal of significant importance and accept that it was appropriate for the appellant to deploy significant resources given its high-stakes nature , &amp;rdquo ; Outerbridge wrote . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; However , at its core , this appeal had a narrow focus on the facts and law , a modest record , and very little procedural difficulty . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At one point , though , he said six lawyers worked a total of 225.6 hours at an effective hourly rate of $450 an hour on the issues &amp;mdash ; and Helen Sato lost . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although her brother Hiroyuki lived with his wife , worked and had friends in Luxembourg , and hadn&amp;rsquo ; t lived in Canada since 1999 , the courts concluded he was &amp;ldquo ; domiciled&amp;rdquo ; in B.C. and his sisters and their children were disinherited. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This meant his estate of about $2 million went to his Japanese wife , Makiko. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The case drew legal attention because the applicable provincial law at the time held that Sato&amp;rsquo ; s 2013 marriage revoked his 2011 will . Under Luxembourg law , the will would have remained valid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. law has since been changed and , after the &lt;i&gt;Wills , Estates and Succession Act &lt;/i&gt; came into effect on March 31 , 2014 , a marriage no longer revokes a will . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hiroyuki &amp;ldquo ; Rex&amp;rdquo ; Sato , who immigrated from Japan in 1969 , was a global banker whose career saw him working and living in Toronto , Vancouver , the Cayman Islands , Tokyo and Guernsey . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He moved to Luxembourg in 2009 and , for income tax purposes , the Canada Revenue Agency had considered Sato a non-resident since 1999. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During a visit to family in B.C. in May 2011 , he wrote a will leaving the bulk of his estate to his two sisters , naming Helen as executrix , and their children . He apparently never returned to the province . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In April 2013 , he married Makiko in Luxembourg , where he kept his personal effects , filed taxes and had inquired into whether he would be eligible for an old age pension . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But in 2014 he was diagnosed with cancer . Sato died in Japan in 2015 while receiving medical treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , B.C. Supreme Court Justice Gordon Funt concluded Sato was &amp;ldquo ; domiciled&amp;rdquo ; in B.C. at the time of his marriage because he asserted to the CRA when he left the country that he would return and intended to retire here . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Funt was bound by &lt;a href= " https : **33;17877;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;a 1959 case&lt;/a&gt; in which the Supreme Court of Canada said a person&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; domicile&amp;rdquo ; was determined by a two-pronged test : Did Sato reside in Luxembourg and did he intend to make it his permanent home indefinitely ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Sato lived in Luxembourg , Funt said he did not intend to make it his permanent home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He called the &amp;ldquo ; Key Document&amp;rdquo ; a CRA **27;17912;TOOLONG form filed by Sato when he moved to the Caymans in which he stated he planned to retire in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Helen appealed , saying Funt interpreted and applied the high bench&amp;rsquo ; s test too narrowly and &amp;ldquo ; in a manner incompatible with fairness , public policy , and modern conceptions of a person&amp;rsquo ; s intention to settle . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the &lt;a href= " https : **33;17941;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Court of Appeal agreed&lt;/a&gt; with Funt &amp;mdash ; the will was invalid under the old provincial law . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( T ) he deceased was not particularly fluent in French , which was the principal language in Luxembourg . He also found that the fact that the plaintiff was Japanese , and not from Luxembourg , militated against finding that the deceased intended to retire there . &amp;hellip ; There was no written document reflecting an intention to change his previously expressed intention to retire in Canada . &amp;hellip ; While the deceased had made several statements in the past about a desire to retire in Japan , those did not support the proposition that the deceased intended to reside in Luxembourg permanently . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The appeal was heard in a day and involved limited factual disputes , no transcript evidence , and no interlocutory applications , Outerbridge noted in his ruling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; ( Mark ) Weintraub , Q.C . ( of Clark Wilson LLP ) had primary carriage of this appeal and is experienced in the field of estates and trusts , having been called to the bar in 1983 , &amp;rdquo ; the registrar added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He was not counsel at trial and worked with three other partners on this file , ranging in years of call from 1997 to 2010 and hourly rates from $385 to $575 . He employed one associate , called to the bar in 2017 , with a rate of between $240 and $295 . A sixth outside counsel argued the appeal , called to the bar in 1986 , who billed 28.3 hours of time for preparation and attendance at a rate of $550 per hour , eventually reducing his invoice to $15,000 , exclusive of taxes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I accept Makiko Sato&amp;rsquo ; s argument that the use of six counsel resulted in some duplication of effort . &amp;hellip ; While I agree it may have been reasonable to involve additional counsel for some aspects of the appeal , particularly to provide an impartial view of the issues , I am unable to agree that the level of responsibility justifies the full amount of time billed . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Court of Appeal ordered costs borne by Sato&amp;rsquo ; s estate , blaming the litigation on his failure to clarify his will after being diagnosed with cancer . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;17976;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;18007;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;18045;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; Ian MulgrewFri , 21 Feb 2020 23:17:41 **45;18078;TOOLONG ...
