No charges were laid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , he was twice arrested and convicted , but never jailed for assault or for breaching no-contact orders as part of his probation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He spray-painted one of her homes with racist epithets , torched another and dropped off an eviscerated rat at yet another . Police were called . No charges were laid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It all ended 12 years ago when , against incredible odds , the United States granted her asylum under the United Nations Convention Against Torture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She didn&amp;rsquo ; t have a lawyer , only two law students who with a professor&amp;rsquo ; s help took it on as a class project . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; U.S. Immigration Judge Kenneth Josephson relied on court precedents in concluding that domestic violence constitutes persecution , noting , &amp;ldquo ; If the government is unable or unwilling to control persecution , it matters not who inflicts it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There was no meaningful assistance provided to her , &amp;rdquo ; he said , according to a transcription of his oral decision . He noted that she had made more than 30 attempts to get help from police and spent time in more than a dozen different transition houses across Canada and the United States . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Obviously , Canada is a democratic , first-world country , &amp;rdquo ; Josephson said . &amp;ldquo ; While it is rare for a citizen of Canada to seek asylum , it is not rare to have claims presented on the basis of domestic violence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The judge also leaned heavily on Lisa Rupert&amp;rsquo ; s affidavit describing how women are treated by Canadian police and courts . Rupert is the YWCA&amp;rsquo ; s vice-president of housing services and violence protection in Vancouver . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Between 2003 and 2016 , only 79 of 276 Canadian applicants &lt;a href= " https : **33;18226;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;were given asylum&lt;/a&gt; , according to the U.S. Justice Department . Because the reasons for decisions aren&amp;rsquo ; t tracked , a spokesman said it&amp;rsquo ; s not known how many were escaping domestic violence or gangs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because Rachel is still deemed by Canadian police to be at high risk , Rachel is a pseudonym . For her protection , other identifying details have been deliberately omitted or altered from the mountains of documents that she has meticulously saved over the years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At our first meeting , Rachel insisted on one thing : &amp;ldquo ; This story is not about him ( the perpetrator ) or the people he is involved with . &amp;hellip ; They get enough publicity for being the creepy people who they are . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The story , she said , is about the failure of the Canadian police and courts to protect her and others like her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel is furious with Canada . She bitterly points to the country&amp;rsquo ; s boast that it is a world leader when it comes to women&amp;rsquo ; s rights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Between the RCMP and the court system , they dropped the ball and slid me down a million crevices , and then they did everything they could to cover it up . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now in her mid-50s , she lives at the edge of poverty in subsidized housing , scraping by on part-time and temporary work to supplement a $212-a-month disability pension from the U.S. government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I want the Canadian government to acknowledge what happened and repair as much of the damage as they can , &amp;rdquo ; she said during one of many conversations over the past six months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel has paid dearly for her safety . It&amp;rsquo ; s cost her everything she&amp;rsquo ; s ever had and nearly everyone she&amp;rsquo ; s known and loved . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She can never return to Canada . If she were to come even for a visit , she might be denied re-entry to the U.S. because the reason she was given asylum is that she&amp;rsquo ; s at risk if she returns home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel has had to reinvent herself in a place where no one knew her or why she was there . She&amp;rsquo ; s had to do it without any credentials , because her hard-earned college certificates are in her old name , and without job references because contacting Canadian employers risks having her new identity exposed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She&amp;rsquo ; s struggled with the effects of the trauma and abuse she&amp;rsquo ; s endured , as well as guilt over the pain her life has caused her children . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Exile has also alienated her from Canada&amp;rsquo ; s safety net , including health care , social assistance and the Canada Pension Plan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s in addition to what she lost earlier when fear forced her to give up permanent custody of one of her children , cut off contact with her elderly parents , abruptly leave jobs and sell the family home she inherited from her parents in order to finance her fugitive life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After 12 years in hiding , Rachel yearns for home . Canada Day , Canadian Thanksgiving and even Boxing Day trigger memories of happier times and thoughts about what might have been . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When she contemplated visiting Canada earlier this year , Canadian police advised her that she would be at high risk even if she only came for a few days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The United States is the only place on the continent where she is safe . The man who hunted and abused her can&amp;rsquo ; t cross the border because of his criminal convictions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But even now , she&amp;rsquo ; s extremely cautious , fearing he&amp;rsquo ; ll find her again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , her abuser has carried on . He&amp;rsquo ; s served jail time for forcibly entering a home and assaulting another woman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;FATEFUL FIRST MEETING&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nearly 30 years ago , the vivacious , single , 20-something mom was singing with a band in a bar and attracted the unwanted attention of a guy who was never going to take no for an answer . It changed her world forever . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After she rebuffed him at the bar , he surreptitiously followed her home that night . The stalking had begun . He&amp;rsquo ; d turn up at odd places . When she refused to go to his house for a barbecue with her child , he called repeatedly until she finally relented . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She thought that might be the end of it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was only the beginning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His home was a grow-op . When she realized that , she grabbed her child and fled . He grabbed a rifle and fired a shot at her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The phone was already ringing when she walked in the door of her home . She knew too much , he said . If she made trouble , his gang would kill her and her family . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel changed her phone number , moved and quit her job . But a few weeks later , he was standing over her in her bedroom with a knife . He raped her repeatedly , pressing a pillow into her face to muffle her screams so she wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t wake her child . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It went on for three days before he agreed that the child should be allowed to go stay with her father . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the next few weeks whenever she left the room , he went with her , carrying the switchblade knife . He began inviting some of his friends over . The more compliant she was , the more freedom he gave her . She began plotting her escape to a friend&amp;rsquo ; s house in another community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But he found out , took her car keys and her money and assaulted her . A few weeks later , he coerced her into taking him with her and the violence escalated . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He punished minor slights by locking her in the basement . In her U.S. immigration affidavit , Rachel wrote that he started humming the music from Psycho. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The RCMP report from one of the assaults that sent Rachel to hospital includes her statement describing how he wrapped a sheet around her neck and choked her before he lunged at her with a large knife . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was thrown against a wall , thrown to the ground and kicked , according to the RCMP victim assistance supplementary report . He kept repeating that he was going to kill her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When police interviewed Rachel about the assault , they didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to hear about anything that had gone before that , she told the immigration judge . They refused to listen when she tried to tell them about how he&amp;rsquo ; d coerced her into living with him , tortured and beaten her before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , they were the first of many to describe him as her boyfriend and suggest the violence was the result of her bad choices . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although he was arrested , they didn&amp;rsquo ; t detain him . They escorted him out of town as if it were all part of a Wild West movie . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was no movie . A few days later , Rachel was released from hospital . As she was scrambling to pack the car and leave , he came out from behind the garage , grinning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Where are we going now ? &amp;rdquo ; he asked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A month later and in another town , he beat her until she was unconscious . Once again , police weren&amp;rsquo ; t interested in what had happened before , only what had happened that night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was charged with aggravated assault , but he later pleaded guilty to assault and was sentenced to nine months of probation and ordered to attend anger-management classes . There was no restraining order . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That night , he found her and raped her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18261;TOOLONG ... title= " As part of a relentless campaign to control her , Rachel 's tormentor coerced her into prostitution and made her audition for a porn film . His abuse was only beginning . " alt= " As part of a relentless campaign to control her , Rachel 's tormentor coerced her into prostitution and made her audition for a porn film . His abuse was only beginning . " data-portal-copyright= " CARL DE SOUZA " **28;18297;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1221409 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Within that first year , he coerced her into prostitution and made her audition for a porn film . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He also got her pregnant . When she refused to have an abortion , he assaulted her . Police came , but no charges were laid . A month after the child was born , he breached the order , robbed and assaulted her , burning her with a cigarette and punching her in the jaw . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Strongly recommend that the accused be released only if a restraining order is put into effect , &amp;rdquo ; the attending officer wrote . &amp;ldquo ; No contact direct or indirect as accused harassing victim by repeated phone calls . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also in the report is the accused&amp;rsquo ; s comment : &amp;ldquo ; She&amp;rsquo ; ll pay for this . She will know how this feels . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why police responded as they did , why he was never jailed for breaching no-contact orders and why he was never jailed at all are all questions that haunt Rachel and remain unanswered . Police don&amp;rsquo ; t comment on individual cases and , aside from their decisions , judges don&amp;rsquo ; t comment at all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For 17 years , Rachel describes her life as a cat-and-mouse chase . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I thought he&amp;rsquo ; d eventually give up and move on . I didn&amp;rsquo ; t think it would be a 17-year problem or that I would eventually have to leave the country , &amp;rdquo ; she told me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I kept thinking , &amp;lsquo ; Now , the police will do something . Now , it&amp;rsquo ; s going to stop . &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the timeline chronicling her torment runs to eight pages . He&amp;rsquo ; d breach the orders . She&amp;rsquo ; d escape to a shelter and he&amp;rsquo ; d find her . He&amp;rsquo ; d beat her ; police would be called . Only twice were restraining orders issued . He was never sent to jail . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When he couldn&amp;rsquo ; t catch and assault her , he&amp;rsquo ; d vandalize her home or threaten her employers . When he couldn&amp;rsquo ; t find her , he&amp;rsquo ; d threaten her parents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One summer , she and her child lived off the grid in a tent bought at Zellers . When the $300 that she&amp;rsquo ; d hidden from him ran out , she begged a telephone operator to find the number for a women&amp;rsquo ; s shelter and put her through . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Less than a month later , her relentless and well-connected abuser found them there . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another time and in a different shelter , a gang-connected woman wheedled her way in to deliver the message that he was watching . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel relinquished permanent custody of her child from a previous relationship as a protection from the violence that permeated her life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Later , exhausted from the threats and running , Rachel asked the child protection ministry to take the child that she&amp;rsquo ; d had with her abuser into temporary care on the condition that the child&amp;rsquo ; s father not be contacted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But a social worker broke that agreement and contacted Rachel&amp;rsquo ; s abuser even though his name is not on the child&amp;rsquo ; s birth certificate . Because of that breach of privacy , Rachel very nearly ended up having to share custody with the man who was making her life hell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Not only would it have meant regular contact with him , Rachel could never have got asylum in the U.S. With a custody order in place , she could have been charged with abduction if she had taken the child out of the country without his permission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , his custody attempt was the impetus for her exile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;REPEATED PLEAS FOR HELP&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , Rachel has approached the Canadian government for help . She&amp;rsquo ; s kept every email and letter , along with names and phone numbers of the various officials she&amp;rsquo ; s spoken to . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Initially , she asked for compensation for the house she was forced to sell at below market price in 1997 to finance her fugitive life . When it sold again recently , it was for $1.4 million . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last fall , she tried to get help accessing disability benefits under the Canada Pension Plan , which she paid into from the time she started a part-time job as a high-school student . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To get benefits , she needs a birth certificate and social insurance number . Rachel believes it&amp;rsquo ; s too risky to apply for CPP under her old name , so she needs new documents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After a flurry of email exchanges and phone calls , nothing has happened , just as nothing happened in the 1990s when Rachel begged police to give her a new identity . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the problems is Canada&amp;rsquo ; s disjointed system , name changes and birth certificates are provincial . Social insurance numbers and CPP are federal . Each requires a separate application . Each application costs money that Rachel can ill afford . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But even before she can apply , Rachel would have to apply to be allowed to apply from outside Canada . That&amp;rsquo ; s a whole other process . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For nearly 30 years , Rachel has been told there&amp;rsquo ; s another problem with getting her name changed in Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When she was in her late teens , Rachel defrauded a telephone company of $2,000 worth of telephone service by using a fake name . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was kid stuff , poor-people stuff , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She pleaded guilty and was sentenced to three years&amp;rsquo ; probation with 200 hours of community service and the requirement that she repay the money . She tried , but couldn&amp;rsquo ; t manage to do all of that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even with the support of her probation officer , the judge refused to amend the probation order and clear the way for a later pardon , or what&amp;rsquo ; s now called a record suspension . Because of her record , her only safe choice was an extreme one . Flight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The United States gave her a waiver before granting her asylum and a new identity . Why shouldn&amp;rsquo ; t Canada do that for her now ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3 style= " text-align:left ; " &gt;STILL AT RISK&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rachel has lived in fear for half her life . She still struggles to accept that for as long as her assailant is alive , her life is at risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Violence , threats and coercion forced her into hiding , into exile and into poverty that affected not only her but her children . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unable to return to her country of birth , she missed major milestones in her children&amp;rsquo ; s lives . She is unable to visit her parents&amp;rsquo ; graves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But among the facts of her life that Rachel finds most galling is that her punishment for defrauding a phone company of $2,000 was three times as long as any sentence her assailant ever received for nearly killing her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s cruel and absurd . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;18327;TOOLONG " **36;18358;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **27;18396;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;18425;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;18456;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? NewsNationalWomenDaphne Bramham : After decades of promises , has Canada finally reached a tipping point ? http : **34;18599;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;18635;TOOLONG ... title= " Supporters gather in Victoria to support Wet'suwet'en chiefs who oppose the Coastal GasLink pipeline . " alt= " Supporters gather in Victoria to support Wet'suwet'en chiefs who oppose the Coastal GasLink pipeline . " data-portal-copyright= " KEVIN LIGHT " **28;18671;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1219348 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;18701;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Countless words have been written in voluminous reports with hundreds of recommendations regarding the promise that Canada&amp;rsquo ; s relationship with Indigenous people will be transformed . Often years in the making and costing millions of dollars , the reports are encyclopedic , in both the good and the dull sense . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Warmly welcomed by politicians , the full reports with their many volumes are rarely read by them or by anyone else , including journalists and experts offering sage commentary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The excuses are easy : The reports are too long . We are too busy to read more than the executive summaries . And how much easier it is to reduce it all to a simple debate over whether using the word genocide is appropriate to describe the murders and disappearances of so many Aboriginal women . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For every recommendation , promises are made to give due consideration . But after public attention has inevitably and quickly pivoted to the latest Instagram-able issues , it has been easy for politicians to decide the recommendations are too costly in dollar terms , political capital , or both . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has wasted so many opportunities . Why is anyone surprised by the disruption to national rail service , or by protests that have kept legislators and others from their work ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only surprise is that the tipping point finally forcing a resolution to generations of talks seems to be the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en hereditary chiefs&amp;rsquo ; refusal to allow a natural gas pipeline to run through their traditional territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every little thing that makes a difference &amp;mdash ; to paraphrase the subtitle of Malcolm Gladwell&amp;rsquo ; s book The Tipping Point . He argues that there are three essential requirements to tip the balance and force change : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There must be strong leaders with influential and charismatic friends , which is a good description of the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en chiefs and climate activist Greta Thunberg , who has accused Canada of violating children&amp;rsquo ; s rights because of its continued support for oil and gas development . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There has to be a &amp;ldquo ; stickiness factor&amp;rdquo ; that compels an idea or phenomenon to stick in people&amp;rsquo ; s minds and influence their future behaviour . That might , in this case , include small things such as the now-ubiquitous acknowledgements at every gathering of whose unceded territory people are meeting on . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The final element is context , and for this , I&amp;rsquo ; ll stick to only the most recent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eight years ago , Idle No More shut down multiple border crossings , blocked railway lines , disrupted traffic with flash mobs and garnered international attention . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It petered out when then-Prime Minister Stephen Harper promised high-level dialogue , not with Idle No More&amp;rsquo ; s female founders and leaders , but with then-Assembly of First Nations Chief Shawn Atleo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Five years ago , the Truth and Reconciliation Commission&amp;rsquo ; s 11 pages of recommendations provided a roadmap for overcoming the legacy of residential schools . &amp;nbsp ; Prime Minister Justin Trudeau committed to implementing all 94 recommendations in December 2015 . The government&amp;rsquo ; s progress is tracked online at &lt;a href= " http : **34;18737;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That raised Indigenous peoples&amp;rsquo ; expectations , as did the appointment of Jody Wilson-Raybould as justice minister . But many hopes were dashed with the government&amp;rsquo ; s purchase of the Trans Mountain Pipeline and its subsequent re-approval , as did **25;18773;TOOLONG ; s demotion and eventual ouster from the Liberal caucus following her testimony about how Trudeau tried to convince her not to prosecute SNC-Lavalin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Which brings us to the gas pipeline going through Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en territory that is backed by John Horgan&amp;rsquo ; s NDP government &amp;mdash ; the same government that less than a year ago promised to bring B.C. laws in line with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Adding to the frustrations are 1,200 murdered and missing women , health outcomes that lag other Canadians by a wide margin , and 27 years of B.C. treaty negotiations that have yielded only eight finalized agreements , involving only 38 per cent of the province&amp;rsquo ; s Indian Act bands . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And , yes , there&amp;rsquo ; s climate change that also disproportionately affects Indigenous people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Senator Murray Sinclair , who chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission , wrote in a recent blogpost that what is needed to resolve the Wet&amp;rsquo ; suwet&amp;rsquo ; en pipeline dispute are &amp;ldquo ; positive acts . &amp;rdquo ; But he is not optimistic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Frankly , given Canada&amp;rsquo ; s intransigence , and the rising sense of injustice felt by Indigenous leadership throughout the country , I do not like where this is heading . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is a rich irony that among the strongest voices deriding protesters as radical activists and urging police to take action against them are themselves using the spectre of western separatism to get their way on pipeline approvals. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada is in the midst of an existential crisis with the intersection of Indigenous rights , climate change and the economy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is no simple solution . Certainly , it can&amp;rsquo ; t be solved by company-sought court injunctions enforced by police , or by any other court rulings . It hasn&amp;rsquo ; t worked before in Canada and it hasn&amp;rsquo ; t worked in other democratic societies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s future depends on federal , provincial , Indigenous , business and community leaders as well as its citizens talking in good faith and with respect about what Canada should be and could be , not only a decade from now , but a century from now . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;18800;TOOLONG " **36;18831;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamThu , 20 Feb 2020 17:33:57 **45;18869;TOOLONG ... **34;18916;TOOLONG Mulgrew : B.C. cannabis police ' blink , ' and reverse their stance on evidencehttp : **32;18952;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;18986;TOOLONG ... title= " Trees of Eden Grown co-owner Alex Robb recently got notice from B.C. BusinessCannabis LegalizationCannabis Small **38;19303;TOOLONG Todd : The morality of religion , driverless cars and everything elsehttp : **36;19343;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19381;TOOLONG ... title= " Azim Shariff is a social psychology prof at UBC who is studying morality around driverless cars . " alt= " Azim Shariff is a social psychology prof at UBC who is studying morality around driverless cars . " data-portal-copyright= " Mike Bell " **28;19417;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1216609 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Azim Shariff is becoming known as a go-to expert on the ways morality relates to religion , driverless cars , IQs , organ transplants , artificial intelligence and how we view people who are &amp;ldquo ; busy . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean the University of B.C. social psychologist comes across as at all moralistic &amp;mdash ; even when I asked how he exposed the big mistake in one of the decade&amp;rsquo ; s most &amp;ldquo ; surprising&amp;rdquo ; and widely cited studies on how religion shapes morality . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff lead a team that discovered a high-profile University of Chicago research project had incorrectly concluded that children in Christian and Muslim households are more stingy than youngsters in non-religious households . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In doing so , Shariff also uncovered some favourable findings about the children of Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since his own research had suggested a religious upbringing often increases kindness towards others , he led four colleagues in asking for access to Jean Decety&amp;rsquo ; s extensive data on the generosity of 1,200 children in six countries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff&amp;rsquo ; s group discovered there had been a coding error : The Chicago team&amp;rsquo ; s calculations in 2015 of how children performed in sharing coloured stickers with one another had , in effect and without being too technical about it , mixed up nationalities with religiosity. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What&amp;rsquo ; s worse , as a few international media outlets reported in 2019 , the Chicago team&amp;rsquo ; s eventual retraction didn&amp;rsquo ; t receive a fraction of the scientific and media coverage that trumpeted the original negative findings about religion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In addition , virtually no media outlet has publicized a key result of the corrected data : That Canadian children emerged as the most sharing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Canadian children were found to be more generous than those from South Africa , Turkey , the United States , Jordan and China . &lt;/p&gt; Todd : Is it OK to ask , ' Where are you from ? ' &lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;19525;TOOLONG ... Todd : Higher education has given up on the meaning of **25;19561;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff doesn&amp;rsquo ; t want to overemphasize the results , however . He says the children weren&amp;rsquo ; t too far apart based on nationality and , anyways , no one knows what factors produced the Canadian children&amp;rsquo ; s relatively so-called &amp;ldquo ; pro-social behaviour . &amp;rdquo ; For instance , many offspring in China are their parents&amp;rsquo ; only children , Shariff said , which is often associated with being self-focused. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have an axe to grind either for or against religion or any country . And he&amp;rsquo ; s wary of those who do . He&amp;rsquo ; s appreciating the chance to collaborate with the Chicago group to expand their research , which will now test the moral behaviour of children in 12 nations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born in Toronto to a Muslim family from India , the 38-year-old associate professor and Canada Research Chair says he drifted away from the family faith in his early teens . But , while studying psychology at the University of Toronto , he came intrigued by religion and ethical reasoning . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Teaching at UBC he&amp;rsquo ; s noticed many students crave to be taught morality , even in a &amp;ldquo ; paternalistic&amp;rdquo ; way . Today&amp;rsquo ; s young people seem to be reacting against , he says , the s &lt;a href= " http : **34;19588;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;o-called " values-free " education&lt;/a&gt; typically offered by secular colleges and universities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff&amp;rsquo ; s own original research has found when people &amp;mdash ; including Christians , Muslims , Jews , atheists &amp;shy ; and agnostics &amp;mdash ; are asked to think about religion , they become more generous not only to members of their own group , but also to those outside their group . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And a new potentially controversial international study lead by Britain&amp;rsquo ; s Cory Jane Clark , in which Shariff took part , found &lt;a href= " https : **33;19624;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;religiosity and high-IQs were important factors in reducing violence&lt;/a&gt; , since each is associated with self-control . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After looking at data across many countries ( not named in the paper ) , the scholars theorize that religion is more effective in reducing violence in societies with relatively lower average IQs . They don&amp;rsquo ; t want people to jump to conclusions , however . Shariff notes IQs are determined both by genetics and environment , and a society&amp;rsquo ; s average IQ tends to correlate to levels of education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Never mind that there are many things beyond religiosity and IQ that influence morality , including the presence of police , taxation measures and secular philosophy , says Shariff. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In contrast to ancient religions , another thing increasingly swaying our ethics is high technology . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s particularly the case with the kind of algorithms created to make life-altering medical ethics decisions about who gets priority for a donated organ and about the moral programming of self-driving cars . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every time a driver makes a decision about how close to veer toward a bicyclist or whether to tailgate , he or she is making a moral choice , Shariff says . So he and colleagues have been researching whether the algorithmic decisions of driverless cars are compatible with wider human morality . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; MIT researcher Edmond Awad collaborated with Shariff and others to create a web-based experimental driving platform called &lt;a href= " http : //moralmachine.mit.edu/ " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Moral Machine&lt;/a&gt; , which has now been played by several million people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Moral Machine throws virtual drivers into stark moral dilemmas , such as having to choose between crashing into innocent pedestrians or saving their own lives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19659;TOOLONG ... title= " Moral Machine is an online experimental platform that asks participants about the moral choices they would make while driving . In this test the driver must decide between running down some elderly males or swerving and killing herself . " alt= " Moral Machine is an online experimental platform that asks participants about the moral choices they would make while driving . In this test the driver must decide between running down some elderly males or swerving and killing herself . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19695;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1215033 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shariff says the kinds of ethical responses that driverless car algorithms &amp;mdash ; and lawyers worried about legal liability &amp;mdash ; come up with to these somewhat &amp;ldquo ; cartoonish&amp;rdquo ; scenarios are not necessarily those of empathetic humans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That said , they&amp;rsquo ; re finding the morality of people can change by country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Moral Machine asked online drivers to choose between mowing down a business executive or a homeless man , Shariff and colleagues found people in egalitarian Nordic countries were just as likely to protect the homeless person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But citizens of highly unequal countries , such as those in South America , were more protective of the business executive . Another Moral Machine experiment found Asians more likely than North Americans to save elderly pedestrians , not just young ones , from harm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since researchers are discovering humans show a startling range of responses to driving dilemmas , the question arises : Who will be granted the authority to program the life-and-death decision-making of self-driving vehicles ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the subject of robots , Shariff has also been looking into the economic morality associated with working , particularly if many are going to lose their jobs to automation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His experiments show that most of us , from Europe to Korea , view busyness as &amp;ldquo ; a moral signal of character , &amp;rdquo ; even when such people are not doing anything meaningful . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A key question Shariff is working on is how society will view the masses of people who could be replaced by Artificial Intelligence , such as truck drivers , who might end up living on a basic income supplied by taxpayers : &amp;ldquo ; Will we think they are valuable members of society ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The moral decisions linked with everything we interact with are profound &amp;mdash ; and Shariff and his adventurous colleagues are helping us pay attention to their powerful consequences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **26;19725;TOOLONG " **33;19753;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **25;19788;TOOLONG " class= " twitter-follow-button " data-show-count= " false " &gt;Follow @DouglasTodd&lt;/a&gt; Douglas ToddTue , 18 Feb 2020 16:33:26 **45;19815;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Geoff Robins/AFP via Getty Images/File " **28;19932;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1196325 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A Prince George man may face a rare third trial after an appeal throwing out his second conviction underscored the need to train judges in sexual misconduct cases . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After two expensive , emotional trials &amp;mdash ; one before a jury &amp;mdash ; the province&amp;rsquo ; s high bench found both justices made serious errors despite the attention in recent years on the need for care and sensitivity in dealing with these prosecutions plagued by myths and stereotypes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spurred by concerns raised by the #MeToo movement and former CBC-host Jian Ghomeshi&amp;rsquo ; s high-profile , controversial 2016 trial , the federal Liberals last week introduced Bill C- &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;5 &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;to ensure newly appointed superior court judges are properly trained for sexual cases . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It also would require the Canadian Judicial Council to report on efforts to provide similar training to sitting judges and amend the Criminal Code to ensure judges provide reasons on the record for sexual offences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The bill mirrors previous legislation introduced by former Conservative MP Rona Ambrose . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are some issues &amp;hellip ; that really are above politics , &amp;rdquo ; she said , supporting the proposed changes while standing with Minister for Women and Gender Equality Maryam Monsef and Justice Minister David Lametti. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her bill passed the House with bipartisan support before moldering in the Senate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This case exemplified the issues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; B.C. Supreme Justice Lance Bernard , the second trial judge , edited his reasons after they were delivered &amp;mdash ; although the three-justice panel did not address that ground of appeal , deciding he erred more significantly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In my view , reversible error in law is reflected in the edited version of the reasons for judgment , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19962;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;said Justice Gregory Fitch&lt;/a&gt; , supported by colleagues Mary Saunders and Christopher Grauer. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; As a consequence , it is unnecessary for this court to address the extent to which trial judges can edit their oral reasons for judgment to properly dispose of this appeal . In these circumstances , the issue is best left to be explored another day . &amp;hellip ; I am of the view that a new trial is required &amp;hellip ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In February 2015 , at the first trial , a jury found Paul Peter Veeken guilty of sexually interfering with a young girl . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the appellate bench tossed that decision , saying B.C. Supreme Court Justice Elliot Myers failed to properly instruct the jury in that trial . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The unanimous decision concluded the jury&amp;rsquo ; s reasoning might have been improperly influenced by testimony from the girl&amp;rsquo ; s mother . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The jury should have been instructed that what R.&amp;rsquo ; s mother said she was told ( about Veeken ) was hearsay and was not proof of the truth of what she had been told , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19997;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Justice David Frankel wrote&lt;/a&gt; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; More importantly , the jury should have been specifically instructed that it must not rely on that evidence to conclude Mr. Veeken was a person of bad character who was , therefore , more likely to have committed the offence . &amp;hellip ; Simply instructing the jury to &amp;lsquo ; ignore&amp;rsquo ; the evidence was not sufficient to ensure a fair trial . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Veeken , now 47 , was re-tried &amp;mdash ; this time before a judge alone . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After the second trial , in December 2018 , Bernard found Veeken guilty again of inappropriately and deliberately touching the girl over the course of about two years starting when she was 10 , often under the guise of tickling or playing with her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When testifying , Veeken admitted to hosting get-togethers for groups of children at a family cabin where they would use a hot tub and watch movies &amp;mdash ; with no other adults present . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He acknowledged providing candy and ice cream along with toys and children&amp;rsquo ; s movies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The girl complained to her parents about Veeken in 2013 after being warned at a babysitting course about men and conduct of concern . They went to police . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bernard reputedly concluded Veeken groomed the girl for his own sexual gratification while &amp;ldquo ; hiding in plain view&amp;rdquo ; by using the other children as a &amp;ldquo ; smokescreen of sorts . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In December 2018 , he said the victim was a &amp;ldquo ; naive young girl&amp;rdquo ; enthralled by Veeken : &amp;ldquo ; It was a child&amp;rsquo ; s dream that sadly turned into a nightmare . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The appeal division , however , said his verdict was fatally flawed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The judge was certainly entitled to reject the appellant&amp;rsquo ; s evidence and find that it did not raise a reasonable doubt about his guilt , &amp;rdquo ; Fitch concluded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The difficulty in this case arises because of the judge&amp;rsquo ; s conclusion that he could neither accept the appellant&amp;rsquo ; s evidence nor find that it raised a reasonable doubt in the absence of independent and reliable evidence supporting his account . To approach the issue this way was to erroneously shift the burden to the accused to adduce evidence that confirmed his denial of wrongdoing &amp;hellip ; it taints his reasons as a whole . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Veeken&amp;rsquo ; s lawyer Scott Wright described the case as &amp;ldquo ; basically he said , she said . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s tough ( to explain ) because the trial court reasons have not been released yet from the second trial and they shed a bit more light on the other grounds of appeal , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s challenging and it&amp;rsquo ; s a tough spot for trial judges to be in &amp;mdash ; to articulate why it is you believe somebody or disbelieve somebody . So , certainly there&amp;rsquo ; s some sympathy there for the process they have to undertake isn&amp;rsquo ; t easy to articulate something that is sometimes just a &amp;lsquo ; feel&amp;rsquo ; thing in terms of accepting what somebody is telling you . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sentenced to two years in jail and one year&amp;rsquo ; s probation , Veeken has served his custodial time , Wright added , so he didn&amp;rsquo ; t think a new trial necessary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " The ( B.C. Prosecution Service ) is reviewing the decision carefully , " said spokesman Dan McLaughlin . " No final decision has yet been made regarding the next steps in the prosecution . TravelLocal NewsNationalDouglas Todd : What 's with the British names for new luxury buildings ? http : **30;20600;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20632;TOOLONG ... title= " In Metro , developers tends to choose English or Latinate names for luxury buildings ... because it works with buyers , including those from Asia " alt= " In Metro , developers tends to choose English or Latinate names for luxury buildings ... because it works with buyers , including those from Asia " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20668;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1214200 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; A contender for most striking name for a new Vancouver condominium building may be The Empire at the Park . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the world of luxury housing , the names of tony apartment buildings are often considered the &lt;a href= " http : **34;20698;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;most effective way to market them&lt;/a&gt; to buyers , both local and global , who are looking for exclusivity and prestige . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet The Empire at the Park , also known as The Empire at Queen Elizabeth Park , could not be more reflective of British heritage , even colonialism . For a globalized , cosmopolitan city like Vancouver , it seems counterintuitive that the names of many &lt;a href= " http : **34;20734;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;new luxury buildings&lt;/a&gt; are often British , with others linked to Latin languages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Vancouver luxury market targets foreign buyers as much as it does domestic ones . And whatever developers are doing with English-sounding and Latinate names seems to be working . The stylish units of The Empire at the Park , at Cambie and 29th , which run in the $1.2 million to $1.6 million range , sold out quickly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When it comes to marketing high-end British Columbia housing , is it possible the Britishness of the place is part of its brand appeal , even in a city where more than four out of 10 people have Asian roots ? English and familiar Latin-based names are prevalent in most new costly condo buildings , including the many flying up along Cambie Street . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Chelsea , named after a posh neighbourhood in London , is selling units for $3.3 million . A two-bedroom condo in the Cambie Collection&amp;rsquo ; s Grayson building , built by the very British-sounding Pennyfarthing Development Corp. , goes for about $1.5 million . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mansion Global Magazine says the trend to using names as brands really took off in London in the 1990s , when &amp;ldquo ; a lot of overseas money came into the city , and people were all of a sudden demanding luxury apartment buildings that didn&amp;rsquo ; t previously exist . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The name of London&amp;rsquo ; s tony Lancaster building , for instance , plays on English heritage . One Hyde Park emphasized its uniqueness . The new Ritz-Carlton and Versace apartments in London capitalize on Western luxury brands , which helped make them the rage in the Middle East and Asia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;20770;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;20812;TOOLONG ... Vancouver 's renters pummelled by demovictions and **35;20920;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Many people in Asian countries value both the English language and Western products , says economic consultant Jean-Noel Kapferer . In his book , Abundant Rarity : The Key to Luxury Growth , Kapferer writes about how &amp;ldquo ; Asian consumers feel safer buying prestigious Western brands with which individuals around them are familiar . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whether appealing to buyers in the West or East , access to green space also helps explain how the most popular name for North American buildings is &amp;ldquo ; Park , &amp;rdquo ; suggesting a special location with pastoral charm . Apartment Guide Magazine says &amp;ldquo ; Park&amp;rdquo ; has been used in the names of more than 1,400 apartment and condominium blocks , with &amp;ldquo ; Village&amp;rdquo ; clicking in at 1,200. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20957;TOOLONG ... title= " Promotional image for Empire at the Park condo complex , on Cambie near Queen Elizabeth Park " alt= " Promotional image for Empire at the Park condo complex , on Cambie near Queen Elizabeth Park " data-portal-copyright= " Screen shot from Empire at the P " **28;20993;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1213048 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s luxury developers are crazy about the name &amp;ldquo ; Park . &amp;rdquo ; In addition to Empire at the Park , there is Park House , on 59th near Cambie , where prices run to $4 million a unit . And Westbank Corp . continues to erect hundreds more elite condos at Oakridge , where some sell for $9.9 million . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are more inventive names , however , including The ARC , from Concord Pacific . " data-portal-copyright= " HO " **28;21566;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1212698 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As B.C. heads into the fifth year of a public health emergency due to the high number of opioid overdose deaths , Vancouver Island still doesn&amp;rsquo ; t have a single residential-treatment for youth . Provincewide , the number of youth beds and services lag demand . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For youth who do get one of those precious treatment beds , their transition back to community-based services is badly planned and poorly managed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Had all of that been in place , 16-year-old Elliot Cleveland Eurchuk might have survived his addiction rather than being counted among the 4,850 British Columbians to have died between January 2016 and Oct. 31 , 2019. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the teen&amp;rsquo ; s legacy could be &amp;mdash ; should be &amp;mdash ; that Health Minister Adrian Dix and Premier John Horgan making addictions treatment as much of a priority as harm reduction . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;21596;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **29;21631;TOOLONG from the coroner&amp;rsquo ; s inquest into Eurchuk&amp;rsquo ; s 2018 death released on Monday provide some direction : More acute-care beds for youths including a residential treatment centre in Victoria ; more and better access to addictions services ; and resources for early detection of mental-health and substance-use disorders among youth . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For more , the government ought to dig out its copies of the 2018 &lt;a href= " https : **33;21662;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;report&lt;/a&gt; from the B.C. It also recommended &amp;ldquo ; recovery high schools&amp;rdquo ; where not only are drugs and alcohol are strictly prohibited , treatment and services are part of the curriculum . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Men aged 19 to 59 make up the overwhelming majority of the people who have died of opioid overdoses . " data-portal-copyright= " Rattankun Thongbun " **28;22444;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1202572 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Despite the scandalous over-representation of Indigenous people in our country&amp;rsquo ; s prison system , the B.C. Court of Appeal turned a deaf ear to a plea from a First Nations man whose life was shaped two generations before he was born . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The three justices asked : &amp;ldquo ; What should we do with him ? &amp;rdquo ; His lawyer Hovan Patey answered : &amp;ldquo ; Anything but lock him up and throw away the key . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He wasn&amp;rsquo ; t persuasive enough . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22474;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;The case&lt;/a&gt; highlights the inter-generational cost of colonialism and residential schools as well as the challenges facing judges , the vast majority non-Aboriginal , trying to compensate for it : The crippling historical wounds and scar tissue Indigenous people bear are the very reason some are considered a threat to public safety . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Johnny Wilfred Troy Awasis was designated a dangerous offender in June 2016 and sentenced to an indeterminate term of imprisonment after convictions for two sexual offences in August 2011. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A troubling corollary to the news that Indigenous overrepresentation in Canada has hit new highs &amp;mdash ; one-in-three men behind bars &amp;mdash ; is that a dangerous offender designation is a virtual guarantee an Aboriginal man will die in jail , receiving only toe-tag parole . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Patey argued that was grossly disproportionate to Awasis moral culpability and manifestly unfit given the 38-year-old&amp;rsquo ; s tragic background . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He proposed a long-term offender declaration , a sentence of eight to nine years ( less time served ) , and a 10-year supervision order given the evidence of Awasis&amp;rsquo ; treatability. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That is a very , very significant sanction with a lot of safeguards built into it , but it is not a sentence that will guarantee he&amp;rsquo ; ll die in jail , &amp;rdquo ; Patey added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like many Indigenous offenders , Awasis wasn&amp;rsquo ; t brought up , he was dragged up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His parents and grandparents went to residential schools . His mother Bertha Johnny , of the Anaham First Nation in the B.C. Interior , was raped at 13 by a priest and gave birth to a child surrendered to social services . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She moved to Vancouver , became addicted , lived on the street , and bore two more children by different fathers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then she met Wilfred Awasis , a member of the Thunderchild Cree Nation from Saskatchewan , described as a &amp;ldquo ; violent alcoholic , &amp;rdquo ; and they had four children , the second Johnny . The family lived for a while on the Anaham Reserve , and then in Saskatchewan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When his father was later imprisoned , his mother and Johnny returned to the Downtown Eastside. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At six , he was left with an aunt and , when his mother didn&amp;rsquo ; t show up for a month , Awasis was placed in a residential school for about seven months . He was emotionally , physically and sexually abused . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was seven when his mother retrieved him and returned him to a squalid hard-scrabble life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; School was a disaster , not only because of his life , but also his learning disabilities . He stopped showing up in Grade 8 . He was using marijuana at 10 , alcohol and cocaine at 12 , and was in the courts at 13. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Johnny was repeatedly apprehended by the Ministry of Children and Family Development , then returned to his mother in an unconscionable cycle of poverty and neglect . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By 18 , he was living in a drug house and dealing to support his cocaine habit : He has never worked . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He fathered a child in 2005 with a partner , also addicted , and the child was taken into care . Awasis was convicted of assaulting her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His record is book-length &amp;mdash ; mischief , assault , extortion , robbery , theft , escaping custody , break-and-enter , attempted theft over $5,000 , uttering threats , assaulting a peace officer , being unlawfully at large &amp;hellip ; and a sexual assault in 2006. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In November 2010 , he was released on parole to the Circle of Eagles , a halfway house focusing on Indigenous culture and providing spiritual counselling by elders . He was on his way back to prison within an hour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was released again and once more parole was quickly suspended . After a third release , back to Circle of Eagles in June 2011 , parole was again revoked. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The reason each time : He immediately got drunk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Awasis was finally released at the end of July 2011 when his sentence expired . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Within 10 days , on Aug. 8 , he threatened a woman at a social services office . The following day , he committed the first sexual assault in this appeal , and on Aug. 31 , the second . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was arrested on Sept. 3 , 2011 , and imprisoned . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since his youth , Awasis was described as &amp;ldquo ; out of control , &amp;rdquo ; unable to experience empathy or feel for his victims , a child &amp;ldquo ; who never had a chance . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His correctional service &amp;ldquo ; healing&amp;rdquo ; plan included abstaining from substance abuse , counselling , maintaining a connection to his heritage , upgrading his education , accepting responsibility and being honest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given that he can focus for about as long as a goldfish and has symptoms of fetal alcohol syndrome , severe personality disorder , psychopathic traits , cognitive and addiction issues , I&amp;rsquo ; m not surprised he&amp;rsquo ; s had trouble &amp;ldquo ; healing . &amp;rdquo ; They might as well have asked him to Awaken the Giant Within . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , he is the face of the victims of colonialism , and the Supreme Court of Canada has been telling judges for a quarter-century to have compassion and not to write them off . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet , not only did the trial judge condemn Awasis to indefinite incarceration because she considered &amp;ldquo ; public protection&amp;rdquo ; paramount regardless of his &amp;ldquo ; reduced moral blameworthiness , &amp;rdquo ; the appeal division concurred . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The judge was not satisfied , based on the appellant&amp;rsquo ; s history , that his motivation to change was sincere , or that he had the capacity to change , which were findings open to her on the evidence , &amp;rdquo ; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22509;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;wrote Justice Barbara Fisher&lt;/a&gt; , supported by benchmates Harvey Groberman and Patrice Abrioux. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here is the conundrum : For minor cases , &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;judges use Gladue reports , other tools and information provided to craft more appropriate sentences for Aboriginal offenders . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;In serious cases like this , however&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; , the exercise seems to shift&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; from the Supreme Court 's instruction to reduce or eliminate the use of incarceration for Indigenous people , and instead , they ask : " How do I get around that here ? " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Mr. Awasis ' case puts this starkly in focus : He committed serious offences , but has suffered some of the most tragic and impactful effects of colonialism imaginable , " lawyer Patey explained . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " His life was affected two generations before he was born . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; It 's difficult to say an offender has reduced moral blameworthiness , but then impose the severest sanction in Canadian law . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was frustrated : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We keep saying we&amp;rsquo ; re going to do this , but in the most difficult situations , in those troubling contexts , it&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;lsquo ; Yes , we acknowledge all of these principles , yes , we acknowledge all these factors are present , yes , we must do what we can to reduce the over-representation of the Aboriginal population in prison , BUT&amp;rsquo ; &amp;hellip ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I think that&amp;rsquo ; s what has happened here , and that&amp;rsquo ; s what we see . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead of condemning Awasis , the judges had an alternative with a long-term offender sentence that would have respected the Supreme Court&amp;rsquo ; s direction and given him a chance &amp;mdash ; as slim as it might be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;22544;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;22575;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;22613;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; Ian MulgrewSat , 08 Feb 2020 00:31:06 **45;22646;TOOLONG ... security rules do n't violate Charter rights , Federal Court ruleshttp : **35;22693;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;22730;TOOLONG ... title= " Port of Vancouver file photo " alt= " Port of Vancouver file photo " data-portal-copyright= " NICK PROCAYLO " **28;22766;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 934404 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;22796;TOOLONG ... But such measures are minor compared to the astonishing rules concocted by other public officials to deflate housing bubbles and soften rent shocks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Asian countries are much &lt;a href= " https : **33;23842;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;less open than Western nations to allowing foreign nationals to affect their property values&lt;/a&gt; by investing in their land . Faced with skyrocketing prices and rents , often combined with stagnant local wages , governments across the political spectrum realize they&amp;rsquo ; re called to devise a range of policies to calm prices and guard vulnerable tenants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Such regulations and taxes can counter the factors driving up prices , according to Knight Frank , a consultancy . Soaring valuations are caused , Knight Frank says , by a sharp global rise in the number of millionaires , increasingly convenient flights from Asia to the West , record low interest rates and urban infrastructure megaprojects , such as Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s proposed subway to UBC. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Developers and their often-close political allies welcome the economic and population growth &amp;mdash ; and customarily claim the only way to create more reasonably priced housing ( and hike their profits ) is to increase density and reduce so-called red tape . But many economists say it&amp;rsquo ; s impossible to build one&amp;rsquo ; s way to affordability. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Rather counter-intuitively , building more houses is not the right prescription . House prices won&amp;rsquo ; t fall until the tide of cash flowing into the market abates . &amp;hellip ; The best way to do this is through the tax system , &amp;rdquo ; says &lt;a href= " https : **33;23877;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Ann Pettifor&lt;/a&gt; , director of Policy Research in Macroeconomics . Without stopping money funnelling into expensive areas , Pettifor says the market will simply absorb it and prices will keep rising . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;23912;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;23954;TOOLONG ... The biggest sources of immigrants to Canada &amp;mdash ; China , India and the Philippines &amp;mdash ; all impose various bans on non-resident buyers . That means millions of new Canadians are already familiar with &lt;a href= " https : **33;24154;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt; housing rules that protect local sovereignty&lt;/a&gt; . Similar curbs on non-resident ownership are in place in Indonesia , Thailand , Singapore , Malaysia and Hong Kong . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like in Canada , many of Australia&amp;rsquo ; s big cities are also super-attractive to foreign buyers , typically from Asia . But , unlike Canada , Australia keeps track by requiring every foreign national who wants to buy a dwelling to register . And , to limit the depletion of its older , more affordable housing stock , Australia innovatively restricts offshore residents to buying only new dwellings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The policy variations go on and on . In Denmark , foreign nationals from outside Europe can not buy real estate unless they prove they are permanent residents and will live full-time in the dwelling . Even European Union citizens can not buy summer homes on Denmark&amp;rsquo ; s sought-after coast . Though large European countries like France and Germany are fairly open , small Switzerland has erected more barriers than Denmark . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even in Canada , which champions the unfettered global movement of capital and humans more than almost any other nation , Liberal Prime Minister Justin Trudeau finally promised in the fall election campaign to follow the lead of B.C. and impose a one-per-cent tax on the assessed values of homes owned by non-resident non-Canadians . The NDP&amp;rsquo ; s Jagmeet Singh called for a national 15-per-cent foreign-buyers tax . &lt;a href= " https : **33;24189;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;We 'll see if they follow through . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What&amp;rsquo ; s being done for tenants ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Given the increasingly often-outrageous cost of home ownership , more people now rent in North America than before . So some governments are moving harder to counter gouging. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Like Vancouver , popular Berlin is growing by almost 40,000 newcomers a year . So its average rents have more than doubled in a decade . Politicians are going far to protect the city&amp;rsquo ; s tenants . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Berlin&amp;rsquo ; s government has just &lt;a href= " https : **33;24224;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;frozen most rents for five years , while capping them at about US$1 a square foot&lt;/a&gt; . The German capital has also become the first in the world to say landlords can not charge rents higher than what the previous tenant paid . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In response to justified fears that Berlin&amp;rsquo ; s laws will kill any incentive to construct new purpose-built rental stock , the government decided any building that went up after 2014 will be exempt and rents will eventually be allowed to rise by 1.3 per cent a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Spain and the Netherlands also have nationwide rent-control measures , and have capped rents to the inflation rate . And they&amp;rsquo ; re not alone . Even the staunchly free-enterprise U.S. is home to five states with broad rent-regulation measures ; California , New York , New Jersey , Maryland and Oregon . Some Canadian cities are similar . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But they&amp;rsquo ; re not as groundbreaking on behalf of renters as a host of other jurisdictions . Spain has a five-year-minimum on rent contracts , to guard against hikes . And when sought-after Barcelona began being flooded by 20 million tourists a year , losing more than 20,000 rental units to Airbnb , &lt;a href= " https : **33;24259;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;city politicians cracked down&lt;/a&gt; . So have many other cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Netherlands not only got tough on landlords who crank up rents in the name of renovating , Amsterdam has found a way to give high priority to families for mid-priced rentals and the national government promises to provide free lawyers to tenants who need to sue landlords . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not to mention the dramatic efforts going into social housing . Germany , for example , puts $2 billion a year into housing projects . In lovely Vienna , Austria , 62 per cent of citizens are in social housing ( compared to one per cent in the U.S. ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is truly no shortage of imaginative ideas for aiding people squeezed too hard by the housing market . " data-portal-copyright= " AlexRaths " **28;24596;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1206871 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **32;24626;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some corporate-owned , long-term care homes in B.C. are getting money for nothing , while not-for-profits may be getting less than they need for their services to be sustainable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the bottom line is that the losers are both vulnerable seniors and taxpayers who are footing the $1.3-billion annual bill . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To be clear , it may be unconscionable , but for-profit operators who run a third of all the long-term homes and beds in B.C. are not breaking any rules . Just as it&amp;rsquo ; s fair to assume that not-for-profits , who account for another third of the total , aren&amp;rsquo ; t deliberately leaving money on the table . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The problem is that the system is broken . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;24660;TOOLONG ... title= " B.C. Seniors Advocate Isobel Mackenzie ( Richard Lam/PNG ) " alt= " B.C. Seniors Advocate Isobel Mackenzie ( Richard Lam/PNG ) " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;24696;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1207232 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Patients and their families have been complaining for years . On Tuesday , B.C. Seniors Advocate Isobel Mackenzie clearly set out the evidence in her report , &lt;a href= " https : **33;24726;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;A Billion Reasons to Care&lt;/a&gt; , which comes within a few months of Island Health taking over three privately operated homes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mackenzie&amp;rsquo ; s funding review is a scorching indictment of the government&amp;rsquo ; s failure to properly manage one of the largest contracting relationships it has with service providers . To some extent , Mackenzie said , the government is handing long-term care operators blank cheques . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She said the rules haven&amp;rsquo ; t kept pace with the fundamental shift in government procurement policy that began 20 years ago when long-term care was contracted out to private operators who were then allowed to opt out of the Health Employers Association of B.C. , which once bargained on behalf of all publicly funded , health-care employers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rules are non-existent , vague or not uniformly applied . Direct care hours , for example , aren&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily separated out from the hours that care aides spend on food service or housekeeping . Financial monitoring is scant with no requirement for detailed or audited reports . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2017-18 , for-profit operators failed to deliver 207,000 hours of care for which the B.C. government paid them . Were they fined ? No . They got to keep the money . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , not-for-profit operators delivered 80,000 hours of care more than they were contracted to provide . Those extra hours were paid for either by lower costs in another area or by other funding sources . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is true that all operators face a staffing crisis that Mackenzie describes as being of epidemic proportions , with nearly 90 per cent of care homes not able to meet minimum staffing guidelines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But it&amp;rsquo ; s partially self-inflicted . For-profit operators&amp;rsquo ; wage costs for each hour of direct care is lower across all classifications than the costs at not-for-profits and the homes run directly by health authorities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some for-profits are paying care aides , who provide two-thirds of the care , nearly a third less than the industry standard , which works out to $6.63 an hour . Part of the difference is that for-profit operators are more likely to hire part-time rather than full-time workers , which eliminates the need to pay benefits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Raise the salaries , says Mackenzie , and workers will follow the money . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The government and health authorities should also follow the money . Rather than setting a minimum wage or requiring that all operators pay the industry standard , Mackenzie says to simply end the incentive to not deliver the care . If operators didn&amp;rsquo ; t deliver 207,000 hours of care , they should have been required to give that money back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But there are no penalties in any of the contracts . Don&amp;rsquo ; t deliver and , ka-ching ! , the bottom line suddenly looks a lot better as taxpayers&amp;rsquo ; money transforms into shareholder profits . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Disturbingly , Mackenzie found that contracts varied both between and within health authorities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All spoke to delivery of care , &amp;rdquo ; she said Tuesday . &amp;ldquo ; But none specified the type of care . None outlined any legal requirements to provide the care . And none had explicit penalties for non-compliance. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every health authority also had different reporting systems . Different ones allowed expenses to be claimed differently . There were also anomalies between the profit and non-profit operators , including for-profits having surpluses 12 times higher and profits three times higher . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The health authorities allowed for-profit operators to claim building expenses at 20 per cent of their revenues compared to the **25;24761;TOOLONG ; nine per cent . They also allowed mortgage interest rates considerably higher than market rates , double the depreciation rates , unexplained lump-sum payments to contractors working for affiliated companies , unspecified management fees in addition to administrative expenses that are higher than non-profits. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One concern Mackenzie has about non-profits claiming lower building expenses is that they will not be able to upgrade their facilities as they age , meet any new accessibility requirements that may be required , or expand to meet the tsunami of demand from an aging population . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It all needs to change and change quickly before even more public money is funnelled into corporate profits at the expense of vulnerable seniors who aren&amp;rsquo ; t getting the care they need and deserve . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;24788;TOOLONG " **36;24819;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamWed , 05 Feb 2020 17:40:58 **45;24857;TOOLONG ...
