NewsNationalDaphne Bramham : Allowing paroled murderers to visit brothels is n't just stupid , it 's illegal and deadlyhttp : **34;25409;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;25445;TOOLONG ... title= " Maryl ? ne L ? vesque was killed in a Sainte-Foy hotel room Jan. 22 . Parolee Eustachio Gallese was arrested in connection with the death . Photo : Facebook " alt= " Maryl ? ne L ? vesque was killed in a Sainte-Foy hotel room Jan. 22 . Parolee Eustachio Gallese was arrested in connection with the death . Photo : Facebook " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;25481;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204666 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is unbelievable that men who have killed their intimate partners would not only be allowed , but encouraged , to go to brothels while they are on parole and out on day passes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But that&amp;rsquo ; s exactly what Canada&amp;rsquo ; s parole board agreed to last September for Eustachio Gallese , 51 , who had brutally murdered his wife in 2004. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He had sexual needs , his caseworker told the board . But because Gallese wasn&amp;rsquo ; t deemed ready to have relationships with a woman , buying sexual services was the solution to satisfying his &amp;ldquo ; sexual needs . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s a solution that blatantly disregards the fact that buying sexual services is a criminal offence , as is operating a brothel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , more tragically , the order was approved with cruel disregard for the unsuspecting women on whom Gallese was set loose . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Jan. 23 this year , Gallese turned himself in to Quebec City police and pointed them to the hotel room where they found the body of 22-year-old Maryl&amp;egrave ; ne L&amp;eacute ; vesque . He&amp;rsquo ; s since been charged with murder . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; L&amp;eacute ; vesque had defensive wounds and had been stabbed , according to Le Journal de Quebec . The newspaper also reported that L&amp;eacute ; vesque had worked in a massage parlour and that Gallese was a regular customer , and had bought her gifts including a television for Christmas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;25511;TOOLONG ... title= " Maryl ? ne L ? vesque was killed in a Sainte-Foy hotel room Jan. 22 . Parolee Eustachio Gallese was arrested in connection with the death . Photo : Facebook " alt= " Maryl ? ne L ? vesque was killed in a Sainte-Foy hotel room Jan. 22 . Parolee Eustachio Gallese was arrested in connection with the death . Photo : Facebook " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;25547;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1204673 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; But both the Montreal Gazette and Le Soleil reported that Gallese had been banned from the brothel because he had been violent with several others who worked there . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; L&amp;eacute ; vesque made the mistake of meeting him at a hotel . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 1997 , Gallese was convicted for conjugal violence . Seven years later , Gallese murdered his 32-year-old partner , Chantal Desch&amp;ecirc ; nes , beating her first with a hammer and then repeatedly stabbing her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was sentenced in 2006 to life in prison with no chance of parole for 15 years , and deemed at high risk of committing violence against a partner a year later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , at some point , that risk evaluation was revised to moderate and in 2016 &amp;mdash ; five years before he was due for parole &amp;mdash ; Gallese was allowed supervised outings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last March , he was released to a halfway house . The parole board denied him full parole last September at a hearing . A written summary of the decision indicates that parole board members were caught off guard when Gallese discussed his interactions with women over the previous six months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; During the hearing , your parole officer underlined a strategy that was developed with the goal that would allow you to meet women in order to address your sexual needs , &amp;rdquo ; it says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It went on to say : &amp;ldquo ; The hearing allowed us to realize you managed , and this with the approval of your case-management team , relations with women that the board considers inappropriate . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a strategy , the board noted , that &amp;ldquo ; paradoxically constitutes a worrying and significant risk factor . &amp;rdquo ; It ordered a re-examination of the terms in six months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two months shy of that re-evaluation , L&amp;eacute ; vesque is dead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; How many other parolees , if any , have similar orders in place is not clear . The Parole Board of Canada did not respond to questions before this column&amp;rsquo ; s deadline . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But even if it is a singular case , the decision in Gallese&amp;rsquo ; s case reflects some deeply disturbing notions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The first is that men &amp;mdash ; even violent criminals &amp;mdash ; have a right to satiate their sexual appetites with another person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The second is the perverse idea that if a violent man is incapable or not ready to form a healthy relationship with another person , it&amp;rsquo ; s OK for him to engage in unhealthy relationships where , as the buyer , he has power over the seller . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , putting the sexual needs of a violent criminal ahead of the safety of other Canadians , including those who do sex work , suggests a grotesque hierarchy that is an affront to the constitutional and moral ideals of equality . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two former parole board members have posited that the reason Gallese was allowed to visit massage parlours is that 14 of Quebec&amp;rsquo ; s parole board members have less than three years&amp;rsquo ; experience and several have never dealt with cases involving dangerous offenders . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They suggest that more experienced board members might have challenged the caseworker&amp;rsquo ; s plan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That may be so . But it does raise questions about what qualifications these government-appointed board members have . One might expect that at the very least they are reasonable people who are reasonably well-informed. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But what reasonable person would knowingly place a violent offender in an illegal brothel to commit the criminal offence of paying for sex ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t seem unreasonable that parole board caseworkers , as well as inexperienced parole board members , ought to know at least something about the murdered and missing Indigenous women , or the epidemic of sexual violence that translates into one death every 36 hours , or the fact that only five per cent of sexual assaults are ever reported , partly because all but one in five of those will be dismissed as unfounded by police . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Public Safety Minister Bill Blair ordered an investigation by Corrections Canada and the parole board to determine the circumstances of Gallese&amp;rsquo ; s release and provide recommendations for change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We want to be clear that the use of sexual services is not a practice we support in the case management of offenders , &amp;rdquo ; Esther Mailhot , Corrections Canada&amp;rsquo ; s communications adviser , said in an emailed response . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Corrections is taking Gallese&amp;rsquo ; s case &amp;ldquo ; very seriously&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; any recommendations &amp;hellip ; will be reviewed and implemented to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Why this tragedy happened is simple : The people responsible for keeping the public safe failed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The more complicated question is , how did the institutions and the culture at both Corrections Canada and the parole board allow those individuals to fail so spectacularly ? So , too , did the photo of a pheasant at Newark airport and a story about Wally , an emotional support alligator . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Beyond that , who hasn&amp;rsquo ; t heard a story or two about people circumventing no-pet rules with therapists&amp;rsquo ; letters bought online along with a cute little coats for their dogs emblazoned with &amp;ldquo ; emotional support animal&amp;rdquo ; or ESA . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; ESAs are not like service dogs . Service dogs are specially trained to do a wide range of tasks , such as providing assistance to people who are blind and acting as an early alert system to people with epilepsy. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fact is there&amp;rsquo ; s no agreed-upon definition of emotional support animals , which is why there&amp;rsquo ; s a Noah&amp;rsquo ; s ark of animals queuing for flights alongside their people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Westjet has felt it necessary to spell out on its website what animals are banned from flying in the passenger cabin . &amp;nbsp ; The list is both bizarre and strangely delightful ( unless they were to show up in the seat next to me ) . &amp;nbsp ; It includes : animals with tusks , horns , or hoofs , amphibians , ferrets , goats , hedgehogs , reptiles , rodents , snakes , spiders and sugar gliders ( a nocturnal gliding possum ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Air Canada has kept it simple : Service dogs only . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But who qualifies for an ESA , what kind of animal is acceptable and what training it needs is so opaque that the Canadian Transportation Authority is doing a public consultation to see whether more or better regulations are required . Anyone who wants to voice an opinion has until Feb. 7 to send email to &lt;a href= " **34;26026;TOOLONG " **41;26062;TOOLONG . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , the &lt;a href= " https : **33;26105;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;U.S . Department of Transport is proposing&lt;/a&gt; to restrict flying to service dogs with specialized training who help people with disabilities , after receiving 3,065 complaints from passengers in 2018 ( up from 719 in 2013 ) about animals defecating , urinating and biting on flights . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; An ESA is an example of a well-intended idea that has metastasized and developed into a world of nonsense , &amp;rdquo ; according to Jeffrey Younggren , a forensic psychologist and clinical professor at the University of New Mexico&amp;rsquo ; s department of psychiatry and behavioural sciences . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He was lead author on a 2019 &lt;a href= " https : **28;26140;TOOLONG ? doi= ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;paper&lt;/a&gt; published by the American Psychological Association that looked at the ethical challenges of certifying emotional support animals . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among their recommendations was more research on effects of ESAs on patients , which echoed a 2018 British &lt;a href= " https : **33;26170;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;review of studies&lt;/a&gt; on emotional support animals published by BMC Psychiatry that found quantitative evidence relating to the benefits of pets to be mixed and in need of further study . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Younggren and his colleagues said before prescribing ESAs , therapists must not only diagnose the person as psychologically disabled with significant impairment in functioning , but certify that the animals are trained and their presence helps the condition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That means , Younggren wrote , &amp;ldquo ; You have to see the person with the animal . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But online there&amp;rsquo ; s none of that . One company&amp;rsquo ; s website says : &amp;ldquo ; If you live in Alberta , Ontario , British Columbia or Newfoundland and Labrador , you can get your ESA Letter from the comfort of your Home for Less than USD 1/Day ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After a quick , click-through questionnaire about how often you&amp;rsquo ; ve felt sad , angry , depressed , frightened , paranoid or suicidal in the last couple of weeks , a phone conversation with a therapist &amp;hellip ; and , of course , paying the money &amp;hellip ; then , you and your pet are good to go . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To make it more official looking , the company also offers a choice of four different styles of dog coats in a range of fabrics for your &amp;lsquo ; certified&amp;rsquo ; ESA dog . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For more choices , there&amp;rsquo ; s Amazon where you get everything from ESA harnesses and leashes to a medallion for $10.25 that claims ( erroneously ) that the emotional support animal is protected by federal law . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Neither Canada nor the United States has federal laws regarding ESAs . What exists is a patchwork with rules that may cover airlines , but could be different from laws regulating airports or even restaurants in airports . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are also other provincial or state laws that apply . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In B.C. , for example , the only exemptions to no-pet rules in condominiums and rental properties are those covered by the Guide Dog Service Animal Act . But a 2016 B.C. Human Rights Tribunal ruling suggested that under the Human Rights Code , an exemption for uncertified pets may be required if not having that pet could put the individual at significant risk . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s no doubt Canadians and Americans love their pets almost to distraction . In 2018 alone , Canadians spent $8 billion on pets , which was nearly double the amount only three years earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Where once dogs and cats might have been sent to kennels , they&amp;rsquo ; ve morphed into pet spas where part of the service is sending daily emails and videos to their vacationing &amp;lsquo ; parents . &amp;rsquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But while service dogs have long proven their worth as constant companions , there&amp;rsquo ; s still some way to go before emotional support animals and their owners get the same kind of consideration . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because , while it may all be part of a developing country adventure to share space on buses with chickens and goats taking their final trip to market , having a turkey as a flight companion or as a next door neighbour is a different thing altogether . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;26205;TOOLONG ... title= " A long list of bizarre and strange animals are queuing for flights alongside their owners . " data-portal-copyright= " Rattankun Thongbun " **28;26503;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1202572 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; After 48 years of criminal defence work and advocacy for prisoners&amp;rsquo ; rights , Abbotsford lawyer John Conroy was staggered at the new numbers revealing the swelling tide of Indigenous people being kept locked up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I started practising in 1972 and I&amp;rsquo ; m 72 years old , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; How can things be worse ? But they are . Here we are in 2020 and it&amp;rsquo ; s worse than ever . I do not understand with the amount of attention and amount of information we have that we&amp;rsquo ; re still in this situation . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The appalling statistics suggest a modern , racially divided Bedlam. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Conroy pointed out &amp;ldquo ; 73 per cent of the men and 80 per cent of the women have the criteria for qualifying for a current mental disorder , 29 require follow-up with mental health services , 25 per cent have some kind of cognitive deficit , 10 to 23 per cent fetal alcohol spectrum disorder ( FASD ) , acquired brain injuries &amp;hellip ; it goes on and on and on . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indigenous people constitute less than five per cent of the population yet now they account for one-in-three of the men in jail , more than four of 10 incarcerated women . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the Prairies , the numbers are worse &amp;mdash ; more than seven out of 10 are Aboriginal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2017-18 , Aboriginal adults represented three-quarters of admissions to custody in Manitoba ( 75 per cent ) and Saskatchewan ( 74 per cent ) . Those provinces also have the highest proportion of Aboriginals , 15 per cent and 14 per cent , respectively . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Compared to 2007-08 , admissions of Aboriginal males increased the most in B.C. ( 83 per cent ) , from 3,932 to 7,181. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Decades of well-meaning Indigenous legal policies have produced the opposite of what was intended &amp;mdash ; increasing incarceration riven by racism &amp;mdash ; a visible disconnect between years of compassionate rhetoric and hard-hearted practice . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;26533;TOOLONG ... title= " Abbotsford lawyer John Conroy : ' There are judges who are sending these people to prison and they seem to be disproportionately sending them to prison compared with non-Aboriginal people . ' " alt= " Abbotsford lawyer John Conroy : ' There are judges who are sending these people to prison and they seem to be disproportionately sending them to prison compared with non-Aboriginal people . ' " data-portal-copyright= " Handout " **28;26569;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 417321 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Having an Indigenous federal attorney general didn&amp;rsquo ; t help &amp;mdash ; the numbers went up on Jody **25;26599;TOOLONG ; s watch as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The shocking report by the country&amp;rsquo ; s correctional investigator , Dr. Ivan Zinger , asserts that the number and proportion of imprisoned Indigenous individuals has reached historic highs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Providing independent oversight of the Correctional Service of Canada , with some 19,000 full-time employees and 53 institutions , Zinger says Indigenous custody rates have accelerated ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Indigenization of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s prison population is nothing short of a national travesty , &amp;rdquo ; Zinger added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since April 2010 the Indigenous inmates have increased by 43.4 per cent ( or 1,265 ) , whereas the non-Indigenous incarcerated population has declined by 13.7 per cent ( or 1,549 ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are judges who are sending these people to prison and they seem to be disproportionately sending them to prison compared with non-Aboriginal people , &amp;rdquo ; Conroy noted . &amp;ldquo ; Why are so many being sentenced to prison ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Year after year , Zinger has documented that Indigenous inmates are disproportionately classified and placed in maximum security institutions , over-represented in use of force and self-injurious incidents , and historically were more likely to be placed and held longer in solitary . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indigenous offenders serve a higher proportion of their sentence behind bars before being granted parole . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Worse , a national recidivism study shows it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t help &amp;mdash ; Indigenous offenders reoffend at much higher levels , as high as 70 per cent on the Prairies. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When you look at the cases coming down the pipe , it isn&amp;rsquo ; t hopeful . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;26626;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;26668;TOOLONG ... Mulgrew : Coverage not denial needed in medicare **27;26832;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Numbers from the Legal Services Society of B.C. indicate Indigenous people account for about one-in-three legal aid criminal cases and about one in four in family cases before the courts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For some reason , in spite of all the hopeful and aspirational rhetoric , legal stakeholders refuse to recognize the reality of Indigenous Canada or the circumstances in which many Aboriginal people live . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When you read the facts of the case , you can&amp;rsquo ; t help but shake your head and say this guy never had a chance , &amp;rdquo ; Conroy said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;A fundamental problem is that few native communities have the resources , the infrastructure or the capacity to handle violent offenders , so it 's very difficult for them to make a claim in court that they should n't be jailed or argue for early release . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a result , more and more Aboriginal men are &amp;ldquo ; banished&amp;rdquo ; across Canada &amp;mdash ; a medieval punishment legally meted out by Indigenous communities to keep away members it can not control . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Similarly , detailed accounts ordered by the Supreme Court of Canada on the effects of colonialism and the social-economic circumstances of an Aboriginal offender -- so-called Gladue Reports -- are seen by some Indigenous advocates as valuable tools to assist judges in crafting appropriate sentences but in the prison bureaucracy they can be detrimental . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;A report showing a history or prevalence of violence can cause a minor offender to be sent to a maximum instead of medium institution . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Over my 25 years dealing with prison law , I have seen a big change from focus on helping a prisoner rehabilitate to managing potential PR problems , &amp;rdquo ; veteran Vancouver defence lawyer Donna Turko said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Various concerns are in play , she explained -- judges ca n't be too easy on violent offenders as native communities need protection , too , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;sentencing circles and diversion-style programs are scarce and &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;parole boards seem increasingly afraid of public opinion and reluctant to release offenders . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;26861;TOOLONG ... title= " Vancouver defence lawyer Donna Turko : ' Over my 25 years dealing with prison law , I have seen a big change from focus on helping a prisoner rehabilitate to managing potential PR problems . ' " alt= " Vancouver defence lawyer Donna Turko : ' Over my 25 years dealing with prison law , I have seen a big change from focus on helping a prisoner rehabilitate to managing potential PR problems . ' " data-portal-copyright= " Arlen Redekop " **28;26897;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1004722 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mostly , though , a shadow has always fallen between the rhetoric about and the reality of Aboriginal crime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider a case in central B.C. involving an older native man who endured residential school and became a dysfunctional alcoholic living off the land . One day , he got very , very drunk and shot a woman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He spent months in pre-trial custody , went in-custody alcohol treatment , took counselling training and , while out on bail for more than two years , acted as a counsellor in his community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But he is facing a mandatory minimum sentence of four years and the Crown wants six years in a federal pen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , the defence wants a provincial sentence of less than two years with an additional conditional term in the community &amp;mdash ; that way he would be incarcerated close to his family , not shipped somewhere across the country . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Which will have a better outcome for the individual , which for the community ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If your aim is to punish and exact a measure of vengeance , a six-year term makes some sense &amp;mdash ; but if it&amp;rsquo ; s long-term healthier citizens and communities , well &amp;hellip ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Bold and urgent&amp;rdquo ; action is needed , Zinger said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; People such as Conroy have been ardently arguing that since the 1970s . It obviously hasn&amp;rsquo ; t mattered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;26927;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;26958;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/ianmulgrew " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **31;26996;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;a href= " **27;27029;TOOLONG " &gt;CLICK HERE&lt;/a&gt; to report a typo. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Is there more to this story ? " data-portal-copyright= " YWCA " **28;27345;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1221060 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Statistics Canada&amp;rsquo ; s latest figures suggest only five per cent of sexual assaults were reported in 2014 and , of those , one in five was dismissed by police as unfounded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One reason may be that Canada&amp;rsquo ; s national force itself has been racked by sexual harassment , discrimination and sexual abuse . In 2016 , the RCMP apologized to female officers and staff and agreed to a $100-million settlement with complainants. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Criminal Code was amended in 2016 to clarify the consent provisions , provide more onerous interim release requirements for offences involving violence against an intimate partner and increase the maximum prison term for repeat offences with abuse of an intimate partner being an aggravating factor in sentencing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But assessing how Canada is doing when it comes to gender-based violence is difficult because the information collected by provinces is fragmented and isn&amp;rsquo ; t designed to allow comparisons among provinces , as both the United Nations Human Rights Commission&amp;rsquo ; s rapporteur and others have pointed out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , the statistics are grim , especially for Indigenous women and girls whose risk of violence is five times higher than that of other Canadians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Every two and a half days , a Canadian woman is killed by an intimate partner . Eight in 10 women report having experienced intimate partner violence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because of the pervasiveness of sexual violence in women&amp;rsquo ; s lives , women are now more likely than men to be victims of violent crime , &amp;rdquo ; according to the &lt;a href= " https : **33;27375;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;UN rapporteur 's report&lt;/a&gt; released in July . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;27410;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;27452;TOOLONG ... the odds , a Canadian woman is granted asylum in the U.S. under the UN Convention Against **28;27487;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Technology is one reason it is now more difficult for women fleeing a stalker . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; With technology , people are now able to track their partners much more easily , &amp;rdquo ; Rupert said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If you want to stay safe , the advice is stay off of all social media . Don&amp;rsquo ; t use apps on your phone and don&amp;rsquo ; t use technology in ways that are so much part of our lives , said Rupert , adding , &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not fair and it&amp;rsquo ; s imposing another punishment on the victim . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;There was a time when provincial legal aid programs provided lawyers in cases of domestic violence . " That was amazing , " Rupert said . " I wish we could go back to that . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last year , Ontario eliminated funding for it . British Columbia eliminated it several years ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even for women willing to take the extreme measure of leaving Canada , it&amp;rsquo ; s harder . Twice in the last two years , two different U.S. attorneys general have ordered that domestic violence and gang affiliation are acceptable reasons for granting asylum . The first order was overturned in the courts , the second is under appeal . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s another twist . An unintended consequence of the well-meaning Hague Convention on International Child Abduction is it binds women to their abusers , often forcing them to remain in countries where they are not citizens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; If a father has a custody order , women who flee abroad with their children can be charged with abduction . Child abduction carries a penalty of up to 10 years in prison . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2019 , StatsCan &lt;a href= " https : **33;27517;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;reported&lt;/a&gt; that the percentage of non-permanent resident women living in Canadian transition houses was six times higher than in the general population . The number of non-resident children was nearly 10 times higher . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Because of that , YWCA-Vancouver has three rooms permanently designated for them along with funding to help them apply for citizenship . Japanese women have been the most frequent occupants , followed by Americans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for how many women fleeing from domestic violence and gangs in other countries come here and are granted asylum , nobody knows . The Canadian government doesn&amp;rsquo ; t track that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The best information comes from a 2018 CBC &lt;a href= " https : **33;27552;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **27;27587;TOOLONG that found 15 per cent of female refugee claimants who arrived between 2013 and 2017 listed gender persecution ( a.k.a. domestic violence ) as their primary reason before religious , ethnic or political persecution . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of the nearly 3,000 domestic violence claims heard by the Immigration and Refugee Board , 58 per cent were accepted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For generations and across most societies , domestic violence has been hidden away . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Historically , women and children were not deemed to have rights , so domestic violence was seen as a private matter , not a public concern . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That notion persists , as does the faulty belief that someone who assaults a loved one is less of a monster than one who abuses a stranger and less of a risk to others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have to recognize that the people they are assaulting are members of society , that there is a cost to those people and to their family members and a financial cost to the larger society , &amp;rdquo ; says Rupert . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We need to recognize that there is a risk to other people and the other partners of those people as well as to the children that even trickles down to grandchildren . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;27616;TOOLONG " **36;27647;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamMon , 27 Jan 2020 21:44:00 **45;27685;TOOLONG ... &amp;amp ; ChildHealthLifeLocal **45;27732;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ahmed said the officer was within his rights to decide that Reyes Garcia had misrepresented information about the money laundering investigation when he first applied for an electronic travel authorization that would allow him repeated entry to Canada as a visitor . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But Ahmed sided with Reyes Garcia&amp;rsquo ; s claim that he was denied due process by the CBSA. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In my view , it was open to the officer to form his own opinion as to an alleged misrepresentation based on the interview and the applicant&amp;rsquo ; s ( electronic ) application , &amp;rdquo ; Ahmed said in a written ruling released Jan. 22. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; However , although it was open to the officer to form an opinion as to an alleged misrepresentation &amp;hellip ; the officer did not have the authority to make a final admissibility determination . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The judge said Canadian immigration law says the CBSA officer could have written a report of his concerns and sent the matter to the Immigration Division to hold an inadmissibility hearing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Only the minister&amp;rsquo ; s delegate or the Immigration Division may make such findings , the judge ruled . &amp;ldquo ; Therefore , the officer erred in finding that the applicant had misrepresented and that he was therefore inadmissible , &amp;rdquo ; Ahmed said . &amp;ldquo ; I find the officer breached procedural fairness and that the officer&amp;rsquo ; s decision is unreasonable . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ahmed set aside the original CBSA decision and sent the case back for another officer to consider . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Last fall , Postmedia obtained a transcript of Reyes Garcia&amp;rsquo ; s interview with the CBSA agent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In it , the agent alleged Reyes Garcia and his business partner Manuel Barreiro had been misusing foreign companies , including one set up in B.C. called Kross Investments Ltd. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What connects you to Manuel is a money-laundering scandal in Mexico , &amp;rdquo ; CBSA agent Rahim Bajwa said to Reyes Garcia , citing conversations found on the Mexican man&amp;rsquo ; s cellphone. &amp;ldquo ; There is discussion about money leaving Mexico and entering Canada &amp;mdash ; discussion about you and Manuel attempting secret meetings in Canada and opening up false companies in Canada . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reyes Garcia said the allegations against him and his business partner stem from a &amp;ldquo ; political problem&amp;rdquo ; in Mexico . He said the former Mexican president&amp;rsquo ; s party targeted Barreiro for investigation because he had business with a rival presidential candidate . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Reyes Garcia said that while allegations were made against him in the Mexican media , he was never charged and has been cleared of any wrongdoing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He voluntarily returned to Mexico after his airport interview , but filed the Federal Court challenge to regain his travel document . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bajwa , the CBSA agent , noted that on Reyes Garcia&amp;rsquo ; s cellphone were details of financial transactions involving cash sent from Mexico through the B.C. company to a Swiss bank . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In the most basic form , what is happening right now is called money laundering . These activities and these sorts of transactions are confined to money laundering &amp;mdash ; money leaving Mexico , going through Canada and various other parts of the world , &amp;rdquo ; Bajwa said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Once the money has left Mexico , it is difficult to trace . Money launderers are aware of this and try their best to hide the trade because they don&amp;rsquo ; t want anything to come back to them . This is done because the money is earned through illegitimate means , including drug trafficking , embezzlement , misappropriation of funds etc. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;&lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; **52;28638;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;blog : **42;28692;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **39;28736;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Kim BolanSat , 25 Jan 2020 22:30:03 **45;28777;TOOLONG ... NewsNationalIan Mulgrew : Coverage not denial needed in medicare crisishttp : **34;28824;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;28860;TOOLONG ... title= " " alt= " " data-portal-copyright= " Getty Images/iStockphoto " **28;28896;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1179250 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;28926;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Medicare is in crisis across Canada while governments fiddle and insist there is no place for private insurance to cover medically necessary care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A new report by the &lt;a href= " https : **26;28962;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Fraser Institute&lt;/a&gt; says the de facto ban looks like folly since we are alone among 17 countries &amp;mdash ; including Australia , Germany , Switzerland and the Netherlands &amp;mdash ; who provide universal health-care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada has the longest wait times , ranking in 2016 in last place for the percentage of patients who waited four weeks or longer to see a specialist , last for the percentage of patients who waited four weeks or longer to get treatment , and last for the percentage of patients who waited four or more hours in emergency departments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Written by Steven Globerman , the 46-page study by the conservative think tank says eliminating the prohibition could shorten health care queues and encourage cost-efficient innovations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The idea of using private insurance to cover some or all health-care costs &amp;mdash ; instead of taxpayers paying for it &amp;mdash ; has been pilloried in Canada for many years , but it&amp;rsquo ; s a common feature of other universal health-care systems around the world , &amp;rdquo ; said the resident scholar and Addington Chair in Measurement , professor emeritus , Western Washington University . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Trouble is , medicare in this country is a patchwork quilt &amp;mdash ; there are a baker&amp;rsquo ; s dozen jurisdictions and medical systems . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As a result , you should get private insurance for travel within Canada so you don&amp;rsquo ; t wake up in a hospital in another province or territory owing a small fortune for an ambulance trip or other service for which you aren&amp;rsquo ; t covered . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At the marathon B.C. medicare constitutional trial , which includes a challenge to the province&amp;rsquo ; s ban on private insurance , it was evident both levels of government would rather Canadians remained in the dark , mistakenly believing they have the best health care system in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most cogent expert opinion and the data presented during more than three years of evidence , however , indicated the situation instead is dire , and this latest study echoes that view . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Titled &lt;a href= " https : **33;28990;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Understanding Universal Health Care Reform Options : Private Insurance&lt;/a&gt; , the report released Tuesday underscores Canada&amp;rsquo ; s laggard performance compared with other developed countries providing universal health care : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2016 , no one in Germany waited four months for elective surgery , but nearly one in five Canadians did ; only one in a hundred waited more than an hour in a French emergency room , while 29 in 100 Canadians sat around waiting to be seen ; in the Netherlands , 77 per cent of patients got a same-day appointment , only 44 per cent of Canadians did . Even Americans do better than us. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the 2000s , the Supreme Court of Canada wrestled with the issue of private insurance in a Quebec case known as &lt;a href= " https : **33;29025;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The majority held that a ban on private insurance was unconstitutional given pernicious waiting times in the public system . For all the government hand-wringing , however , the decision did not result in significant change . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regulation minimized the procedures private insurance could cover &amp;mdash ; hip and knee replacement and cataract surgery ( those with the longest queues ) , who may provide the surgeries and where they may be provided . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Quebec medicare endures. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other nations allow two options : full coverage of all medically necessary services or supplementary coverage that facilitates faster access to medical procedures and treatments , a wider selection of providers and amenities such as private rooms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There is little legal scope or opportunity in Canada for either . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Without any evidence , both senior levels of government insist allowing such private insurance will reduce public access to health care or let the well-heeled obtain &amp;ldquo ; better&amp;rdquo ; care . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The official fearmongering includes predicting the very death of Medicare . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No developed country has experienced such a catastrophe by providing private insurance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And the rich in Canada can already get quicker , perhaps even &amp;ldquo ; better&amp;rdquo ; care , anytime with a cheap flight to the U.S. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the evidence from Europe indicated , Globerman maintained a private health insurance market might reduce wait times for most if not all services . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In this regard , he noted the poor would enjoy improved access notwithstanding that their access would not be identical to that enjoyed by wealthier Canadians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Interestingly , Globerman believed that the most significant benefit flowing from private insurance could be innovation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His research indicated models like Canada&amp;rsquo ; s often limit or restrict access to innovative medical treatment in the interest of short-term cost savings , while private insurers have stronger incentives to embrace innovations that may increase short-term costs but ultimately save money by improving long-term health outcomes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Globerman added &amp;ldquo ; a systematic reevaluation of allowing access to private health insurance for basic services seems appropriate , especially in light of theory and evidence that argues , on balance , that doing so would have net social benefits . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But I&amp;rsquo ; m sure his report will be dismissed by government and vested interests as right-wing propaganda . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Better to stick with the current three monkeys&amp;rsquo ; approach &amp;mdash ; hear , see and brook no discussion about medicare&amp;rsquo ; s ailments and potential cures . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;29060;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;29091;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; In both places , middle-class young people are being squeezed out of home ownership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though there are differences between the affluent housing markets in New York and Vancouver , which are routinely ranked among the &lt;a href= " http : **34;29381;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;world 's sought-after destinations&lt;/a&gt; , the downward trend is similar in the East and West Coast cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As with New York&amp;rsquo ; s flashy highrises , many luxury condos with spectacular views in Vancouver are going un-bought . Dramatic price drops are also occurring among the posh single-family residences of Metro Vancouver , where prices have plunged by more than one-quarter since the peak in 2017. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Global media outlets have noted that popular Canadian singer Michael Bubl&amp;eacute ; last year had to sell his sprawling West Vancouver mansion for 28 per cent less than its assessed value . It was bought by the only one who showed interest : An increasingly hard-to-find buyer from China . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Prices have plummeted by more than 25 per cent in the past two years across hilly West Vancouver , which is often ranked as the municipality with the highest per capita income in Canada . A similar dip has occurred in the city of Vancouver and many of its suburbs , where assessed &lt;a href= " http : **34;29417;TOOLONG ... went down by more than 11 per cent in 2019 alone . &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;29453;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " http : **34;29495;TOOLONG ... Most of these swank tower homes are priced at more than $2,400 a square foot , completely out of reach of local wage earners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet that&amp;rsquo ; s a common square-foot cost for thousands of other exorbitant condo units being built in this West Coast city , which is often ranked among the world&amp;rsquo ; s most unaffordable . The gap between median wages and median housing costs in Vancouver is far greater than in New York City , which has the advantage of being a global financial centre . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Knight Frank Global Real Estate Consultants , which tracks prices in 15 of the world&amp;rsquo ; s most sought-after cities , projects that New York City&amp;rsquo ; s overall housing prices will fall again in 2020 , by 4.4 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s housing values are &lt;a href= " https : **33;29697;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;forecast to tumble even more this year , by 10.2 per cent&lt;/a&gt; overall , which Knight Frank says will be the steepest drop in all 15 of the world&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; prime&amp;rdquo ; cities ( which include London , Hong Kong , Los Angeles and Dubai ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Developers globally thought the way to make money was to build luxury , &amp;rdquo ; says a Vancouver-based real estate analyst , &lt;a href= " http : **34;29732;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Steve Saretsky. &lt;/a&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; But the general theme is the luxury market in global cities has really died off . It&amp;rsquo ; s going to be a sluggish market in Vancouver . The luxury bid , particularly out of China , has really slowed down . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tighter local government regulations are a factor . The B.C. government&amp;rsquo ; s 20 per cent foreign-buyers tax and speculation and vacancy tax , which are designed to discourage offshore and domestic investment , have been working . But they&amp;rsquo ; re similar to rising restrictions in most of the world&amp;rsquo ; s top housing markets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most important thing curbing elite housing is the global economic slowdown , plus restrictions on the amount of money allowed to flow out of China , whose buyers account for one out of four purchases in Sydney and London . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The power of buyers from China has been even greater in Vancouver , which has a much higher proportion of ethnic Chinese residents . China is home to one-sixth of the world&amp;rsquo ; s new millionaires , a cohort that&amp;rsquo ; s been expanding at the rate of 250 an hour for the past eight years , according to The Economist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And the &lt;a href= " http : **34;29768;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;Hurun Global Housing Index&lt;/a&gt; says relatively small Vancouver remains the seventh most sought-after city in the world for investors from China , many of whom are looking for a haven for their capital . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Even though the valuations on Metro&amp;rsquo ; s most pricey single-family homes are clearly declining sharply , one could argue that Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s trendy needle towers are not hit quite as hard as those in New York City . Still , figures indicate a slowdown . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Vancouver&amp;rsquo ; s top-of-the-line developers used to boast they could entirely &amp;ldquo ; pre-sell&amp;rdquo ; towers of condo units ranging from $2 million to $20 million each , before they&amp;rsquo ; re built . Now figures from the Altus Group show a significant portion of the thousands of upmarket condo units being constructed have not found buyers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The market in Metro Vancouver today has kind of switched back to being a local market , &amp;rdquo ; says Saretsky. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The high-end market is coming down . What is moving is the affordable stuff , including the one-bedroom condos in the City of Vancouver . They&amp;rsquo ; re getting multiple offers , and in some cases their prices are actually pushing up , because it&amp;rsquo ; s all anyone can afford , &amp;rdquo ; Saretsky said . Developers , especially in Surrey , Richmond and Langley , are responding again to the domestic market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; High-end developers might end up stuck with more of their units than they would have liked , he said . &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t know if they&amp;rsquo ; re worried , because they&amp;rsquo ; re well-capitalized . If they start discounting prices quite a bit , that kind of screws everybody who bought into the building initially . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Saretsky can&amp;rsquo ; t say how it&amp;rsquo ; s all going to play out for domestic buyers . &amp;ldquo ; Do the reductions at the high end trickle down ? Or does it all trickle up ? &amp;rdquo ; The key thing he knows is the Metro market is now extremely segmented . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s the case in most of the world&amp;rsquo ; s desirable cities , where there is a crisis of homelessness , as well as unaffordability for the middle class , at the same time the world&amp;rsquo ; s multimillionaires have been , at least until two years ago , driving up values . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Whether the downturns in New York , Vancouver and &lt;a href= " http : **34;29804;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;other prime cities&lt;/a&gt; will stretch on for years is difficult to predict . She was a devout Catholic , and I knew what her beliefs were . So I never would have considered assisted dying for her . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 57-year-old former McGill law professor , more comfortable quoting legal precedent than an example from his own life , continued : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; My brothers and I were well aware of what her feelings were . That being said , we did at a certain point have to make a decision that she not undergo further treatment &amp;mdash ; which is in a sense a delegated decision , although fully within her belief structure , within the church&amp;rsquo ; s belief structure , and within the medical structure . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lametti said Canadians have long accepted such delegated decisions when a life was at stake . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30245;TOOLONG ... title= " David Lametti speaks to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau after being presented as Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada at Rideau Hall in Ottawa , November 20 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " REUTERS/Blair Gable " **28;30281;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1187616 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This MAID provides another way for people to chose in an autonomous fashion how they wish to end their life given certain conditions , and usually under very tragic circumstances or sad circumstances or personal circumstances . I think maybe even overwhelmingly positive . &amp;hellip ; And I think there is a large acceptance of the practice amongst practitioners , amongst people who are facing , in particular , terminal illness . Bramham : Outspoken activist against polygamy dieshttp : **36;30495;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;30533;TOOLONG ... title= " Debbie Palmer , a former plural wife from Bountiful , in 2004 . ( Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun ) " alt= " Debbie Palmer , a former plural wife from Bountiful , in 2004 . ( Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun ) " data-portal-copyright= " Ian Smith " **28;30569;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1194741 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;30599;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; If it weren&amp;rsquo ; t for Debbie Palmer , Canadians might not know anything about the polygamous community of Bountiful in southeastern British Columbia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was the first to lift the veil of secrecy that had protected the community from outsiders in the early 1990s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; By demanding criminal charges against the leaders for their abuse of women and children , she became a thorn in the sides of a succession of provincial attorneys-general , police and other politicians . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But she was shunned and shamed by family and childhood friends . Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s activism took a huge toll . She died last weekend at the age of 64. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Palmer was the oldest in a family of 47 children . When she was only six , her mother died , leaving Debbie and her two siblings to be raised by their father&amp;rsquo ; s other five wives , who had multiple children of their own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At 15 , Palmer was one of Bountiful&amp;rsquo ; s first child brides . In a religious ceremony , she became the sixth wife of the community&amp;rsquo ; s leader , Ray Blackmore . He was 40 years older than her . Palmer was a widow by 18. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The community&amp;rsquo ; s elders &amp;ndash ; all men &amp;mdash ; placed her in another plural marriage to an man who was so abusive that she was released and later married Marvin Palmer with whom she had five children . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But life in Bountiful finally became intolerable and , in 1988 , the mother of eight fled becoming one of the first women in either Canada or the United States to escape without leaving any of her children behind . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Almost immediately , Palmer began telling her story to journalists , including Sally Armstrong from Chatelaine and The Province&amp;rsquo ; s Fabian Dawson . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When the RCMP ended its investigation in 1992 and recommended charges against Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s father , Dalmon Oler , and against Winston Blackmore , the **26;30635;TOOLONG ; s ministry decided not to proceed . Taking advice from former B.C. Supreme Court chief justices , it was determined that Canada&amp;rsquo ; s law against polygamy was unconstitutional . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30663;TOOLONG ... title= " Debbie Palmer , a former plural wife from Bountiful , in 2004 . ( Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun ) " alt= " Debbie Palmer , a former plural wife from Bountiful , in 2004 . ( Ian Smith/Vancouver Sun ) " data-portal-copyright= " Ian Smith " **28;30699;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1194741 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Disappointed , but not daunted , Palmer convinced then-women&amp;rsquo ; s equality minister Penny Priddy to fund a report about polygamy and the physical and sexual abuse of women in &amp;ldquo ; a religious community in B.C.&amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Life in Bountiful report revealed a pattern of forced marriages , rigid demands of obedience , and a &amp;ldquo ; distinct culture &amp;hellip ; that limits individual rights to the point of virtually eliminating them . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It questioned whether children raised there could ever be capable of exercising free choice , including giving informed consent to sex and marriage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was so explosive that the government refused to release it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rancher Faye Street had been on the committee that helped put the report together . &amp;ldquo ; I met with every goddamned minister and everybody I could to talk about what was going on in there , &amp;rdquo ; she told me in 2007. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I used to go home and not be able to sleep because I kept thinking , &amp;lsquo ; How can this be happening here . We&amp;rsquo ; re not from the Ozarks. &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , Palmer became friends with Jon Krakauer , whose 2003 book , Under the Banner of Heaven , focused international attention on the fundamentalist Mormons. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2004 , Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s sister Jane Blackmore also fled Bountiful . The midwife and ex-wife of the once powerful bishop Winston Blackmore couldn&amp;rsquo ; t have been more different . Debbie was a passionate , emotional firebrand . Jane is reserved , cautious and uncomfortable with the activist role that has frequently been forced upon her as a witness subpoenaed to testify against her ex-husband , her stepbrother and others . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At that time , both were enmeshed in a series of other events that were unfolding &amp;mdash ; a schism between two factions in Bountiful , the manhunt for Warren Jeffs , the prophet of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints , and Utah&amp;rsquo ; s and Arizona&amp;rsquo ; s successful seizure of FLDS assets that were to be used to compensate polygamy&amp;rsquo ; s victims , including the so-called Lost Boys forced out of their communities to make polygamy&amp;rsquo ; s cruel arithmetic add up in favour of old men . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s self-published and thinly disguised autobiography titled Keep Sweet : Children of Polygamy was briefly a Canadian bestseller in 2006 , even though it was not readily available in Creston &amp;mdash ; the town nearest to Bountiful. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But by then , Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s information was mostly historic . With a growing number of people leaving the FLDS , the spotlight had shifted and Palmer retreated into private life &amp;mdash ; not even emerging for B.C.&amp;rsquo ; s subsequent constitutional reference case or later trials . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet without her pioneering efforts , two former fundamentalist Mormon bishops &amp;mdash ; her stepbrother James Oler , and Winston Blackmore , her brother-in-law and stepson &amp;mdash ; might never have been convicted of polygamy , and Oler and Brandon Blackmore ( another of Palmer&amp;rsquo ; s stepsons ) and his wife , Gail Blackmore , might never have been jailed for illegally taking their under-aged daughters to the United States for coerced marriages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The admonition to women and girls to Keep Sweet might have remained , spelled out in white stone on the mountainside above the government-funded school . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To anyone exposed to her unrelenting anger and what was , at the time , her seemingly incredible tales of abuse , Palmer could be exhausting and , at times , exasperating . She needed to be all of that and more in order to be heard . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And , in the end , Palmer proved Margaret Mead&amp;rsquo ; s contention that it is the few caring people who change the world . Deborah Ann Oler Palmer was one of those who changed hers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;30729;TOOLONG " **36;30760;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Twitter : @bramhamdaphne &lt;/p&gt; Daphne BramhamWed , 22 Jan 2020 18:27:57 **45;30798;TOOLONG ... **45;30845;TOOLONG ... @@31732832 <h> Solar panels in Portugal . <h> Referenced Symbols <p> It 's becoming clearer by the hour that the coronavirus pandemic represents an unprecedented global threat to both public health and global economies . The speed of the crisis and the change to our everyday existence , as well as the threat to our most vulnerable , is astonishing and has all of us reflecting on our values and investments . <p> But even in these dark early days , it 's possible to make out what could be a silver lining : The crisis points to the potential of a new normal that 's better for our climate future as investors reweight their portfolios in light of current events . <h> Stress test <p> The virus has already given us a sneak peek into our dependencies on energy prices and the transition to a low-carbon future , a kind of stress test . The virtual freezing of air travel and shutdowns of factories has dramatically reduced air pollution in China and Italy , and will likely result in a significant drop in energy demand and , thus , carbon emissions , at least for a time . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ market falls of recent days , which were also influenced by Saudi Arabia 's move to flood the world with cheap oil , we 've seen that the renewable energy sector and other companies less reliant on fossil fuels have been relatively favored by investors . <p> Of the S&amp;P 500 SPX , -4.33% companies , we 've identified 200 as leaders in managing climate risk . Collectively those 200 are outperforming the rest of the S&amp;P 500 by 33% since the panic began . <p> Those 200 leaders were identified in our scoring of companies ' underlying climate change readiness , essentially because of their ability to manage climate risks . They include American Electric Power AEP , -11.58% , an investor-owned utility that has focused on modernizing its grid and investing in renewables ; NextEra Energy NEE , -7.41% , which has set aggressive carbon-reduction goals relative to its competition ; Delta DAL , -0.74% , which committed to carbon neutrality long before other airlines ; and Tesla TSLA , -0.02% , whose distinction from other automakers is self-explanatory . An example of a company not among those @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ unlike other energy producers has n't attempted a major pivot away from fossil fuels . <h> Flight to renewables <p> There 's reason to believe that this investment trend could outlast the coronavirus crisis and the current oil shock . Or , at least , investors would be smart to maintain this shift as a kind of " flight to quality . " <p> Because , in effect , these events are acting like a grand natural experiment that simulates what will happen in the future when governments make the sweeping policy changes that will be needed to head off dangerous climate change . Changes such as carbon taxes , bigger subsidies to renewables , and tougher regulation on land use or energy efficiency . <p> In effect , COVID-19 is providing a test for how well companies are prepared for a volatile future in which energy consumption , its associated carbon intensity , and policy changes will be dictated by climate change . <p> By giving investors a painful lesson in these risks , ranging from energy-price volatility to policy impact , this crisis could help create a clearer @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ since pre-industrial times to well below 2.0 degrees Celsius ( 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit ) . Companies are sensitive to market signals , and when investors move to low carbon investment pastures , companies are likely to be nudged away from fossil fuel dependency . <h> ESG funds <p> The performance of environmental , social and governance investments amid the intense volatility of recent weeks appears to bear this out . The sector has defied skeptics who warned that it would be among the most vulnerable to a market reverse after seeing a record amount of inflows last year . <p> For instance , fund flows into ESG ETFs have held up far better than the wider market -- a difference of only 8% of ESG ETFs saw outflows , compared to almost a quarter of all others . <p> While it remains to be seen how durable some of our investing and climate behavior changes will endure beyond the crisis , we do know there will be some new habits formed , resulting in fundamental realignments of consumption toward lower-carbon outcomes . <p> The coronavirus-induced stampede by business people and @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , for example , is likely to result in less demand for transport over the long term as people grow used to fewer physical interactions . Carbon-heavy industries are also likely to emerge from the crisis in a much weaker state , handing a natural competitive advantage to companies that are investing in energy efficiency , renewable energy and low carbon practices . <h> Risk of isolationism <p> The way governments and societies respond to this crisis will go a long way to determining whether it results in a more sustainable future . <p> To be sure , there is a risk that some countries will respond by withdrawing deeper into national isolationism -- China 's recent decision to expel American reporters being one example -- and reducing international cooperation . The United States could respond by doubling down on its domestic supplies of oil and gas to promote a localized , self-sufficient economy . <p> That would be a misguided reaction , in our view . This is a moment when the world needs to revive international cooperation , both to stamp out the coronavirus and to work on @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ change and manage the risks of transition to a new kind of economy . <p> Thomas H. Consequently , much research has focused on China 's influence on climate change but somewhat less has been written about the impact of climate change on China . China experienced explosive economic growth in recent decades , but with only 7% of the world 's arable land available to feed 22% of the world 's population , China 's economy may be vulnerable to climate change itself . We find , however , that notwithstanding the clear warming that has occurred in China in recent decades , current understanding does not allow a clear assessment of the impact of anthropogenic climate change on China 's water resources and agriculture and therefore China 's @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ definitive conclusion , future work must improve regional climate simulations -- especially of precipitation -- and develop a better understanding of the managed and unmanaged responses of crops to changes in climate , diseases , pests and atmospheric constituents . <h> Main <p> Climate change and its impacts on water resources and crop production is a major force with which China and the rest of the world will have to cope in the twenty-first century1,2 . In China , despite the growing importance of industry , agriculture has a central role in ensuring the food security and welfare of 1.3 ? billion people . At first glance , a map of China 's climate and ecosystems ( Fig. 1 ) reveals an uneven distribution of water resources between the south , where water is abundant , and the drier north . We highlight the main areas of vulnerability and sources of uncertainty based on recent literature and published data . We present an analysis progressing from well-observed recent trends to more uncertain model projections and mechanisms . The first section deals with recent climate change observations and projections from climate models . Particular attention is given to drought and flood extremes . The second section addresses past and projected future trends in water resources , investigates whether the recent changes are unusual or within the bounds of normal climatic variability , and assesses the contribution of human withdrawals of water versus climate forcing . In this context , we review changes in glacier mass balance and their impact on hydrosystems . This can be addressed by using regional models fitted with aerosol and chemistry effects on climate and improved description of land -- atmosphere feedback processes , to enable improved impact studies and to design cost-effective adaptation measures4 . <h> A country of drought and floods <p> China is at risk from heavy rainfalls , heatwaves and drought5,13,14 . Heatwaves have occurred more frequently during the past 50 years , except over central China15 . A significant reduction of cold days in winter has also been observed16 . Trends in heavy rainfall events causing floods show high spatial heterogeneity13,14 . These extreme events seem to become more frequent over northwestern China and the mid- to lower reaches of the Yangtze River @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Yangtze River13 . Meanwhile , a general decrease in the number of rainy days has been observed across the entire country ( see Box 1 ) . According to regional climate models , the frequency of heatwaves and rainfall extremes in the future may increase over most of the country17 . <p> Drought is one of the most severe manifestations of climate variability in China . It is a source of concern for agriculture and human life , given that the country is already quite dry18 ( 3.32 ? ? ? 106 ? km2 of drylands ) . Over the past six decades , very severe droughts hit China in the 1960s , in the late 1970s and early 1980s , and in the late 1990s19 . Recently , northeastern China has suffered particularly from drought20,21 while , surprisingly , arid regions of northwestern China have enjoyed less-severe droughts ( Fig. 1 ) , as indicated by rising lake levels and increased vegetation cover on desert margins22 . <p> A key question is whether northeastern China will continue to suffer from drought in the future . Here again , results @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ uncertainty . Under the IPCC A1B scenario7 , it is predicted that the recently observed dipole of drier northeast China and wetter northwest China may further intensify23 . In contrast , under the IPCC B1 scenario7 , a decrease of drought in northeast China is projected24 . To understand and project drought occurrences better , we need to pay more attention to the effects of soil moisture feedbacks on climate25 . Analysing the big droughts of the twentieth century26 should further help researchers to identify key drought traits such as duration , intensity and extent , the processes that affect ecosystems and water resources most adversely , and the differences in regional responses . <h> River runoff and water resources <p> As the demand by agriculture , industry and households for water increases , its availability is becoming a key factor in China 's development27,28 . China 's total fresh water volume is 2.81 ? ? ? 1012 ? m3 , with 2.7 ? ? ? 1012 ? m3 of surface water and 0.83 ? ? ? 1012 ? m3 of groundwater29 . Although this water resource is large in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ per capita water resource is only 25% of the world average30 . Moreover , the distribution of water resources is spatially and seasonally uneven . The north of the country , similar in land area and population to the south , holds only 18% of the total water despite having 65% of the total arable land . By contrast , the south receives water from summer rainfalls , which is often ' wasted ' through flooding . <h> Observed trends <p> In this context , a key question is how the drying of northeastern regions coupled to the warming trend across China has affected water resources . This question is difficult to answer , because one must disentangle the effects of climate change from those of increased human withdrawal . We reviewed runoff changes in the two largest river basins of China : the Yangtze River and the Yellow River ( Fig. 1 ) . The Yellow river is a perfect example of a large northern catchment sensitive to drying trends , conjugated with intense human withdrawal ( 109 million people concerned ) . The Yangtze River , on the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ its central and middle reach ( 487 million people concerned ) . In addition , we selected the Tarim River ( Fig. 1 ) , the largest inland river in China , as a case study of the effect of glacier retreat on river runoff . <h> Many influences on variable trends in runoff <p> The Yangtze River shows only a small and statistically insignificant increase in annual runoff31,32 since 1960 ( Fig. 2a ) . In autumn , many gauged headwater catchments even record decreasing runoff , an observation explained partly by declining regional precipitation33 . In summer , the middle and lower Yangtze reaches show a positive runoff trend33 driven by increasing precipitation . About 50% of the summer precipitation is received as rainstorms , bringing an increased risk of summer flooding in the Yangtze over the past 40 ? years ( ref. 34 ) . In the lower reaches of the Pearl River further south , a trend similar to that of the lower Yangtze River is observed . The runoff has increased by 12% since the 1960s , owing to an increase in precipitation35 . <p> @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ two major Chinese rivers . <p> a , Observed inter-annual variation in the Yangtze River annual runoff at the Datong station ( red dot on China map in inset ; grey shading indicates the area of the Yangtze River basin ) from 1960 to 2000 . This decline is more pronounced from the upper to the lower basin36 . Daily drying-up of the river is observed more frequently at the Lijin hydrological station at the Yellow River mouth over the last 40 ? years , especially during the 1990s37 . The onset of daily drying-up is occurring earlier in the year and the period of zero flow has lengthened37 . The observed decrease in the runoff of the Yellow River is interesting because it reflects both climate change impacts and over-extraction of water for irrigation , industry and domestic usage38 . Increased withdrawals can explain about 35% @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ the lower reaches ( see Fig. 2b ) over the last half-century39 . This case study shows that , even for such a heavily managed river , climate is dominant in controlling runoff . When projecting the future of both the Yangtze and the Yellow River , however , not only precipitation trends , but also glacier melt come into the picture . These changes are analysed below . <h> Waning glaciers <p> Changes in glacier mass balance critically affect river runoff and agricultural development in China and south Asian countries . China has 46,377 glaciers , covering an area of 59,425 ? km2 ( refs 40 and 41 ) . Owing to the current pronounced warming , more than 80% of the glaciers in western China are currently in a state of retreat42,43,44,45 ( Fig. 3 ) . Temperature reconstruction suggests that the last five decades were the warmest in the past 500 years over the Qinghai -- Xizang Plateau46 . In the Qinghai -- Xizang Plateau , glaciers shrank by 7% ( 3,790 ? km2 ) over the past four decades45 , with an average decrease in thickness @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ balance observations are scarce , several lines of evidence support a mass loss by Chinese glaciers43,44,47,48 . For instance , the mass balance of the Hailuogou valley glacier ( 26 ? km2 ) shifted from an accumulation of 109 ? mm ? yr-1 during 1971 -- 1985 to a net loss47 of 538 ? mm ? yr-1 during 1986 -- 2004 . The Urumqi Glacier No.1 , the glacier in China with the longest observation history and the one studied in most detail , has lost mass at the rate of 234 ? mm ? yr-1 over the past five decades49 . <p> Figure 3 : Observed annual rate of change in glacier area at 22 monitoring stations in western China over the past 30 -- 40 ? years . <p> A negative rate indicates a shrinking glacier42,98 .
